However, small log-probability improvements for person/abstract conditions do not consistently exceed both random controls, and the wrong-country control slightly increases country-class top1 to62.5% while worsening every paired margin. These mismatches show why one must report full-vocabulary metrics alongside the paired contrast.

Scope of recovery: mean no-prefix-minus-context paired-margin gaps are1.124(country),0.948(city),1.075(person),0.676(abstract). Restoration's aligned gap recovery, sum(gain*gap)/sum(gap²), is16.6%,8.8%,7.8%,11.6%, respectively. This is not the ratio of mean gains to mean gaps (for country that different statistic is30.8%), nor a percentage of all model computation explained. Most prefix-associated changes remain outside the restored edge, and template removal changes more than the isolated coefficient.

Interpretation: the source-dependent payload and context-dependent edge strength have separable, causally relevant roles. The existing lexical operator is therefore a useful candidate computational unit, with routing treated as another component. This does not yet prove that the same unit is reused across tasks or identify a feature manifold. The intervention depends on native prefix values and a target-specific baseline coefficient; it is not an autonomous replacement program.

Limits:128 correlated rows represent only four target pairs and sixteen distractor words. This is an intervention on previously opened discovery contexts, not held-out generalization. Two fixed random directions are limited controls, not a distributional null estimate. Strengthening an answer-supporting edge could improve answers without explaining why its native coefficient changed; no optimality or model-error-repair claim follows.

Control output norms match within1.53e-7relative. Hypotheses narrowed: pure magnitude-only explanation is inadequate because equal-norm task directions beat random and donor identity explains substantial variation. Strong arbitrary donor-context conjunction is not needed for this one scalar task in these contexts. Leading interpretation is a shared functional read direction with recipient-dependent gain and finite-scale curvature. Competing explanations include correlated discovery prompts, a generic task-output bottleneck, and a shared component inherited from the rank-one embedding intervention itself. The latter is particularly important: we deliberately constructed all source changes from one number-decoder intervention, so discovered response rank is not evidence that arbitrary natural computation is rank one. Earlier100-output transport results and this single-output result measure different objects and are not contradictory.

Next fit the donor potency from source directions using discovery reference responses and predict recipient gain from clean context, with simple mean/norm controls. The concrete target for a featurizer is causal response coordinates, potentially simpler than activation geometry; no claimed manifold yet.

Paired edits add P(donorwrite-recipientwrite) to the native recipient. The full donor patch in that recipient context is the reference. KL here is KL(native model output || reconstructed-state output), in nats, not the full-donor-reference KL used in prior experiments. ## H1002 — Frozen noun contrast follows actions more than background tools, with limited novel-verb transfer

Previous turn was progress: H1001 found compact noun-contrast transfer and exposed fragment vocabulary dependence. This turn tests the frozen nounrank1 direction with crossed background tools and actions. Eighty unique prompts,72paired comparisons,80native forwards plus1008intervention forwards=1088total. No new fitting, prompt replacement, or revised answer groups.

Four subjects cross background knife/key with cut/unlocked, sliced/opened, ate/entered, cooked/locked. Background appears in a separate sentence: A knife lay nearby. The pilot cooked the. Action pairs hold background fixed; nuisance pairs swap background while action stays fixed. Two additional coupled novel-tool/action contrasts use fork/ate versus card/entered and spoon/tasted versus code/accessed. These latter probes are not factorial. All pairs share the final determiner. Seven arms: identity, full donor, frozen nounrank1, oldtask128, their129dimensional union, and paired +/- residual noise norm-matched to the rank1 edit.

The native gate remains four pairs, >=75%both endpoints category-correct, >=50%intended full-vocabulary top1. Five of ten action cohort/condition cells pass. Failed cells are diagnostic only; no individual correctness filtering.

| Action cohort/background | Native gate | Frozen rank1 effect/full | Rank1 relative full-patch KL |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| cut/unlocked,knife |pass|0.686|0.278|
| cut/unlocked,key |fail|0.702|0.417|
| sliced/opened,knife |pass|0.943|0.511|
| sliced/opened,key |pass|1.053|0.555|
| cooked/locked,knife |pass|0.359|0.539|

| fork/ate versus card/entered |fail|0.268|0.854|
| spoon/tasted versus code/accessed |fail|0.277|0.955|

Effect/full is a ratio of mean signed answer-margin changes, not an additive explanation fraction. Relative KL compares full-donor-patched output to component-patched output and normalizes by identity. Overshoot above1 on an answer contrast is not whole-output equivalence. Strong answer preservation still leaves substantial distribution mismatch.

Frozen rank1 mean absolute margin changes from background swaps are0.048,0.060,0.027,0.062 across the four verb cohorts, versus action-change signed means roughly0.4–0.8. The direction is more sensitive to action contrasts than these background substitutions, but is not nuisance-invariant. Matched random-noise absolute effects are~0.005–0.017; observed nuisance sensitivity is meaningful enough to retain as a limitation. Full-write background swaps themselves change margins by0.052–0.120, so background is not causally irrelevant to the model.

Native failures cannot be equated with absence of the intended behavior. Inspection of the first subject shows sensible omitted top predictions: ate food, entered cockpit, tasted sauce, accessed website, among others. Some outputs also repeat the nearby tool, e.g. cooked knife. The fixed food/access token lists are incomplete and the category framing does not cover all actions cleanly. Do not broaden lists after seeing these results and then call this a passed held-out test. A future category redesign needs fresh independent examples.

Interpretation: the existing direction captures a reusable but narrow action-conditioned food/access contrast and retains lexical/background effects. Novel cooking/locking transfer of36–41% weakens a generic noun-expectation interpretation. This control round supports keeping it as a provisional contrast anchor, not a universal semantic module. Fragmentrank4 remains source-specific and should not become a general morphology label.

Stopping criterion for this side investigation has been reached: we have a fixed direction, demonstrated transfer and explicit confounds sufficient to define a narrow supervision target. Next return to joint representation evaluation: compare old task span plus this frozen direction with an equal-size random residual extension, and evaluate old-task retention, competent new contrasts and natural-text fidelity. Use existing discovery-fitted geometry; do not train on these control/evaluation prompts. This gives the featurizer loop a concrete deliverable without prolonging the single-task mechanism detour. Keep whole-state reconstruction distinct from donor-difference fidelity and retain old task holdouts.

Decision: keep noun rank1 as a provisional causal contrast anchor, not a verified abstract semantic feature. Two-seed confirmation co-membership-pair Jaccard0.541. On the54confirmation states whose current token occurs at leastfourtimes, observed Jaccard0.445 versus mean0.264/max0.346 under64within-exact-token shuffles of the second seed's assignments. Twenty hypotheses registered before follow-up behavioral tests (full evidence/discriminators saved in JSON):
1. Sentence restart after boundary: Match current boundary token; vary whether sentence ended; measure next-token start distribution and residual edits.
2. Clause-completion punctuation readiness: Same final lexical token in complete versus incomplete clause; test punctuation probability and causal swaps.
3. Determiner-to-noun continuation: Hold final determiner fixed across predicted noun categories; compare residual versus token-only effects.
4. Within-word continuation: Separate token-internal continuation from new-word boundaries, matching current BPE token where possible.
5. Coordination and list continuation: Parallel items versus completed list with same conjunction; validate on several semantic domains.
6. Prepositional argument completion: Match final preposition and manipulate expected argument type; use neutral-topic controls.
7. Discourse connective continuation: Compare connective uses with same token in other constructions; test completion distributions.
8. Entity-category expectation: Hold formatting and current token fixed while changing entity-category cues.
9. Domain-specific vocabulary state: Cross topic and syntax factorially; test whether effects follow domain or syntactic position.
10. Heading/list formatting state: Compare identical content in prose, headings and lists; examine continuation format.
11. Delimiter closure state: Fresh matched quotation/bracket-open versus closed contexts, with length controls.
12. Local morphology constraints: Use token-valid inflection/derivation pairs with lexical and boundary controls; avoid existing tense holdout training.
13. Prediction uncertainty: Stratify by native entropy and test whether cluster patterns persist within strata.
14. Unexpected-continuation state: Compare continuation surprisal at matched token/position; avoid using future tokens for fitting.
15. Current-token identity artifact: Exact-token matched controls and token-conditioned subtraction on discovery data only.
16. Absolute position artifact: Report cluster occupancy by position and replicate at new predeclared positions.
17. Residual-norm/outlier artifact: Norm-matched strata and robust removal of predeclared extreme-norm states.
18. Document/style/boilerplate artifact: Document-block resampling and new-document replication; count independent documents.
19. Task-span domain shift: Compare train-only natural PCA and task PCA on separate pilot documents with downstream fidelity.
20. Clusters are quantization, not natural units: Compare continuous subspace prediction and multiple cluster counts on discovery only; require causal selectivity before naming units.

Prioritize sentence restart/clause completion, noun-phrase continuation and within-word continuation, with current-token, position and document controls. Do not retrofit strong semantic names to these clusterings. The next deliverable should be fresh token-valid behavioral contrasts plus finite residual-component interventions; proposals that merely reproduce token identity or fail native competence should not enter retraining.

## Previous continuation: H990

## H990 — Learned decoder coverage and encoding both fail; train-only PCA is a stronger local baseline

Previous turn was progress: H989 integrated expanded context data into sixteen new joint models and evaluated eight frozen baselines. This turn distinguishes decoder-span coverage from encoder/support error using all24 frozen models, rather than another objective sweep.

For every evaluated pair, compare actual encoded donor-minus-recipient reconstruction with the least-squares projection of the TRUE write difference into (a) all128 decoder atoms and (b) the union of the recipient/donor gates' actually selected atoms. These are teacher-informed diagnostic ceilings. Union-support projection is permissive: it may assign coordinates differently for each evaluated pair and does not define consistent single-state coordinates. Its gap to encoded error combines coordinate-inference and pair-consistency limitations; it cannot isolate a particular encoder defect. Full-span minus union-span performance diagnoses the limitation of the current selected supports.

PCA controls fit centered training states only, with32 or up to128 components, capped at numerical rank using singular-value threshold1e-6 relative to the largest. They are ordinary frozen linear projection baselines, not teacher-fitted oracle coefficients: projecting a difference equals subtracting separately projected states. No validation labels or differences fit their basis. The dense-coordinate budget differs from group sparsity. Frozen small6 has rank40, expanded6 rank131 and expanded7 rank139, consistent with unique-prompt counts minus one; PCA128 on small6 actually has40components. PCA bases are shared across seeds/objectives within each data regime, so duplicated scores are not independent replicates.

Twelve fixed-budget fits: two seeds, two architectures, three objectives (reconstruction, reconstruction plus real answer labels, reconstruction plus independently shuffled within-family labels).128 shared dictionary atoms,32 groups, fixed membership matrices, same coordinate/gate encoders and six label heads. ## H978 — Output-aware weight-derived readouts improve compact composition transfer

Previous turn was progress: H977 separated compact result directions from input-span transfer and found adjective PCA input restriction to be the main bottleneck. For unit output direction u define F=L^T diag(Down^T u) R + R^T diag(Down^T u) L. Then the scalar local cross term is a^T F n. Given a frozen negation basis N, store G=F N. Predict u times (a^T G)(N^T n). Output rank1/4 crossed with negation rank1/4 is tested. Rank1 output/rank4 negation requires four adjective linear readouts, four negation readouts, four scalar products and a single output direction; vectors can be correlated and are not claimed independent semantic units. Three random-negation-span controls use the same weight-derived construction.

Inputs a,n remain quartet main-factor vectors, not independently encoded single states. This is therefore a compact operator on factor inputs, not a deployable state-based featurizer. Weight access and supervised discovery factors are explicit priors.

KL ratio measures discrepancy between predicted-local-removal and teacher-local-removal output distributions, normalized to no edit; lower is better.

## Previous continuation: H970

## H970 — Attention5 primarily transports composed interaction from adjective and period positions

Previous goal turn was progress: H969 finite interaction removals identified attention5 as the strongest earlier final-token site. This turn reconstructs attention5 by source token and head, then factorizes each source contribution into routing weights and projected mixed values. All96 locked states retained; only familiar original-format quartets are used for interpretation/ranking because other cohorts fail native competence.

Architecture check: this checkpoint uses CausalBilinearSelfAttention with two normalized/rotated QK pairs. Its routing weight is the product of their dot products divided by head_dim squared, without row normalization or softmax. These weights can be signed and are not probabilities. Values mix current-layer projections with the native layer0 value bus before head output projection. An initial assertion expecting the single-QK variant failed before any forward evaluation; the implementation was corrected against the checkpoint config and actual model source. No results from the incorrect variant were produced.

Each source/head contribution is P*V, where P is a scalar routing weight and V the mixed value projected into residual space. With four-state coefficients indexed by constant, adjective a, negation n and interaction an, the exact interaction is:

P0*V_an + P_an*V0 + P_a*V_n + P_n*V_a.

Call these transported value interaction, routing interaction, and cross terms. This is an algebraic decomposition on native states, not a causal mediation result. In particular V_an already exists before attention5 aggregation, but could have been computed at any earlier layer or introduced through input normalization.

Competent-cohort signed projection onto the total attention5 interaction:
- Value interaction at common aligned token slots:96.81%.
- Routing interaction:3.24% common slots plus0.030% noncommon slots.
- Cross terms:-0.112% common slots plus0.030% noncommon slots.

Source-role shares: adjective50.06%, suffix48.41%, prefix1.48%, explicit not token0.060%. The period immediately after the adjective supplies44.83% by itself; later sentiment-label tokens supply the remaining suffix contribution. A tiny direct not-token share does not mean not is unimportant: it can alter representations at later positions. Head4 supplies37.55%, head7 supplies32.33%, head6 supplies13.57%; these are native-trajectory projection shares, not intervention effects or attention probabilities. Indices zero-based.

Token alignment uses character offsets and prefix/negation/adjective/suffix role plus within-role token index. Missing slots receive zero P and V; factor allocation at such slots depends on that convention. Report common versus noncommon separately. On the competent cohort all adjective positions are single tokens, and noncommon slots contribute only0.060% of total signed projection. Thus the main transported-value conclusion comes from common slots, not the missing-token padding rule. All aligned and unaligned source contributions are saved for independent replay.

Audit:96/96 whole-model forward examples; native logits replay exactly. Reconstructed final-token attention outputs differ by at most3.06e-7 relative; full interaction differs from the prior float32 capture by6.55e-6 relative. Product factorial identity holds to1.32e-15. Independent NumPy contraction over original unaligned source positions reproduces the saved interaction within3.44e-15, and summary aggregation matches. Inputs unchanged, outputs finite. No training or reserved-test access; natural-document pool26,112.

Interpretation: attention5 appears primarily to gather already-composed content, prominently from the adjective and following period. Together with MLP12's inherited-input result, this moves the search for original composition upstream and to earlier token positions. Neither attention5 nor MLP12 has yet been shown to implement a reusable negation operator.

Next: finite selective removals of transported-value versus routing/cross interaction at attention5, with role/head removals and norm-matched controls. Then trace validated source-position interaction through earlier blocks rather than continuing to inspect the final token alone. H961 frozen context-bridge predictor evaluation remains pending.

## Previous continuation: H967

## H967 — MLP12 predominantly transforms an already-present sentiment interaction

Previous turn was progress: H966 supplied a full adjective-polarity by negation panel and established a composed-valence signature with narrow native competence. H967 captures the actual normalized MLP12 input and the residual immediately before its RMS normalization on all96 locked states. The four familiar original-format quartets remain the sole native-gate-passing cohort; other cohorts remain diagnostics.

For a,n in {-1,+1}, write normalized input x=c0+a*ca+n*cn+a*n*ci and define B(u,v)=Down((Left u)*(Right v)). The actual MLP is ungated bilinear with an output bias. Its exact factorial interaction is:

C_out = [B(c0,ci)+B(ci,c0)] + [B(ca,cn)+B(cn,ca)].

The first bracket transforms interaction already present in normalized input (inherited); the second creates interaction from separately indexed adjective/negation components (local cross product). Bias contributes only to the constant. This is an exact finite-panel algebraic decomposition, not a globally identified causal ontology. Inherited includes any interaction introduced by RMS normalization, so it cannot all be assigned to earlier layers without a further trace.

On the competent familiar-A cohort, signed projection of inherited interaction onto total output interaction is99.620%; local cross-product projection is0.380%. These shares sum to one by algebra but are not fractions of whole-model computation or variance explained; they can be negative or exceed100% in general. In the frozen sentiment output coordinate, the local term similarly accounts for0.394% of the summed interaction coefficient. Raw pre-normalization input already has53.08% of its centered factorial squared norm in the interaction component, versus53.45% after normalization. Similar fractions do not prove normalization is irrelevant, but establish that interaction is present before it.

Each state's native MLP write was then edited by subtracting a*n times one or both output components, retaining native residual and attention paths. These interventions are algebraic output edits and may be off-manifold; they do not remove upstream interaction itself.

| Removed output interaction | Mean loss in intended-sentiment margin | Mean KL(native||edited) | Binary accuracy, 16 competent-cohort endpoints |
|---|---|---|---|
| None (identity) |0|0|100%|
| Inherited component |0.4062|0.006951|93.75%|
| Local cross product |0.00234|0.00000236|100%|
| Both |0.4086|0.007083|93.75%|

The inherited-term intervention has the much larger effect, consistent with the exact decomposition. Most endpoints still retain correct binary answers after removal, so MLP12 is neither the only relevant pathway nor established as necessary for every answer. Across failed native cohorts, inherited vector shares range98.98–99.62%; these are model-mechanism diagnostics, not evidence of semantic competence.

Independent verification: reconstructed actual writes using all weights and Down_bias (max relative error8.22e-7). Exact bilinear interaction identity holds to5.82e-15 relative. Separate direct evaluations of the actual double-precision MLP on synthetic inputs recover the local term by a four-corner contrast with ci omitted, and the inherited term by a symmetric difference around c0 along ci. These144 local MLP evaluations match saved terms within2.71e-8 relative. Thus the central result does not rely solely on a self-check of the expanded polynomial formula.

Runtime audits:480/480 whole-model forward examples (96 captures,384 edits), plus144 local MLP evaluations; capture replay exact; identity logit error2.19e-5; raw-to-normalized replay1.91e-6; exact four-state reconstruction9.09e-13 absolute; independent summary aggregation; finite outputs and unchanged sources. No training or reserved-test access; natural-document pool26,112.

Interpretation: on this panel, MLP12 primarily transforms already-composed input into a sentiment output direction. A strong causal site and a clean output direction did not identify the site that originally composes adjective polarity with negation. This distinction should inform featurizer objectives: result directions and reusable operations need separate validation.

| prepositional:both | 0.567–0.730 | 0.567–0.730 | 0.518–0.679 |
| prepositional:distractor | 0.449–0.579 | 0.534–0.638 | 0.422–0.548 |
| prepositional:subject | 0.695–0.882 | 0.860–0.974 | 0.625–0.802 |
| relative_clause:both | 0.592–0.636 | 0.592–0.636 | 0.559–0.593 |

The raw-activation encoder improves joint KLratio over the full template prototype in all12 cell/seed comparisons, but only by.027–.080. Therefore much of H959's gain is compatible with template/number-conditioned response prototypes; there is a smaller additional activation-dependent benefit. This is not evidence that the model literally uses these labels or stores these prototypes. The labels are supplied by the experimenter, while the activation encoder infers its prediction from state vectors.

Pooling templates worsens fidelity substantially, especially for relative clauses. Template-transfer label prototypes often fare worse than zero MLP change: relative-clause full-prototype KLratios1.32–2.48, and prepositional subject-only1.41–1.54. Context-specific response patterns matter; simply naming the same subject/distractor variables does not align the output behavior across these templates. Limited training support, not an intrinsic impossibility of shared computation, remains a plausible explanation.

A decisive design lesson: full and additive prototypes are exactly identical on both-number flips. With signed factors h,d in{-1,+1}, the interaction hd is unchanged under (h,d)→(-h,-d). Such contrasts cannot test the interaction contribution. Independent subject-only and distractor-only flips expose it. On prepositional subject changes, removing the interaction worsens KLratio from.695–.882 to.860–.974; on distractor changes from.449–.579 to.534–.638. Relative-clause gains from the interaction are small or inconsistent, and additive subject-only prototypes are slightly better in KL. These are interactions in the fitted finite-state representation, not proof of a unique mechanistic product.

Task margins and KL again disagree: additive prepositional subject prototypes improve the task-margin error while worsening KL. Avoid promoting components using only one selected task score. Absolute intervention KL remains small on this panel.

Audit:4,704/4,704 live forwards; native identity2.20e-5; exact joint replay7.29e-6; centered-state and additive/interaction algebra errors3.42e-13; loop consistency2.52e-16; independent saved-prototype replay2.62e-8 relative; both-flip interaction cancellation exact. Training/evaluation endpoints and groups independently checked disjoint; aggregate metrics independently recomputed. Inputs unchanged, finite results, no backbone/span training or reserved-test access. Natural document pool26,112.

Interpretation: we have a small supervised, context-sensitive description of causal output changes with some lexical transfer. The evidence does not yet support a general recovered unit or meaningful unsupervised manifold. Current strongest alternatives are (1) template-conditioned prototypes plus lexical corrections; (2) a shared computation expressed in context-dependent coordinates; (3) an underdetermined encoder that fails extrapolation because training contexts are too sparse; and (4) context-dependent downstream sensitivity creating different quotient representations of the same upstream information.

Next: stop tuning this two-template panel. Freeze encoders/prototypes and construct prospective context bridges with fixed input-only choices: nearby prepositional variants, nearby relative-clause variants, and changed distractor lexemes, with complete number factorials and native competence checks. Compare generalization as input geometry and syntax vary. This will separate small within-family shifts from across-family shifts before spending more effort on a richer encoder or calling the groups manifolds. Include failure cases and zero-change/full-distribution controls; preserve the original reserved test.

## Previous continuation: H958

## H958 — Most downstream-metric gains survive consistent feature states

Question: are H957's teacher-informed coefficients merely independent corrections for each directed intervention, or can a single set of state coordinates reproduce much of the gain? A fixed linear decoder requires each intervention coefficient to be z(donor)-z(recipient), with antisymmetric reversals and zero sums around closed loops.

For each four-state factorial quartet, fit centered state potentials to all12 directed oracle coefficient vectors by least squares on the graph incidence matrix. Use separate MLP/joint targets and a shared target averaging both paths. Retain both original budgets, both seeds, unscaled potentials, and common-quartet rescaling that preserves consistency while respecting every edge norm budget. Evaluate every candidate on both downstream paths, including cross-path transfer. Frozen .1/top8 span; no weight training. Per-quartet potentials remain teacher-informed and fit to observed states, not predicted from activations.

Original budget1 oracle inconsistency is substantial. Median triangle-closure RMS relative to edge RMS is.51 prepositional/.41 relative clause for joint-path coefficients; reversal inconsistencies .51/.38. Projection removes median28.5%/22.0% of coefficient norm (ranges22–44%/15–29%). Exact teacher and Euclidean projection controls obey consistency to9.16e-7 relative, supporting that the oracle violations are not floating-point artifacts.

Despite this coefficient change, much of the live output-distribution improvement survives. Budget1 joint-path KLratios (relative to zero MLP change), ranges across seeds:

| Factorial cell | Independent joint-edge oracle | Consistent joint states | Consistent shared states |
|---|---|---|---|
| prepositional:both | 0.351–0.498 | 0.364–0.529 | 0.365–0.530 |
| prepositional:distractor | 0.295–0.403 | 0.305–0.415 | 0.304–0.414 |
| prepositional:subject | 0.393–0.548 | 0.434–0.644 | 0.433–0.643 |
| relative_clause:both | 0.387–0.400 | 0.415–0.424 | 0.415–0.424 |
| relative_clause:distractor | 0.469–0.490 | 0.496–0.512 | 0.495–0.512 |
| relative_clause:subject | 0.253–0.296 | 0.294–0.312 | 0.295–0.313 |

Shared consistency raises joint KLratio modestly, to.295–.643 across these cells, compared with.253–.548 for the independent-edge oracle and.688–.998 for original learned top-eight effects (H957). Most of the downstream-metric gain therefore does not require unconstrained per-edge freedom. Sharing state coordinates across MLP-only and joint paths adds little penalty beyond within-path consistency here.

Task-margin tradeoffs remain: prepositional subject-only error rises from46–51% for independent edges to60–92% for consistent shared states, despite preserving substantial KL improvement. Relative-clause subject-only error rises from4.6–7.4% to12–13%. Thus a consistent distribution-focused representation is not automatically a good explanation of the selected task margin.

Norm constraints are not the main cost: minimum common rescaling is.926 at budget1; budget2 needs no rescaling. Exact graph projection is verified both by pseudoinverse and the complete-graph closed form. Consistency closure after projection is3.43e-16 relative; solution disagreement9.10e-13 absolute; capped norm ratios<=1. Native identity2.20e-5; historical joint-margin replay7.29e-6; original edge-oracle margins agree with H957 within1.15e-5 and KL within3.86e-8. Independent summary aggregation<1e-12. All11,424 expected live forwards completed; hashes unchanged; no new teacher endpoint data, model training, or reserved-test access; natural document pool26,112.

Interpretation: on these finite observed states, a consistent eight-dimensional teacher-informed representation preserves much of the behavioral-equivalence advantage. This is stronger than independent intervention corrections, but still much weaker than a reusable learned featurizer. Each quartet has its own additive gauge; no encoder predicts unseen states, and the disconnected quartets do not establish global identifiability. The constraint is necessary for fixed additive decoders, not for every nonlinear/context-conditioned computation model. Uniform coefficient-space projection is not globally KL-optimal; losses here do not prove a lower bound for consistent representations.

Next: predict these coordinates from activations with strict lexical holdouts. Fit differences of a shared encoder so arbitrary per-quartet offsets cannot leak into targets. Compare raw normalized-state linear features against the frozen64 bilinear product features, and retain the original top-eight encoder and teacher-informed state oracle as controls. Hold out complete noun families across both templates, with a separate cross-template transfer check. Fix regularization without tuning on held-out downstream scores. Success would show some learnable transfer of the downstream-metric representation; failure would distinguish finite-data existence from reusable computation.

## H957 — Downstream metric recovers behavior unavailable to Euclidean projection

Tested whether frozen moderate-penalty top-eight output directions can reproduce teacher output changes using coefficients chosen for a downstream metric. Both seeds, all168 factorial swaps, isolated MLP and joint residual paths retained. No weight training. For each recipient, central finite differences at1% and0.5% of teacher effect norm estimate output-logit Jacobians. Center logits/Jacobians under the exact target distribution, then solve weighted least squares with a small ridge and explicit coefficient norm budgets1x and2x the teacher MLP-effect norm. Orthonormal basis coordinates make these output-edit norm budgets. All candidates are replayed through the nonlinear model.

This is a teacher-informed per-example oracle. It estimates the capacity of a frozen span under this procedure; it is neither a learned predictor nor a globally optimized KL bound. Both finite-difference scales, both budgets, and all failures are retained. Euclidean projection, actual top-eight response, zero MLP change, and exact teacher intervention provide controls.

The Fisher coefficients substantially improve output fidelity without changing the span. Across cells, budget1 joint KLratios are.253–.548, versus actual.688–.998. The same directions can reproduce more of the downstream distribution than their learned or Euclidean coefficients achieved.

The gain is incomplete and metric-specific. Prepositional subject-only task error remains46–51% even while joint KLratio improves to.393–.548; relative-clause subject-only task error improves to4.6–7.4%. Interpretation: the user's distinction among activation faithfulness and output-distribution equivalence is experimentally consequential. A compact span can be much more adequate under a downstream metric than Euclidean projection suggests. However a different coefficient vector per directed intervention may describe a collection of local compensations rather than a reusable feature representation.

Next: test coefficient integrability on the complete factorial graph. A fixed additive representation requires c(A→B)=z(B)-z(A), so reversals must negate and every closed loop must sum to zero. Quantify oracle violations against exact/Euclidean controls, project the oracle edge coefficients onto consistent state potentials, and replay those changes downstream. This separates the expressive gain from direction-by-direction freedom from a representation that can assign one feature state to each activation. It is still a teacher-informed diagnostic; transfer learning should follow only after this consistency check.

Coefficient error nevertheless matters downstream: for the complete64 moderate fit, subject-only prepositional joint KLratio falls from.905–.966 (actual, H955) to.500–.520 with L2-oracle coefficients. ## H951 — Causal contribution concentration improves dominant-product reproducibility

Question: does H949's penalty merely compact responses arbitrarily, or do independently trained models acquire corresponding products? All four penalties and both seeds retained. No refitting. Two Hungarian matchings use either whole symmetric bilinear tensors or full product response matrices on discovery anchors (equal task energy normalization), then evaluate on existing held-out full and rank-one contrasts. Independently selected dominant products are also compared directly, without matching on evaluation data. A whole-product response includes both its scalar response and output vector.

For the independently discovery-selected dominant product, held-out full-intervention response cosine across seeds is:

| Penalty | Agreement | Sentiment |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | .004 | .137 |
| .01 | .560 | .683 |
| .1 | .894 | .982 |
| 1 | .003 | .107 |

At .1, dominant response amplitudes still differ: seed1/seed0 norm ratios .847 agreement and .941 sentiment; relative response disagreement is 45% and 19%, respectively. Teacher errors remain 74–79% agreement and 58–60% sentiment for these single products. Reproducibility is not teacher fidelity.

The .1 dominant sentiment pair has whole tensor cosine .585, versus agreement .095. Their behavior is more similar on the observed data than their global bilinear functions. Factoring response similarity confirms scalar finite-response cosine .990 agreement/.9997 sentiment and output-direction cosine .903/.982 (absolute values remove compensated sign gauge). This suggests residual disagreement lies substantially in output direction and amplitude, while the observed scalar response profiles align. These task-conditioned, correlated contrasts do not identify behavior on new input directions.

Eight-product sums at .1 are even more reproducible: cosine .987 agreement/.997 sentiment and relative disagreement 16%/8%. Functional matching gives energy-weighted individual product cosines .861/.979, but unweighted means only .055/.241. Therefore the result is carried by dominant products; the small residual products remain unstable. Giving all products equal weight would obscure this distinction. The weighted statistic uses evaluation energy for descriptive reporting only, never for selecting the matching or subset.

Reuse check: the dominant product index differs between agreement and sentiment in both seeds. Agreement-dominant product response norms are 48–56% of the agreement teacher norm but only 1–10% of the sentiment teacher norm. Sentiment-dominant products are 69–73% on sentiment and 4–12% on agreement. These are response-norm ratios, not explained-variance fractions. The top-eight sets overlap in 5–6 indices, but this includes weak residual products and does not establish shared computation. The evidence favors task-selective dominant responses on this panel.

Audit: functional self-cosines within 1.23e-15 of one; explicit materialized response-vector cosines agree with factored Gram formula within 6.67e-16. All assignments are permutations; inputs unchanged; finite outputs. Product response cosine independently factors into scalar and output cosines within 1e-12. Zero new model forwards; no reserved-test use; natural document pool unchanged at 26,112. Only two seeds, supervised anchors, and an extensively reused development panel limit the conclusion.

Conclusion: adding a causal contribution prior improves not only compactness but also dominant functional reproducibility in this setting. It has not established unique global units, a broad ontology, or cross-task computational reuse. This is an informative advance beyond arbitrary coordinate stabilization: held-out intervention responses, not merely latent labels, align more strongly. However both models learned the same narrow anchor tasks, so a fresh transfer test is essential.

Next: freeze .1 as an exploratory candidate together with unpenalized and .01 controls, preserve all other fits as diagnostic controls, and evaluate novel competent contexts/combinations with native teacher effects. Do not further optimize penalties on the existing panel. Include task cross-interventions and output distribution checks; prioritize new input directions over more paraphrases of the same templates.

## Previous continuation: H949

## H949 — A causal contribution penalty concentrates learned responses, with a fidelity tradeoff

Question: can a preference for fewer whole bilinear products turn the previously distributed anchored response into a compact explanation?

Design: eight fits, two seeds and four predeclared penalty weights (0, .01, .1, 1), each initialized from the same-seed H946 effect-anchor fit. All use 64 products, identical parameter count, 2,000 steps and matched natural minibatches. The base objective preserves natural reconstruction/random-probe effects and the 15 discovery anchor pairs. Added cost is the sum of smoothed quarter powers of each product's squared finite-response contribution, normalized by teacher response energy and averaged equally over the two tasks. This charges entire contributions, is invariant to factor scale and compensated signs, and penalizes splitting an identical contribution into multiple copies. It is not a global storage or exact active-product penalty.

Results on existing held-out full interventions (relative vector-norm error; lower is better):

| Penalty | Agreement: top-8 error vs complete student | Sentiment: top-8 error vs complete student | Agreement: all-64 error vs teacher | Sentiment: all-64 error vs teacher |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 81–84% | 64–70% | 72.5–72.7% | 56.5–56.6% |
| .01 | 33–45% | 21–24% | 72.7–73.0% | 56.7–56.8% |
| .1 | 23–24% | 13.6–13.7% | 73.5–73.7% | 58.2–58.3% |
| 1 | 84% | 67–81% | approximately 100% | approximately 100% |

The .1 penalty's top eight products have teacher errors 73.3–73.6% agreement and 57.8–58.0% sentiment: concentration is not solely a relative metric artifact. With that penalty, one sentiment product already approximates the complete student within 25% error in both seeds. Agreement reaches that threshold with 2 or 8 products depending on seed. These are discovery-greedy selections, not optimal subsets; selected counts are limited to the tested grid. Subset errors need not be monotonic because contributions can interfere.

Interpretation: the distribution across many products was partly adjustable through the training objective. A moderate contribution cost substantially concentrates the anchored response while modestly worsening already-incomplete teacher fidelity. The largest penalty instead suppresses the response. This supports a compactness/fidelity tradeoff, not discovery of unique, semantic, or reusable computational units. Natural random-effect fidelity remains poor (roughly 102% error at .1); these models are not general MLP substitutes. The same repeatedly used development panel is not a fresh confirmatory test.

Verification: all eight checkpoint predictions replay exactly. Independently materializing every product's output contribution agrees with the factored energy formula to 1.82e-7 relative error. Factor rescaling and compensated-sign changes preserve the cost exactly in the tested checks. Analytically splitting a contribution in two increases the smoothed penalty by about 1.41x. Input hashes unchanged; finite outputs; zero whole-model forwards in this experiment; reserved test untouched; natural document pool remains 26,112. Full downstream output fidelity and cross-seed component correspondence remain untested for these fits.

Next: test both complete fits and discovery-selected top-eight contributions in the live downstream model, retaining every penalty and seed. Compare isolated MLP and joint residual-plus-MLP intervention effects, full-distribution KL, and zero-change baselines. Only then assess whether the concentrated components transfer and match across seeds.

Match products across seeds using cosine of the COMPLETE tensor out_j ⊗ sym(left_j,right_j), computed by analytical Gram matrices. Effect error is RMS discrepancy in donor-induced answer-logit margin change divided by reference-effect RMS, pooled within task. Ranges include all three seeds, not confidence intervals. Only four transfer lexical pairs/domain underlie these values; correlated endpoints/templates are not independent replicates. Agreement task itself has a tiny reference effect for these attention sites and relative errors over100%; no positive agreement claim.

Binding native KL is .00307 continuous, .00238–.00311 learned groups, .00215–.00336 random groups. Binding edited KL is .00269 continuous, .00212–.00253 learned, .00223–.00379 random. Thus both whole-distribution and margin comparisons show close competition, not evidence that discrete group membership is required. Name copying benefits from learned groups here, but country copying does not. No universal architecture winner.

The important change from H934 is the continuous baseline: discovery-only CV chose weaker penalties, reducing binding effect error from about14% under alpha .01 to6.36%. The prior apparent need for grouped baselines was partly regularization-dependent. Random geometric groups can contain context; this is not proof of semantic absence or a perfectly capacity-matched null. The continuous model also consumes native query features, so it does not explain how upstream computation constructs those features or replace the whole model.

### Interpretation limits and next experiment

A discrete context baseline plus within-group continuous variation is useful for some pathways. This is compatible with locally structured computation, but does not prove semantic manifolds or that discrete groups are fundamental. The hybrid has additional structure/capacity; a strong continuous-only baseline must receive fair model selection. All strongest results are at the weakest regularization tested (.01), so this grid has not located an interior optimum. No claim of optimized model-class superiority is warranted.

Next choose regularization using discovery-only lexical cross-validation, expanding the predeclared range toward weaker penalties, then evaluate frozen choices once on the existing research-transfer panel. Add a comparable prototype/correction control with nonsemantic grouping (for example a fixed random partition/gate) to test whether improvements require meaningful query grouping rather than extra capacity. Keep native distribution and intervention fidelity as separate outcomes. After model choice is fixed on discovery data, repeat excluded-template and disjoint-sample checks rather than tuning on their failures.

These comparisons are exploratory on a repeatedly used evaluation panel. A genuinely new task/template panel is still needed for strong generalization claims. The broad objective remains identifying reliable computational units, not maximizing performance on these examples.

This distinguishes reproducibility of a cluster ontology from reproducibility of an operation. Different partitions can support similar causal predictions. Stable predictions do not identify a unique feature grouping, and unstable grouping alone does not establish that the approximated computation is wrong. Both must be measured.

### Research decision and next experiment

Do not label one prototype partition as the model's settled semantic units. The evidence supports a family of useful context discretizations for parts of language and binding, with weaker copying fidelity. This matches the broader possibility that functionally equivalent data-based representations can differ in internal grouping.

Next compare frozen prototype means with a small continuous query-to-coefficient model and a prototype-plus-continuous-correction model, using the same discovery/evaluation separation and fixed regularization choices. Preserve task-blind fitting and report every predetermined setting. Evaluate native KL, donor-intervention KL and effect fidelity, alongside cross-sample stability. A correction that reduces baseline drift but worsens causal response is not a clear improvement. If continuous-only prediction matches the grouped model, discrete groups may be an explanatory convenience rather than necessary computational structure. This comparison should precede a manifold or hierarchy claim.

### Interpretation and next test

This weakens an explanation based solely on memorizing the exact training template. It does not distinguish semantic context from shared final tokens, common syntax, lexical categories or similar query geometry. The source templates are close paraphrases and copying formats are shallow variants. No continuous manifold is established by discrete prototype success.

Next test sample stability independently of initialization: fit on disjoint lexical subsets while holding the prototype count and template protocol fixed, then compare assignments on a common evaluation panel and compare causal effect profiles. Do not choose a seed by downstream success. Separately test whether the native-distribution drift comes from coefficient prediction or from grouping distinct contexts under one prototype—for example, retain the same frozen gate while allowing a small discovery-fitted continuous correction within each group. That is a targeted featurizer extension, but it must beat the uncorrected and continuous-without-groups controls before being interpreted as meaningful manifold structure.

The stable objective remains to identify reusable units of computation, not merely a small surrogate that passes these prompts. Evidence now favors lexical carriers plus context-dependent routing for this partial pathway, with template transfer and remaining fidelity failures explicitly bounded.

The one-prototype models exactly reproduce the pooled-distance baseline for all seeds, which is an independent implementation sanity check. All H929 baseline metrics also replay exactly. Thus gains at larger prototype counts cannot be attributed to a changed baseline implementation.

### Live gates and limitations

Only20 of5,184 prototype gate evaluations switch cluster relative to the unedited query state; none require a fallback for an uncovered distance. This verifies that gates were recomputed, but also shows these interventions offer a weak stress test of gate dynamics. More challenging edits may cross boundaries more often.

The surrogate is task-blind in fitting and gating but still uses native query computations, pretrained token-value vectors and native current-layer values. It approximates a persistent attention component; it does not replace whole heads or explain how query states arise. Prototype count, stable partitions and intervention fidelity do not yet demonstrate semantic manifolds. Surface form, final-token identity and lexical category can still explain the clusters.

### Next test

Refit with one template excluded and evaluate the excluded template with the other lexical half held out as well. Run both template directions, preserve all predetermined prototype counts/seeds and account for any unsupported relative positions without fitting on evaluation data. Compare with the same models' within-template lexical transfer. This distinguishes template memorization from reusable context organization. Independently refit on disjoint discovery samples to test partition stability beyond random initialization. Failure should identify which context distinctions need richer featurizers rather than justify adding labels after the fact.

## Previous continuation: H930

## H930 — Task-blind query prototypes recover useful context groups, with uneven stability

H929 required supplied context labels to predict coefficients well. H930 fits groups from query activations without domain, task, template or correctness labels. It screens whether such groups are stable and predict persistent-value writes; downstream causal fidelity is not yet tested in this experiment.

### Implementation and splits

At each fixed reader, concatenate the two normalized final-token query vectors before rotary position encoding (256 coordinates). Fit independent k-means models with1,2,4,8 prototypes and three predetermined seeds, on the96 discovery examples. No evaluation examples enter prototype or coefficient fitting. For each prototype, average discovery routing coefficients by distance from the final token. Gate evaluation examples by their nearest query prototype and predict their coefficient vector. Uncovered distances would fall back to the discovery positional mean; no fallback was needed.

Queries are captured before rotary encoding to avoid directly clustering the rotary phase. They can still encode position, final-token identity, syntax and lexical context. Task-blind fitting does not imply task-pure or semantic groups. Clustering uses a fixed pretrained coordinate system and Euclidean distance; no gauge-invariant representation is claimed.

The96 evaluation examples use familiar transfer lexical pairs across agreement, language, binding and copying. The coefficient target is native routing and the reconstruction target is the unprojected persistent head write. This is not feature discovery from reconstruction alone: causal validation remains required.

### Local write prediction and stability

Write error is pooled RMS reconstruction error divided by the RMS native persistent write; zeroing has ratio1. Adjusted Rand index (ARI) measures agreement of held-out cluster assignments across seeds, ignoring arbitrary cluster numbering;1 means identical partitions. The one-cluster ARI is trivially1.

Retrospective discovery composition separates language task and binding task into their own groups. The remaining two groups mix agreement task and parts of agreement copying with other copying contexts. This is useful structure, not a perfect unsupervised task ontology.

### Interpretation and next test

Small task-blind query codebooks can identify context distinctions that improve coefficient prediction. The useful representation may consist of lexical carriers plus a small context state selecting how to route them. However, prototype stability is measured across initialization seeds on the same discovery sample, not independently sampled datasets. Template and final-token confounds remain. These groups are discrete prototypes, not verified continuous manifolds.

Next test prototype gates during live intervention rollouts, so earlier edits can change later queries and their assignments. Evaluate predetermined4- and8-prototype models across all three seeds, retaining the1-prototype baseline and H929 context-mean reference. Measure native KL, full donor-value intervention KL and answer-effect fidelity. Do not select the best seed or prototype count after outcomes. Stability alone cannot justify replacing the model's computation; the intervention test must show what the groups preserve. After that, assess new templates and disjoint fit samples before semantic labeling.

## H929 — Context-specific coefficient means transfer, but generic positional rules miss causal behavior

H928 verified token-identity aggregation and full-distribution fidelity using donor routing. H929 asks whether simple coefficients fitted on discovery examples can replace live routing for the persistent component. This removes oracle donor coefficients from the prediction model, while retaining native token-value vectors and current-layer values.

### Design

Use agreement, language and binding with matched copying controls and two templates each. Fit the first four lexical pairs per domain (96 examples); evaluate the other four (96 examples). All evaluation examples were used in earlier research and are not pristine holdouts.

Three rules are fixed before evaluation. Context mean knows domain, task/copy family and template and averages each absolute position's coefficient. Distance mean pools discovery examples by distance from the final token. Family-distance adds only task/copy knowledge to that positional rule. Zeroing and native routing are controls. All rules act jointly on the persistent components of the previously fixed L8H3, L13H0 and L14H4 readers, across all source positions, retaining live current-value contributions.

Evaluate each rule with native persistent values and with values from the opposite lexical endpoint. The donor shares task/template and token alignment. Native-routing donor interventions remain live at later readers after earlier edits. For each rule, intervention effect is its donor-value output minus its own native-value output; compare this with the native-routing intervention effect. This distinguishes matching baseline predictions from preserving causal response.

Context recognition is supplied metadata here. No claim is made that the model has learned or that the experiment has discovered those context labels.

Native KL compares native model with predicted native-value output. Edited KL compares the reference native-routing donor intervention with the rule's donor intervention. ### Implication and next experiment

A small contextual coefficient rule can preserve substantial behavior without compressing the lexical vectors themselves. However, one generic position rule is inadequate across these contexts. This motivates testing discrete or low-dimensional context states as activation features, rather than treating all lexical directions as one small manifold.

Next capture the final-token attention query activations at the fixed readers and fit task-blind query prototypes on discovery examples. Use predetermined prototype counts, multiple seeds and held-out lexical evaluation, without task/template labels in fitting or gating. Compare prototype-based coefficient prediction with the context-mean upper reference, generic positional rule, and native routing on both native KL and value-intervention fidelity. Audit the query/key attention formula before interpreting any learned groups. This tests whether useful unsupervised context labels can be recovered from model state, directly returning to the featurizer/manifold objective. Success would still need cross-seed stability, new-template transfer and selective interventions before a semantic manifold claim.

H927 showed low answer-margin error after matching swapped names by identity. H928 checks whether that conclusion survives full-vocabulary evaluation and audits a task-blind representation of the persistent-value pathway across diverse existing tasks.

### Full-distribution fidelity

For each of128 familiar QA transfer rows, both contrasts and each of three exploratory heads, compare full donor-head replacement with identity-aligned routing-only replacement and position-aligned routing-only replacement. KL is KL(full edited distribution || approximate edited distribution). The baseline is KL(full edited distribution || native distribution), corresponding to making no edit. Lower ratios are better. Top1 agreement is with the full intervention, not correctness on the task.

|event_swap|L14H4|2.25e-06|0.00073|1.693|100.00%|
|same_fact_reword|L14H4|3.96e-06|0.00130|1.711|99.22%|

At L14H4, identity-aligned event-swap routing has KL2.25e-6 and retains only0.073% of the no-edit baseline discrepancy. Position-aligned routing is worse than no edit, with ratio1.69. Across all six head/contrast cells, aligned ratios range0.00063–0.05075, whereas position-aligned ratios range1.69–1.86. Thus answer-margin fidelity was not hiding a large overall distribution mismatch on this panel.

Fidelity is approximate, not exact: maximum vocabulary-logit errors range about0.0077–0.0867, and L14H4 rewording disagrees with full-edit top1 in one of128 rows. The weakest relative KL result is L16H3 rewording. These are comparisons on previously explored names, heads and templates, not independent broad generalization evidence.

### Task-blind token aggregation audit

The persistent value at each source position depends on token identity. Its attention contribution can therefore be written as a sum over unique tokens: each token's value vector multiplied by the sum of signed routing coefficients over its occurrences. The existing value-mixing scalar multiplies both sides. No task labels, semantic roles, clustering or learned sparse dictionary are needed for this equality.

A shared token/head dictionary takes the first observed vector for each token; subsequent occurrences are checked against it. Store source-position lists with each token so individual-occurrence provenance is retained. Audit the three previously captured readers L8H3, L13H0 and L14H4 across agreement, language, binding and matched copying,192 examples total.

|Domain|Family|Head/examples|Mean positions|Mean unique tokens|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
|agreement|task|96|5.00|5.00|
|agreement|copy|96|7.00|4.00|
|language|task|96|6.50|6.50|
|language|copy|96|7.00|4.00|
|binding|task|96|12.00|11.00|
|binding|copy|96|7.00|4.00|

All576 local component reconstructions agree to a maximum relative norm error2.34e-7 and absolute component error7.45e-6. Same-token values vary by at most1.53e-5 in the cached floating-point calculations. The audit spans discovery and transfer examples; dictionary extraction here is an algebraic validation, not a train/test feature-recovery experiment.

This is an architecture-derived identity, not an empirical discovery of a semantic manifold. It exactly reorganizes the persistent component and merges repeated tokens; it does not compress the full model, merge different tokens, explain routing, or replace current-layer values. Position-specific interventions still need the retained occurrence coefficients/provenance. No full-model forwards are claimed for the aggregation audit itself.

### Research implication and next test

A useful partial data-based representation is now concrete: reusable token-value vectors plus context-dependent signed coefficients, with positional provenance. It handles shared directions without counting repeated contributions incorrectly and makes the correspondence between swapped identities explicit. This is a structured baseline against which more flexible learned dictionaries, groups and DAGs should be judged; it does not establish their superiority or replace their manifold-validation requirements.

The remaining hard problem is predicting and explaining the coefficients. Next test whether discovery-fitted simple coefficient models preserve native outputs across agreement, language, binding and copying, using fixed template/position rules versus models conditioned on task context. Retain separate native-distribution KL and intervention fidelity: fitting outputs alone can hide the wrong causal response. Do not use oracle donor coefficients as evidence that the coefficient computation has been learned. Where such simple rules fail, localize which coefficient changes require contextual activations before choosing a richer featurizer.

## Previous continuation: H927

## H927 — Name-identity alignment removes most apparent routing–value interaction

The previous experiment found a large explicit cross term in a position-aligned finite-change decomposition. H927 tests whether that term persists when the swapped event names are aligned by identity. This directly addresses the user's data-based canonical-form idea: an explanation should distinguish stable computation from arbitrary correspondence between coordinates.

### Alignment and intervention

At the two event-name positions, jointly permute donor routing coefficients and donor mixed-value vectors so each name matches its recipient occurrence. Leave every other position unchanged. Both experimental contrasts reverse the event-name order, and token-ID equality is asserted after alignment. Joint permutation preserves the donor attention sum exactly; it is a reindexing of contributions after the model has run, not a modification to its positional encoding or evidence that the model performs this permutation internally.

With aligned donor coefficients and vectors, repeat routing-only, value-only, cross-only, simultaneous routing+value, all-three, cached full replacement and identity interventions. The same three exploratory heads, all128 familiar transfer rows and both contrasts are retained.

### Causal comparison

Cross effects are RMS changes in the second-event-name margin. Routing error compares the aligned routing-only intervention with the unchanged full donor-head replacement, normalized by the full effect's RMS. This is answer-margin fidelity, not yet full-distribution fidelity to the full edited output.

|Contrast|Head|Position-aligned cross RMS|Identity-aligned cross RMS|Aligned routing vs full RMSE|Relative routing error|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|event_swap|L14H4|0.3817|0.00381|0.00302|1.22%|
|event_swap|L14H6|0.1969|0.00480|0.00379|3.68%|
|event_swap|L16H3|0.1783|0.00077|0.00114|1.42%|
|same_fact_reword|L14H4|0.3937|0.00404|0.00390|1.60%|
|same_fact_reword|L14H6|0.2009|0.00586|0.00569|5.63%|
|same_fact_reword|L16H3|0.1800|0.00142|0.00479|6.02%|

At L14H4, the event-swap cross term shrinks about100-fold, from0.38166 to0.00381. Aligned routing alone reproduces the full margin effect with1.22% relative error; same-fact rewording gives1.60%. All three heads show substantial reductions, though the weaker L16H3 rewording effect has6.02% relative routing error. Value differences at non-name positions remain for rewording, so name alignment is not expected to erase all contextual change.

The full swap's effect remains exactly the same as in the earlier experiment. Its apparent attribution changes: before alignment, moved lexical vectors created large value and cross terms; after alignment, the difference is mostly reassignment of coefficients over stable lexical identities. These two decompositions describe the same total head-output change but define different intermediate interventions. Their components should not be mistaken for unique, invariant causal units.

### Research implication

This is stronger evidence for identity-indexed routing over lexical carriers than for a large standalone interaction feature in this panel. It also qualifies H926: the large cross term was necessary for that position-aligned expansion, but was not itself evidence of an independently meaningful computation unit. Small lexical spans failed, yet respecting the correspondence between identities produces a simple and faithful answer-margin account.

The alignment uses known token identities and event occurrences. It is an oracle correspondence, not a learned unsupervised featurizer or a general canonical form. Repeated tokens, alternate tokenizations, contextual values and out-of-distribution contexts remain unresolved. The task itself still exhibits a shortcut; faithful modeling of that shortcut does not establish semantic binding.

### Next test

Evaluate a task-blind identity aggregation of the persistent-value pathway. Because its value vector is fixed by token identity, repeated occurrences of a token can be grouped by summing their signed routing coefficients, with that token's value decoded once. Verify this algebra and numerical fidelity across the existing agreement, language, binding and copy panels, then assess the remaining current-value pathway separately. Preserve the distinction between preserving native outputs and preserving position-specific interventions: merging occurrences loses access to individual-source edits unless provenance is retained.

For the approximate aligned-routing account, measure KL to the full edited distribution, not only the answer margin. Then test coefficient transfer across discovery/transfer identities and templates with the alignment rule fixed before outcomes. These steps would tell us whether a useful data-based representation extends beyond this hand-aligned name-swap panel, without prematurely declaring a manifold verified.

## Previous continuation: H926

## H926 — The missing finite-change interaction is local to attention, with little downstream nonadditivity

H925 found that adding separate routing and value effects badly predicts a full donor-head swap. H926 tests the two competing explanations directly at exploratory heads L14H4, L14H6 and L16H3, retaining all128 transfer rows and both contrasts.

Let native attention routing and values be A,V and donor counterparts B,W. The exact head-output change is R+U+C, with R=(B-A)V, U=A(W-V), and C=(B-A)(W-V), summed over source positions. Intervene separately on R,U,C, jointly on R+U, and jointly on all three. Compare these with the cached full donor-minus-recipient head write. All remaining computation runs live.

This attention product identity is already known from the architecture; the empirical question is which term explains the observed failure of separate causal effects to add.

### Results

All numbers are RMS changes/errors in the recipient second-event-name margin. Downstream RU nonadditivity compares the simultaneous R+U edit with the sum of separate R and U logit effects. Cross increment compares full replacement with simultaneous R+U. Cross-context nonadditivity compares that increment with the cross-only effect.

|Contrast|Head|Full effect|Separate-sum error|Downstream RU nonadditivity|Cross increment|Cross-context nonadditivity|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|event_swap|L14H4|0.2465|0.3808|0.00140|0.3802|0.00353|
|event_swap|L14H6|0.1029|0.1966|0.00027|0.1965|0.00092|
|event_swap|L16H3|0.0802|0.1781|0.00010|0.1781|0.00038|
|same_fact_reword|L14H4|0.2439|0.3927|0.00150|0.3921|0.00386|
|same_fact_reword|L14H6|0.1011|0.2006|0.00030|0.2005|0.00101|
|same_fact_reword|L16H3|0.0794|0.1798|0.00010|0.1798|0.00039|

At L14H4, event-swap separate-sum error is0.38079. The explicit cross increment is0.38022, whereas downstream RU nonadditivity is0.00140. The cross-only effect is0.38166 RMS and differs from its contextual increment by0.00353 RMS. All three heads and both contrasts show the same ordering. These are comparisons of magnitudes, not additive percentages of explained variance.

The evidence therefore attributes the large gap mainly to the omitted local finite-change cross term, not downstream nonlinear processing of the two individual writes. The full effect can be smaller than the cross term because components cancel. Signed means also hide this: cross-only mean effects are about-0.0005 to-0.0014 despite much larger RMS effects. Per-endpoint fidelity is necessary.

Adding all three terms reproduces full donor replacement: margin RMS mismatch about1.5–1.8e-6, with full-vocabulary maximum logit mismatch9.06e-6. This is an implementation check, not independent proof of a discovered feature.

### Interpretation caveat and next test

This cross term is relative to the recipient-centered, position-aligned decomposition. It is not a coordinate-invariant new unit of computation. The same bilinear change can be written exactly as delta-A times midpoint-V plus midpoint-A times delta-V, without a separate cross term. Moreover, both experimental contrasts move names between event positions. Aligning a donor coefficient with the value at the same position may mismatch identities that moved.

Next compare position alignment with name-identity alignment. Permute donor routing and values together at the two event-name positions so that each name aligns with its recipient occurrence. Such joint reindexing leaves the full donor head output unchanged. Recompute the component geometry and causal effects to test whether the large cross term shrinks when name identity is aligned. If it does, much of the interaction reflects coefficient/value reassignment under a token swap; if it persists, investigate context-dependent routing beyond that reassignment. Retain non-name positions and both contrasts, verify permutation invariance, and distinguish this analysis reindexing from changing the model's positional computation.

This is directly relevant to a data-based canonical representation: the representation should track stable relationships and preserve behavior, rather than declare every large coordinate-dependent cross term a separate feature. The experiment has not yet identified a canonical form or verified a manifold.

Several other heads contribute, so the whole-layer effect should not be assigned to one head. At L14H4, event-swap full replacement has mean drop0.232 and RMS0.246. Mixed-value replacement has mean0.244, RMS0.321; persistent-bus replacement nearly matches it. Across endpoints their effect RMSE is0.00306. Current-value-only RMS is0.0031. The same pattern appears for same-fact rewording and the other highlighted heads.

Thus persistent lexical values dominate this value-change component. This is consistent with earlier observations, but not sufficient to explain the full operation: routing-only L14H4 has mean effect-0.0107 yet RMS0.193. Averaging signed effects would hide substantial context dependence.

### Nonadditivity is the next discriminating question

At L14H4, the sum of separately measured routing-only and mixed-value-only logit effects differs from the full replacement by RMSE0.381 for event swaps and0.393 for same-fact rewordings. These discrepancies exceed the full replacement's RMS effect. Comparable discrepancies occur at L14H6 and L16H3. Similar mean effects therefore do not establish a faithful decomposition of individual responses.

Two mechanisms can cause this: the explicit local routing-times-value cross term, and nonlinear downstream response when writes are combined. This experiment audits the exact local algebra but does not distinguish their causal importance at the output. Do not conclude routing is dispensable or assign additive percentages to its contribution.

Next intervene on the exact cross term, the simultaneous routing-plus-value write, and their sum at the highlighted heads, retaining both contrasts. Compare a simultaneous combined edit against the sum of separate logit effects to measure downstream nonlinearity. Compare the combined edit with and without the cross term to measure its contextual effect. Verify that adding all three local terms reproduces full donor-head replacement. This directly tests whether the reusable unit is an interaction between a routing coefficient and a lexical vector, rather than either factor alone.

## H924 — Late attention writes carry the largest event-order contrast effects

H923 separated candidate-name promotion from the unexplained event-order preference. H924 localizes two matched contrasts across all18 layers, testing final-token attention and MLP outputs separately. The128 transfer rows are all retained regardless of task competence. Names and templates are familiar; this is localization on an existing panel, not fresh generalization evidence.

The event-swap donor toggles sender identity while holding list order, extra mention, wording and question fixed. Exactly the two event-name tokens change. The same-fact-reword donor changes sent-to into received-from or vice versa, preserving sender/recipient identities but reversing event argument order and changing the event wording. All pairs have equal token lengths, identical final tokens, and identical pre-event and post-event context. These contrasts separate changes to the fact from changes to its surface order, though the latter also changes lexical wording.

For each recipient, replace one native final-token attention or MLP output with its donor output. Other token positions, modules and downstream computation remain live. ### Interpretation and next experiment

The strongest final-token pathway for this shortcut lies in late attention writes in the current scan. This is a localization result, not a complete circuit: no single patch reproduces the full donor response, and effects cannot be summed as independent causal shares. Patching a donor write can also introduce context mismatch.

Next decompose all nine heads at L14 and L16 for both contrasts. Compare native donor head-output replacement with routing-only, mixed-value-only and persistent/current-value contributions. This distinguishes whether the difference originates in routing, which values are carried, or their interaction. Keep all heads rather than presuming H4 remains the selector: H923 found strong candidate support but incomplete shortcut explanation at that head. Any head selection from this scan is exploratory and will require transfer confirmation before a general mechanism claim.

The broader featurizer implication remains that reusable operation and reusable low-dimensional activation geometry are different hypotheses. We are locating the operation before choosing a representation to approximate it.

## H923 — List-value promotion supports candidate names but does not explain the event-order preference

The preceding screen found second-event-name preference on explicit-fact QA despite failures to switch answers with the question. H923 retains all256 conditions, including failures, and tests each of the five name occurrences' persistent-value contributions at the three previously fixed readers. It also removes all five name contributions at one reader together. No readers or cases are selected using the new results.

Each ablation removes lamb times native signed routing times the layer-0 value for that occurrence, before the head output projection. Current-layer values, other positions and all other computation remain live. These are local zero ablations, not global stream deletions. Readouts include both names' logits/log probabilities, full-distribution KL, task accuracy and the event-second versus event-first margin independently of which answer was requested.

### Transfer results at L14H4

Baseline second-event-name preference is94.53%; mean name margin is0.620. Task accuracy is50.78%. The table aligns initial-list occurrences by the identity's later position in the event, rather than averaging over physical list position. Positive margin drop means reduced second-event-name preference.
