Removing the list occurrence of the second event name reduces its logit by1.033 and drops its binary preference to6.25%. Removing the other list name lowers that other name's logit by1.086 and raises second-name preference to100%. Thus the initial-list values strongly support both candidate names. Their opposing effects cancel when averaged by physical list position: a near-zero mean margin change would misleadingly hide substantial individual effects. Identity-aligned means and RMS effects are therefore reported alongside positional results.

By contrast, removing the event-first or event-second occurrence yields only about0.06 mean margin drop and RMS changes below0.10. Removing all five name contributions at L14H4 lowers both name logits substantially but leaves86.72% second-name preference. This reader's name-value pathway therefore does not fully account for the event-order shortcut. The result does not establish strict independence: nonlinear compensation, current-layer values and other readers remain possible contributors.

L13H0 also promotes initial-list names, with smaller aggregate effects. Removing all its name contributions leaves94.53% second-name preference. L8H3 name-value effects are small on this format. All per-endpoint, per-query, discovery and transfer outcomes are retained rather than collapsing the analysis to successful task cells.

### Interpretation and next experiment

The evidence separates a reusable candidate-promotion operation from the operation that chooses between candidates. In the original sentence-completion panel, L14H4 also suppressed the repeated sender. In this explicit QA panel it mainly supports initial-list names, while much of the event-order preference survives removal of its local name-value inputs. A shared component can contribute to both competent behavior and a shortcut; its presence alone does not determine the behavior's meaning.

Next localize where the event-order preference arises. Use controlled event-argument swaps with names, list order, extra mention and question held fixed where possible; record native final-token residual/logit changes and test full attention/MLP donor substitutions across layers. Because an event swap can change the stated fact, score the event-order preference separately from task correctness and use matched semantic-preserving sent-to/received-from pairs as a second contrast. Start with native competence and token-alignment audits, then compare the two contrasts rather than treating all donor differences as one mechanism. Keep the earlier fixed readers as candidate-support controls instead of attributing the remaining preference to them by default.

This is localization toward a reusable computation model, not evidence that a manifold or an abstract binding feature has been verified.

## H922 — Explicit-fact queries reveal an event-order shortcut, not reliable semantic role switching

H921 showed useful transfer of signed occurrence coefficients in the original incomplete-sentence panel. H922 tests a limitation of that account: whether routing adapts when the more-repeated name is the requested answer. The fixed screen independently crosses name-list order, sender identity, extra-mentioned identity, sent-to versus received-from event wording, and sender versus recipient question.

Example: “Yesterday, John and Mary met. John sent a letter to Mary. John was smiling. Question: Who sent the letter? Answer:” and the same context asking who received it. Received-from reverses event argument order while preserving who sent to whom. This is a lexical argument-order reversal, not grammatical passive voice. Each name occurs once in the list and once in the event; the extra sentence gives one name a third occurrence. All256 rows are retained, with no prompt changes after results.

### Competence

Each cell has16 endpoints from four pairs, two list orders and two sender identities. Binary competence requires both sender-identity endpoints correct within each pair/order. The prior .75 paired-binary and .50 exact-top1 thresholds apply.

No discovery cell passes. Four transfer cells pass, but they align with the second event argument: recipient in sent-to wording, sender in received-from wording. Both questions are not reliably answered for the same facts. These selected successes therefore cannot justify a claim of question-sensitive role binding.

### Shortcut diagnostic

Binary preference below compares the two names, independently of the requested answer. “Both queries correct” requires the preference to change appropriately when the question changes, holding all facts fixed.

|Split|Wording|Prefer second event name|Prefer extra-mentioned name|Both queries correct|Same preference across queries|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|discovery|sent_to|0.688|0.406|0.062|0.875|

On transfer names the model prefers the second event name in95.3% of sent-to and93.75% of received-from rows. Both questions are correct for only3.125% of context pairs. The same name remains preferred across question changes in96.875% and93.75%, respectively. Extra-name preference stays near chance. This rules out interpreting high accuracy in isolated cells as general role-sensitive behavior; event-order preference is a plausible explanation requiring causal testing.

Question changes do affect the output distribution (mean query-pair KL about.014–.017), so the model is not literally invariant to the query. Nor does event-order correlation establish a causal mechanism or prove the model lacks semantic information. It describes the behavior of these prompts.

### Implications and next test

Do not extend a prompt-rescue search or fit a semantic routing model on only the passing cells. H921's shared occurrence computation remains supported within its competent original templates, but extension to explicit question answering is unverified. The three-name-occurrence rule cannot be directly transplanted into this five-occurrence format without specifying a new mapping.

Use this panel as a negative control with an observable alternative behavior. Test local persistent-value contributions from each of the five name occurrences at the fixed readers, using the same causal method as H920. Evaluate effects on event-second versus event-first name preference regardless of requested answer, alongside task correctness, name log probabilities and full-distribution KL. Compare event-name ablations with the final extra mention and initial list. This can determine whether the model reuses lexical promotion machinery to implement an event-order shortcut. Report all query conditions; successful causal explanation of a shortcut is not successful semantic binding.

## Previous continuation: H921

## H921 — Discovery-fitted occurrence routing transfers across name identities

H920 supported candidate promotion and repeated-sender suppression through signed persistent-value routing. H921 replaces those routing coefficients with means fitted only on discovery names, retaining each recipient's own lexical values. This directly tests a reusable operation, following H919's failure to find a small transferable name-value span.

### Design and scope

Fit the coefficient for each name occurrence on the first four name pairs, balanced over sender identity and list order. Evaluate the other four name pairs across both templates and list orders, plus copying. Evaluate the three frozen readers separately and jointly. The fitted coefficients replace only persistent-value contributions at the named occurrences. Current-value contributions, other positions, other heads and downstream computation remain live. In joint edits, later readers' live routing is subtracted before adding the fitted contribution; the implementation does not subtract stale cached routing after an earlier edit.

Own-mean coefficients use the matching template; other-format uses the other template; pooled averages both. The occurrence model additionally ties both initial-list coefficients, so it needs no distinction between sender and recipient within the list. Wrong-occurrence swaps list-other and repeated-sender coefficients; sign-flip reverses all pooled coefficients. Zero removes all selected name-value contributions. Identity leaves them unchanged. No fitting or outcome selection uses transfer names, but these names are familiar from prior experiments and are not a pristine holdout.

### Joint three-reader transfer

Error ratios compare deviation from native behavior with zeroing the same name contributions. Low KL and error indicate fidelity; improved accuracy alone does not. Native binding accuracy is87.5%, copying100%.

|Family|Replacement|Margin RMS error|Error / zero|Native→edited KL|KL / zero|Top1|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|copy|identity|0.000|0.000|0.00000|0.000|100.00%|
|copy|zero|1.084|1.000|0.14164|1.000|100.00%|
|copy|own_mean|0.274|0.252|0.00563|0.040|100.00%|
|copy|other_format|0.314|0.289|0.00752|0.053|100.00%|
|copy|pooled|0.288|0.266|0.00627|0.044|100.00%|
|copy|occurrence|0.288|0.266|0.00627|0.044|100.00%|
|copy|wrong_occurrence|0.288|0.266|0.00627|0.044|100.00%|
|copy|sign_flip|3.281|3.026|1.18640|8.376|62.50%|
|task|identity|0.000|0.000|0.00000|0.000|87.50%|
|task|zero|2.424|1.000|0.30841|1.000|40.62%|
|task|own_mean|0.268|0.110|0.00492|0.016|84.38%|
|task|other_format|0.392|0.162|0.03657|0.119|96.88%|
|task|pooled|0.295|0.122|0.01225|0.040|90.62%|
|task|occurrence|0.326|0.134|0.01465|0.047|90.62%|
|task|wrong_occurrence|8.049|3.320|1.52221|4.936|0.00%|
|task|sign_flip|4.864|2.006|0.99177|3.216|0.00%|

Joint own-mean binding error is0.268 logits, only11.0% of zeroing's2.424; KL is0.00492 versus0.3084 for zeroing. Pooled coefficients remain useful (error ratio.122, KL.01225), and tying initial-list roles is only somewhat worse (error ratio.134, KL.01465). Other-template transfer is less faithful than own-template transfer despite higher accuracy: its KL is0.03657 while top1 improves to96.875%. This is a concrete demonstration that correctness and mechanistic fidelity differ.

Wrong-occurrence and sign-flip joint edits produce0% binding top1. At L14H4 alone, own-mean margin-error ratio is.130 and KL.00445; wrong-occurrence also yields0% top1. This supports the importance of how lexical contributions are assigned and signed, not just their presence.

Copying own-mean joint error ratio is.252 and KL.00563. The copy wrong-occurrence control is exactly equivalent to pooled coefficients here: both positions carry the same token's persistent value, so swapping two coefficients preserves their sum. It is an algebraically degenerate control, not evidence of insensitivity to arbitrary wrong routing. Binding wrong-occurrence is nondegenerate because it exchanges coefficients attached to different names.

### Interpretation

These experiments support a reusable signed occurrence rule over relatively distinct lexical vectors. A small lexical span failed, while a handful of coefficients substantially preserved the causal contribution across names. Sharing an operation therefore need not mean sharing a small activation subspace. The occurrence-only fit further weakens the need to posit separate semantic sender/recipient features for these templates.

This remains a partial model. It uses externally annotated name positions, retains native values and the rest of the model, and does not explain how the model computes the routing or identifies occurrences. It neither replaces whole heads nor establishes the complete binding circuit. There are only four transfer name pairs; repeated endpoints and templates are correlated. Wrong controls can be strong off-native perturbations, so their failures complement rather than replace the positive fidelity test.

### Next information-gaining test

Break the current confound between repeated identity and semantic role. Use a fixed competence screen where the repeated entity is sometimes the expected answer: matched active/passive or subject/object query variants, with name-list order and identity counterbalanced. Retain all conditions before examining outcomes. Compare the frozen occurrence rule with actual routing on competent conditions. A fixed repetition-suppression rule predicts the wrong response when repetition and the required answer coincide; context-sensitive routing should change sign or allocation. Failed competence conditions cannot adjudicate the mechanism and must be reported separately rather than prompt-tuned until successful.

If competent counterexamples exist, test whether the new routing profile transfers across names and whether the existing local rule fails selectively there. This tests compositional computation directly and reconnects the result to choosing featurizers that represent operations as well as activation geometry.

## H920 — Counterbalanced binding supports candidate promotion plus repeated-sender suppression

H919 rejected tiny discovery-name difference spans as useful transfer representations. H920 therefore tests the operation applied to lexical values. It crosses list order with sender identity independently, using the same eight name pairs and two frozen templates. For example, both “John and Mary ... John sent a letter to” and “Mary and John ... John sent a letter to” request Mary. Copy controls are included once rather than duplicated for a nonexistent list-order factor. No outcomes are filtered.

### Native competence

All discovery cells have 100% exact top1. On transfer names, template A has 75% and template B 100%, identically for both list orders. Every pair has correct binary name discrimination in all cells. Copy controls have 100% top1. All cells pass the prior competence gate. This excludes a simple fixed-list-position answer rule for this panel; it does not establish broad syntax generalization or distinguish semantic roles from repetition heuristics.

### Occurrence ablations

At each of the three frozen readers, remove only the local persistent-value contribution from one name occurrence: initial-list sender, initial-list other name, or repeated sender. Other heads, current-layer values and downstream computation remain live. These are zero ablations of local contributions, not global value deletions or natural donor substitutions. No manifold claim follows from them alone.

The table gives transfer means across four pairs, two templates, both list orders and both sender identities. “Other logit” means the wrong answer, which is the sender. Positive margin drop means the ablation harms correct-versus-sender discrimination. Signed routing coefficients are not probabilities.

|Reader|Removed occurrence|Native signed routing|Correct logit change|Sender logit change|Margin drop|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|L13H0|list_sender|-0.296|-0.015|-0.677|-0.662|
|L13H0|list_other|-0.307|-0.588|+0.181|+0.770|
|L13H0|sender_repeat|0.159|-0.034|+0.318|+0.353|
|L14H4|list_sender|-0.237|-0.042|-1.338|-1.296|
|L14H4|list_other|-0.253|-1.156|+0.119|+1.275|
|L14H4|sender_repeat|0.321|-0.090|+1.615|+1.705|

At L14H4, removing the initial sender occurrence lowers the sender logit by 1.338, improving discrimination. Removing the initial other-name occurrence lowers the correct logit by 1.156, harming discrimination and lowering top1 from 87.5% to 68.75%. Removing the repeated sender occurrence raises the sender logit by 1.615 while changing the correct logit by only -0.090. Correct-versus-sender margin falls by 1.705, although top1 remains 87.5%. Thus accuracy alone hides a substantial suppression effect.

L13H0 shows the same qualitative pattern at smaller magnitude. L8H3 has weaker effects. Copying L14H4 has negative routing to both repeated-token occurrences; removing either reduces the correct token's logit, especially the first occurrence. This is compatible with a common lexical carrier used differently through signed routing.

The role of downstream computation matters: routing sign alone does not identify promotion or suppression. The ablations establish the net downstream effect for these contexts. Changes in log probability, as well as logits and full-distribution KL, are saved to avoid relying solely on raw-logit interpretations.

### List-order check at L14H4

|List order|Occurrence|Mean routing|Margin drop|
|---|---|---:|---:|
|0|list_sender|-0.233|-1.293|
|0|list_other|-0.256|+1.303|
|0|sender_repeat|0.323|+1.742|
|1|list_sender|-0.241|-1.298|
|1|list_other|-0.251|+1.248|
|1|sender_repeat|0.319|+1.668|

These are correlated endpoints from four transfer pairs, not independent large-sample statistical evidence. The counterbalance strengthens the operational hypothesis but does not establish an abstract recipient feature. Candidate promotion plus repeated-token suppression could solve these prompts without general semantic binding.

### Decision and next test

Prioritize a reusable signed-routing rule over a tiny lexical subspace: promote both listed candidates and suppress the repeated sender. Fit role-aligned routing coefficients on discovery names only, then replace native coefficients on transfer names while retaining recipient value vectors. Compare role/occurrence-matched coefficients with deliberately wrong mappings, native/self controls, and copying. Include separate evaluation of role mapping versus simple occurrence mapping: the current panel makes the repeated entity the sender in every task, so those explanations remain confounded. A later competence-screened syntax panel must separate repetition from semantic role before asserting abstract binding.

Measure fidelity to native behavior and full-vocabulary KL, not only whether the answer remains correct. A mean coefficient that preserves high accuracy may still fail to reproduce the original computation. Keep all discovery and transfer cells, including failures.

### Verification

1,152 forwards: 96 native plus each selected reader's identity and occurrence ablations. Identity replay is exactly zero; source hashes unchanged; all results finite. All name continuations are single tokens; occurrences are identified by token IDs with asserted counts. Native logits, persistent values, full routing vectors, per-endpoint logit/log-probability changes and KL are saved. No reserved test or added natural documents; document pool remains 26,112. Broad goal active.

## Previous continuation: H919

## H919 — Small discovery-name value spans fail causal transfer

H918 established a causal carrier: the persistent values read by L14H4 strongly affect binding. H919 asks whether this carrier is a small reusable subspace. It is a linear baseline for the manifold/featurizer question, not a new BSF fit.

### Design

Fit uncentered SVD to four persistent-value differences between discovery name pairs. One copy/template-A record per pair supplies the fit; no transfer names contribute. Evaluate ranks 1, 2 and 4 at each of the frozen L8H3, L13H0 and L14H4 readers. Three seeded random subspaces at each rank are controls. Use the same head-specific basis across binding/copying and both templates. Project the donor-minus-recipient bus difference, retain native routing, and run the downstream model live.

Evaluation uses the four other name pairs, previously used in earlier experiments, not a pristine test set. The reference is H918's full bus swap. Compare answer-effect RMSE and KL(full edited distribution || projected edited distribution) against doing nothing. Ratios near one mean little improvement over no intervention; zero means perfect reproduction. Captured value energy is measured separately.

### Rank-4 transfer results

|Family|Reader|Value energy captured|Effect error / doing nothing|KL / doing nothing|Random rank-4 effect-error range|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|copy|L8H3|0.040|0.961|0.968|0.976–0.980|
|copy|L13H0|0.016|0.981|0.977|0.961–0.973|
|copy|L14H4|0.026|0.990|1.009|0.967–0.976|
|task|L8H3|0.040|0.947|0.899|0.946–0.985|
|task|L13H0|0.016|0.982|0.962|0.962–0.969|
|task|L14H4|0.026|0.986|0.976|0.961–0.979|

Ranks 1 and 2 also fail to recover substantial effects. The discovery rank-4 span reconstructs its four training differences to numerical precision, but captures only 1.6–4.0% of transfer differences. At L14H4, binding effect error remains 98.6% of doing nothing and KL remains 97.6%. No persuasive advantage over random controls appears. This is not a formal significance test; there are only four transfer pairs, and endpoints/templates are correlated.

The result rejects this small paired-difference span as a useful transferable representation. It does not establish that no nonlinear manifold exists, or that larger or differently sampled dictionaries cannot work. Four arbitrary lexical contrasts are weak coverage of name identity. Persistent values may preserve many distinct identities while sharing the rule that routes or reads them. Hence shared computation need not imply low-dimensional activation differences.

### Hypothesis refresh: 20 alternatives

1. Names have high-dimensional token-specific value codes; the shared computation is routing.
2. A shared downstream readout transforms many lexical codes without compressing them to a small span.
3. The relevant subspace is larger than four dimensions and needs broader discovery coverage.
4. The arbitrary discovery pair differences miss semantic organization present in individual name vectors.
5. Nonlinear or union-of-subspace geometry exists despite failure of a global linear span.
6. Routing encodes sender versus recipient role independently of name identity.
7. Routing primarily exploits repeated-token identity rather than an abstract role.
8. Position or recency heuristics explain much of this narrow binding panel.
9. Name-specific query/key interactions modulate routing, preventing simple coefficient transfer.
10. L14H4 carries an exclusion signal that suppresses the sender rather than directly representing the recipient.
11. The head directly promotes the alternative name through context-dependent downstream processing.
12. Signed attention coefficients reverse a common lexical write between copying and binding.
13. Later MLPs transform the same value direction differently across contexts.
14. Final normalization amplifies or attenuates apparently task-specific effects.
15. Several readers redundantly carry the same lexical information.
16. Reader interactions are nonlinear, so individual-head effects understate joint dependence.
17. The persistent stream supplies identity while current-layer values supply small but necessary context corrections.
18. Other source positions, rather than the changed sender position alone, supply the decisive recipient information.
19. The present templates reward shallow completion that will fail altered syntax or entity order.
20. Full-vocabulary effects arise partly from broad name-likelihood shifts rather than selective binding computation.

These are candidate explanations, not equally supported claims. H918 most directly supports persistent lexical information (1), and H919 makes insufficient coverage/high dimension (3–4) plausible. A shared routing/readout rule (2,6,7,12) is the highest-information next target because it can explain reuse without requiring activation compression. Position/template shortcuts (8,19) and suppression versus promotion (10,11,20) are essential competing controls.

### Next experiment

Use a fixed counterbalanced binding panel that independently changes which name is listed first and which name is the sender, across both templates. Retain all eligible cases and check full-vocabulary competence before interpreting intervention results. Measure signed routing to each name occurrence and separate correct-name promotion from sender suppression. Then transfer routing coefficients between name identities while retaining the recipient's own values and positions matched by role, comparing same-role and wrong-role donors. Include native/self controls and copying controls. This tests a reusable operation directly; it avoids treating successful compression as a prerequisite for shared computation.

### Verification and execution accounting

The retained run has 1,376 forwards. A first complete run failed only an overly strict static-token cache tolerance: 1.1444e-5 versus 1e-5. The panel's earlier 1e-4 tolerance was restored, then all 1,376 forwards were rerun; total compute is 2,752 forwards. This numerical tolerance revision is disclosed rather than hidden.

Identity edits exactly reproduce native logits, and full bus edits exactly replay H918. Native-cache maximum logit discrepancy is 1.24e-5. Basis orthogonality error is 1.22e-15; discovery rank-4 reconstruction relative error is 7.26e-16. Source hashes unchanged and results finite. Fits, singular values, endpoint metrics and random-control outcomes saved. No reserved-test evaluation or added natural documents; pool remains 26,112. Broad goal active.

## Previous continuation: H918

## H918 — Binding effects at L14H4 are carried predominantly by the persistent value stream

The previous turn completed H917 and changed the next experimental priority. H918 returns to the existing competent binding and matched copying panel. It tests all eight name pairs, both templates and both endpoints. First four pairs remain discovery; last four are transfer. These transfer names have appeared in earlier experiments and are not a pristine test set. No features or heads are selected using these results: the heads are the previously specified L8H3, L13H0 and L14H4.

### Intervention and implementation

For recipient final-token routing A and mixed values V, head output is sum(A*V). The donor is the opposite source-name endpoint in the same pair, template and family. Routing-only uses donor routing with recipient values. Mixed-values-only uses recipient routing with donor values. Bus-only changes only the persistent layer-0 value contribution at this reader; current-values-only changes the remaining value contribution. Full replacement uses the cached donor head output. All edits are applied before the head output projection; all other heads and downstream computation run live.

The model's actual mixing coefficient is used without an extra amplitude rescaling. The bus intervention changes this local reader's consumption, not the persistent stream globally. Identity deltas are zero. Exact local decomposition includes the routing-by-value cross term; downstream answer effects need not add linearly.

The strongest binding effect among these frozen readers is L14H4: full replacement drops top1 to 37.5%; mixed-value and bus-only swaps both reach 43.75%. Copying shows substantial margin changes without top1 failure, illustrating why accuracy alone is insufficient.

Routing-only changes are smaller in this endpoint comparison. This does not establish that routing is unnecessary: native routing remains essential to reading values, these endpoints may induce similar routing, and only three heads are tested. The result localizes a causal carrier; it does not prove a manifold, a binding-specific feature, or completeness of the circuit.

### Next information-gaining test

Fit uncentered paired-difference subspaces of the persistent head-specific name values using discovery pairs only, with ranks 1, 2 and 4 plus matched random controls. Replace the full donor bus difference by its projection, preserving the recipient's actual routing and downstream computation. Evaluate on transfer names in both binding templates and both copying controls. Compare projected intervention effects with the full bus intervention using answer-effect error and KL to the full edited distribution. Report captured value energy separately. The critical possibility is that a shared lexical carrier works for both tasks while context-dependent routing/readout determines its use. Failure of a small subspace would instead favor high-dimensional lexical identity or insufficient discovery coverage.

## H917 — Crossing label assignment with field order does not establish competent abstract task switching

H916 confounded label meaning with demonstration field order. H917 independently crosses A/B meaning with A-first/B-first records, while keeping the instruction's semantic order fixed: language, then country. Two shared demonstrations use Argentina and Australia; neither occurs in evaluation. All four conditions and all eligible countries are retained. Mapping 0 assigns A to language; mapping 1 assigns B to language.

|Cohort|Record order / mapping|Language exact top1|Copy exact top1|
|---|---|---:|---:|
|Old|A first / 0|68.75%|100%|
|Old|A first / 1|6.25%|100%|
|Old|B first / 0|31.25%|93.75%|
|Old|B first / 1|6.25%|100%|
|New|A first / 0|8.33%|100%|
|New|A first / 1|0%|100%|
|New|B first / 0|8.33%|100%|
|New|B first / 1|0%|100%|

Only old-country A-first/mapping-0 passes the existing joint competence gate. There is no competent counterbalanced mapping pair, and no new-country language cell passes. Field order matters in mapping 0, but reversing the assignment fails in either order. These results do not isolate a pure label bias or establish absence of an abstract task representation; they establish that this particular arbitrary-label protocol is unsuitable for interpreting reliable task switching.

The binary language-answer comparison is misleading here: all old-country pairs and five of six new-country pairs prefer the correct language over the other country's language, despite low full-vocabulary accuracy. Comparing the intended language against the current country's name yields preference fractions equal to the language top1 fractions in this table. The model often prefers the copying answer. This diagnostic is saved separately, and is not treated as a complete readout of internal task selection.

### Decision and next experiment

Stop extending this arbitrary-label prompt rescue sequence. The matched natural-language query evidence from H915 remains evidence for query-conditioned processing, not a proven mapping-invariant semantic operator. Return to competent binding tasks and their matched copying controls. Their weak single-MLP effects in H906 motivate attention/value-bus interventions before fitting another small MLP feature basis.

For the next experiment, separate routing from carried value: use native donor/recipient substitutions at the previously specified reader heads, with identity and full replacement controls. Fit any candidate shared value subspace on discovery name pairs only; evaluate its effect fidelity on the other name pairs and both templates. Retain copying controls and measure full-distribution KL as well as answer margins. This reconnects the featurizer objective to causal structure: a useful manifold must preserve the component's effects and transfer, not merely reconstruct its activations. Head-specific effects should be measured before interpreting low-rank recovery.

224 native forwards; 112 within-mapping one-query-token controls and 112 cross-mapping same-query checks pass. Source hashes unchanged; results finite. No intervention or fitted operator in this experiment. No reserved-test evaluation or new natural documents; the document pool remains 26,112. The broad research goal remains active.

## H916 — Arbitrary-label remapping fails symmetrically competent language behavior; demonstration order is confounded

The previous turn made progress: H915 found query-specific L13 processing under matched surfaces, but the lexical query words still differed. H916 tests arbitrary labels A/B whose requested operations swap across contexts, before fitting or interpreting any operators.

Mapping0 assigns A=language and B=country copying. Mapping1 reverses that assignment. D0/D1 provide two shared demonstration records (Argentina/Spanish and Australia/English); I0/I1 add an explicit mapping instruction. Each record lists A then B. The same final query label can therefore request either operation across mappings. Demonstration countries are excluded from the evaluation inventory. All four conditions are fixed before outcomes, with every eligible result retained.

### Token controls and native competence

112 within-mapping task/copy pairs have identical lengths/final tokens and exactly one changed query token. Another112 cross-mapping checks verify the same query label/suffix and equal length when comparing different requested operations. These controls do not make the whole prefixes identical across mappings; their content necessarily specifies different assignments.

Fourteen eligible country pairs produce224 rows. The prior continuation-token exclusions remain unchanged. Competence uses the previously defined minimum-pair, both-endpoint binary, and50% exact top1 thresholds.

|Cohort|Condition|Task top1|Copy top1|Task both-binary|Copy both-binary|Joint pass|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
|old|D0|0.000|1.000|1.000|1.000|False|
|old|D1|0.000|1.000|1.000|1.000|False|
|old|I0|0.875|1.000|1.000|1.000|True|
|old|I1|0.312|1.000|1.000|1.000|False|
|new|D0|0.000|1.000|0.833|1.000|False|
|new|D1|0.000|1.000|0.833|1.000|False|
|new|I0|0.417|1.000|0.833|1.000|False|
|new|I1|0.000|1.000|0.833|1.000|False|

Copying has100% top1 throughout. Demonstration-only language has0% top1 in both mappings. Adding explicit instructions improves mapping0 language, with87.5% old-country top1, but mapping1 reaches only31.25%. New-country instruction cells both fail (41.7%/0%). There is no jointly competent pair of counterbalanced mappings; old I0 alone cannot support a mapping-invariant semantic-operator claim.

### Binary source discrimination concealed wrong-task preference

The prior binary margin compares two countries' language answers, not language versus copying the current country. A diagnostic comparison of the intended language against that same country's name shows language is never preferred in D0/D1, in either cohort. Old I0 prefers language in93.75% of endpoints; old I1 only31.25%. New I0 reaches50%, new I1 zero. Thus high binary language preference can coexist with preference for the other operation's answer. This validates the need for full-vocabulary competence and suggests retaining a task-choice diagnostic in future screens.

These comparisons describe output preferences, not complete internal task selection or proof that no language computation occurred. No intervention or operator fit is run here.

### Design confound and next test

The record order was fixed A then B. Swapping label meanings therefore also swaps whether language output appears first or second in demonstrations; the explicit instruction's semantic ordering changes too. The observed asymmetry cannot be assigned solely to label identity or mapping ability.

Next cross label mapping with demonstration field order, and control instruction ordering separately or hold semantic instruction order fixed. For example, keep “language is field X; country is field Y” as the instruction sequence while X/Y swap, and evaluate both A-first and B-first records. Predetermine all combinations and retain failures. Check joint competence and same-country language-versus-copy preferences before interpreting operators. Do not rescue the present test by selecting only the successful mapping or dropping difficult countries.

This failed screen narrows the experimental design; it does not refute abstract task representations or validate a lexical-only account. The model may be sensitive to demonstration order or arbitrary-label instruction format. Binding pathways and the broader shared-dictionary/manifold objective remain open.

## H908 — A shared context-dependent map transfers better than a small lexical subspace

### Exact algebra clarifies the controls

For normalized recipient u and source change d, a bilinear MLP obeys F(u+d)−F(u)=J(u)d+Q(d)=J(u+d/2)d, where J is its input Jacobian and Q is the quadratic change. Bias cancels. A fixed discovery mean m therefore defines two different approximations: J(m)d approximates the midpoint partner, while J(m)d+Q(d) approximates the recipient partner. Adding Q is not automatically more faithful when m is closer to the midpoint than to u.

The native recipient MLP output remains the offset in every condition; only its finite change is approximated. No input projection discards the country-specific change. All mean fits are frozen before evaluation. Family/template labels choose the diagnostic mean, so this is not yet a task-blind operator-selection mechanism.

### Language task effects at L13/14

Error ratio is effect RMSE versus the exact full donor substitution divided by the no-change RMSE. KL compares exact-edited and approximate-edited output distributions. The opposite-family mean uses copying discovery examples in the same template; pooled task means average both task templates.

|Layer|Partner approximation|Effect-error ratio|Exact-to-approximate KL|
|---|---|---:|---:|
|13|native_linear|0.434|0.04227|
|13|own_linear|0.334|0.00558|
|13|own_quad|0.290|0.04644|
|13|task_pooled_linear|0.331|0.00607|
|13|task_pooled_quad|0.304|0.04763|
|13|opposite_linear|0.790|0.03614|
|14|native_linear|0.595|0.11354|
|14|own_linear|0.389|0.00554|
|14|own_quad|0.292|0.10462|
|14|task_pooled_linear|0.392|0.00634|
|14|task_pooled_quad|0.300|0.10535|
|14|opposite_linear|0.698|0.01956|

Own-context midpoint approximations reach effect-error ratios0.334/0.389, compared with roughly0.80–0.86 for the previous rank4 input-subspace fits. Pooled task means perform similarly (0.331/0.392), suggesting that a context-dependent linear map can process unseen country changes without requiring those changes to share the small discovery span. This is a deliberate change of hypothesis and information budget: the mean-partner method retains the full source change and original weights, so it is not a matched-capacity compression victory.

Copy-context means are worse on language (ratios0.790/0.698, KL0.03614/0.01956), supporting context specificity. On copying, own-context midpoint means yield KL0.00398/0.00324, whereas pooled task means give0.02889/0.02931. Thus a single task mean does not reproduce all contexts, and the controls support reusable context-dependent processing rather than one universal map.

### Margin fidelity can reward distributionally wrong approximations

Adding the quadratic term to the own mean improves language effect-error ratios to0.290/0.292, yet worsens KL from0.00558→0.04644 at L13 and0.00554→0.10462 at L14. At L14, even the opposite-family-plus-quadratic condition has ratio0.274 while KL is0.09598. A target margin alone can favor a substantially less faithful intervention distribution.

Likewise, native-linear-only effects are not a reliable substitute for the full change: native J(u)d omits Q, whereas the midpoint form accounts for the exact quadratic effect through its evaluation point. These controls identify a finite-intervention geometry issue rather than proving that quadratic computation is unimportant.

### What this establishes and what remains

The data are consistent with a shared context-dependent transformation acting on many lexical directions. They do not establish a low-dimensional manifold, a compact learned dictionary, or automatic task labels. J(m) retains the original bilinear weights and may be high rank. Current means are diagnostic context summaries; downstream attention and other sites still participate in the task.

Next freeze these means and test additional country/language pairs and prompt variants with competence and tokenization checks specified before looking at intervention outcomes. Keep full-distribution fidelity alongside target margins, and retain failed competence cells. Independently compare means fitted from disjoint discovery country sets before treating the operator as canonical. This is more informative than further shrinking the lexical span on the same small panel. Binding still needs its separate attention/value-bus investigation; broader shared-dictionary/manifold objectives remain open.

Ranks1/2/4 plus seeded random rank4 are evaluated on four disjoint country pairs in task/copy contexts. Full and projected source changes are inserted only at the final-query MLP, with exact bilinear quadratic terms and live downstream computation. Projected normalized inputs are not renormalized; no norm-matched selectivity claim is made.

### Copying and interpretation

At L13–14, task-trained rank4 bases capture only about6% of copying changes; effect-error ratios remain0.825–0.861. No successful shared copying mechanism emerges. These results do not disprove structured language computation or a higher-dimensional lexical representation. Four discovery country contrasts provide a very limited span, and new countries may use distinct directions.

The distinction now worth testing is a shared operation versus a shared low-dimensional activation subspace. An operation can process many country-specific directions without those directions collapsing onto one to four axes. Repeatedly increasing rank on four contrasts cannot distinguish that possibility from insufficient lexical coverage.

Next preserve each recipient's full paired source change and test whether discovery-only context means can approximate the bilinear partner state that processes it. Compare own task-template means, pooled task means, and matched copying means, with exact/native-linearized/quadratic controls. This tests reusable context-dependent processing without first throwing away most of the lexical change. It is an operator-reuse diagnostic, not a learned low-dimensional feature claim or a parameter-compression result. Broader manifold, shared-dictionary, and binding-pathway work remains incomplete.

All-layer task RMS effects are2.438 agreement,3.109 language and0.785 binding; corresponding KL values0.3269,0.3070,0.0413. ### Research decision

L12 inherited from the number investigation was a poor language localization choice. Next compare discovery paired-change and pooled subspaces at L13/L14, keeping L12 as a reference and explicitly treating the new layer choice as screening-derived. Ask whether low-dimensional subspaces recover actual donor-intervention effects there, with copying controls and held-out pairs. Later independent validation is required before a generalization claim.

For binding, avoid assuming the same MLP-local computation. Return to the previously identified attention/value-bus pathways or test a broader site intervention before investing further in a low-rank MLP unit. Shared-dictionary, manifold, and reusable-computation claims require evidence across these different mechanisms, not only a number case study.

### Finite intervention definition

At final-query L12, form the difference from the recipient's live normalized MLP input to its matched opposite-source donor's cached normalized input. Projected normalized inputs are not renormalized. Task paired-subspace interventions change their norm by at most about0.2% in the reported rank1/4 conditions; this is a limitation, not a norm-matched causal isolation claim. Full changes preserve the donor normalized norm to numerical precision.

## H904 — Stable, compressible directions need not track the task-distinguishing changes

The previous turn made progress: H903 found that retaining group means did not give a reliable advantage over nearby-capacity flat approximations for the fixed number component. H904 broadens the diagnostic to existing language and binding tasks, retaining agreement as a reference.

Language examples ask for the main language spoken in a country (for example Italy/Japan). Binding examples ask for the recipient in a two-name sentence (John and Mary, with the sender changed). These differ from a universal binary number label: endpoint0/1 is arbitrary across country/name pairs and must not be treated as a shared semantic class.

### Fixed discovery/transfer design

Use cached normalized L12 pre-MLP activations from the earlier competent-domain panel. For each domain and template, first four pairs (eight task endpoints) fit the leading centered input PC. Origin is the discovery mean projected on that axis. Fit output PCs of its exact contextual cross-write C(w) using the same discovery endpoints. Last four pairs are disjoint transfer cases, evaluated in both templates and matched copying. No new layer or PC selection, natural evaluation, live intervention, or reserved-test evaluation occurs.

Two distinct metrics: input-axis capture is the fraction of each paired endpoint-difference vector's squared norm projected onto the axis, averaged over four transfer pairs. Output error is relative RMS reconstruction error for the native cross term tC(w), normalized by its removal error. Small output error does not show that the axis represents the task or that the component has meaningful downstream influence.

Across templates, language input axes have absolute cosine0.955 and output PCs0.896, compared with agreement0.729/0.748 and binding0.714/0.448. Language's relatively stable directions still capture little paired source-change energy. Stability is therefore a separate criterion from relevance to the controlled contrast.

The chosen L12 layer came from the number investigation, not a claim that it is optimal for language or binding. All discovery panels are tiny, reused and deliberately structured. The earlier task competence screen supports examining these domains, but this cached geometry experiment does not remeasure live task competence or prove causal relevance of the new axes.

### Next experiment and scope

Compare pooled activation PCs against subspaces fitted to paired source-change vectors, using discovery pairs only. Retain ranks1/2/4 and evaluate on disjoint pairs without treating endpoint order as a common semantic label. This addresses whether extraction is missing the relevant variation rather than merely finding compressible background structure.

Pair construction is experimental supervision, not automatically discovered task labels. A successful contrast-conditioned subspace would still require causal selectivity, stability, novel combinations, and an unlabeled recovery method before being called a fundamental unit. The broader BSF/shared-dictionary/manifold objective remains open; number is no longer the sole test case.

## Previous continuation: H903

## H903 — Retaining cluster means does not beat nearby-capacity flat approximations

The previous turn made progress: H902 showed that excessive or output-based clustering can move number information into group means, degrading residual-only approximation. H903 tests whether restoring those means repairs the failure. Keep H902 input-cluster assignments and discovery data frozen for K=2,4,6,12; compute each input centroid and contextual-output mean from its assigned discovery endpoints.

For new inputs, route to the nearest normalized-input centroid. Compare cluster mean only; cluster mean plus a single shared residual direction; the prior global-mean residual approximation; and flat PCA rank K+1. Conditional coefficients are exactly compiled from the fixed bilinear weights, avoiding explicit C computation for the approximation. The exact C is computed for intervention/verification controls.

For number interventions, compare recomputing the route on the changed number coordinate (live conditional approximation) with keeping the native route (a diagnostic intervention protocol). Both keep the exact context-only and quadratic MLP terms. The exact contextual write C(w) is invariant to changing only the number coordinate, since w stays fixed. Thus router changes are an additional approximation behavior, not an inherent change in this exact component.

### Competent grammar fidelity

All fits are evaluated on the reused64-context H893 panel. G passes the previous grammar gate, H fails and remains separate. No best K or fit is selected. Native KL ratio uses removal of the same cross term as denominator. Effect RMSE compares exact versus approximate number-flip margin changes relative to each condition's own native baseline.

|K|Global-mean residual effect RMSE|Conditional live effect RMSE|Fixed-route effect RMSE|Flat rank K+1 effect RMSE|Conditional native KL/removal|Flat native KL/removal|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|2|0.255|0.238|0.238|0.197|0.233|0.224|
|4|0.189|0.179|0.179|0.172|0.268|0.209|
|6|0.178|0.180|0.182|0.151|0.266|0.199|
|12|0.312|0.298|0.303|0.101|0.286|0.175|

Retaining cluster means slightly improves some intervention errors, but does not repair the K12 failure: competent G effect RMSE0.312→0.298, compared with flat rank13 at0.101. Conditional native KL/removal worsens0.260→0.286 there. Cluster means alone perform poorly, with G effect RMSE1.184–1.353, versus removal0.688.

Flat rank K+1 beats the conditional variant on both competent G native KL and effect RMSE at every tested K. The same direction holds for pooled grammar: K12 conditional effect RMSE0.231 versus flat0.074. Copying offers no strong contrary evidence: conditional K12 native KL/removal0.778 versus flat0.583, effect RMSE0.046 versus0.039. Small copy effects still do not imply recovery of its mechanism.

### Capacity and routing accounting

The conditional approximation stores K input centroids, K output means, one decoder and one encoder direction, plus scalar offsets/distance biases: approximately(2K+2)d+K+1 coefficients. Flat rank K+1 stores approximately(2K+3)d+K+1. With d=1152, conditional/flat counts are6915/8067,11525/12677,16135/17287,29965/31117. The flat comparator has1152 extra coefficients, so this is nearby-capacity evidence, not an exactly matched parameter or FLOP comparison. Common number-axis/origin/quadratic components and full-model evaluation machinery are excluded from both counts. Training costs and hard-routing costs are not matched.

Under the number flip, nearest-centroid routing changes on0/64,1/64,2/64 and57/64 contexts for K2/4/6/12 respectively. Yet fixing native routes produces only small changes in effect RMSE and does not repair K12. This rules out route switching as the sole explanation of poor conditional fidelity. It does not prove that every switch is harmful or that better routing cannot help a different representation.

### Research decision

Do not keep adding routing complexity to this isolated component without new evidence. Algebraically C(w) is affine in w for a fixed number axis; the full cross term is t times that affine map. A flat approximation is therefore well matched to this particular subproblem. The result does not refute nonlinear grouped featurizers for the full bilinear MLP, shared-atom representations across multiple axes, or computational DAGs.

The useful finding is narrower: grouping exposed a causally relevant direction hidden by pooled variance, but hard conditional means do not provide a reliable capacity advantage here. Next broaden the diagnostic to existing competent language and binding contexts, using the cached domain-specific captures/fits to identify whether contextual output dimension and causal selectivity resemble the number case. Keep input-axis choice, reconstruction, native fidelity, and intervention fidelity separate. This is a better next discriminator than further tuning a router on the repeatedly reused grammar panel. Shared dictionary/manifold validation and diverse-task reuse remain outstanding.

### Consequence for featurizer design

The next design should preserve between-group structure as well as within-group variation, rather than assume group means can be discarded. This connects to the user's shared-dictionary/hierarchical proposal: groups can select or refine reusable components without deleting computations carried by their differences.

Next test a fixed input-cluster conditional approximation that retains cluster-mean contributions alongside shared residual directions, including the failed K=12 case. Compare with global-mean residualization, cluster-mean-only, and appropriate capacity baselines; count additional means/gating parameters explicitly. Runtime cluster assignment must use only activations and frozen discovery centroids, with all K values retained. Test transfer and causal fidelity before interpreting clusters as task labels. Other competent computations must still be included before drawing a model-wide conclusion; number is a case study, not a complete ontology.

## H901 — Discovery-only clustering recovers the useful context partition in the two-template case

The previous turn made progress: H900 froze a within-template covariance rule, showed improvement over four shuffled-label controls on new combinations, but both new grammar templates failed the full-vocabulary competence gate. H901 evaluates those unchanged rules on the earlier panel with a competent grammar subset, and asks whether template labels are necessary for recovering the discovery partition.

### Fixed clustering rule and scope

Use the same32 discovery endpoints from eight regular nouns in templates A/B. Run Euclidean Lloyd K-means with K=2, deterministic farthest-pair initialization, and a100-iteration cap, separately on normalized L12 MLP input activations and exact contextual output writes. No template or number labels are used to fit clusters or select a run. Both rules are retained. Residualize output writes by the resulting cluster means, take their first PC, and decode with the same global mean and exact affine coefficient.

K=2 is a structural prior motivated by the two-template design; it is not inferred automatically. The number axis was already discovered and fixed in earlier task-directed work. Output-write clustering uses that axis and model weights; input clustering does not need the output write to assign discovery clusters, but its subsequent output fitting still uses the fixed axis. This is not end-to-end unsupervised discovery of a computational unit.

Both methods converge without empty clusters: input in2 iterations, output in3. Each yields groups of16/16 and matches template labels perfectly up to permutation; agreement with singular/plural labels is50%. The derived residual direction matches the labeled within-template direction to floating-point precision. Group labels are not used at evaluation time, and no runtime routing is introduced.

### Live validation on the reused panel

Evaluate64 H893 contexts, including competent grammar G and failed-gate grammar H, plus matched copying. Nouns and grammar templates are absent from output discovery, but this panel was repeatedly used in prior diagnostics. The result confirms behavior on a competent subset; it is not untouched confirmation or evidence of generalization to arbitrary datasets.

### Interpretation and next stress test

A meaningful context partition can be recovered without endpoint labels in this restricted example, and removing between-group covariance exposes a direction with better intervention fidelity. This supports testing conditional/grouped featurizers, rather than interpreting the largest pooled variance direction as the fundamental unit. It still does not validate a manifold: cluster identity could reflect easy prompt/template differences, and the number-related component was supplied upstream.

Next stress the grouping rule on the six-template discovery mixture and multiple fixed K values, retaining all outcomes and measuring whether clusters capture template variation, number, or lexical identity. A grouping that partitions number itself may erase the target signal when residualized. Test this failure mode before generalizing the approach or using clusters as unsupervised task labels. Then extend the same separation of grouping, geometry, and causal tests to other competent computations (language/binding/copying), rather than treating number as representative of the full model. The wider BSF/shared-dictionary/manifold objective remains incomplete.

### Research direction

The result identifies a concrete extraction failure: broadening a dataset changes which variation PCA prioritizes, and its leading direction can preserve substantial variance while missing a causally useful conditional operation. This connects directly to featurizer design: a group of activations should not be validated solely by explained variance, decodability, or unchanged native answers.

Next test a fixed within-template covariance extraction rule against pooled PCA, with the same mean and matched rank, plus shuffled-template-label controls. Use template labels only as an explicit diagnostic aid; such a rule would not yet supply unsupervised task labels or validate a BSF alternative. Freeze the rule before evaluation on additional lexical/template combinations, and keep native distribution fidelity distinct from intervention fidelity. If the advantage survives, investigate whether unlabeled grouping can recover the same conditional structure. The broader manifold and reusable-computation objective remains incomplete.

Natural inputs carry no grammar-task labels here, so this experiment does not measure number-task competence in natural text.

### Updated hypotheses and discriminating experiments

1. A recurring one-dimensional number signal exists: supported by most disjoint discovery fits; test larger balanced lexical splits.
2. Variance ordering hides number behind lexical variation: supported by H895; compare fixed unsupervised extraction rules on independently frozen panels.
3. Number requires a small subspace whose basis rotates: partially consistent, but low full-span overlap limits it; compare principal angles as discovery size grows.
4. A single unique direction exists and small-sample noise explains variation: unresolved; learning curves and bootstrap recovery separate noise from persistent variation.
5. Multiple redundant number directions implement similar effects: possible; displacement-matched interventions and joint ablations can distinguish redundancy.
6. Number direction depends on syntax/template: plausible from A/B differences; cross-template balanced discovery is needed.
7. A shared number direction has context-specific output writes: supported locally; fix the input axis while varying output-fit discovery data.
8. The contextual write is genuinely rank1: not established; held-out output-rank curves must improve causal fidelity, not just reconstruction.
9. Higher output rank is necessary: possible, though H893 rank7 gains were modest; compare ranks at fixed input axis and discovery coverage.
10. Output instability mainly reflects eight-endpoint discovery samples: plausible; fit size curves without changing axis or evaluation panel.
11. Natural text contains contexts absent from grammar discovery: plausible; balanced discovery coverage with prospective evaluation can test it.
12. Weak component influence explains small natural KL: directly supported by removal controls; always report component influence alongside approximation error.
13. A few influential contexts dominate aggregate improvement: supported by average/majority disagreement; characterize influence distributions without fitting an outcome gate.
14. A useful task-blind gate could separate supported contexts: possible but unvalidated; require an independently trained gate and untouched evaluation.
15. Top-token margins amplify small distribution errors: compatible with top changes at low KL; measure native top-two margins prospectively.
16. Number units are specific to agreement rather than copying: supported by synthetic selectivity; extend to other competent number-dependent tasks.
17. Lexical identity contaminates recovered coordinates: plausible; contrast-balanced discovery and new regular/irregular combinations discriminate it.
18. Compact input-output operators are more canonical than latent axes: not established by H894; compare operator stability at matched displacement and origin.
19. Coordinate-origin choices alter the apparent decomposition: established algebraically in H890; retain fixed origins and distinguish gauge-dependent pieces from full interventions.
20. Neither scalar nor block featurizers alone identify computation: consistent with the accumulated separation of decoding, geometry and causal fidelity; test reusable conditional operations against matched scalar/block/shared-dictionary alternatives.

The highest-priority unresolved split is discovery coverage versus intrinsic output rank, with weak natural influence as a required control. Next hold the number axis fixed and vary output-fit sample size, lexical/template coverage, and rank using separated discovery/validation partitions. This prevents input-axis changes from confounding the output question. Freeze resulting rules before any new confirmation panel; do not reuse the384 documents as fresh confirmation after tuning. Keep the failed unit and all current results in the ledger. Manifold validation and the original broader featurizer objective remain incomplete.

### Number survives below the leading PC

For the failed old-transfer template-B fit, PC1 captures only1.03% of the singular/plural centroid-difference energy and has50% discovery number accuracy. PC2 captures22.07% with62.5% accuracy. PC3 captures76.01% and has100% accuracy. These are descriptive diagnostics of existing labeled discovery data, not a selected replacement unit or new confirmation test. Variance fractions for the first three PCs are32.47%,22.47%,20.69%: the highest-variance direction is not the best number direction.

Nearest-centroid decoding fitted in the failed fit's first two PCs transfers with100% accuracy to all four other template-B noun sets, despite capturing only21–29% of their number-centroid difference energy. Classification therefore gives a much weaker criterion than recovering most of the geometric contrast. A low-dimensional supervised readout may succeed without demonstrating a stable, complete computational representation.

### Input subspace overlap and transfer

For equal-rank orthonormal bases V and W, overlap below is the mean squared singular value of V W-transpose:1 means identical subspaces,0 means orthogonal. It is normalized by rank; adding unrelated directions can decrease it even when a shared direction remains. Number capture measures the fraction of a different noun set's centroid-difference energy projected into the source subspace. Transfer accuracy uses source-trained nearest centroids, so the decoder is supervised even though PCA is not.

Each template summary averages ten unordered geometry comparisons and twenty ordered transfer comparisons across disjoint noun sets. Endpoints and comparisons are dependent; these are descriptive means, not independent confirmation samples.

### Research implication and next experiment

This distinguishes missing information from an extraction rule that orders it poorly. The failed first PC does not imply absent number representation. Conversely, perfect number decoding does not validate a featurizer's manifold or conditional computation. Reconstruction-variance objectives may prioritize directions differently from causal relevance.

Do not replace the failed unit with its retrospectively identified PC3 and claim confirmation. Keep all ten H894 units frozen. Next evaluate them, together with exact component-removal controls, on the remaining384 locked natural documents. That measures prospective native-output fidelity and component influence without selecting the best fit. Input-subspace diagnostics do not answer whether output subspaces or compiled operators are stable; those and larger balanced discovery learning curves remain open. The original BSF-alternative comparison and manifold/computational interpretation objective remain active and incomplete.

### Research implication and next generalization boundary

The candidate has progressed from a labeled direction to a compact approximation of an actual native bilinear component that also preserves much of its causal behavior. The next boundary is selection and context breadth. The target is H890's midpoint-centered cross-term intervention Δcross=δ*C(w), not the full coordinate flip or the entire MLP. ### Agreement intervention fidelity

Relative error compares individual expected-number margin changes under the approximation with the exact cross-only intervention, before averaging examples. KL compares the exact edited output distribution with the approximated edited distribution. Its ratio uses KL(exact edited || native unedited) as denominator; it is not a fraction of semantics explained.

|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

A low margin error therefore does not imply complete output-distribution fidelity. Polarity-separated errors and absolute margin-effect errors are retained in the analysis.

Copying does not show the same successful rank1 transfer. Its individual cross-intervention margin errors are about25–60% at rank1 and26–69% at rank7, with KL ratios still0.226–0.527 at rank7. ### Compiled conditional operation

Write the rank1 approximation as C_hat(w)=mu+beta(w)*v, where v is the discovery output principal direction. Because C(w) is linear in w, beta(w)=v·(C(w)−mu) is itself an affine function of the normalized native input u after accounting for the frozen coordinate origin:

beta(u)=encoder·u+offset,

Δcross_hat=δ*mu + δ*beta(u)*v.

The encoder is derived analytically from the model's Left/Right/Down weights and v. It does not require computing the full C(w), and no new parameters are fitted to the transfer examples. The saved compiled units contain the frozen number axis/origin, discovery number centroids, context encoder/offset, and the two output vectors. There are separate axis/family units; this is not a single universal task-blind unit.

This representation has a number-dependent write and a product of number change with a context coefficient. It is concrete evidence for a compact conditional computation within the tested intervention. The experiment does not establish the semantic interpretation of beta, its stability across models, or that the rest of the layer can be omitted. It also does not show that an unsupervised featurizer would discover this decomposition without the present task-guided investigation.

### Next fidelity test

Replace the native centered cross component t*C(w) with t*C_hat(w), keeping the context-only and squared components intact, and test native output fidelity before any coordinate intervention. Then check whether the same compact operation preserves the causal effects across fixed coordinate doses. This separates a model of an intervention from a faithful representation of a component of the native computation. Use the current fitted parameters without selecting ranks on the replacement results, and retain wrong-family/random controls plus vocabulary-wide error. The copying lexical-coverage learning curve remains outstanding.

## Previous continuation: H890

## H890 — L12 number–context interaction carries most of the centered flip effect, but finite curvature matters

Decomposed L12's bilinear output exactly along each frozen number direction and intervened on the resulting output changes separately. With the coordinate centered at the discovery singular/plural midpoint, the number–context cross term alone reproduces most of the full flip's mean agreement-margin reduction. However, a separate native-displacement expansion has a large quadratic remainder. Attribution depends on the coordinate origin and on whether one decomposes the function or the finite intervention. The result supports a number–context interaction, not a uniquely linear semantic unit.

### Exact decompositions and causal intervention

Let b be the unit number axis, u the normalized MLP input, and a the coordinate origin. Set t=u·b−a and w=u−t*b. For F(u)=Down[(Left u)*(Right u)]+bias:

F(u)=F(w)+t*C(w)+t²*Q,

where C(w)=Down[(Left w)*(Right b)+(Left b)*(Right w)] and Q=Down[(Left b)*(Right b)]. Changing t to t' while fixing w gives the exact output change (t'−t)*C(w)+(t'²−t²)*Q.

Test both a=0 (w orthogonal to b) and a equal to the discovery number-midpoint expressed in absolute coordinates (w has a fixed nonzero b-coordinate). The full coordinate intervention is identical under both origins. Centered w must not be described as orthogonal context.

Also decompose the same flip around each native input: ΔF=δ*J(u)b+δ²*Q, with δ=t'−t. This local-linear/local-quadratic split is invariant to the arbitrary coordinate origin. It is different from the coordinate-cross/coordinate-square split.

For each frozen axis, apply full change, coordinate-cross change only, coordinate-square change only, local-linear change only, local-quadratic change only, or identity, at L12. All later computation stays live. Use the same120 eligible task/copy endpoints as H889. This is posthoc mechanistic decomposition of the newly localized L12 effect, not new lexical confirmation. Output-component interventions need not correspond to a realizable single input-coordinate change.

### Agreement margin reductions

|Cohort|Axis|Full flip|Centered cross term|Centered square term|Native local-linear term|Native local-quadratic term|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|irregular|A|2.039|2.012|0.127|1.141|1.622|
|irregular|B|1.400|1.419|0.024|0.619|0.957|
|new_regular|A|1.883|1.751|0.191|1.207|1.888|
|new_regular|B|1.126|0.994|0.162|0.715|0.831|

The centered cross term gives0.994–2.012 margin reduction compared with full1.126–2.040. The centered square term is smaller,0.024–0.191. These are separate causal output interventions; their final-margin effects need not sum because downstream computation is nonlinear. At the MLP output vector, the decomposition itself is exact.

The origin control matters. Under the absolute origin, cross effects range1.033–1.705 and square effects−0.011–0.516. Full-flip effects remain unchanged. Moving the coordinate origin reallocates contributions between cross and square terms without changing the computation, so neither term alone is a coordinate-independent ontology.

The native-displacement quadratic term has large separate effects,0.831–1.888. Therefore the large direct coordinate flip is not faithfully described by a first-order approximation alone. This does not contradict H879's accurate centered response approximation for much smaller L8H3 headwrites: the interventions, sizes and response summaries differ.

### Endpoint polarity exposes cancellation

Pooling regular and irregular task examples, the centered cross term reduces the correct-number margin for both singular and plural endpoints: axis A2.523/1.223, axis B1.060/1.324. In contrast, the native local-linear term increases the singular margin (drops−1.604/−1.033) while reducing the plural margin (drops3.957/2.373). The local-quadratic term largely does the reverse: singular drops3.916/2.185 and plural drops−0.388/−0.405. These complementary effects are hidden by a single mean. The full flip reduces both endpoint margins.

This makes the midpoint-centered interaction a useful description of number polarity in these examples, while preserving the warning that attribution is origin-dependent and downstream interactions prevent unique mediation percentages. Both axes, both cohorts and copying controls remain in the saved analysis.

### Interpretation and next step

The candidate computation is a scalar number-related coordinate modulating a context-dependent output vector C(w), with additional quadratic structure. The exact algebra follows from a bilinear layer; the empirical contribution is that the frozen, semantically validated direction's cross-term intervention transfers most of the measured native agreement-margin effect. It does not establish that C(w) itself is low-dimensional, stable, semantic, or shared across arbitrary tasks.

Next assess whether the cross-term output vector is reusable across nouns and templates, using discovery-only estimates and explicit native-effect fidelity on transfer examples. Compare a mean interaction vector, a small discovery-derived subspace and recipient-specific vectors, with polarity-separated evaluations. That tests whether this is a compact computational operation rather than a scalar gate on a large uncontrolled context-dependent vector. The copying lexical-coverage learning curve remains open; the agreement decomposition does not resolve the general featurizer problem.

### Verification

3,000 full-model forwards. Native and identity logits replay exactly. Bilinear coordinate recomposition relative error 1.99e-15; equality of coordinate and local-displacement flip decompositions 1.87e-15; double formula versus native float module relative error 8.24e-07. H889 full-flip margin replay error 0. Origin-invariant full/local controls replay within 0. All hashes unchanged and outputs/KL finite. No reserved test evaluated; natural-document pool unchanged at26,112. Broad research goal active.

## Previous continuation: H889

## H889 — Number-axis effect survives norm controls, is selective for agreement, and concentrates at L12

The direct agreement effect from H888 is almost unchanged when total normalized-input norm is preserved exactly. It increases across the fixed quarter/half/full dose ladder, exceeds four locally matched random controls, and is much larger for agreement than for copying the same nouns. Layer12 is the largest single-layer contributor in every cohort/axis comparison. These results strengthen the candidate component while still falling short of a complete or uniquely necessary agreement circuit.

### Design and controls

Use all120 task/copy endpoints in the originally eligible H887 cells: irregular B/C and new-regular A/B. Apply both frozen task-trained axes to every context, including copying; no copying-specific direction is fitted. At each selected MLP final-token input, interpolate the coordinate toward the frozen opposite-number centroid by doses0.25,0.5,1.0.

Compare the raw coordinate change with an edit that simultaneously reaches the same target coordinate and preserves the original total input norm. The latter rescales the coordinate-orthogonal component to stay on the same sphere; it therefore is not a pure one-direction displacement. A radial-only control changes only overall norm to match the raw edit's norm. Four random controls per axis/layer move along random tangent directions with the same norm and chord distance as the number-directed spherical edit at that current state. Later trajectories need not match, because earlier edits alter subsequent inputs.

CoreL11–16 receives the dose/control panel. Each of its six layers and the L8–10/L17 complement also receives full-dose raw and sphere edits. All conditions were declared before this run's outcomes. Random controls use four draws, not an exhaustive null distribution. No refitting, task-label-based pair filtering, or axis selection occurs.

### Full-dose agreement and copying effects

Values are reductions in the appropriate native expected-answer logit margin. Agreement uses is versus are; copying uses the original source noun versus its singular/plural counterpart.

|Cohort|Axis|Agreement raw drop|Agreement norm-preserved drop|Norm-only drop|Copy norm-preserved drop|Random norm-preserved drop range|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
|irregular|A|2.385|2.391|-0.010|0.184|0.062–0.324|
|irregular|B|2.228|2.231|0.000|0.349|0.221–0.409|
|new_regular|A|2.771|2.774|-0.007|0.273|0.075–0.424|
|new_regular|B|2.749|2.751|-0.004|0.395|0.217–0.437|

Native agreement margins are4.783 irregular and5.339 regular. Full norm-preserved flips lower them by2.231–2.774, whereas matched copying margins fall by0.184–0.395 from native3.893/4.319. Copying effects are nonzero, so selectivity is relative rather than perfect. Agreement vocabulary KL is0.088–0.126 versus copying0.019–0.026 under the sphere edit. The norm-only control has negligible margin effect; norm inflation is not a sufficient explanation of the observed agreement change.

Across all cohort/axis comparisons, mean agreement margin drops increase monotonically with dose. At quarter dose they are0.461–0.777, at half dose1.361–1.796, and at full dose2.231–2.774. This is a mean dose response over fixed examples, not a guarantee of monotonicity for every individual example. Binary expected-answer accuracy remains100% in the reported full-dose conditions; the margin effect is substantial but does not establish decisive control of the final prediction.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

L12 has the largest marginal effect in each comparison, with drops1.126–2.038. These single-layer effects are not an additive partition of the joint effect: downstream responses and interactions differ under each intervention. L12 is selected for follow-up from this result, so a later test must distinguish exploratory localization from prospective validation. The two axes also differ materially in L12 effect size despite both decoding number well, another reason not to equate classification accuracy with a unique causal direction.

### Interpretation and next computation test

The evidence now combines unsupervised discovery, frozen semantic labeling, irregular-noun transfer, direct causal effects, norm controls, dose dependence and relative task selectivity. It supports investigating the number direction as part of a conditional computation. It still does not establish a universal manifold, a complete agreement circuit, or a stable ontology across training seeds/models.

Next analyze L12's bilinear computation along the frozen direction. Writing normalized input as orthogonal context plus a scalar coordinate gives an exact decomposition into context-only output, a coordinate-linear cross term, and a coordinate-squared term. Audit that decomposition against the actual MLP output and use separate causal interventions to test which term carries the native margin effect. This can distinguish a reusable number-dependent operation from an axis that merely perturbs many unrelated computations. Keep both frozen axes and transfer nouns; avoid picking channels based on the test outcome without a new validation split.

The copying lexical-coverage learning curve remains outstanding. Its prior fidelity failure is not explained by the current agreement-selectivity experiment and remains part of the broader representation question.
