The prior goal turn made progress by freezing H872's six context gains and defining a no-refit check. H873 then screened new countrypair combinations and continuation variants. H874 tests the frozen gains. ForL13H0/L14H4, gains transfer well to new pairs in familiarA/B formats, but become harmful in the competent newC format. This contradicts a format-independent copying-to-capital scalar-gain hypothesis. It does not invalidate the exact source-value/routing factorization at the reader.

### Frozen confirmation protocol

All12 new pair combinations of24 familiar countries, fourformats, twofamilies and192endpoints retained. H872 discoverygains and reader choices were frozen and hashed before new outcomes. Identity and predictednative source-midpoint head edits are independently audited against direct mixed-value edits. Positive/negative common-amplitude writes use the same country direction and amplitude in matched copy/capital contexts.

As inH872, orient responses to countryA→B and average both endpoints within each lexicalpair. Familiar-format results averageA/B; newC and diagnosticD are separate. The measured copying-context symmetric finite-amplitude response is the predictor input; multiply it by the frozen gain to predict the same country or capital output contrast's response in the capital context. This is conditional response transfer, not intervention-free prediction of native model behavior. Native routing is measured anew, not predicted by the gain model.

### Relative response RMSE, no refitting

Late-reader frozen gains achieve7.5–9.4% error on new pairs in oldformats, substantially below no-gain errors13.7–30.9%. In new competentC, their errors rise to27.1–29.8%, worse than no-gain errors10.8–22.1%. Allfour late-reader mappings show this failure, with saved pair-bootstrap intervals. For exampleL13H0 country-response RMSE rises from.076[.054,.098] inA/B to.276[.244,.303] inC. L8H3 remains less accurately captured overall, with27.5–39.5% frozen-gain errors across these cohorts.

CapitalD failed the predefined full-vocabulary competence gate inH873 and is retained only as a diagnostic. Its late-reader frozen-gain errors are19.6–22.4%, also worse than no gain, but this is not positive task-level generalization evidence. No individual failing cases were discarded and no replacement gains were fitted.

High response correlation does not rescue the failed amplitude prediction. For exampleL13H0 country pair correlation remainsabout.957 inC while frozen-gain RMSE is.276. A relationship can preserve lexical ordering yet have the wrong scale. Familiar-format averaging may also smooth variation; per-format mechanisms need investigation rather than treating the pooledA/B gain as a universal constant.

### Hypothesis refresh

|#|Hypothesis|Current evidence / next discrimination|
|---:|---|---|
|1|The source bus is a fixed token-local content map|Supported by static-value and same-token audits.|
|2|A reader's source-value edit factors into content × signed routing|Exact within floating-point tolerance for tested interventions.|
|3|Task effects can reverse through routing sign|Causally supported by H872 sign controls.|
|4|One late-reader context gain is format independent|Contradicted by competent newC.|
|5|Frozen gains generalize to new lexical pairings in familiar formats|Supported for late readers on these12combinations.|
|6|Final residual RMS explains much of format gain variation|Plausible, not tested; measure native norms next.|
|7|RMS tangential projection matters beyond a scalar norm ratio|Plausible; compare full normalization formula with norm-only model.|
|8|Final logit-cap saturation changes readout gain|Plausible; include the actual30tanh readout in analytic controls.|
|9|Later MLP responses cause the remaining format dependence|Plausible; isolate frozen-update versus live downstream effects.|
|10|Later attention/routing responses cause it|Plausible; separate from MLP changes after basic normalization test.|
|11|Finite edit amplitude rather than local sensitivity causes failures|Possible; use an amplitude sweep only if analytic controls leave ambiguity.|
|12|Head direction alone determines downstream behavior|Weakened by equal-write context dependence.|
|13|Earlier readers have more context-dependent responses because more layers remain|Consistent but confounded with head identity.|
|14|Source occurrence count explains cross-task effects|Affects routing magnitude, but not the whole fixed-write downstream gap.|

|16|Binary competence suffices for task interpretation|Rejected by failedbinding/capitalD full-vocabulary checks.|
|17|Many featurizer atoms imply a high-dimensional task computation|Weakened by within-union rank1 intervention results.|
|18|A scalar/vector feature can be globally labeled by one task|Weakened by shared readers and context-dependent sign.|
|19|An explicit shared operation can transfer more reliably than a reconstruction group|Promising, but unsupervised discovery and broad transfer remain unverified.|
|20|A data-based canonical description requires a context-dependent downstream metric|Strengthened; uniqueness/minimality and practical learned recovery remain open.|

### Next discriminating experiment

Keep the failed frozen-gain predictions unchanged. Measure native final residual states on the old and new contexts. First test the parameter-free RMS ratio as a candidate context gain. Then predict the finite head-write response through the residual skip path with later updates held fixed, using the actual final RMS normalization, unembedding andlogitcap. This analytic baseline separates output normalization/readout effects from changes induced in later computations. It is a counterfactual frozen-update model, not the actual model unless validated against live interventions.

If normalization accounts for the format shift, a conditional response metric may be a better representation target than fitted task gains. If not, localize later computation effects before adding model capacity. Do not silently fit format-specific gains and call that generalization. The overall goal still includes task-blind featurizer recovery, manifold verification and broader tasks; these controlled country experiments establish only a scoped mechanism.

## Previous continuation: H872

## H872 — Coefficient sign controls the L14H4 reversal; downstream context adds gain and residual variation

H871 showed a fixed country-bus contrast multiplied by a context-dependent signed coefficient. H872 interchanges those coefficients while holding recipient context, reader and source direction fixed. TheL14H4 copying/capital reversal follows coefficient sign. Equal-sized writes nevertheless have context-dependent downstream gain; late readers are more consistent across these contexts thanL8H3. This supports a reusable content-map-plus-routing description without claiming a context-independent whole-model computation.

### Intervention definition

All144 H870 endpoints and all3 frozen readers retained. Every arm adds gamma times the same donor–recipient country-bus contrast to the final-query head output. Arms use nativegamma, the other task's gamma for the same countrypair/format/endpoint, foreignsign withnative magnitude, foreignmagnitude withnative sign, and native signflip. Identity controls remain. Failedbinding rows are retained as diagnostics and use copying as their foreign-context source; conclusions below concern competent copying/capital.

These are counterfactual head-write perturbations. They interchange coefficients of the midpoint-contrast perturbation; they do not replace the entire native attention pattern or guarantee naturally realizable query/key states. The native head activation and all other model state remain in place before the added perturbation. No scale is fitted for these causal arms.

### Sign and magnitude controls

Entries are native paired answer-gap fractions removed. Negative values mean the intervention increases the intended distinction. Values above100% mean reversal of the aggregate distinction, not a probability or more-than-total mediation.

|Recipient task|Reader|Native coefficient|Foreign coefficient|Foreign sign only|Foreign magnitude only|Native sign flipped|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|copy|L13H0|54.1%|119.6%|54.1%|119.6%|-49.4%|
|copy|L14H4|-46.5%|30.2%|31.0%|-34.8%|47.7%|
|copy|L8H3|26.7%|4.3%|26.7%|4.3%|-20.2%|
|capital|L13H0|49.8%|23.0%|49.8%|23.0%|-43.7%|
|capital|L14H4|8.7%|-11.9%|-9.6%|8.8%|-8.3%|
|capital|L8H3|1.5%|10.0%|1.5%|10.0%|-1.5%|

AtL14H4 in copying contexts, the native-coefficient perturbation increases the copying distinction46.5%; using capital coefficients instead removes30.2%. Foreignsign alone removes31.0%, while foreignmagnitude withnative sign still increases the distinction34.8%. In capital contexts, the native perturbation removes8.7%, but copying coefficients increase the distinction11.9%; foreignsign alone gives the same direction of reversal. Thus sign, not amplitude alone, is a decisive cause under these fixed-recipient interventions.

L13H0 andL8H3 have matching native coefficient signs across copying/capital, so their foreignsign arms reproduce native effects. Their foreign-coefficient changes follow magnitude: for exampleL13H0 capital coefficients applied to copying remove119.6% of its aggregate gap, whileL8H3's smaller capital coefficients reduce its copying effect from26.7% to4.3%. The former is a strong counterfactual perturbation, not evidence that natural copying routes all its computation through that reader.

### Same-write response across contexts

For each pair/format/endpoint/reader, define a shared amplitude sqrt(abs(gamma_copy × gamma_capital)). Apply both positive and negative versions in both recipient contexts. The source direction and amplitude then match across tasks to floating-point precision. Measure symmetric finite-amplitude responses for the same output contrast in both contexts: countryidentity or capitalassociation. These are not infinitesimal derivatives.

Raw correlations across both endpoint orientations can be inflated by a shared sign flip. Therefore orient every response to the same countryA→B contrast and average formats/orientations within each of12 lexicalpairs before correlating. Fit a single through-origin gain on8 discoverypairs and evaluate it on4 transferpairs. No gain was used in the causal interchange arms above.

|Reader|Output contrast|Canonical pair correlation|Discovery gain, capital context / copy context|Transfer relativeRMSE, gain1|Transfer relativeRMSE, frozen gain|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|L13H0|country|0.971|0.837|0.246|0.075|
|L13H0|capital|0.973|0.897|0.216|0.114|
|L14H4|country|0.780|0.852|0.226|0.085|
|L14H4|capital|0.880|0.797|0.366|0.126|
|L8H3|country|0.696|0.963|0.282|0.250|
|L8H3|capital|0.776|0.930|0.323|0.308|

ForL13H0/L14H4, one discovery-fit gain reduces transfer error to about7.5–12.6%, versus21.6–36.6% without gain adjustment. L8H3 retains25–31% error after gain adjustment. This is consistent with more downstream context sensitivity for the earlier reader, but depth is not experimentally isolated here: reader identity and computation differ too. Twelve lexicalpairs and four transferpairs are insufficient to establish a universal law.

### Updated interpretation and next step

The supported candidate computational unit is a static content direction, selected/scaled with a signed contextual coefficient, followed by a reader write and context-dependent downstream response. The observed sign reversal is causal under the coefficient controls. The downstream response is reusable approximately, not exactly, and cannot be replaced by an unqualified fixed linear map.

This matters for featurizers: a stable dictionary direction alone omits the computation that selects, signs and scales it. Conversely, representing the operation does not require treating the full activation cloud as an intrinsically high-dimensional semantic manifold. It remains unproven that a learned shared dictionary/group/DAG model can discover this relation task-blind, or that a common fit transfers beyond these country examples.

Freeze the content/routing definition and discovery gains. Next evaluate new country-pair combinations and continuation variants without refitting, with a competence/alignment screen reported independently of intervention results. Compare raw native-gamma prediction, frozen-gain response prediction and matched-operation controls. Failures should distinguish lexical-map dependence, routing changes and downstream context dependence. Do not train or name another semantic manifold solely because this adaptive panel fits a compact description. The broader diverse-task and unsupervised-recovery requirements remain open.

## Previous continuation: H871

## H871 — Matched country directions reveal shared reader use and context-dependent sign reversal

H868–870 established a matched-country panel competent for copying and capital retrieval, while country-as-agent binding failed full-vocabulary competence. H871 now performs frozen-reader source-value interventions on every eligible endpoint. L13H0 contributes strongly to both copying and capital retrieval. L14H4's contribution supports capital retrieval but opposes the copying margin, accompanied by a context-dependent change in effective signed routing. This is stronger evidence for reusable content maps with contextual coefficients than for a fixed task-specific head label.

### Exact intervention and algebra

Retain all12 country pairs, twoformats, threefamilies and144 endpoints at frozenL13H0,L14H4,L8H3. Native local values and query/key computations are unchanged at the selected reader. Add half the donor-minus-recipient static bus difference, multiplied by that reader's value-mixing coefficient lambda, only at the changed source positions in its mixed-value tensor. The persistent bus itself remains native, so other readers do not receive edited bus inputs.

Apply the edit at either every query position or only the final query. Independently predict the final-query head perturbation by

    delta_head = gamma(context) × [B(donor token) − B(recipient token)]
    gamma(context) = lambda / 2 × sum(native signed routing at changed source positions).

B is the fixed layer0 token-value map for that head index. Copying has two changed source occurrences, capital one. Within each context their bus contrasts are exactly identical, so summing routing coefficients is exact. The effective coefficient gamma is signed and is not a probability. Its sign includes lambda as well as the signed attention pattern. No signs, scales or directions are fitted to task outcomes.

### Results

Values are native paired answer-margin fractions removed. Negative values mean that midpoint-erasing the source-value contrast increases the intended behavioral distinction. These are not accuracy losses or unique mediation fractions. Diplomatic binding rows are retained only as failed-task diagnostics.

|Task|Reader|Final-query gap removed|All-query gap removed|Mean signed gamma|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
|copy|L13H0|54.1%|55.6%|-0.612|
|copy|L14H4|-46.5%|-47.4%|0.389|
|copy|L8H3|26.7%|26.8%|-0.419|
|capital|L13H0|49.8%|50.1%|-1.282|
|capital|L14H4|8.7%|8.7%|-0.256|
|capital|L8H3|1.5%|1.6%|-0.075|
|binding|L13H0|13.7%|13.5%|0.328|
|binding|L14H4|57.5%|57.7%|1.035|
|binding|L8H3|1.6%|1.6%|0.058|

For competent copying, L13H0 removes54.1% of the pair gap at the final query, compared with49.8% for capital retrieval. Its effects remain positive on transfer rows,55.1% and47.5%, respectively. The earlier apparent capital specialization is therefore not a general property of that reader independent of vocabulary and prompt format. This experiment does not separately identify how much of the change from the earlier panel is lexical versus format-driven.

L14H4 removes8.7% of the capital gap, but its erasure increases copying's gap by46.5%. The pointwise lexical-cluster intervals are[4.7%,13.3%] and[-60.4%,-36.8%]. The negative copying effect appears in both discovery and transfer subsets. All48 copying endpoint coefficients are positive, whereas39/48 capital coefficients are negative. For a fixed country pair at this reader, the source-value contrast is the same; contextual coefficients can reverse the direction of the head perturbation. This is consistent with the observed effect reversal, but downstream state can still modulate the effect of a head vector.

L8H3 is more copy-weighted on this panel:26.7% versus1.5% capital gap removal. Final-query and all-query edits give similar aggregate effects for these frozen targets, suggesting that much of their measured source-value influence is expressed at the final query here. This is not a general claim that nonfinal reads are irrelevant.

The country and associated-capital output contrasts are both recorded in every context. AtL13H0, final-query erasure reduces country/capital paired gaps by3.13/3.09 raw logit units in copying contexts and5.83/5.80 in capital contexts. These coupled changes support a shared lexical/association readout hypothesis, but do not identify where the association was learned or prove identical downstream computation. Cross-output raw gaps are not normalized when their native denominators could be small.

### What this adds, and what remains open

H739 already demonstrated a static bus map and cross-context substitutions. H871 adds frozen-reader tests on matched country-token contrasts in independently screened competent copying and capital continuations, including theL14H4 sign reversal and a final-query/all-query comparison. It does not discover the signed-attention architecture anew.

The current best description is a fixed content direction multiplied by a context-dependent signed coefficient, followed by a reader-specific write map and downstream computation. That is a computational relation, not merely a cluster of activation vectors. It motivates testing explicit shared computations in addition to dictionary geometry. Signed scalar/block encoders can already express negative coordinates; this result does not show that they are incapable of representing the states. The missing test is whether a learned representation exposes the reusable relation reliably without task-supervised selection.

Next freeze same-pair source directions and interchange only effective routing coefficients between copying and capital contexts. Compare native coefficient, matched foreign-context coefficient, sign-flip and magnitude-matched controls at the same reader and same recipient state. This will test how much behavioral variation follows the coefficient rather than downstream context. Interpret such interventions as counterfactual head-write operations, not necessarily natural attainable attention patterns. Retain both formats/splits, failed-binding controls and prior native task competence, without selecting favorable pairs. New combinations are still needed for stronger generalization.

## H867 — Shared value storage is consumed by task-dependent readers, with partial reuse

H866 localized five-task dependence across persistent bus slices. H867 now tests every downstream reader layer2–17 and every head index0–8,144 reader locations, plus native and global controls. Capital retrieval is concentrated atL13H0, binding atL14H4, and copying atL8H3. Several readers also contribute to other tasks, so the emerging organization is shared token storage with task-dependent routing/readout and partial reader reuse, not one universal semantic block.

### Intervention and scope

Resume from the boundary after block1 with native residual sequence and embedding anchor. At the selected reader layer only, supply the pair-midpoint value-bus slice, removing the native pair contrast in that128-dimensional slice. Other bus slices stay native. Supply the original native bus at every other layer, while propagating the selected reader's residual effects normally. Thus this isolates direct access to that slice at a particular reader without suppressing downstream consequences through residual/local-value/routing changes.

All76 aligned H843 pairs and all5 task families are retained. Include native replay, complete-bus midpoint and all9 globally erased slices to reproduce H866 controls. Rankings below are exploratory; every reader, including small and negative effects, remains in the saved results.

### What is shared?

L14H4 contributes37.1 percentage points to binding,6.8 to capital retrieval and5.2 to copying. L13H0 contributes48.4 to capital retrieval,9.2 to binding and4.0 to copying. These are candidates for shared reader operations, but effect overlap alone does not show that the same directions or transformation serve every task. Different task vocabularies, source positions, query patterns and output groups remain confounded in the current panel.

H866's bus slice4 copying effect is spread across readers: L8H4, L10H4 and L14H4 all contribute. It is not solely the binding-dominant L14H4 operation. Conversely, capital slice0's global47.9-point effect is largely localized atL13H0's48.4-point marginal effect; slight overshoot is allowed because effects are conditional and downstream computation is nonlinear.

Summed reader-local effects approximately track global single-slice effects for several prominent slices: binding slice4 sums42.0 points versus42.1 globally; sentiment slice1 sums15.7 versus15.8. Capital slice0 sums46.8 versus47.9 and copying slice3 sums24.4 versus26.0. These are empirical comparisons, not proof of additivity or an exhaustive interaction decomposition.

### Prior evidence and split check

L13H0's role agrees with H739's static token-bus map and content substitution results. H778's L5H5 copying decomposition included mixed local values and routing, whereas this experiment isolates persistent bus inputs. These are different interventions; a small L5H5 bus-only effect does not contradict the earlier full-head result.

Selecting the strongest reader from discovery rows givesL8H8 agreement,L13H0 capital,L14H4 binding,L8H1 sentiment,L8H3 copying. Their transfer-row effects are1.2%,37.6%,39.1%,10.3%,24.2%, respectively. The transfer rows were withheld from this ranking, but have been reused throughout research; this is not a fresh confirmation. Bootstrap intervals are descriptive and uncorrected across many correlated tests.

### Research decision and next experiment

Before training another featurizer or declaring a shared computational DAG, separate lexical content from task/query role. FreezeL13H0,L14H4,L8H3 as prospective reader targets. Build a common-source-vocabulary panel crossing copying, binding and associated capital retrieval, with new combinations and task-appropriate answer groups. Keep the same source token contrasts and aligned source positions where possible; vary the query/role. Screen native competence and token alignment before interpreting interventions, retaining exclusions transparently.

At these readers, decompose native source-value contribution versus context-dependent routing using the existing signed-attention machinery. Test whether fixed content directions transfer across task/query combinations while routing controls their use. Include unchanged-source/query controls and held-out lexical combinations. This can distinguish shared storage consumed differently from a reusable reader computation; geometry or head-index sharing alone cannot.

The five-task map guides where a future featurizer belongs. It does not itself validate manifolds, unsupervised task labels, hierarchical gates or reusable computational DAG nodes. Those remain open requirements in the broader research goal.

## H866 — Value-bus slice profiles differ across tasks, with partial cross-task reuse

The previous turn made progress through H864–865: local relay erasure preserved most decisions, while whole-value-bus erasure strongly reduced binding/capital/copy discrimination. H866 localizes those effects across all nine128-dimensional bus slices, retaining all five tasks and every slice. Capital retrieval concentrates most strongly in slice0, binding in slice4, and copying in slices3–4. This is a useful map for subsequent feature/reader tests, not a semantic feature ontology.

### Reconciliation with earlier evidence

H739 already established a token-local static bus map for an L13H0 reader and tested content substitutions across capital/binding/copy contexts. H778 decomposed an L5H5 reader's head edit into routing, mixed-value and interaction terms. H866 does not rediscover those mechanisms. It measures native contrast dependence on all head-index bus slices across the newer common five-task panel.

A bus slice is reused by that head index in multiple downstream layers. Erasing slice0 is not equivalent to ablating L13H0 alone. Likewise, earlier L5H5 copying evidence involved mixed local/bus values and routing; it does not require global bus slice5 to dominate copying. Context-dependent readers, local values and persistent token storage must remain distinct.

### Shared storage and nonadditivity

Slice4 contributes42.1 points to binding,20.7 to copying and15.7 to capital retrieval when erased alone. That makes it a candidate for cross-task content reuse; it does not show that the same directions or computation inside the slice serve all three tasks. Different lexical items, readout maps and routing could explain the apparent sharing. A head-index block is an architectural partition, not a discovered manifold.

Binding's single-slice losses sum to96.3 points compared with97.0 for full-bus erasure; conditional effects are similar. Capital single losses sum to77.9 versus90.5 jointly, and copying76.8 versus84.9. Retaining slice0 in an otherwise erased bus restores56.9 points for capital versus47.9 lost when erasing it alone. Copy slice3 similarly restores31.4 versus26.0 lost alone. These observations show context-dependent, nonadditive effects under midpoint interventions; they do not determine a unique redundancy or synergy allocation.

Agreement's entire bus effect is only4.3 points, so slice8's3.9-point effect concerns a small route contribution. Sentiment has a stronger slice1 contribution15.8 points but remains dependent on residual and combined routes, as H865 showed. No representation should be judged against all tasks at this site alone.

Choosing the largest single-slice effect using only discovery rows selects8/0/4/1/4 for agreement/capital/binding/sentiment/copy. Their transfer-row effects are3.4/38.5/43.8/15.5/14.4 points. The copying winner changes when considering the full panel: slice3 has the larger aggregate effect. All split/slice outcomes are saved. This is a held-out-from-ranking diagnostic on extensively reused research data, not fresh confirmation; shared lexical/template structure limits independence.

Next distinguish shared storage from shared computation by restricting the established bus intervention to specific downstream reader layers. Start with all readers for the same frozen slices, without selecting a layer from these new outcomes. Compare isolated reader erasure with global persistent-slice erasure, audit bus restoration for later readers, and use the existing static-map/routing analyses as controls. A shared slice used by task-specific readers supports a different ontology from one shared reader operation. Then test cross-task/lexical combinations before training or labeling another manifold model.

## Previous continuation: H865

## H865 — Diverse-task contrast erasure distinguishes value-bus dependence from residual/route interactions

H864 found that a single layer4 relay coordinate contributes to agreement/sentiment but is not required for most correct answers. H865 broadens the necessity diagnostic to all five competent task families at the previously verified early boundary. Binding, capital retrieval and copying strongly depend on value-bus contrasts under this intervention; agreement and sentiment show more distributed route dependence and interaction.

### Design and metric

Use all76 aligned H843 task pairs and both recipient contexts at the boundary after block1. Keep three persistent state components separate: residual sequence R, layer0 value bus V, and normalized embedding anchor E. For each of all8 subsets, replace the selected components with the elementwise pair midpoint in both contexts; retain native unselected components. Run blocks2–17 and the output head. No featurizer or supervised direction is fit. This is a controlled contrast-erasure factorial on a reused panel, not a new discovery of the persistent value route already studied in H844 and earlier work.

Primary outcome is the fraction of the native paired answer-margin distinction removed. Both examples use identical answer groups. This avoids an easy denominator error: the runner's inherited per-recipient gap_fraction summary is half the paired contrast removal. Use the explicitly paired analysis below. It is not a unique natural mediation fraction; erasure can create off-manifold states, and route interactions make additive causal attribution inappropriate.

### Results

|Task|R erased|V erased|E erased|R+V erased|Binary accuracy, native → V erased|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|agreement|32.7%|4.3%|6.2%|65.8%|100.0% → 100.0%|
|capital_recall|0.5%|90.5%|1.8%|92.7%|96.2% → 76.9%|
|entity_binding|1.2%|97.0%|-0.1%|99.4%|100.0% → 59.4%|
|sentiment|28.6%|25.1%|4.3%|83.3%|100.0% → 100.0%|
|sequence_copy|9.3%|84.9%|3.4%|93.1%|100.0% → 68.8%|

Equalizing V removes97.0% of binding,90.5% of capital-retrieval and84.9% of copying distinctions. Corresponding binary accuracies fall to59.4%,76.9%,68.8%. Native capital accuracy is96.2%, not100%; the existing task family passed its competence gate without every pair being correct. Margin loss and accuracy need not track proportionally because residual margins and biases can preserve the answer after a large reduction.

Agreement behaves differently: R erasure removes32.7% of the native distinction, V4.3%, but jointR+V65.8%. Sentiment loses28.6% underR,25.1% underV, and83.3% jointly. These combined effects exceed the sum of separate losses and support route interaction or compensating information under the chosen intervention. They do not establish a unique redundancy decomposition. E also interacts: agreementR+E loses60.4% despite separate losses32.7% and6.2%.

Equalizing allR,V,E makes paired suffix logits exactly identical, removes100% of every task's paired distinction, and yields50% binary accuracy. This is a completeness check on the captured suffix state, not an independent discovery about model representation. Native replay and identical-answer-group checks pass.

### Implication for the manifold program

A useful representation must be evaluated where a computation actually depends on it. Residual featurizers at the layer4 relay remain useful diagnostics for agreement/sentiment, but their successes or failures cannot settle feature organization for binding/copying/capital retrieval. The bus provides a stronger causal target for those tasks.

The layer0 value bus is token-local storage. Strong dependence on it does not mean it contains an already-contextualized binding relation. Downstream attention readers combine stored values with context-dependent routing. Any manifold/feature interpretation must distinguish lexical content directions from reader selection and transformation. Prior reader/bus studies already establish parts of this mechanism; reconcile new tests with them instead of claiming rediscovery.

Next localize contrast dependence within the9 value-head slices, keeping allheads and allfive tasks, before committing to another large featurizer fit. Compare single-slice midpoint erasure with complete-bus erasure, preserve native residual/anchor, and report nonadditivity and per-task correctness. Then relate shared or task-specific slices to existing reader interventions and test held-out lexical/query combinations. A token-identity code or a head partition alone is not a semantic manifold or reusable computational DAG.

## Previous continuation: H864

## H864 — Task information at the relay is causally relevant but not required for most correct answers

H863 showed that a single supervised direction approximates most of each learned union's intervention effect. H864 tests the more demanding question of local necessity. Removing that direction's native pairwise contrast reduces answer-margin distinctions, but generally leaves the selected answer intact. Even erasing the full raw-state contrast at this one position does not remove most native behavioral discrimination.

### Protocol

Retain all20 nominal64-slot unions, five architectures and both seeds/discovery axes. For recipient state b0 and donor b1, add one-half of the projected difference. Apply the reciprocal edit to b1. Both contexts then have the same coordinate in the targeted span, while preserving their native complementary coordinates and all other model state. Test union, within-union rank1, and orthogonal complement. Include original supervised task axes, two fixed Gaussian rank1 controls, and the full raw-state midpoint. All156 recipient contexts, both agreement and sentiment, remain included.

The paired behavioral distinction is margin(context0) minus margin(context1), with the same answer groups. Gap fraction removed is the reduction in the sum of these paired distinctions divided by the native sum. This is distinct from the earlier donor-transfer slope and cannot be equated with a mediation fraction. Midpoints may be outside the native data manifold; local erasure is not global model ablation.

### Main results

Values separated by slashes are seeds8351/8352. Native binary answer-group accuracy is100% for both tasks. Full-vocabulary correctness is a different metric: native sentiment top-group accuracy is76.7%, agreement100%.

The scalar/block rank1 directions remove about5.6–6.1% of the native agreement distinction and12.7–17.1% of sentiment distinction. The complete raw relay midpoint removes9.4% and25.0%, respectively. Agreement remains100% correct even after full relay erasure; sentiment drops to96.7% binary accuracy, compared with98.3% for most scalar/block rank1 erasures. Thus these are partial task-carrying coordinates, not established necessary concept units.

For scalar/block unions, rank1 erasure closely approximates full-union erasure. Complement-only erasures have negligible net task-gap effects. Gaussian direction controls also have nearzero effects. Full-vocabulary sentiment top-group accuracy falls from76.7% to61.7% under full relay midpoint, and to63.3% under the supervised sentiment axis midpoint. Answer-group decisions therefore conceal some distributional changes; raw logits, margins, top-group decisions and native-to-erasedKL are all retained.

### Interpretation and next action

The useful signal is low-dimensional relative to the selected union, but the model's task performance remains supported by other state. This may reflect redundant routes, information at other positions, or causal contribution that is too small to flip robust margins; this experiment does not distinguish those explanations. Earlier donor swaps demonstrated transferability, not necessity, and H864 makes that distinction explicit.

To avoid extending conclusions from two tasks at one site, next apply controlled route-contrast erasure at the already verified early boundary across all five competent task families. Separate residual sequence, persistent value bus, and embedding anchor, including combined erasures. Binding, copying and capital retrieval have strong prior value-bus transfer evidence; the new question is whether erasing their bus contrast diminishes native discrimination, and whether other routes compensate.

## H863 — Does a component union require multiple computational directions?

H862 completed causal tests of nested feature unions, changing the next question: many dictionary atoms may be required because the dictionary is misaligned with a simple task signal, not because the model's computation is intrinsically high-dimensional. H863 splits every frozen ranked union into a task-aligned rank1 direction and its orthogonal complement, and evaluates both causally. The prior goal turn therefore made concrete progress; the broad research goal remains active.

### Exact experiment

All60 ranked unions from H862 are retained: five architectures, two seeds, two discovery-task axes, and nominal8/32/64 atom-slot budgets. Let Q be an orthonormal basis for a union and a the discovery task axis. Define v=QQᵀa/||QQᵀa||. For each native donor–recipient contrast δ, the full edit is QQᵀδ, the rank1 edit is v(vᵀδ), and the complement is their difference. These edits sum exactly in activation space, but their downstream effects need not add.

Patch each edit into the recipient's raw preMLP4 state, retaining the rest of the state and model computation. Test both agreement and sentiment, all156 recipient contexts from78 aligned H849 pairs. Also rescale the rank1 edit to the full union edit norm as a pairwise oracle amplitude control. No new basis fitting, encoder training, seed selection, or downstream outcome selection occurs. These directions remain discovery-task-supervised; this is not unsupervised feature recovery.

### Main finding and research decision

At nominal64 slots, the within-union rank1 direction reproduces92.4–98.7% of the union effect scale in19/20 own-task fit comparisons. The remaining learned-shared seed2 sentiment case reaches85.1%, with relative effectRMSE0.294 and a wide lexical-pair interval. The other19 relativeRMSEs range0.064–0.146. Agreement complements have isolated slopes between-.0073 and.0017; sentiment complements range.0089–.0849. InteractionRMSE remains0.052–0.117, so neither a perfectly linear sum of causal effects nor exact one-dimensional sufficiency is established.

Mean KL(union||rank1) ranges0.000128–0.000936 nats at64 slots. These distributions are close on this panel, but the comparison is to the union intervention, not to the unmodified model or full donor swap. The rank1 edit already retains about85–92% of the union edit norm on average, consistent with concentrated task contrasts. Rescaling it to full union norm worsens answer-effectRMSE in19/20 comparisons; the unscaled coordinate is generally more faithful than indiscriminate magnitude restoration here. This does not contradict H859's average benefits for full natural reconstruction: the operations, references and data differ.

The most likely interpretation is that these unions represent a simple task signal in an inconvenient dictionary basis. The result weakens the claim that needing many learned atoms is evidence for an intrinsically multidimensional computational manifold. It remains compatible with off-axis contextual modulation and with richer computation on other tasks. Because the axis and union were selected with discovery-task supervision, the experiment is a diagnostic upper bound on representation organization, not an unsupervised solution. Conditional concentration was plausible from discovery geometry; the additional evidence here is that it survives causal intervention and distributional comparison on the reused lexical/format/gap panel.

### Next step: necessity, then other computation sites

Stop treating further compression as the end goal. Freeze these rank1 directions and test whether removing their donor–recipient coordinate difference diminishes the native behavioral distinction. Use pair-midpoint coordinate erasure, full-union erasure and complementary-coordinate erasure, retaining native state elsewhere and evaluating both recipients. This tests local necessity of the contrast coordinate, rather than only its ability to transfer a signal. It must not be described as global model necessity because redundant routes and other sites remain intact.

Then extend the same behavioral verification to the already identified binding/copy/capital value-bus sites. Agreement and sentiment at one residual relay are insufficient to choose a general feature ontology. The user's broader manifold, reusable-computation, held-out-combination and diverse-task requirements remain open.


### What this test can and cannot establish

If a rank1 direction approximates a union, the union's useful task signal can be concentrated in a rotated coordinate. That weakens the inference that a large learned group collection establishes an intrinsically multidimensional computational manifold. It does not show the full original relay state is one-dimensional, that arbitrary language behavior is captured, or that the learned encoder discovers the useful coordinate without supervision. H862's full unions already retained only part of the full native relay effect.

Nonzero complement effects or interactions leave room for contextual modulation and additional computational directions. Even close answer-effect agreement is not identical to whole-distribution fidelity; KL(union||rank1) is saved explicitly. Rank1 rescaling uses donor-pair information and changes the edit, so any improvement from it cannot be attributed to an independent single-input featurizer.

## H862 — Nested component unions: distributed representation versus dictionary fragmentation

The previous goal turn made progress by testing individual components causally in H861. H862 now tests whether unions improve transfer, while separating decoder geometry, native encoding, and edit magnitude. All five architectures and both seeds remain included.

### Protocol

Rank groups by overlap with each H848 discovery-supervised task axis. Freeze nested prefixes at nominal8/32/64 atom slots. Signed scalar dictionaries select8/32/64 atoms; block/shared dictionaries select1/4/8 groups of8. Use one random nested group ordering per fit/task as a control. Evaluate every candidate on both agreement and sentiment, all78 H849 pairs and both recipient directions. Selection does not use downstream outcomes, but it is task supervised and the panel is reused research data.

Projection transfers the native donor–recipient difference projected onto the combined decoder span. Encoded transfer uses the selected active coordinates decoded once per atom, scaled by each input's native raw RMS. For overlapping groups, an atom is included if at least one selected group is active; multiplicity never amplifies it. The rest of the recipient state stays native. A third control rescales the random projection to the ranked projection's edit norm for the same pair. This norm control is a pairwise oracle, not an implementable single-input featurizer. The original discovery rank1 task axis is a supervised reference.

### Geometry and interpretation limits

At nominal64 slots, scalar and block spans have rank64. Fixed-shared spans have ranks57–59; learned-shared spans42–47. Random unions are matched in group count, not necessarily actual rank for overlapping architectures. These are not strict equal-capacity architecture comparisons.

Rank64 scalar/block unions contain about56.6–68.7% of the discovery task-axis energy. Fixed-shared unions contain51.7–58.6%; learned-shared unions32.2–40.3%. Cross-seed union overlap remains limited: about0.22–0.32 for scalar/block,0.30–0.36 fixed-shared, and0.46–0.47 learned-shared, measured by twice projector intersection trace divided by total rank. Higher learned-shared overlap does not imply higher causal fidelity: its dictionaries cover fewer directions and its gates remain problematic.

A crucial distinction: needing many learned atoms does not prove the model's computation is intrinsically high-dimensional. A single task direction can be fragmented across a dictionary whose axes are poorly aligned with it. The rank1 supervised reference makes that alternative explicit. Likewise, successful projection with weak encoded transfer points to inference/routing losses, not absence of representable signal. Even the chosen top-overlap unions are a heuristic, not an optimal subset search.

## H861 — A reproducible sentiment atom is a selective partial contributor; block contributions vary across seeds

The previous turn made progress by completing H860's cross-seed stability experiment. H861 now intervenes on components in all five architectures and both seeds. The scalar48 sentiment atom identified by discovery-axis overlap and geometric matching transfers a small but selective sentiment signal in both seeds. Larger effects occur in some eight-dimensional blocks, but geometric matches do not reliably preserve their causal role. This supports partial contributors and possibly distributed computational subspaces, not a complete one-feature-per-concept ontology.

### Experiment

Freeze each seed's group with maximal overlap with each H848 discovery-supervised task axis. Also retain the seed2 geometric match of each seed1 selection. Add two randomly sampled nonselected groups per fit, matched in dimension. This yields50 labeled candidates, some deliberately duplicated when own and matched selection coincide; duplicated candidates are not independent evidence. Selection is saved before downstream outcomes. Evaluate all78 H849 aligned lexical/format/gap pairs in both directions,156 recipient contexts. Both agreement and sentiment are evaluated for every candidate.

Two interventions separate available geometry from encoder usage:

- Projection transfers the part of the native raw donor–recipient difference lying in the component's decoder subspace. It bypasses the encoder and tests geometric capacity.
- Encoded transfer adds the difference between donor and recipient decoded component vectors, scaled by each native state's raw RMS. The rest of the recipient state remains intact. Shared-group vectors require the group's own gate and use its union-coded member coordinates. Because groups overlap, these edits are not additive attributions of independently removable groups.

No gain tuning or norm calibration is applied. The encoded component map is not H857's globally renormalized full reconstruction. Random groups are dimension matched, not edit-norm matched; edit magnitudes are recorded. The natural-featurizer training was task blind, but component selection here is explicitly supervised.

Block8 seed2's own agreement-selected block reaches projection/encoded slopes0.404/0.325, while seed1's own block reaches0.063/0.013. Learned shared-group agreement candidates have exactly zero encoded transfer despite nonzero projection effects. Some groups contain relevant directions but their native gates/coordinates do not transmit the signal on these examples. This is consistent with previous unstable routing and coverage collapse. It does not establish that overlapping groups cannot work with different training.

### Updated hypotheses and discriminating next experiment

Evidence now favors three live explanations: task signals are distributed across several components; some individual partial contributors are reproducible; and gating/coefficient inference loses usable signal present in decoder spans. Finite optimization and seed-dependent allocation remain alternatives. Geometric alignment by itself is insufficient to assign a stable computational identity.

Next freeze a nested ordering of groups by discovery-axis overlap and test unions at increasing total dimension, retaining both seeds. Compare native encoded sums/unions with projection onto the combined decoder span and the existing supervised rank1 axis. Shared atoms must be included once. Include random unions at matched dimension and norm-matched edits where feasible. If small unions recover the effect consistently while individual identities differ, that favors a distributed subspace description. If projection succeeds but native encoding fails, prioritize inference/routing rather than semantic labeling. After sufficient coverage, test necessity by removal and extend across binding/copy/capital at their verified active sites. The user's diverse-task requirement remains outstanding beyond agreement/sentiment at this relay site.

## Previous continuation: H860

## H860 — Reproducible orientation does not establish reproducible feature groups

The prior goal turn made progress: H859 completed a frozen512-document output-fidelity confirmation. This experiment moves from fidelity to the user's manifold-verification requirement. Existing layer4 featurizers show above-random geometric agreement across two seeds, but weak individual group stability. Learned overlapping-group activities are particularly unstable. No architecture earns a semantic-manifold label from these results.

### Protocol and definitions

Use all ten frozen H852 fits, no retraining or task-based selection. A scalar feature is a one-dimensional decoder subspace; blocks and shared groups have eight dimensions. Projector overlap is the sum of squared cosines of principal angles divided by group rank: one means the same subspace, zero means orthogonal. It is invariant to signs and coordinate rotations inside a group. Compute a one-to-one assignment across seeds maximizing total overlap, using dictionaries alone.

Then evaluate the matched groups on all512 H859 natural states. Activity means the magnitude of the decoded vector from that group's active coordinates. Shared groups additionally require their own gate to be active; their overlapping activities do not sum to the reconstruction and are not independent causal attributions. These are native encoder activities, before optional norm calibration.

Eight signed ambient-coordinate permutations of the second dictionary preserve all its internal geometry while breaking alignment with the first. Reoptimizing the matching gives mean overlap only0.0085–0.0101 and median activity correlations aroundzero. Thus trained fits share preferred ambient directions, but most matched groups are far from identical. The fraction of groups with overlap greater than0.5 is8.8% for scalar48,5.7% for scalar64,1.6% for block8, and0% for both shared architectures. These thresholds are descriptive, not prevalidated manifold criteria.

A posthoc diagnostic centers each matched activity within token identity. There are197 occurrences in40 repeated-token types;315 singleton tokens contribute zero after centering. Scalar/block correlations remain modestly positive; learned-shared correlation is-.0055. With256 permutations of occurrences within each token type, learned-shared lies inside the central95% null range[-.0280,-.0054], whereas the other architecture medians exceed their corresponding ranges. These are descriptive conditional permutation diagnostics, not uncertainty over training seeds, corrected hypothesis tests, or proof of semantics.

### Relation to known causal directions

Postfit inspection against the discovery-supervised agreement and sentiment axes checks whether the same named behavior is concentrated in a matched component. It usually is not. For block8, the seed1 group with most agreement-axis energy has16.9%, but its geometric match in seed2 has3.8%; for sentiment the corresponding figures are27.0% and1.1%. The axes may be distributed across several differently organized groups.

One exploratory candidate is scalar48's sentiment-associated atom: seed1 atom15 matches seed2 atom126, contains11.4% versus24.0% of the sentiment-axis energy, and has activity correlation0.689. This is not a recovered sentiment feature: selection used a supervised axis, the energy fraction is incomplete, and specificity is untested. Fixed-shared agreement also shows similar axis energies across a matched pair, but only0.170 activity correlation. All candidate results are retained, not just favorable examples.

### What to test next

The leading possibilities are (1) scalar/block dictionaries recover a distributed computational subspace whose partition into groups is nonunique, (2) some genuinely reproducible components coexist with many interchangeable reconstruction directions, and (3) learned shared gates fail to converge to stable partitions, consistent with their earlier membership-coverage collapse. Two seeds and finite training do not distinguish these fully. Above-null orientation can also reflect common covariance rather than reusable computation.

Next use the task-axis-selected scalar48 sentiment pair as an explicitly supervised diagnostic candidate, alongside both tasks' top-axis components and matched random controls. Remove or transfer each component while retaining the reconstruction residual, compare effects across agreement/sentiment and token/distance variants, and keep both seeds. Freeze selection on discovery axes before evaluating effects. Quantify a component's fraction of the full relay effect and off-target changes. If individual components fail but matched unions succeed, test the distributed-subspace hypothesis rather than forcing semantic group names. Binding/copy/capital require their previously verified active sites; do not use absence of early-layer effects as negative evidence about those tasks.

## Previous continuation: H859

## H859 — Frozen norm calibration confirms average output fidelity gains, with individual and token-coverage limits

The fixed single-input calibration lowers mean next-token KL in all20 model/coefficient comparisons on512 documents disjoint from featurizer training and development. All20 paired95% bootstrap intervals exclude zero on the improvement side. However,37–49% of individual documents get worse, and the unseen-token stratum is mixed. This verifies a useful inference option, not a semantic manifold or universal improvement.

### Context and definitions

The featurizers approximate the model's1152-dimensional state immediately before the layer4 MLP. Ten fits comprise signed sparse scalar dictionaries at48/64 active coordinates, blocks of8, fixed overlapping groups over shared atoms, and learned overlapping groups; two seeds each. These are the existing finite-training-budget implementations, not a matched-parameter architecture verdict or an exact Grassmannian BSF reproduction.

For each input, subtract its training-derived token mean. The calibration restores the length of the bias-centered reconstructed residual to the native residual length, then restores the input's overall raw RMS. It carries one extra native norm scalar; it is not a free improvement at identical information budget. LS means least-squares coefficient fitting within the support already selected by the encoder; no gates or dictionaries are retrained. Learned and LS coefficients each have calibrated and uncalibrated versions.

KL(native||replacement) measures disagreement with the original model's entire next-token distribution; lower is more faithful. Ground-truth cross-entropy is recorded separately and answers a different question. Replace the full raw state at a locked position and run the rest of the model, using the prefix ending there. This is direct reconstruction replacement, not a donor-difference task intervention.

### What this changes

Combined with H857's worse activation reconstruction and local MLP derivative errors, the confirmation strengthens the case for measuring whole-model fidelity directly. Reconstruction error alone is insufficient for choosing representations for causal interpretation. Shared-group fits still have poorer absolute fidelity than the sparse scalar fits here; restoring norm does not fix collapsed membership coverage or establish reusable shared computation.

The manifold program remains the objective. Next, freeze calibrated and uncalibrated scalar/block controls and examine whether candidate components recur across seeds, support coherent within-component variation, and produce specific causal changes across competent tasks. Include agreement and sentiment relays plus binding/copy/capital tasks at their demonstrably active sites, rather than treating a weak early-layer effect as a failed feature. Predefine matched random-subspace, token-conditioned, and off-component controls. Held-out combinations and selective component removal are the tests for reuse; visual clusters or reconstruction gains alone are insufficient. Keep shared-group alternatives as explicit comparisons and diagnose coverage before giving their groups semantic names.

|shared_learned_8351|0.1931|0.1645|0.1819|0.1593|
|shared_learned_8352|0.1959|0.1562|0.1892|0.1546|

Norm retention improves all20 aggregate mean comparisons, but not every document. Depending on model/variant, about45–72% of documents improve. Paired64-document bootstrap intervals are saved and uncorrected; many include zero. For example learned scalar48 seed8351 meanKL change is-.00741 with interval[-.01299,-.00255], while block8 seed8352 is-.00483 with interval[-.01969,.01177]. Mean improvements alone do not establish robust universal superiority.

NexttokenCE changes are available on56 examples per variant. They can have either sign, including occasional improvement relative to the original model. Such negative CE changes on this tiny subset are not evidence of a better language model, and CE is not a substitute for faithfulness to the original output distribution. Both metrics remain distinct in the records.

**Research implication.** We now have an implementable single-state modification with promising task and natural whole-output behavior, even though it increases activation error and localMLP response error. Thus neither reconstructionMSE nor the chosen local derivative metric is sufficient to rank representations for end-to-end fidelity. It does not follow that larger feature norms are always useful, that the learned groups are meaningful, or that all dimensions discarded by the representation are irrelevant. The fixed/learnedshared models remain substantially less faithful than scalars under these fits, even after calibration.

The relevant notion of a good representation must specify the purpose: activation reconstruction, local operator approximation, original-output KL, and ground-truthCE are different objectives. This supports the user's data-based/function-based canonical-form direction, but we have not established uniqueness, a minimal canonical form, a semantic manifold, or general reusable computation units.

**Next confirmation.** Freeze the per-state rule and all40 variant checkpoints/prediction procedures. Use a document-disjoint natural panel not used in H851/H852 fitting or selection, preferably the already trackedH837 pool with a clear scoped-freshness statement. Evaluate direct whole-outputKL/TV and paired uncertainty without tuning gains or selecting a seed. Retain uncalibrated and LS controls, token-coverage strata, and individual harms. Only then consider retraining with a different objective or using the calibrated featurizer as the default for manifold interpretation.

Source/model hashes unchanged, metrics finite; no reserved-test use; natural-document pool26,112 unchanged. ## Previous continuation: H857

## H857 — A consistent norm-aware encoder improves most relay effects but worsens natural local fidelity

**Main result.** The pairwise-oracle norm benefit partly survives in a genuine single-input encoding function. With no task directions or gain fitting, residual-norm retention improves answer-effect error in57/60 aggregate model/task/gap cells. But full-output task KL improves in only46/60 for learned coefficients (43/60 for LS), and natural-text reconstruction/local-MLP fidelity worsens for every model. This is a tradeoff, not a universally improved featurizer.

**Single-state rule.** Let C be token-centered normalized input, beta the decoder bias, and C_hat its learned or fixed-support least-squares reconstruction. Define:

`C_hat_norm = beta + (C_hat-beta) * ||C-beta|| / ||C_hat-beta||`.

Add the training-token mean, normalize the fullshape and restore that input's own rawRMS to define one raw reconstruction F(input). Form interventions as native recipient + F(donor)-F(recipient). This preserves recipient reconstruction error and is cycle-consistent by construction. It requires one additional residual-norm scalar beyond token identity and rawRMS already accessed. Gates, dictionaries and supports remain frozen. Bias is retained; zero reconstruction-norm cases would fail explicitly rather than receive an arbitrary direction (none occurred).

This differs fromH853/H854, which normalized after adding the decoded donor difference to the native recipient shape. Compare calibrated and uncalibrated variants withinH857; improvements relative to older numerical tables cannot all be attributed to the norm rule.

**Adjacent-prompt learned-coefficient examples.** Values describe preservation of the full raw relay effect, not native task accuracy. Full tables retain both seeds, all architectures/gaps, and independent LS variants.

## H856 — Task-direction-free contrast norm restoration rescues much of active-span fidelity

**Main result.** Restore the original donor contrast's norm after projecting into the frozen active decoder span, without loading a task direction. This improves answer-effect fidelity and full-output KL relative to ordinary projection in every one of the60 model/task/gap aggregate cells tested. Much of the previous oracle deficit is attenuation rather than complete absence of a useful direction. Learnedshared models still retain substantial deficits.

**Rule and scope.** For true rawpreMLP4 contrast delta and projector P onto the union of the two native active atom sets:

`p = P delta`

`norm_restored = p * ||delta|| / ||p||`.

This holds the projected direction and support fixed and restores exactly the original contrast magnitude. No task-direction file, task label or task effect enters this formula. Also test fixed gain2 as a separate exploratory control, specified before this run. All10 fits, all78 H849 pairs, both directions and all gap variants retained. These are raw-state edits with no postpatch normalization, matching H855 rather than H854's shape/radius protocol.

Fixedgain2 can also improve effects, but may overshoot and does not reliably beat the parameter-free norm-restoration rule. **Important limitation.** This is a pairwise oracle, not a repaired single-input featurizer. It requires the full donor-recipient contrast and both active supports. In general, such pairwise corrections need not be expressible as F(donor)-F(recipient) for one consistent encoding function; they can violate cycle consistency. It also increases Euclidean reconstruction error compared with orthogonal projection. Thus improved behavior does not establish a data-canonical representation or an interpretable atom/group.

**Updated hypothesis tournament (20 alternatives).**

1. Reconstruction-optimal projection attenuates useful contrasts — strongly supported byH854–856.
2. The frozen sparse spans entirely lack task directions — weakened; constraints are feasible and norm restoration often works.
3. Full512-dimensional capacity is required — weakened for these task effects; active spans suffice after calibration in many cases.
4. Encoder coefficient error alone is the bottleneck — weakened; independent stateLS gives mixed causal results.
5. Learned support selection loses useful content — still plausible; full-span oracles outperform active spans, but objective/dose confound attribution.
6. Learnedshared membership collapse is a primary defect — supported as one defect, not the sole explanation.
7. Simply fixing coverage solves shared groups — weakened by fixedshared underperformance.
8. A task-aware metric is essential to improve fidelity — weakened for pairwise contrast calibration, unresolved for single-state learning.
9. A single scalar completely determines causal output — contradicted byH850 partial-writer counterexamples.
10. A compact task-specific axis summarizes many natural donor contrasts — supported byH848–849, within limited tasks.
11. One generic axis explains both agreement and sentiment — weakened by low overlap and cross-task controls.
12. The axes are distributed across learned atoms — compatible with weak individual atom alignment and useful aggregate spans.
13. Context features are written by multiple modules — supported byH850 native decomposition/interventions.
14. Early final-position state is the universal location — contradicted by depth/source-position results.
15. Agreement's relay depends on adjacency or wording — supported as a limitation; moving-relay versus signal-loss distinction open.
16. Sentiment's relay is strictly adjacent-token copying — weakened by retained effects with inserted words; broader formats remain untested.
17. Persistent lexical values plus contextual readers are reusable computation units — supported on prior panels, not the whole model.
18. Token-mean coverage explains all featurizer failures — weakened by same-token and correct-site results, but affects nonlinear encoding.
19. A per-state norm channel can reproduce the pairwise calibration benefit — live and directly testable next.
20. Pairwise behavior preservation may not define a consistent representation/manifold — unresolved; test single-state encodings and cycle consistency before claiming canonical form.

**Next experiment.** Try a direction-free, single-state inference rule: retain native residual norm as one additional scalar, rescale learned or least-squares reconstructions around their decoder bias, then form donor differences normally. Freeze supports and dictionaries, evaluate both natural-data reconstruction/operator fidelity and all existing task cells. This is an implementable encoding function, unlike the current pairwise oracle. Do not tune gain on these task outcomes. If it fails, investigate contrast-aware or response-weighted training with independent task confirmation rather than declaring the featurizer repaired.

## H855 — Active spans can match the causal coordinate, but edit magnitude explains much of the apparent rescue

**Main result.** Every frozen donor/recipient active-union span tested can represent the independently frozen task coordinate. A constrained least-squares edit often restores most of the full relay's answer effect. However, scaling the ordinary Euclidean projection to the constrained edit's norm produces nearly the same rescue in many cases. Thus these results do not uniquely support a semantic-coordinate-aware objective over a simpler attenuation/calibration explanation.

**Exact diagnostic.** With orthogonal active-span projector P, true raw donor contrast delta and frozen unit task direction q:

`p = P delta`

`constrained = p + Pq * [qᵀ(delta-p)] / [qᵀPq]`.

This is the minimum Euclidean-error vector in the fixed span satisfying qᵀedit=qᵀdelta. It deliberately uses task supervision and the donor pair, so it is an oracle rather than a task-blind featurizer. UnlikeH854, these interventions operate directly in rawpreMLP4 coordinates without subsequent normalization/radius restoration. They need their own raw-reference comparison.

All10 fits and78H849 pairs retained, both directions. Controls: ordinary projection, other-task-coordinate constraint, Euclidean direction scaled to the own-constrained totalnorm, minimum-norm edit matching only the coordinate, direct task-rank1 edit, full rawdonor, identity. Same supports/subspace throughout. No unrepresentable constraints: smallest tested own/other-direction projected energy .0698, maximum active dictionary condition number4.98.

Ratios above100% indicate overshoot, not better-than-perfect fidelity. The constrained edit's mean norm is about1.03–1.50 times the full donor contrast norm in these adjacent cells; the largest ratio across all cases is1.946. The norm-matched control itself uses the task-dependent constrained norm, so it is not yet a task-blind solution; H856 tests a direction-free norm rule.

Other-task constraints have little benefit, but that alone does not prove semantic specificity: they barely change the edit because the other coordinate has little native contrast. A strong comparison must control magnitude as well as which coordinate is enforced. The minimum-norm coordinate-only edits also work reasonably, but they introduce off-axis state within the span and do not establish that the model reads only one scalar.

**Interpretation.** H854's good full-dictionary result did not mean512 coordinates were necessary to reproduce the task effect: current active spans can carry the salient coordinate when coefficients are changed. Yet same-coordinate interventions still differ in output, especially learnedshared sentiment, and constrained effect error ranges widely. This is compatible with a compact signal distributed across learned atoms, attenuated by reconstruction/support choices, with downstream context and off-axis interactions. It does not establish a recovered semantic group or manifold.

## Previous continuation: H854

## H854 — Sparse selection and reconstruction objectives both limit causal fidelity

**Main result.** Frozen dictionary spans can represent substantially more of the relay effect than the learned sparse encodings express. But correcting coefficients or minimizing contrast reconstruction error on the active span does not reliably improve causal fidelity. Thus the current shortfall cannot be reduced to a single encoder bug, and reconstruction-optimal coefficients are not automatically computation-preserving coefficients.

**Four diagnostics.** All10 H852 models, all78 H849 pairs, both directions, all gap variants remain fixed. Each edit uses the same native-shape plus reconstructed contrast intervention as H853, restoring recipient radius.

1. **Learned:** original donor-minus-recipient decoder reconstruction.
2. **State LS:** independently least-squares reconstruct each input on its own frozen active atoms, retaining decoder bias, then subtract the two reconstructions. This needs no donor pair or task label to encode each state. It is a plausible inference refinement, not a new trained model.
3. **Union oracle:** least-squares project the true donor contrast into the union of both native active supports. This uses both inputs/supports jointly and is a diagnostic pairwise oracle, not a deployable single-state encoder.
4. **Full oracle:** project the contrast into all512 dictionary atoms. This has much higher rank/cost and is not a matched-capacity improvement.

For learnedshared we additionally test the101 atoms covered by any membership. This distinguishes accessible atoms from the remaining, often untrained/inaccessible dictionary columns. Every projection uses float64 SVD with a relative singular-value cutoff; ranks and conditioning retained.

**Adjacent-prompt causal preservation.** Entries are percentages of the exact-shape relay effect, seed8351/8352 separately; they are not native task accuracy or fractions of unique mediation.

|Task|Model|Learned|State LS|Union oracle|Full512 oracle|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|agreement|scalar48|58/73|65/82|50/61|92/92|
|agreement|scalar64|57/73|61/73|50/52|91/91|
|agreement|block8|57/72|60/77|57/75|92/89|
|agreement|shared_fixed|19/31|28/42|30/54|93/91|
|agreement|shared_learned|21/17|23/19|33/16|85/86|
|sentiment|scalar48|74/55|76/58|60/55|89/86|
|sentiment|scalar64|57/56|57/55|47/52|90/87|
|sentiment|block8|66/53|62/49|62/58|87/90|
|sentiment|shared_fixed|52/42|40/54|47/49|83/82|
|sentiment|shared_learned|17/6|17/9|20/10|75/78|

Full dictionary effects are about89–93% for scalar/block agreement and86–90% for scalar/block sentiment. However, full rank is512 versus state supports40–64 and active unions48–106. Higher rank is a major confound; this is evidence of available capacity, not proof that a512-dimensional code is a good feature explanation. The supervised one-dimensional task contrast remains a different, task-informed comparator.

**Reconstruction and causal fidelity can disagree.** Every union-oracle contrast is at least as accurate geometrically as the learned contrast, as required by least squares and confirmed numerically. Yet scalar48 seed8351 agreement preservation falls57.6%→50.4%, while geometric relativeRMSE improves .897→.754; task-effect error worsens .447→.509. Sentiment for that same model falls74.4%→60.5% preservation while geometric error improves .808→.701. Therefore a reconstruction-optimal contrast can discard or weaken directions that matter to the downstream task. These are counterexamples to using reconstruction error alone as causal faithfulness.

Independent state LS improves per-state reconstruction for every input, but can worsen contrast reconstruction and downstream effects. For example sentiment block8 seed8351 effect preservation declines66.4%→62.5%; other cases improve. This does not justify replacing all encoders with least squares without a broader behavior check.

**Shared-group diagnosis.** Learnedshared covered spans have rank101, compared with40–57 per-state active ranks and48–71 pair-union ranks. The covered-span oracle preserves about63–64% agreement and33–36% sentiment adjacent effects, versus17–22% and6–17% for learned encodings. All512 columns improve further, but unused atoms make that an inaccessible artificial capacity expansion. Coverage collapse and support/coordinate inference both contribute; neither alone explains all errors. Fixedshared has full512 coverage yet weak active behavior, so simply enforcing coverage is unlikely to solve the problem.

**What we can and cannot infer.** The total dictionary often contains useful directions spread across atoms. That does not establish an interpretable atom/group, nor show that current sparse gates select the right computational subspace. Euclidean reconstruction is insensitive to which errors downstream readers amplify. MoreoverH850 already showed equal scalar coordinates can yield different outputs under different off-axis interventions, so even a task-weighted scalar loss is not a complete fidelity criterion.

**Next discriminating experiment.** On the same frozen active spans, compare ordinary projection with a constrained minimum-error projection that preserves the independently frozen causal coordinate, using full raw-state contrasts and an exact raw-coordinate audit. This deliberately task-informed oracle asks whether the span could carry the salient scalar at reasonable edit norm. It is not an unsupervised solution and must not be advertised as one. If it restores causal behavior, test task-blind response-weighted fitting/inference on natural data with independent tasks; if it does not, investigate off-axis interactions and sparse-span limits. Track intervention norm, rank and output effects to avoid claiming success by large off-manifold edits. Revisit the20-hypothesis tournament after this bottleneck test.

**Audits.**6,864 full-model forwards. All bases orthogonal within4.56e-15; no per-state LS reconstruction-error increase and no nesting/projection-error violation. Identity logits and H853 learned-effect replay exact. All sources/checkpoints unchanged, all effects finite; no reserved-test evaluation; natural-document pool26,112 unchanged. Rank/condition metadata and all oracle edits are saved. Previous turn was progress: correct-site task-blind featurizers created the benchmark. This turn distinguishes available dictionary capacity, selected support and a substantive objective mismatch. Broad goal remains active.

Training budget, STE optimization, gate parameterization and support constraints remain alternatives to architectural unsuitability.

**Coverage caveat.**48 relay-token occurrences lack a training-specific mean and use the global mean; token identity remains equal within each patched pair. This removes donor lexical-mean substitution but does not guarantee in-distribution nonlinear encoding. Agreement FormatA/FormatB results are separately retained. Both show substantial scalar/block transfer and weaker shared-group fidelity; do not dismiss all errors as missing means, nor assume centering cannot contribute.

**Next discriminating experiment.** Separate representational capacity from inference: project the true donor contrast into (a) the entire learned decoder span and (b) the union of the recipient/donor active decoder atoms, comparing these oracle coefficients with the learned encoder difference at the same site. These are diagnostic least-squares oracles, not unsupervised discoveries or deployed encoders. If the active span preserves the effect but learned coefficients do not, improve coordinate inference/training. If only the full dictionary works, examine gating/support. If even the full span fails, the dictionary or training distribution misses the relevant direction. ## H850 — The compact relay coordinate is assembled by multiple writers and is not a complete causal state

**Main result.** Discovery-selected writers account for much of the frozen relay coordinate on the new lexical/distance panel, and intervening on them recovers much of the relay's answer effect. No single writer supplies the whole coordinate. The result supports a distributed construction of a compact downstream direction, rather than identifying one neuron/head as the entire feature.

**Exact native accounting.** At the relay token, decompose raw preMLP4 into attention headsL0–4 and MLP writesL0–3, each scaled by subsequent residual-mixing coefficients. This yields49 writer terms. The original embedding contribution cancels in each donor-recipient difference because the relay token is identical. Head contributions use actual native head outputs and output-projection slices. This is an algebraic decomposition of native differences, not an intervention-based attribution of computation.

For each task, rank writers by RMS contribution along the frozen H848 direction on only the8 discovery pairs. Freeze the top3 before examining H849 writer interventions:

- Agreement: L4H5, L3MLP, L2MLP.
- Sentiment: L4H7, L3MLP, L4H6.

On the H849 panel, projection slopes against the total coordinate difference are respectively0.406/0.240/0.097 for agreement and0.326/0.252/0.192 for sentiment. These slopes quantify native accounting, not independent causal percentages. A shared whole MLP module does not establish that both tasks reuse the same internal computation or feature.

**Writer interventions.** At each selected writer's original output site, add the native donor-minus-recipient vector at the relay position. In a separate axial arm, add only its projection onto the task's frozen direction. Run each writer separately and all3 jointly. Downstream modules recompute naturally; multi-writer edits add native deltas to the already perturbed execution, so they are not equivalent to replacing every intermediate output with its donor value. All78 H849 pairs, both directions, retained. The panel is fresh relative to basis fitting, but already used for direction validation; writer results are exploratory follow-up.
