## Previous continuation: H799

## H799 — Identical value-direction interventions have context-dependent effects

Previous turn was progress: H798 showed that native edge removal can lower intended-word confidence under repeated keys yet raise it under different keys, despite similarly negative routing. H799 removes the confound that native edge coefficients differ across contexts.

Use only the competent matching-value cells from H797. For each item/format, choose one canonical first-source mixed-value vector V in L2H5. Audit V across same/different second keys and both later queries. Inject delta*V at the second-source head output before c_proj, with delta=-.5,-.25,0,.25,.5, using exactly the same V, delta and token position within the matched item/format. These deltas are additive coefficient changes, not multiplicative scales of the native edge. Native edge coefficients and all other background states remain those of their respective prompts.

### Exact intervention matching

The native first-source V vectors are exactly equal across key/query contexts, as expected because those changed tokens occur later. Canonicalization therefore introduces no approximation. Output projection weights are shared, so the corresponding residual-stream perturbation is also identical across the compared contexts. This rules out unequal injected direction or magnitude as an explanation of the response difference. It does not make the local background state identical: native edge coefficients and other context-dependent computation can still affect how the perturbation is processed.

### Behavioral result

Mean intended-token log-probability changes in natural-log units:

| Format | Additive coefficient delta | Same keys | Different keys | Paired different-minus-same response |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Vertical bars | +.25 | -.1006 | +.0071 | +.1077 |
| Vertical bars | +.50 | -.4317 | -.0534 | +.3783 |
| Colon/newline | +.25 | +.0007 | +.0866 | +.0860 |
| Colon/newline | +.50 | -.1164 | +.1087 | +.2250 |

At+.50, descriptive paired item-bootstrap intervals for the context difference are [.2503,.5010] and[.1401,.3164]. The same directional context difference appears when querying the first key or the second key separately, rather than arising only from pooling queries. For colon/newline+.50, same-key and different-key mean effects have opposite signs with intervals below and above zero respectively.

This establishes a context-dependent finite response for an identical injected value direction on these prompts. It does not identify a semantic gate or prove that key equality, rather than other correlated local/context states, is the directly used variable.

Negative deltas lower intended log-probability in all four context/format groups. At-.50, same/different-key changes are-.141/-.150 in vertical bars and-.208/-.273 in colon/newline. Positive and negative perturbations therefore do not act as a simple sign-reversed linear response, and a single global coefficient-to-behavior mapping would miss this behavior.

Full-vocabulary accuracy stays at its native96.9–100% across the tested conditions. Distributional effects remain measurable: at+.50, mean KL(native||perturbed) is .1217/.0267 for same/different keys in vertical bars, and .0204/.0181 in colon/newline. Similar KL magnitudes need not imply the same intended-token effect, just as unchanged top1 need not imply unchanged confidence.

### Verification and limits

728 model forwards:104 native matching-value contexts,520 intervention runs,104 independent post-projection checks. Native V invariance max absolute and relative error are exactly zero. Zero-delta logits replay exactly. Native margins match H797 within6.20e-6. Pre-projection delta injection and equivalent post-projection injection agree within1.41e-5 maximum full-vocabulary logit error. All KL values finite and nonnegative; model/input/reference/runner hashes unchanged. Original reserved test untouched; natural-document pool remains26,112.

The panel contains16 aligned vertical-bar items and10 colon/newline items. Query variants are averaged within item for bootstrap; same-key queries are duplicate prompts, not independent evidence. Intervals are descriptive without multiplicity correction. Directions differ across lexical items and formats; exact matching is within an item/format. Finite interventions may leave native activation distributions, so response differences alone do not establish manifold geometry.

### Implication for representation learning

A content vector can be exactly shared while its behavioral response changes with computational background. This supports separating the reusable content representation from the context-conditioned transformation or readout. It does not imply that shared dictionaries cannot work; it means an invariant semantic label or average output effect is an inadequate validation target. A faithful representation must preserve the relevant family of finite responses across contexts, in addition to reconstructing the vector.

Next cross the local second-source residual state with the surrounding key/query context: transplant the pre-MLP residual from same-key or different-key runs, then apply the identical value perturbation in each context. Keep each transplanted baseline and zero-intervention reference explicit. If the response follows local state, local normalization/bilinear geometry may explain much of the modulation; if it follows surrounding context, later readers or other-token paths matter. This is a diagnostic hybrid experiment, not a semantic attribution by itself. Its result can guide which conditioning variables a compact shared representation or computational DAG needs.

### Research decision

The verified computation is a repetition-sensitive signed read whose downstream meaning is context-dependent. Calling it a “repetition suppressor” from its negative coefficient would be wrong: removing it reduces confidence in the repeated answer for same-key prompts. Previous turn was progress: H796 validated frozen L2H5 causal interaction-removal fidelity across vocabulary and observed more-negative routing for matching identities under partial source-output swaps. H797 removes the hybrid-state concern for the routing observation by evaluating fully native prompts.

Source positions and total token length must match across all eight cells of an item/format; no outcomes enter this alignment rule. Capture frozen L2H5's first-value→second-value signed coefficient, its two Q/K factors and normalized-residual cosine similarity. ### Routing result

| Format | Keys | Values differ: mean edge coefficient | Values match: mean edge coefficient | Value-matching change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Vertical bars | Different | -.0294 | -.4462 | -.4168 |
| Vertical bars | Same | -.0316 | -.4672 | -.4356 |
| Colon/newline | Different | -.0336 | -.4936 | -.4600 |
| Colon/newline | Same | -.0358 | -.5068 | -.4710 |

The large negative value-matching contrast is present even when keys differ. Descriptive item-bootstrap intervals are [-.4484,-.3862] and[-.4962,-.4217] for different keys in the two formats. The primary repetition-sensitive routing effect therefore exists on native inputs and is not solely an artifact of the earlier MLP-output substitutions.

Key identity still modulates the response. With different values, matching keys changes the coefficient by only about-.0022 in each format, with intervals spanning zero. With matching values, the key-matching changes are-.0210 and-.0132. The key×value interactions are-.0188 and-.0110, with descriptive intervals below zero. The coefficient is a signed weight, not a probability, and negative routing does not directly establish inhibition of an output word. Q/K factor signs remain consistent with earlier observations: matching values raises the first factor and makes the second more negative.

### Competence limits

With distinct keys and distinct values, candidate accuracy is only65.6% in vertical bars and55.0% in colon/newline; full-vocabulary intended top1 is53.1%/50.0%. These cells fail the established75% contrast-accuracy standard, so this panel does not establish a successful binding algorithm or identify why binding succeeds.

Same-key/different-value cells have conflicting assignments and no accuracy claim. The routing factorial remains measurable in all cells, but behavioral interpretation must respect these differences.

### Identity versus general similarity remains unresolved

Normalized-input cosine increases when values match: for example, with different keys it rises from .597 to .801 in vertical bars and .698 to .836 in colon/newline. A descriptive leave-item-out prediction analysis gives routing-coefficient RMS errors:

| Predictor | RMS error |
|---|---:|
| Format-specific intercept | .2267 |
| Linear input cosine plus format | .1111 |
| Quadratic input cosine plus format | .0885 |
| Key/value identity factorial plus format | .0532 |

These post hoc small regressions diagnose predictive structure, not competing causal explanations. Identity and cosine covary; words overlap across held-out item indices, so this is not lexical generalization. The identity model's lower error does not prove that the head represents a discrete equality feature, and a quadratic scalar cosine is not an exhaustive model of learned geometry. No manifold or learned compact operator is validated here.

### Verification and exclusions

208 native model forwards. All16 vertical-bar item factorials and10 colon/newline factorials survive alignment. Bootstrap intervals cluster by item within each format, are descriptive and not multiplicity-adjusted; formats share items.

### Research decision

The strongest current description is a native value-repetition/similarity-sensitive negative read from the first source to the second, with modest key-context modulation. We have a verified algebraic edge and a transferable counterfactual causal effect, but its role in native prediction remains untested.

Next scale or remove this exact edge in fully native prompts, including the competent matching-value cells, and measure intended-token log-probability, full-vocabulary KL and answer contrasts separately. Retain ambiguous and low-competence conditions only for appropriately limited geometric/response comparisons. This will test whether the negative read changes native prediction in the way a repetition-discounting hypothesis suggests, rather than assigning function from its sign. Any subsequent data-based canonical form or shared-dictionary featurizer should preserve that measured native response as well as the earlier finite source-intervention effects.

    edge_h(a,b) = [(q_h(b) dot k_h(a))/128]

The receiver prompt stays fixed. Source1's L1 output is replaced with identity a; source2's with identity b. The signed attention coefficient is not a probability. Queries at the second source are exactly independent of the first source's intervention, and first-source keys/values are exactly independent of the second source's intervention at this point. | Colon/newline | Mixed | .929 | 1.000 | .929 |

The second-source attention intervention substantially changes the final non-additivity for matching donors. The early query MLP clamp has almost no effect on this readout, despite its nonzero traced activation interaction. The joint arm closely follows the source-only arm. This supports causal relevance of the tested source-attention interaction, while directly illustrating why activation-interaction magnitude alone is insufficient.

These RMS ratios describe the response to specific interventions; they are not uniquely attributed fractions of computation. Remaining interactions are substantial, especially for mixed donors. The experiment does not establish a complete or minimal route.

### Direction of its effect

The source-attention clamp increases average donor specificity rather than erasing it:

| Format | Donors | Baseline specificity | Source-clamped specificity | Mean change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Vertical bars | Matching | .510 | .573 | +.0628 |
| Colon/newline | Matching | .417 | .476 | +.0594 |
| Vertical bars | Mixed | .273 | .299 | +.0261 |
| Colon/newline | Mixed | .227 | .242 | +.0143 |

For matching donors, item-bootstrap intervals for the change are [.0146,.1107] and [.0147,.1157]. Mixed-donor changes have intervals [.0139,.0372] and [.0008,.0279]. These are descriptive intervals over16 reused item clusters per format, with no multiplicity correction. Candidate-specificity definitions are unchanged from H792, and matching/mixed target-set sizes differ.

The interaction therefore modulates or counteracts part of the additive donor signal under these hybrid interventions. It should not be labeled a beneficial content-transmission channel or a harmful native mechanism from this result. Native copying is already competent; stronger counterfactual donor promotion is not necessarily better task performance.

Per-example donor-specificity interaction RMS also decreases: matching-donor values move from .344 to .211 in vertical bars and .367 to .192 in colon/newline. Mixed values move from .143 to .129 and .114 to .104. Query-only values remain essentially unchanged. This separates a genuine change in response structure from a mere change in average specificity.

### Verification

2,048 model forwards: all16 factorial cells,32 item-format contexts,4 arms. Native L1 replacements and additive clamps are exact at requested positions. No-clamp candidate responses and all single-source/identity cells replay the prior reference within9.54e-6. Identity logits replay within1.77e-5. Metrics finite; model/input/reference/runner hashes unchanged. Original reserved test untouched; natural-document pool remains26,112.

No-clamp references and zero-interaction single cells were checked, rather than assuming an additive clamp is behaviorally harmless there. This remains a reused competent-copying panel; independent replication of a newly selected mechanism is still required. The negligible query-clamp result is specific to L2, this site, intervention and readout; it does not establish that query MLPs or normalization are generally irrelevant.

### Next mechanistic discriminator

At layer2, immediately after the L1 source replacements, each source input depends only on its own replaced output. At the second source, its attention query can therefore depend on donorB while the first source's keys/values depend on donorA. With this model's unnormalized attention, the first-source-to-second-source attention edge is a concrete candidate for the observed cross-source interaction.

Next reconstruct that edge's factorial interaction from actual query/key/value factors, audit that its projected contribution explains the module interaction, and then intervene on its head contributions with full-module reference controls. This can identify a specific multiplicative computation rather than introducing a generic learned DAG merely because the architecture permits one. Any compact representation must preserve the remaining identity-specific finite responses, not just match mean activation geometry.

## Previous continuation: H793

## H793 — Factorial interactions appear at the second source before growing at the query

Previous turn was progress: H792 established substantial per-example non-additivity in combining L1 source identities, without a clear average agreement bonus. H793 traces the exact same factorial interventions through downstream computation to localize where the interactions form.

For every H791 item/format, replay the complete4x4 source-identity factorial in one batch. At both source positions and the final query token, capture block-scaled residual input, attention-normalized input, attention output, pre-MLP residual, MLP-normalized input, MLP output and block output for layers1–17. Compute I(a,b)=z_ab-z_a0-z_0b+z_00 for all matching and mixed nonreceiver donor pairs. The two L1 output replacements occur before their outputs are captured. Detailed early-layer captures are saved for subsequent interaction-removal experiments.

### Architectural controls pass

The factorial residual is exactly zero immediately after the L1 output replacements: the two edited positions initially contain separate additive changes. The first source position is exactly independent of the later source identity at every traced stage, as required by causal attention.

At the final query, L2 attention combines the two source changes additively to numerical precision: aggregate interaction/joint-change vector RMS is2.70e-6. The query state entering L2 is unchanged by the earlier-position L1 output replacements. Because this model's attention has no softmax coupling across keys, the first L2 query read sums independent changed-source contributions. This is an architectural consistency check, not evidence that later attention must remain additive.

### Where interaction develops

For matching donors, interaction vector RMS divided by actual joint-change vector RMS is:

| Position and stage | Vertical bars | Colon/newline |
|---|---:|---:|
| Second source, L2 attention output | 1.807 | 2.112 |
| Second source, L2 block output | .868 | .997 |
| Query, L2 attention output | .0000019 | .0000042 |
| Query, L2 MLP-normalized input | .0157 | .0109 |
| Query, L2 MLP output | .0625 | .0489 |
| Query, L2 block output | .0469 | .0400 |
| Query, L3 attention output | .602 | .520 |
| Query, L3 block output | .512 | .483 |

The second source can attend to the first while its own query representation is changed. It therefore becomes a strong early site of source interaction, whereas the final query initially receives an almost additive L2 attention update. At the query, RMS normalization of that combined update introduces a nonzero factorial residual, and the subsequent bilinear MLP output also has a nonzero residual. These observations identify stages of formation; they do not uniquely divide the MLP's residual into propagated normalization effects and newly created bilinear effects.

By L3 attention, the query interaction is much larger relative to its joint change. This is consistent with nonlinear source states being read later, alongside changed query/routing computations. It does not prove that the second source alone causes that growth: intermediate untracked token positions and other pathways could also contribute.

Query block-output ratios subsequently reach about1–2.4 in parts of the network and end around1.14/1.17 at L17 for matching donors. Ratios above1 reflect cancellation in joint-versus-single changes; they are not “more than100% causal contribution.” Different stages have different scales, and a large interaction norm is not evidence that removing it will alter the relevant output contrast.

### Verification

512 model forwards. Final candidate-logit changes replay H792 within1.05e-5, confirming that tracing preserves the measured computation. Identity logits replay within1.67e-5 across batches. L1 post-replacement factorial residual and first-source future independence are exactly zero. L2 query-attention interaction has maximum component .000793 at large activation scale, but relative RMS only2.70e-6; the relative architectural audit passes. All metrics finite and source/model/input/reference hashes unchanged. Original reserved test untouched; natural-document pool remains26,112.

The full trace contains both matching and mixed donors, both formats and all stages; the table focuses on matching donors for readability. These reused competent copying prompts remain a localization panel. The trace is descriptive and cannot establish causal mediation, necessity, a discrete agreement detector, or a learned computational DAG.

### Next causal discriminator

Use the saved factorial captures to replace selected joint-state module outputs with their additive predictions z_a0+z_0b-z_00. Predeclare L2 attention output at the second source and L2 MLP output at the query, individually and jointly, with exact identity and reference replays. Read the resulting final candidate specificity and interaction vectors. This will test whether early source-to-source composition or early query-local mixing actually contributes to the observed output non-additivity, rather than assuming that the largest traced norm is the relevant computation. If neither explains the effect, test later query attention and other positions rather than declaring a minimal route.

## Previous continuation: H792

## H792 — Mixed-source content transfer is nonlinear without a clear average agreement bonus

Previous turn was progress: H791 confirmed donor-specific L1 source effects on fresh vocabulary while showing broad alternative promotion. H792 crosses donor identities to test how the two source representations combine.

For each H791 receiver, run all16 assignments of four native identities (receiver0 and donors1/2/3) to the first and second value-source MLP outputs at L1. This includes receiver/receiver, single-source, matching-donor and mixed-donor conditions. All other computation remains receiver-native and downstream computation is live. The complete factorial and candidate-resolved analysis were specified before outcomes. No model or featurizer was trained.

For candidate-logit changes, the additive prediction is the sum of the two single-source changes (minus the numerically nonzero identity change). The difference from this prediction is the interaction. Candidate vectors are centered before vector-error calculations to remove common logit shifts.

### Mixed donors still transfer content

| Format | Source assignment | Actual mean target specificity | Additive mean prediction | Mean interaction |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Vertical bars | Matching donors | .510 | .534 | -.024 |
| Vertical bars | Mixed donors | .273 | .315 | -.042 |
| Colon/newline | Matching donors | .417 | .449 | -.033 |
| Colon/newline | Mixed donors | .227 | .238 | -.011 |

For matching donors, target specificity is the donor's logit change relative to the mean of nonreceiver/nondonor candidates. For mixed donors it is the mean change of the two donor candidates relative to the remaining nonreceiver candidates. These use different target-set sizes, so comparing the first and second rows directly is not evidence of an agreement bonus. Mean interaction intervals span zero in all four cells, while both matching and mixed donor specificity are positive.

### Balanced agreement test

For each pair of donor identities A/B, compare half of (A/A+B/B) with half of (A/B+B/A), using the same two target words and background candidates. This cancels additive source main effects. Each donor occupies each source equally often, so average squared replacement norm is also balanced (numerical relative difference <6e-8).

The balanced matching-minus-mixed specificity difference is -.0156 for vertical bars (descriptive item-bootstrap interval [-.0605,.0289]) and -.0159 for colon/newline ([-.0726,.0329]). There is no clear positive average specificity bonus for source agreement under this test. This does not prove absence of an agreement mechanism: nonlinear geometry, remaining receiver-native paths and item-dependent effects remain possible. It does weaken the claim that H790's single-versus-joint pattern alone revealed a general agreement detector.

The balanced target-versus-receiver margin difference is -.181 in vertical bars (interval spans zero) and -.436 in colon/newline (interval [-.613,-.265]). A change in binary margin can therefore coexist with little change in target identity specificity, reinforcing the importance of candidate-resolved readouts.

### Means conceal substantial non-additivity

Adding single-source responses predicts average specificity reasonably closely, but individual predictions are poor:

| Format | Assignment | Additive RMS error in target specificity | Actual specificity RMS | Relative error |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Vertical bars | Matching | .344 | .647 | .531 |
| Vertical bars | Mixed | .143 | .392 | .363 |
| Colon/newline | Matching | .367 | .557 | .659 |
| Colon/newline | Mixed | .114 | .377 | .302 |

Across the full centered16-candidate logit vectors, additive relative RMS error is1.030/1.020 for matching donors and .486/.452 for mixed donors. Thus the near-zero mean interaction is cancellation across cases, not an accurate additive computational model.

A follow-up output-geometry diagnostic projects each centered interaction onto the receiver-versus-other-candidates axis. Only31–37% of interaction squared norm lies on that axis. After removing it, relative additive errors among nonreceiver candidates remain .926/.986 for matching donors and .482/.462 for mixed donors. Non-additivity is therefore not captured by a single receiver-confidence term. These squared-energy shares describe an orthogonal output decomposition, not unique causal mediation.

### Verification and scope

512 model forwards for the complete32-item-format by16-assignment factorial. Requested replacements exact. Identity logit replay <=1.77e-5; all candidate-logit changes for overlapping H791 single/matching conditions replay within7.63e-6. All metrics finite; model/input/reference/runner hashes unchanged. Original reserved test untouched; natural-document pool remains26,112.

Both formats retain strong H791 native competence. This is a reused panel for compositional discovery. Each format has16 lexical-item clusters; donor pairs and formats are correlated. Bootstrap intervals average donor pairs within item and are descriptive without multiplicity correction. Fixed output replacements leave other residual pathways native, so results do not directly characterize fully native mixed-value prompts or establish a minimal circuit.

### Research decision

L1 source representations carry partial donor content, including when sources disagree. Neither a simple additive model nor a universal agreement bonus adequately explains their downstream combination. The important unresolved structure is item-dependent nonlinear composition, not just the mean strength of a feature.

Next trace the factorial interaction through downstream attention outputs, MLP outputs and normalized inputs at source/query positions. Determine where interactions first appear and grow, while auditing that the traced runs reproduce the same final candidate responses. This can distinguish normalization effects, token-local bilinear mixing and later cross-position interactions before proposing a learned DAG. A useful featurizer must preserve per-example identity-specific finite responses; matching average reconstruction or average donor promotion is insufficient.

Previous turn was progress: H790 localized stronger effects to L1 value-source positions, but answer-margin changes could not separate actual donor promotion from receiver suppression or repeated-value inconsistency. The new prompts use Greek-label keys and16 transport-value words, keeping the two prior formats (vertical bars; colon/newline) fixed. There are16 items per format and four native variants per item: one receiver word, one designated alternate, and two additional donor words. Donor variants are fixed offsets3/7/11 in the value list; each is a legitimate value for the same key. They test whether effects follow the actual donor rather than any arbitrary alternate answer. Formats share lexical item indices and candidate words recur across items. This is fresh lexical confirmation, not an independent test of new formatting or other task families.

Both formats pass competence: all four native variants choose the correct candidate for every item; pooled intended full-vocabulary top1 is96.875% for vertical bars and100% for colon/newline. No outcome-based prompt or candidate selection was performed.

### Content-specificity result

Source interventions promote the actual donor word beyond a general loss of receiver confidence. Mean log-probability changes (natural-log units) and donor specificity are:

| Format | Site | Receiver log-probability change | Donor log-probability change | Donor-vs-receiver margin change | Donor-specific contrast |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Vertical bars | First source | +.056 | +.773 | +.717 | +.333 |
| Vertical bars | Second source | -.016 | +.546 | +.561 | +.201 |
| Vertical bars | Both sources | -.096 | +.868 | +.964 | +.510 |
| Vertical bars | Query | +.011 | -.003 | -.014 | +.003 |
| Colon/newline | First source | -.123 | +.759 | +.882 | +.284 |
| Colon/newline | Second source | -.137 | +.477 | +.614 | +.165 |
| Colon/newline | Both sources | -.066 | +.666 | +.732 | +.417 |
| Colon/newline | Query | +.009 | +.008 | -.001 | +.004 |

The donor-specific contrast is the donor's logit change minus the mean logit change of the14 candidates other than donor and receiver. The common log-probability normalization cancels in this contrast, so it is also the corresponding log-probability contrast. It tests specificity against this candidate set, not against every vocabulary item.

For both-source swaps, descriptive item-bootstrap intervals for specificity are [.416,.599] in vertical bars and [.320,.505] in colon/newline. All six source/site-format specificity intervals are positive; query effects are tiny. Thus pure receiver suppression is insufficient to explain the source results. Nevertheless, broad alternative promotion also occurs: the donor's log-probability increase is larger than its specificity advantage, and unrelated alternatives can improve substantially.

### Do effects follow the actual donor?

When donor variants2/3 are substituted, compare their actual word with the designated but unswapped alternate (variant1). Both-source swaps favor the actual donor by +.410 in vertical bars (interval [.229,.593]) and +.274 in colon/newline (interval [.078,.472]). The fixed alternate also gains relative to the receiver (+.536 and+.425 respectively), demonstrating a mixture of actual-donor specificity and broad alternative effects.

Single-source discrimination against that fixed alternate is weaker and not uniform: three of four single-source/site-format intervals span zero. The actual donor is the candidate with the largest nonreceiver logit increase in only33.3%/35.4% of joint-source interventions. These data do not support a perfectly selective dictionary lookup or clean content replacement.

### Behavioral limits and the prior joint-source hypothesis

No intervention changes the highest-scoring candidate away from the receiver or makes the donor the full-vocabulary top token. With both-source swaps, mean donor probability rises from .000571 to .000914 in vertical bars and from .000480 to .000633 in colon/newline. Mean receiver probability changes from .436 to .418 and .498 to .484. Donor promotion is measurable but small in absolute probability; this is not transplantation of the complete copying computation.

The earlier finding that both-source swaps were weaker than either single-source swap does not reproduce uniformly. On this panel, joint-source donor-margin gain exceeds both single-source gains in vertical bars and lies between them in colon/newline. Joint-source donor specificity is stronger than either single-source specificity in both formats. This weakens a universal “single-source inconsistency explains the entire effect” account. Context-dependent interactions and broad alternative promotion remain possible. The present panel uses three donors for each designated receiver rather than the earlier reciprocal-pair design, so it is not a controlled decomposition of which distribution change caused that difference.

### Audits

640 total model forwards. Requested output replacements are exact. Identity logits replay within1.77e-5 across batches. The independently computed logit-margin change and difference of log-probability changes agree within1.64e-6. All effects finite; model, manifest and runner hashes unchanged. Original reserved test untouched; natural-document pool remains26,112.

Bootstrap intervals use16 item clusters per format and average donor conditions within item. Shared vocabulary and shared cross-format items limit independence; intervals are descriptive without multiplicity correction. Native patch norms are saved and differ across sites/donors, so no matched-energy causal-efficiency claim follows. All16 candidate responses are saved for further analysis.

### Research decision

There is now a better-supported causal target for representation research: L1 source-output changes contain transferable information about which value was substituted, although the effect is partial and accompanied by nonspecific changes. This is evidence of content-bearing representations at a location, not yet evidence for a low-dimensional manifold, meaningful group partition, or computational DAG.

Next cross the donor identities at the two source positions: coherent A/A and B/B versus mixed A/B and B/A, plus single-source and receiver controls. Track promotion of each actual donor, unrelated candidates and the receiver. This will distinguish independent content contributions from an agreement-sensitive computation and provide a concrete compositional test for a shared dictionary or DAG. Preserve the native-output reference before asking a compressed featurizer to reproduce the identity-specific part of the response.

## H790 — Value-source swaps reveal stronger L1 effects and a non-additive two-source interaction

Previous turn was progress: H789 failed to clearly replicate the final-position L4 copying lead across formats. H790 tests the prespecified source/query localization alternative using native MLP-output replacements, rather than scaling synthetic directions.

On the H789 copying panel, replace the donor MLP output at the first value occurrence, second value occurrence, both values, final query token, or both values plus query. Layers1/4, all sites, reciprocal task edits, answer-preserving key renames and identity controls were specified before outcomes. Token offsets identify the two single-token value occurrences; exact token IDs are checked. Paired runs require equal sequence length and matching source/query positions. Downstream computation is fully live. This is a whole-model intervention readout, distinct from earlier isolated L5H5 value-path tests.

### Main results

Mean donor-directed answer-margin changes for task edits:

| Format | Layer | First source | Second source | Both sources | Query | Sources + query |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Vertical bars | 1 | +1.332 | +1.310 | +.958 | -.021 | +.935 |
| Colon/newline | 1 | +1.523 | +1.380 | +.745 | -.011 | +.736 |
| Vertical bars | 4 | +.118 | +.051 | +.177 | -.017 | +.166 |
| Colon/newline | 4 | +.065 | +.031 | +.095 | +.008 | +.096 |

The L1 single-source effects are consistently donor-aligned in both formats. Descriptive item-bootstrap intervals for first/second source are [1.087,1.579]/[1.033,1.580] in vertical bars and [1.226,1.841]/[1.152,1.637] in colon/newline. Each cell has16 lexical items,32 reciprocal task edits. Both formats have strong native task competence. These observations support location-specific sensitivity and show that weak query-position interventions did not imply weak source-position effects.

However, native source-output changes have larger norm than query changes. This is not a matched-energy site ranking or proof that every source direction is more causally important. L4 source changes have larger norms than L1 source changes but weaker answer effects, so input/output vector norm alone is also insufficient to explain the ranking.

No tested task intervention switches the binary answer preference to the donor (0/32 per site/layer/format). The interventions move margins but do not transplant the complete task computation. This is a donor-output substitution experiment, not proof of necessity or a minimal circuit.

### The informative non-additivity

At L1, replacing both value sources has less mean effect than replacing either individually, despite changing more coordinates. The RMS discrepancy between joint-source effect and the sum of separate-source effects is1.980 for vertical bars and2.473 for colon/newline. At L4 those discrepancies are only .0179/.0078. Adding the query to both-source swaps changes relatively little at either layer.

This sharpens the research question. A single-source swap creates a hybrid disagreement between the repeated value occurrences; swapping both makes the MLP outputs mutually consistent, although other residual paths remain receiver-native. The stronger single-source margin shift could therefore reflect disrupted agreement or suppression of the receiver answer, rather than greater transfer of donor identity. H790 records answer-margin differences and cannot distinguish donor promotion from receiver suppression. The non-additivity is observed; that proposed explanation remains a hypothesis.

### Alignment, controls and numerical audit

All64 reciprocal task edits and32 identity edits survive alignment. Only7/32 nuisance edits survive (1 vertical-bar case,6 colon/newline cases);25 key-renaming edits are excluded by the predeclared token-length/role-position rule. These sparse nuisance results cannot establish broad context invariance. All exclusions and token-role manifests are saved. The final query token is the last key token in vertical-bar prompts but a colon in colon/newline prompts, another reason not to equate the two query interventions semantically.

The initial absolute query-activation replay threshold of1e-4 failed. A diagnostic rerun localized the discrepancy to native MLP activations: maximum component error .001831 after different batching, while native logits differed by2.58e-5 and reference query-swap margins by5.73e-6. The final audited run additionally measured relative activation error (<=1.25e-6 L2), retained the1e-4 behavioral tolerance, and verified exact requested replacements. Identity logits differed by<=2.96e-5. This supports numerical replay agreement at activation scale, rather than silently treating the absolute threshold as passed.

Final audited run:1,126 model forwards (96 native contexts plus1,030 interventions). Two completed diagnostic attempts preceded it, each also1,126 forwards; total executed this experiment3,378. No failed-run results are used for scientific inference. All final metrics finite; source/model/input hashes unchanged. Original reserved test untouched; natural-document pool remains26,112. Bootstrap intervals cluster reciprocal edits by lexical item, are descriptive, and have no multiplicity correction. Formats share lexical items. This reused panel is localization discovery, not an independent confirmation set for a selected site.

### Decision and next discriminator

Prioritize native L1 value-source transformations over the weak final-position feature lead, but do not label the source effects a verified semantic manifold. The immediate experiment should distinguish donor promotion, receiver suppression and repeated-value inconsistency: measure both candidate log-probabilities separately and the full candidate distribution, retain single/both-source conditions, and include unrelated donor identities. Lock the site choices and use fresh prompts for confirmation. A reusable feature should transfer the intended identity specifically, rather than merely reduce confidence when copies disagree. If specificity transfers, compare compact shared representations against full source-output replacements; if not, pursue consistency computation rather than a dictionary-of-identities account.

### Decision

Next compare native donor MLP-output substitutions at the two copied-value source positions versus the final query position on this controlled copying panel. Predeclare individual-source, both-source, query and joint-source/query conditions at L1/L4; audit token alignment and exact identity controls. The purpose is to discriminate location-specific representation from a weak site choice, not to claim a manifold from another favorable average. ## H788 — Native-scale tests weaken the broad L1 story and retain a modest L4 copying lead

Previous turn was progress: H787 separated odd/even responses and discovered that fixed radius .30 extrapolated beyond most native donor displacements. H788 tests the predeclared alternative at fractions .25/.5/1 of each pair's actual donor angle, with both perturbation signs and explicit native input/output references.

For each receiver normalized MLP input, rotate toward or opposite the true donor tangent direction by a fraction of its native angular distance. Apply the same pair-specific angle to within-family shuffled and three seeded random tangent directions. Input norm remains fixed. Radius is matched across controls for each base/edit/layer, not across layers: this measures changes at native scales rather than fixed-size layer geometry. Negative and random directions are synthetic states even when their displacement magnitude matches a native edit; bounded distance does not prove manifold membership.

The same eight families and final-position sites L1/L4 are retained without outcome-based filtering. Native donor MLP input substitution and native donor MLP output substitution are evaluated independently. Positive true-direction fraction1 reaches the norm-scaled donor input. No new lexical/template data or fitting is introduced in this control experiment.

### Main findings

Native-scale L1 first-order module errors are much smaller than in the fixed-.30 tests. At the true positive endpoint:

| Competence-passing family | L1 relative module error | L4 relative module error | L1 native swap margin RMS | L4 native swap margin RMS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Agreement | .142 | .191 | .0366 | .0424 |
| Capital recall | .143 | .210 | .0266 | .1262 |
| Entity binding | .080 | .064 | .0239 | .0493 |
| Copying | .214 | .224 | .1184 | .1248 |

Thus L1 does not generally have the larger nonlinear error at native task scales: L4 is larger in three of the four competent families. This is compatible with the prior matched-radius result, because native L1 displacements are usually smaller. It corrects any interpretation that generic fixed-radius L1 curvature necessarily dominates natural task edits. Relative module error is interaction-vector norm divided by full-change norm, pooled in squared norm; it is not a causal share.

The clearest remaining directional lead is L4 copying. Its paired odd donor-directed mean grows smoothly with native-angle fraction:

| Fraction of native donor angle | True direction | Shuffled task direction | Random pooled |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| .25 | +.01268 | +.00293 | -.00183 |
| .50 | +.02486 | +.00586 | -.00356 |
| 1.00 | +.04576 | +.01176 | -.00642 |

At fraction1, true-minus-random is +.05218 with descriptive item-bootstrap interval [.01904,.08521]. True-minus-shuffled is +.03401 with interval [-.00252,.06464]. The same qualitative pattern holds at smaller fractions: positive true-versus-zero and true-versus-random intervals, but true-versus-shuffled intervals include zero. These use only eight reused items, cluster reciprocal edits and seeds within item, and have no multiplicity adjustment. They prioritize a test; they do not establish independent confirmation, a semantic feature, or a useful compression basis.

The odd effect is distinct from the native positive swap. L4 copying's actual donor-output swap has mean donor-directed effect only +.00274, despite odd mean +.04576: the even component contributes about -.04303 to this signed mean. Consequently the odd statistic cannot be reported as the native swap's net benefit. At L1 copying the odd mean is +.00972 with uncertainty spanning zero, whereas the native swap mean is -.03575. Agreement and capital recall show no clear positive true-direction odd effect on this panel. L4 entity binding has a small positive odd mean (+.01191), but does not clearly exceed shuffled or random controls.

The stronger L1 entity-binding response in the fixed-radius stress test collapses at native scale: native swap margin RMS is .0239 and mean donor-directed effect .00287. This cautions against building semantic feature claims from large off-native perturbations.

### Implementation checks

12,544 model forwards: 11,520 signed/control/fraction interventions, 768 native input/output reference runs, and 256 zero controls. No new natural documents or reserved-test evaluations.

Constant norm error <=1.34e-15; chord-radius error <=4.45e-16. True endpoint versus norm-scaled donor input error <=4.64e-14 relative L2. Actual donor/receiver normalized-input norms differ by at most 1.60e-7 relatively. Native input versus native output substitutions agree within 6.68e-6 answer margin. Positive true endpoint versus actual native output swap agrees within 8.11e-6, so the small norm discrepancy does not materially change this readout. Identity logits differ by at most 2.17e-5 across differently batched runs. All effects finite; source/model/input hashes unchanged.

Competence passes remain agreement, capital recall, entity binding and copying. Other families remain reported but cannot support successful-task interpretation. Original reserved test untouched; natural-document pool remains 26,112. Full records include nuisance edits and all fractions, not just the selected copying lead.

### Decision and next test

The broad hypothesis that early-layer finite nonlinearity directly reveals semantic units is weakened. General layer geometry, native displacement scale and even/odd downstream cancellation jointly explain why the stress tests looked stronger than natural swaps. We should stop expanding this reused panel merely to make a favorable contrast clearer.

Freeze L4 final-position copying as the primary next replication target, with L4 entity binding as a task comparator and L1 as a layer comparator. Use fresh vocabulary and wording, native-angle fractions fixed in advance, opposite signs, shuffled and random controls, actual donor-output endpoint references, and native competence gates. Evaluate odd direction sensitivity and net native-swap effects separately. A reproducible true-versus-shuffled advantage would motivate item-sensitive representations; transfer of shuffled directions would motivate shared family-level operators. Only if that causal structure transfers should a shared-dictionary/manifold featurizer be asked to compress it. No featurizer or manifold is newly validated by H788.

## Previous continuation: H787

## H787 — Sign pairing separates substantial even drift and exposes extrapolation beyond native edits

Previous turn was progress: H786 showed the L1/L4 nonlinear-error ordering in random directions, weakening task-specific interpretations. H787 tests opposite tangent rotations, preserves the exact previous positive-direction controls, and refreshes twenty hypotheses below.

For a normalized MLP input u and a unit tangent t, form v_plus=c*u+s*||u||*t and v_minus=c*u-s*||u||*t, where c=cos(theta), s=sin(theta). Both preserve ||u|| and share the radial displacement (c-1)*u. If Q is the MLP's homogeneous quadratic part, then:

    odd module change = [Q(v_plus)-Q(v_minus)]/2
    even module change = [Q(v_plus)+Q(v_minus)]/2 - Q(u)

The odd term equals c*s times the bilinear cross term between u and ||u||t. The even term equals (c^2-1)*Q(u)+s^2*Q(||u||t). The output bias cancels. The even term therefore includes both radial and tangent-quadratic contributions: this experiment does not attribute all even effects to radial drift alone.

We intervene separately with plus, minus, odd and even module-output changes, using the same true, within-family shuffled and three random directions as H786. Geometry is checked at chord/input radii .05/.15/.30; causal readouts use .30. The paired odd behavioral response is (margin_plus-margin_minus)/2; the paired even response is (margin_plus+margin_minus)/2 minus the native margin. Neither is assumed equal to the response from directly injecting the corresponding module component.

### Results on competence-passing tasks

For true directions at L1, the paired even answer-margin RMS is at least as large as the paired odd RMS in all four competence-passing families:

| Family | L1 odd RMS | L1 even RMS | L4 odd RMS | L4 even RMS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Agreement | .2799 | .3135 | .0674 | .0348 |
| Capital recall | .1808 | .2296 | .2111 | .0848 |
| Entity binding | .2472 | .2657 | .1846 | .0558 |
| Copying | .4170 | .5943 | .1667 | .0834 |

These are response magnitudes, not causal shares. Odd and even components can correlate or cancel.

The positive-direction L1 entity-binding intervention previously had mean donor-directed effect +.2092. Its sign-sensitive component has mean only +.0116; the paired even component accounts algebraically for the remaining +.1976. This demonstrates that the positive-only statistic was mostly not sensitive to the intended direction's sign. L1 copying retains a negative donor-directed odd mean (-.2252); L4 copying has a positive odd mean (+.0531). These are synthetic, site-local perturbations, not native donor swaps or whole-task necessity tests.

True-minus-shuffled donor-directed odd contrasts do not show a clear positive advantage in any of the four competent families/layers on this panel. L1 copying's contrast is negative: -.2195, with an item-cluster bootstrap interval [-.3624,-.0989]. L4 copying exceeds pooled random by +.0589, interval [.0162,.0999], but its true-minus-shuffled interval includes zero. L1 entity binding exceeds random because random odd response is negative, not because true odd response is large. The bootstrap uses eight items per family, groups reciprocal edits/seeds within item, and is descriptive without multiplicity correction; these are exploratory leads, not confirmed discoveries.

Directly injecting the odd module component does not reproduce the paired odd behavioral response. The L1 RMS discrepancy is .2384 for agreement and .5106 for copying; corresponding L4 discrepancies are .0220 and .0569. This confirms that downstream responses depend on the accompanying even component/background. Module-level algebra alone cannot justify additive behavioral attribution.

### Important follow-up diagnostic: native donor distances

After inspecting the parity results, we measured the unit-normalized chord distance between the actual receiver and donor MLP inputs. This diagnostic was not predeclared as a test outcome. At the final position, every one of the 64 L1 task pairs has native chord distance below .30; 63 of 64 L4 pairs do too. For competent families, the medians are:

| Family | L1 native distance | L4 native distance |
|---|---:|---:|
| Agreement | .0526 | .1873 |
| Capital recall | .0460 | .1488 |
| Entity binding | .0309 | .0694 |
| Copying | .1005 | .2382 |

Thus the matched .30 radius frequently extrapolates far beyond the native donor displacement, especially at L1. This does not invalidate the fixed-size geometric comparison, but sharply limits its interpretation as a natural semantic intervention. It also prevents concluding that the sign reversals reflect the native computation. H784's native source-position swaps remain a different experiment and are not refuted by this final-position diagnostic.

### Verification and scope

7,936 model forwards, 5,760 geometry cases. Exact quadratic parity formulas match to 3.02e-14 relative L2. Norm/radius checks remain at numerical precision. Recomputed positive patches match H785 to 4.77e-7; positive margin effects match H786 to 4.77e-6. Identity logits differ by at most 2.17e-5 across batches. Source/model/input hashes unchanged and effects finite. The original reserved test remains untouched; natural-document pool remains 26,112. All eight families are retained, but only agreement, capital recall, entity binding and copying pass native competence. Shared prompts, reciprocal edits, and seeds do not constitute independent replications.

### Current priorities

The best-supported account of the recent fixed-radius results is a combination of general quadratic layer geometry, sign-independent finite responses, and downstream background dependence. Natural task structure remains possible, but these stress tests have not isolated it. The most urgent unresolved alternative is extrapolation beyond native edit scales.

Next experiment: use a fraction of each pair's actual donor angle (e.g. .25/.5/1.0), with positive/negative true, shuffled and random directions at the same pair-specific radius. Include the actual native donor MLP output swap as the endpoint reference and audit any residual norm difference separately. Test whether the odd true-direction effect recovers donor-aligned behavior and exceeds shuffled/random controls within the natural scale. Freeze the design before outcomes. If it does, test held-out lexical/template transfer; if it does not, redirect attention toward site/path localization rather than fitting a new manifold to these final-position states.

### Twenty live hypotheses and the tests that distinguish them

These are competing or complementary hypotheses, not twenty established findings. Priorities reflect current evidence rather than numerical posterior probabilities.

1. **Generic quadratic layer geometry explains much of the L1/L4 contrast.** Supported by H786 random controls. Test sign-paired responses and separate module curvature from downstream gain.
2. **A common radial component of sphere rotations causes part of the apparent semantic effect.** Plausible from the intervention algebra. Compare opposite directions and explicitly isolate radial and tangent-quadratic contributions.
3. **Some task information lies in shared family-level directions.** True and shuffled directions often behave similarly. Freeze directions from discovery items and test new lexicons, templates and item identities.
4. **Item-specific directions carry additional binding information.** Not established by pooled geometry. Test true-minus-shuffled signed behavioral contrasts and fresh name/value permutations.
5. **Representations encode context-conditioned transformations more reliably than fixed activation vectors.** Consistent with background-dependent interventions. Fit compact local operators and compare cross-context finite-response prediction with fixed subspaces.
6. **A small reusable dictionary plus overlapping gates represents those operators.** Still unverified. Compare shared atoms against independent dictionaries at matched capacity, and ablate shared atoms across held-out combinations.
7. **Hierarchical gates capture inclusion relations.** Architecture remains a hypothesis, not inferred from low reconstruction loss. Require implication consistency, specificity and transfer on known nested synthetic structure and real semantic contrasts.
8. **A computational DAG captures reusable bilinear subcomputations.** Plausible for this architecture, but graph recovery remains open. Require interventions on a shared node to affect its distinct consumers and transfer to unseen combinations.
9. **Smooth nonlinear manifolds outperform linear groups.** Not established. Test local chart consistency, held-out interpolation, tangent transport and causal fidelity at matched reconstruction/parameter budgets.
10. **The best activation basis is not the best causal basis.** Supported by reconstruction/KL versus causal-transfer failures. Compare the same compression budgets under activation, KL, CE and finite-intervention objectives.
11. **Most model behavior depends on a small number of locally sensitive output directions.** Context-sensitive sensitivity evidence supports testing this. Evaluate local response spectra and how their span changes across contexts.
12. **Sensitivity changes are largely scalar gain changes rather than rotations.** Prior probe-gain results motivate this. Compare scalar gain, fixed anisotropy and context-dependent orientation on disjoint probes.
13. **RMS normalization contributes important apparent feature interactions.** H784 measured substantial scale-change terms. Separate normalized-input geometry from raw-residual interventions and test finite causal effects of each.
14. **Attention supplies context while token-local MLPs transform copied values.** Consistent with source-position graph-cut controls; broad minimality is unproven. Test path-specific routing/value perturbations on new formats and lexicons.
15. **Persistent value-bus contributions matter despite small isolated norms.** Norms alone cannot exclude conditional roles. Test bus/local combinations with sign and background controls.
16. **Early MLPs carry lexical identity; later ones carry context-dependent refinement.** A possible account of L1/L4 differences. Cross lexical identity with task context while matching displacement and source position.
17. **Cancellation across sites is essential, making additive attribution misleading.** Supported by joint-restoration failures. Test selected site interactions and predict joint effects from a model fit only to single-site responses.
18. **Apparent feature failure reflects vocabulary/category distribution shift.** The previous tools-to-fruits and colors-to-animals changes confound several shifts. Cross within-category versus between-category generalization independently.
19. **Off-native intervention states create effects absent from natural computation.** Still viable for sphere rotations and hybrid swaps. Compare native donor interpolation, norm-preserving paths, and natural-context perturbations at matched distances.
20. **Some apparent task findings reflect weak competence or answer-set artifacts.** Demonstrated as a concern by failed full-vocabulary gates. Require native competence, diverse answer alternatives and task-specific outcome checks before semantic claims.


Priority order: first resolve hypotheses 1/2/19 using native-scale sign controls; then distinguish 3/4/5 with frozen cross-item transfer; only then use the resulting causal targets to compare 6/7/8/9 at matched capacity. Hypotheses 10/11/12/13/17/20 remain evaluation constraints and competing explanations, rather than separate excuses to train more architectures. No manifold, universal semantic dictionary, or fundamental unit of computation is established yet.

## Previous continuation: H786

## H786 — Random directions reproduce the L1/L4 nonlinear-error ordering

Previous turn was progress: H785 established an L1/L4 difference under matched angular input perturbations across eight task families, with direct-input versus analytic-output verification. H786 tests whether that difference requires task-related directions.

At exactly the same H785 base states, compare the true donor displacement, the next sorted item's displacement within the same family and edit type, and three seeded isotropic Gaussian directions. All directions are projected into the current base state's tangent plane, normalized, then rotated on the same constant-norm sphere at chord/input ratios 0.05, 0.15 and 0.30. Shuffling never pairs an item with itself. The random seed is deterministic per item, edit and control, shared across layers before projection. Geometry is measured at all radii; full versus first-order causal output interventions are evaluated at radius 0.30 through all downstream model paths.

The prediction and control definitions were saved before model evaluation. This is a controlled follow-up on the reused H785 panel, not new lexical data. Random directions are size-matched in normalized input space; they do not match activation covariance, module-output magnitude, or downstream gain.

### Result that changes the research interpretation

L1's module-output first-order approximation error exceeds L4's for all eight families, all three radii, both task/nuisance base-edit sets, and each of the three random seeds. The same ordering holds for shuffled directions. Thus the broad L1/L4 ordering does not require true task directions. It supports general layer geometry as an explanation and weakens the interpretation that the ordering itself identifies task-specific features.

This is not evidence that every detail is generic, or that all task directions are equivalent to random. At radius 0.30, competence-passing families have the following pooled relative module errors (interaction norm divided by full-change norm, aggregated in squared norm):

| Family | L1 true | L1 shuffled | L1 random pooled | L4 true | L4 shuffled | L4 random pooled |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Agreement | .641 | .631 | .551 | .303 | .304 | .276 |
| Capital recall | .584 | .541 | .539 | .322 | .305 | .274 |
| Entity binding | .641 | .622 | .618 | .262 | .261 | .246 |
| Copying | .593 | .551 | .533 | .263 | .259 | .266 |

Random-pooled combines three draws per base state; these are not independent task observations. The within-family shuffled control retains task-family structure and often nearly reproduces true-direction geometry. It is not a null of “no task information.”

### Geometry and behavioral specificity remain different

At L1 and radius 0.30, the true/random first-order answer-margin error RMS is .250/.080 for agreement, .143/.168 for capital recall, .145/.261 for entity binding, and .133/.254 for copying. True directions do not uniformly produce greater behavioral approximation error. These are absolute discrepancies, not causal attribution fractions.

Donor-directed mean margin change is also mixed. For L1 entity binding it is +.209 for true directions, +.198 for shuffled directions and +.163 for random directions. For L1 copying it is -.246, -.032 and -.119 respectively. A positive value denotes movement toward the donor's intended answer contrast; these spherical final-position perturbations need not move the answer as a native donor swap would. Random controls can cause structured, base-dependent effects, so positive mean movement alone would not verify a reusable semantic direction.

The same competence restrictions apply: agreement, capital recall, entity binding and copying pass; the other four families fail the predeclared gate and support only geometric descriptions, not successful-task claims. Reciprocal edits, items, families, and seeds are correlated; sentiment/negation nuisance native contexts are duplicated.

### Verification

5,760 module-geometry cases and 4,096 whole-model forwards, including 256 zero-intervention controls. Constant norm preserved to 1.12e-15 relative error and chord radius to 1.67e-16 absolute error. Recomputed true-direction patches replay H785 within 4.77e-7 maximum component error; true-direction answer effects replay within 4.77e-6. Identity logit discrepancies across batches are <=1.72e-5. All effects finite; input, reference, runner and model hashes unchanged. Original reserved test untouched; natural-document pool remains 26,112. No training or featurizer selection was performed.

### Next high-information discriminator

A constant-norm rotation has a sign-independent radial component: for opposite tangent directions, v_plus=cos(theta)u+sin(theta)||u||t and v_minus=cos(theta)u-sin(theta)||u||t. Both include (cos(theta)-1)u. The quadratic map can therefore produce a common even response, including for random directions. H786 does not distinguish that common response from direction-specific odd responses.

Next evaluate paired positive/negative tangent rotations and separate their odd and even module changes and behavioral responses. Compare true, shuffled and random directions, with base-paired inference and competence-passing tasks emphasized. This can distinguish directional semantic effects from generic radial/quadratic responses before fitting more feature groups. Then refresh the broader ~20-hypothesis tournament and choose a transfer experiment targeting the best-supported alternatives. No meaningful manifold or fundamental computation unit is yet verified by these controls.

## Previous continuation: H785

## H785 — L1's greater finite nonlinearity survives angular-size control across eight task families

Previous turn was progress: H784 verified exact factor decomposition and found a large first-order causal-readout error for finite L1 copied-value edits. H785 tests the predeclared prediction that the L1/L4 difference persists after matching normalized-input displacement size and extending beyond copying.

We took all eight transfer items from each of the eight established task families and added the fixed prefix “Complete the following sentence:” plus newline to every context. This creates new contexts but reuses underlying items and vocabulary; it is not an independent lexical replication. The manifest, layer choices, radii, prediction and competence gate were saved before model evaluation. No examples or families were selected based on observed intervention results.

At each final-position normalized MLP input u, project the donor direction onto u's tangent plane. Rotate along that direction on the sphere with radius ||u||, at chord distances rho*||u|| for rho=0.05, 0.15, 0.30. This keeps input norm fixed and makes displacement size equal relative to input norm across L1 and L4. It does not hold the donor direction, local Jacobian gain, activation distribution, or semantic change fixed across layers. The perturbations are synthetic intermediate states, not native prompt interpolations.

For the resulting displacement du, compare the exact bilinear output change against its first-order approximation at u. Apply each output change to the receiver's final-position MLP output and run all downstream computation. This readout covers all downstream paths from that site, unlike H784's two-pass isolation through L5H5 source values. Consequently, effect sizes from the two experiments are not directly comparable.

### Main result

L1 has greater module-output first-order approximation error than L4 in every task family at every tested radius, for both task and same-answer nuisance directions. This includes the four competence-passing families. These are descriptive comparisons of pooled errors, not independent significance tests.

| Relative chord distance | L1 relative output error range across task families | L4 relative output error range |
|---|---:|---:|
| 0.05 | 0.095–0.131 | 0.043–0.056 |
| 0.15 | 0.281–0.379 | 0.130–0.169 |
| 0.30 | 0.523–0.675 | 0.262–0.340 |

Relative output error is sqrt(sum ||interaction||^2 / sum ||full change||^2). It is a first-order approximation error, not an explained causal fraction. The tested finite interaction is measured around the receiver expansion point; midpoint linearization of a quadratic map would give an exact finite difference. Thus these results concern fixed-background linear approximations, not proof that a quadratic function cannot be represented through a moving derivative.

For competence-passing families at radius 0.30:

| Family | L1 relative module error | L4 relative module error | L1 answer-margin error RMS | L4 answer-margin error RMS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Agreement | 0.641 | 0.303 | 0.2498 | 0.0222 |
| Capital recall | 0.584 | 0.322 | 0.1431 | 0.0579 |
| Entity binding | 0.641 | 0.262 | 0.1453 | 0.0507 |
| Sequence copying | 0.593 | 0.263 | 0.1330 | 0.0331 |

Answer-margin error is the RMS discrepancy between first-order and full interventions. Full intervention effect RMS values for those families are respectively L1: 0.3067, 0.1754, 0.3941, 0.6812; L4: 0.0659, 0.2460, 0.2140, 0.1512. Output approximation error and behavioral sensitivity are different quantities; the L1/L4 relation in one does not imply the same effect magnitude in the other. No causal relative-error claims are made where effects are small.

### Competence and scope

The gate requires >=4 token-valid pairs, >=75% correct paired choices at both endpoints, and >=50% pooled intended full-vocabulary top1. Agreement, capital recall, entity binding and copying pass. Context association, negation, relational order and sentiment fail. All eight remain reported, but failed families do not support claims of successful task computation. Relational order has 0% paired choice correctness; context association has 100% paired choice correctness but 0% intended full-vocabulary top1, illustrating why contrast accuracy alone is insufficient.

Task edits use both directions; nuisance edits use the unchanged-answer context; identity edits use zero displacement. Sentiment and negation reuse the same base/nuisance contexts, so their nuisance results are duplicates, not independent evidence. Family and reciprocal-edit observations are correlated.

### Audits

64 pairs, 192 native contexts, no tokenization exclusions and no degenerate tangent directions. Main experiment: 3,264 model forwards. Sphere norm is preserved to 1.12e-15 relative error; target chord radius to 1.67e-16 absolute error. Analytic output replay has <=1.03e-6 relative L2 error. Identity logit discrepancy is <=1.67e-5 across differently batched executions; it is not exact zero. All effects are finite and the manifest hash is unchanged.

An independent implementation check directly replaces the normalized MLP input rather than adding an analytically computed output change. Across all task/nuisance edits, both layers, all eight families at radius 0.30 (384 additional forwards), direct-input versus analytic-output interventions agree within 1.01e-5 answer margin and 1.35e-6 output relative L2. This validates the construction without relying solely on its algebraic self-check. Total forwards including this audit: 3,648. Original reserved test untouched; natural-document pool remains 26,112.

### Research implication and next discriminator

The L1/L4 difference is not explained solely by the original edits having different displacement sizes, and it extends beyond copying at this final-position site. This supports evaluating featurizers on finite transformations across backgrounds. It does not establish semantic specificity, a reusable manifold, or a unique fundamental unit of computation.

The next critical alternative is general layer geometry: L1 might have larger finite interaction for arbitrary tangent directions. Compare seeded random, shuffled-task and true donor directions at the same base states/radii, with output geometry and downstream sensitivity evaluated separately. If random controls reproduce the difference, prioritize context-dependent quadratic geometry over task-specific interaction features. If true directions show additional reproducible structure, test whether shared features or small computational graphs capture that excess. Refresh the broader hypothesis tournament after these controls rather than adding more unmotivated architecture variants.

## Previous continuation: H784

## H784 — Finite L1 value edits require the bilinear interaction term

Previous turn was progress: H783 established non-additive joint restorations and passed exact graph-cut controls. H784 moves inside the implicated L1/L4 MLPs, testing exact algebra before causal interpretation.

For normalized MLP input u, let L=Left(u), R=Right(u), and D=Down. The module is D(L*R)+bias, with elementwise product and no activation gate in this checkpoint. A receiver-to-donor change obeys:

    delta_output = D(delta_L * R) + D(L * delta_R) + D(delta_L * delta_R)

The first two terms sum to the first-order approximation at the receiver normalized input. The third is the finite bilinear interaction. The common output bias cancels. We capture the actual native factors, compute the decomposition in float64, and test each term, their first-order sum, their full sum, and the native output difference at both copied-value positions. Each first-pass intervention adds the selected term to a receiver MLP output. A second pristine receiver run reads only its resulting L5H5 local-value change, with native receiver routing. This preserves the previous isolated-pathway definition.

### Results

All numbers below are answer-margin RMS across aligned edits. Error is the RMS discrepancy from the native single-module donor-output substitution, not from the full donor prompt or the earlier joint restorations.

| Edit | Site | Native site-swap effect RMS | First-order-only effect RMS | First-order error | Interaction-only effect RMS |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Copied-value change | L1 | 0.2458 | 0.4857 | 0.3562 | 0.1882 |
| Copied-value change | L4 | 0.1500 | 0.1612 | 0.0484 | 0.0472 |
| Key rename | L1 | 0.1029 | 0.0989 | 0.0295 | 0.0273 |
| Key rename | L4 | 0.1176 | 0.1238 | 0.0247 | 0.0244 |

For these finite L1 value changes, the first-order approximation is poor, and the interaction term is necessary to reproduce the actual module-output change and its isolated causal readout. The L4 value-change discrepancy is smaller. This does not prove a special L1 computation: differences in input displacement, representation scale, and subsequent transformations could explain the contrast. Separately intervened term effects need not add after downstream nonlinearities.

Neither individual factor change reproduces the full L1 task site swap: left-only and right-only margin errors are 0.1646 and 0.1638. Their similar errors do not establish symmetric semantic roles, nor does naming factors Left/Right assign either one a meaningful gate/content interpretation.

At the module-output level, the interaction norm relative to the full change is 0.686 for L1 task edits, 0.425 for L4 task edits, 0.243 for L1 key renames, and 0.313 for L4 key renames. These are vector norm ratios, not causal shares. First-order terms and interaction can cancel. This receiver-anchored expansion is not a unique semantic decomposition: for a quadratic function, expanding about the midpoint can absorb the finite interaction into the midpoint derivative.

### Normalization diagnostic

We also captured the raw residual immediately before MLP RMS normalization. With r(x)=sqrt(mean(x^2)+epsilon), the normalized-input change decomposes exactly as:

    u_d - u_r = (x_d-x_r)/r_r + x_d*(1/r_d-1/r_r)

The second term is the normalization-scale change. Its norm relative to the total normalized-input change is 0.278 (L1 task), 0.102 (L4 task), 0.486 (L1 key rename), and 0.097 (L4 key rename). It partly cancels the fixed-scale raw-change term in every pooled case. These are geometric diagnostics, not causal tests of normalization, and the fixed-scale raw-change term need not be a pure angular change.

### Verification and limitations

The initial absolute output-decomposition threshold of 1e-4 failed: maximum float32-versus-float64 discrepancy was 0.001263. We did not treat that as evidence against the algebra or silently loosen the absolute threshold. The float64 algebra identity holds to 5.61e-16 relative L2; the maximum relative L2 discrepancy from actual float32 module changes is 2.46e-6. Full reconstructed versus native site-swap readouts differ by at most 9.54e-6 in answer margin, with pooled RMS differences about 2.5e-6. Native site-swap readouts replay H781 exactly. These checks support a numerical-rounding explanation for the absolute discrepancy at the scale of these activations.

These are reused exploratory copying cases. They demonstrate finite nonlinear structure along a selected pathway, not verified manifolds, semantic labels, a complete model explanation, or a causal explanation of all H783 joint-restoration effects. No new featurizer has been validated here.
