## Previous continuation: H783

## H783 — Joint restorations reveal interacting contributions to the copied-value pathway

The question was whether the early/late MLP effects identified by individual restorations combine independently. We jointly restored receiver module outputs during a donor run, at both copied-value source positions, then measured only the resulting L5H5 local-value change in a fresh receiver run. This two-pass intervention excludes other downstream paths. Task edits change copied values; nuisance edits rename keys while preserving the requested answer.

The measured effect is the change in the answer logit margin, summarized as root mean square (RMS) across edits. It is a selected pathway's causal readout, not whole-model accuracy or a fraction of computation explained.

| Receiver outputs restored in donor run | Task surviving margin RMS | Key-renaming surviving margin RMS |
|---|---:|---:|
| None: complete target | 0.2692 | 0.1723 |
| L1 MLP | 0.1154 | 0.1378 |
| L4 MLP | 0.1653 | 0.0875 |
| L1 + L4 MLP | 0.0843 | 0.0706 |
| L3 + L4 MLP | 0.0997 | 0.0614 |
| L1 + L3 + L4 MLP | 0.0714 | 0.0592 |
| All five MLPs | 0.0665 | 0.0566 |
| All five attention outputs | 0.7490 | 0.0000 |
| All ten outputs | 0.0609 | 0.0000 |

Joint MLP restorations suppress more of this readout than either selected individual restoration. The selected three MLPs approach the all-MLP result on this reused panel. This prioritizes those sites for targeted follow-up, but does not establish a minimal circuit or a transferable feature representation.

The contributions are strongly non-additive. Predicting a joint restoration by subtracting the sum of individually removed vectors from the target fails even before the downstream model: the L1+L4 task vector discrepancy is 42.9% of target vector RMS; for all MLPs it is 197.8%. The corresponding margin discrepancies are 0.1370 and 0.5653. Thus assigning independent causal shares to those MLPs would be misleading. These comparisons diagnose context-dependent upstream transformations; they do not identify which nonlinearity is responsible.

Restoring all attention outputs amplifies the task readout to 0.7490. This hybrid keeps changed source embeddings while substituting receiver attention additions, altering the MLP trajectory and potentially removing cancellation. It is not evidence that attention is irrelevant or harmful. The experiment alone does not distinguish cancellation from other nonlinear background effects.

For key renames, all-attention and all-output restorations return local values exactly to receiver values. This is an expected graph-cut control: source embeddings are unchanged, attention imports context, and MLPs are token-local. Restoring each attention output at those positions makes subsequent MLP inputs match the receiver. The zero result verifies the implementation; it is not discovery of a minimal semantic circuit. Task edits change source embeddings and repeated x0 inputs, explaining why an all-output reset need not eliminate their effect.

Audits: 9,024 model forwards, 480 aligned edits (256 task, 96 nuisance, 128 identity), with the same 32 excluded nuisance alignments. Both expected nuisance resets, previous single-site replay, native logits/local values, exact output replacement, identity interventions, and the H780 target readout all match exactly. Metrics are finite and model/input/source hashes unchanged. The original reserved test was not used; natural-document pool remains 26,112. Groups were selected from earlier screens and this panel is exploratory, not independent confirmation.

Research implication: verified reusable units will need to preserve transformations across computational backgrounds, not merely reconstruct activation clouds. The current evidence favors an interacting, context-conditioned value pathway over independent additive module contributions; it does not yet verify a manifold, hierarchy, or computational DAG featurizer.

Next: inspect the exact bilinear MLP algebra at L1/L4 and partition observed changes into the two linear-in-change terms and their interaction, including RMS-normalization effects separately. Validate numerical reconstruction before causal readouts. Then freeze a specific mechanistic prediction and test fresh lexical/context combinations and additional tasks, rather than optimizing further on this copying panel. Return to featurizer/manifold comparisons using those transferable causal criteria.

Previous goal turn was progress: H779 localized answer-change effects to local values at copied-word positions, but its nuisance “other” category mixed unchanged value words with separators. H780 resolves that ambiguity using source roles shared across task and nuisance modes.

For answer-changing task edits, both value-word positions reproduce H779's changed-word component exactly. Their error to the complete value effect remains9.3–17.5% on the novel cohorts. Previous goal turn was progress: H778 showed that receiver routing applied to donor-minus-receiver values approximated task edits much better than routing changes alone. H779 localizes that value term instead of assuming it is already pure word-identity transport.

The intervention destination is always the final L5H5 query. For task edits, the changed positions are the two copied-value words. For nuisance key renames, the changed positions are keys, so the meaning of the changed/other partition differs between modes. The query takes precedence when its token changes, making the partition disjoint and exhaustive.

Independently partition V into(1−lambda)local+lambda layer0bus, with lambda=−.0563965. Capture both streams from the actual model and evaluate the six crossed stream/position components as well. No representation is fitted. All results use the same480aligned edits as H778:256directed task edits,96nuisance edits and128identity edits;32nuisance alignment exclusions remain.

| Task cohort | Complete value-effect RMS | Local-only error to value effect | Changed-word-only error to value effect | Query-only effect RMS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Old keys / old values | .2336 | .0185 | .0308 | .0047 |
| New keys / old values | .2556 | .0185 | .0383 | .0061 |
| Old keys / new values | .3116 | .0180 | .0547 | .0050 |
| New keys / new values | .3036 | .0219 | .0281 | .0057 |

Relative to the full head edit, changed-word-only errors remain29–40%, because routing changes and interaction terms are omitted. Keeping that distinction prevents inflating the result into near-complete model explanation.

Vector norms tell a consistent but non-attributional story: changed-word components have94–98% of the complete value-term RMS, query components about1.7–2.2%, and the persistent bus about7.3–8.7%. Local-stream component norms are slightly above100%, compatible with the signed bus contribution partially cancelling them. These are norm ratios, not percentages of causal responsibility. The layer-zero bus alone has small task margin RMS (.017–.020) and does not reproduce the full value effect.

Nuisance key renaming is different. The local stream almost exactly reproduces the value-only nuisance effect (absolute error.00055–.00101). But the dominant vector change lies in the “other” positions—tokens whose text is unchanged—rather than in the renamed keys or final query. “Other” nuisance components have about99–100% of the value-term RMS, and their absolute margin error to the complete nuisance value effect is.0176–.0464. This weakens a pure context-free word-identity interpretation: changing a key can change local values at unchanged positions. ## Previous continuation: H778

## H778 — Value changes approximate copying edits better than routing changes alone

Previous goal turn was progress: H777 established that the frozen rank-eight contrast bases do not transfer faithfully across lexical changes. H778 moves from compressing whole head outputs to testing the actual attention factorization.

The inspected L5 attention is signed bilinear attention, not softmax attention. After headwise RMS normalization and RoPE, its routing matrix is A=(QK^T/128)⊙(Q2K2^T/128), with a causal mask. The head output is H=A V. V mixes the layer-local value projection with the persistent layer-zero value stream. At L5 the learned mixture coefficient is−.0563965, so this is a non-convex mixture; it must not be interpreted as a probability.

Capture the actual factors from the running model, then for receiver r and donor d decompose:

ΔH = (Ad−Ar)Vr + Ar(Vd−Vr) + (Ad−Ar)(Vd−Vr).

The three terms are routing-only, value-only and interaction, respectively. Their sum is algebraically the full head change. Intervene with each term, routing-plus-value, all terms together and the full native head difference, at query, source and both positions. These are receiver-centered interventions, not unique causal attribution fractions. Reciprocal answer edits are retained.

All256directed task edits and128identity edits are aligned. Thirty-two of128nuisance edits have different token lengths or source positions and are excluded from this factorwise analysis under the prespecified alignment requirement;96nuisance edits remain. Task comparisons therefore use the complete H777task panel, while nuisance aggregates differ from H777 and must not be compared as if they used identical rows.

| Query task cohort | Full effect RMS | Routing-only error | Value-only error | Routing+value error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Old keys / old values | .2373 | .2373 | .0583 | .0343 |
| New keys / old values | .2737 | .2545 | .0993 | .0381 |
| Old keys / new values | .3183 | .3229 | .0801 | .0269 |
| New keys / new values | .3023 | .3254 | .0861 | .0480 |

Errors are absolute RMS differences from the full edit's answer-margin effect. In the three novel cohorts, value-only relative errors are36.3%,25.2% and28.5%; routing-only errors are93.0%,101.4% and107.6%. Routing-plus-value errors are13.9%,8.4% and15.9%. Thus native receiver routing applied to changed values approximates the full task edit substantially better than changed routing applied to receiver values. The interaction still matters, and the result is not perfect causal preservation.

In vector space, value-only component RMS is96–98% of full task-difference RMS, routing25–34%, and interaction11–14%. These norm ratios do not sum to100% because vectors can align or cancel. Their corresponding margin effects also do not add exactly: the RMS discrepancy between full margin change and the sum of separately intervened component margin changes is.0088–.0207 across task cohorts. Applying all components together, however, reproduces the full edit numerically, as required.

This is evidence that the tested copying head edits are largely carried through changes in V, not merely changes in attention coefficients. It is compatible with a compact routing operation acting on variable content, but does not establish compact routing, high-dimensional semantic identity, or a reusable manifold. V already contains upstream contextual computation, and its changes can occur at unchanged tokens—including the query—as well as at copied-token positions. The value-only intervention retains all value dimensions, so its better fidelity is not a matched-rank comparison with the failed rank-eight bases.

Nuisance changes also involve both factors; they do not become a pure routing component. All aligned nuisance, source-only and joint-position results are saved, along with excluded rows. The component conclusions apply to this head, these copying tasks and the receiver-centered decomposition; no necessity or whole-model explanation is claimed.

## Previous continuation: H776

## H776 — Task-informed rank-eight contrasts transfer partially, not uniformly

Previous goal turn was progress: H775 established that small natural-KL gains did not materially preserve copying interventions. H776 asks whether a task-informed representation of the same rank can do better, separating learning-objective limitations from an overly strong claim that rank eight is impossible.

Train on eight predetermined copying pairs: item indices0–3 in semicolon and newline formats. Fit SVD bases to answer-changing activation differences in write geometry, either final-query only or pooled query/source differences. Controls are a basis fitted to nuisance-query differences on those same pairs, ordinary natural write-PCA8, and three fixed random rank-eight write-space subspaces. Every basis has rank eight; the pooled basis is shared across query and source, not eight dimensions per position. No output logits, margin effects or validation outcomes are used to fit or choose a basis.

Test all original32pairs, reciprocal answer changes, nuisance and identity edits at query, source and both positions. Split results by whether item and format were included in fitting. The item holdout is not a vocabulary holdout: cyclic donor pairing causes some answer tokens to appear on both sides of the split. Each crossed cohort contains only four item indices in two formats, with correlated cases.

| Query task cohort | Full effect RMS | Natural PCA8 error | Query-contrast8 error | Pooled-contrast8 error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Training items, training formats | .2350 | .2419 | .0000035 | .0511 |
| Held-out items, training formats | .2043 | .1337 | .1831 | .1813 |
| Training items, held-out formats | .2390 | .2243 | .1283 | .1085 |
| Held-out items, held-out formats | .2669 | .2440 | .2405 | .1799 |

Errors are absolute RMS differences from the full-head edit's answer-margin effect. The query-only training matrix has eight rows, so a rank-eight basis reproduces those training vectors exactly; the near-zero training causal error is an algebraic implementation check, not evidence of discovery.

Held-out transfer is heterogeneous. Pooling query and source contrasts helps on held-out formats: on the doubly held-out cohort its relative effect error is67.4%, versus91.4% for natural PCA and90.1% for query-only contrasts. Random-subspace absolute errors there range.2434–.2566, compared with.1799 for pooled contrasts. But in familiar formats with held-out items, both task-informed bases are worse than ordinary PCA (.181–.183 versus.134). The query-only basis transfers format changes for familiar items substantially better than item changes. None is a reliable universal rank-eight representation.

Vector preservation and effect preservation again diverge. On the doubly held-out cohort, pooled contrasts leave84.9% relative write-vector RMS residual versus80.4% for query-only contrasts, yet preserve the margin effect better. A lower activation reconstruction error alone would select the wrong basis in this comparison. The result is compatible with source contrasts adding behaviorally relevant directions, but it does not by itself establish a reusable source/value computation.

Nuisance controls also expose selectivity limits. On held-out items in familiar formats, the nuisance-trained basis has39.7% relative nuisance-effect error versus71.0% for pooled answer contrasts and76.0% for natural PCA. Conversely, nuisance-trained task error there is.2532, worse than both task-informed and natural bases. This supports distinct contrast-dependent directions on this panel, without proving a clean semantic decomposition or absence of interactions. All nuisance/source/joint outcomes are saved; no favorable subspace is selected post hoc.

Audits:3,072 model forwards; full/PCA margins exactly replay H761; basis orthogonality error<=1.78e-15; training-query relative vector residual1.73e-15; frozen-fit hash unchanged; native identity replay<=2.17e-5; full-donor vector error<=1.77e-5; finite outputs and input/model hashes unchanged. No reserved-test evaluation; natural document pool stays26,112.

Conclusion for the research direction: task-informed directions can improve some held-out causal effects at rank eight, so the earlier failure is not solely explained by rank. But the failure on other item splits and the large remaining errors prevent a verified-manifold claim. This experiment is not a mathematical upper bound on what rank eight can represent and is not an unsupervised featurizer result.

Next: keep these bases frozen and test lexical transfer explicitly. Cross old/new key words with old/new value words across the same formats, using new values disjoint from the eight training value words. Establish native competence before interpreting interventions; include answer-changing and nuisance controls. This distinguishes transferable copying structure from lexical/template-specific directions more directly than the current overlapping-token item split. Report all lexical cohorts, not just the best-performing format.

## H775 — Small natural-KL gains do not establish better causal preservation

Previous goal turn was progress: H774 found a small, uncertain natural-text KL gain with broader training coverage and retained all fits. H775 tests whether that change preserves actual computation under interventions.

Every compressed edit adds F(donor)-F(receiver) to the native activation; downstream computation remains live.

For each intervention, the full head edit supplies the reference answer-margin change and output distribution. We measure margin approximation error and KL(full edit||compressed edit). The latter is distinct from native-to-edit KL: faithfully preserving an important edit can require changing the native output substantially. Relative margin errors are reported only when native task competence passes and full-effect RMS>=.25; absolute errors remain available everywhere.

Nuisance effects also do not consistently improve. For newline query nuisance edits, relative error changes from64.7% for PCA to67.1% for direct KL. The diverse suite was genuinely evaluated across all five families, but its diagnostic power at this particular head/site is limited. Competent agreement, binding and capital-format-B full task effects have RMS only.0035–.0100, so their small absolute errors cannot establish broadly preserved computation. Capital-format-A and both sentiment formats retain their existing native competence failures. These are reported as diagnostics, not silently removed or promoted into successful generalization. Competence-gated relative results are consequently concentrated in copying.

Paired item bootstraps retain reciprocal directions and all schedules within each item. Most direct-KL versus PCA comparisons include zero. Interpretation: these rank-eight natural-data fits are not verified featurizers for manifold interpretation. Neither reconstruction training nor direct-KL training demonstrated a substantive causal gain here. The result leaves two different possibilities: eight shared directions may be insufficient across these computations, or the natural-data objectives may fail to find the relevant directions. Existing higher-capacity curves show that more coordinates can help but do not resolve whether a suitably learned low-dimensional task representation exists.

Next: fit an explicitly task-informed rank-eight contrast subspace on a predetermined subset of copying activation differences, then test held-out items/formats, nuisance controls and actual causal effects against the same references. Use no output outcomes to select directions. Include random/ordinary PCA controls and report training versus held-out vector coverage. This is a diagnostic of representational capacity and transfer, not a mathematical causal upper bound or an unsupervised discovery. If it transfers, the learning objective/data are implicated; if it fails, do not conclude impossibility from one fitted subspace. Only after a reliable representation is established should its geometry be interpreted as a computational manifold.

## Previous continuation: H769

## H769 — A scalar sensitivity estimate transfers to withheld probe directions

Previous goal turn was progress: H768 established context heterogeneity without categorical sampling noise, but did not establish consistent special alignment between errors and their original contexts. This experiment tests whether overall sensitivity inferred from one probe bank transfers to another bank on separate documents.

Design: 32 training documents and 16 validation documents, each at prefix lengths 32 and 120. Training documents exclude the H764 gradient-estimation panel; validation documents exclude the H765/H767 validation panel. All documents were already in the natural research pool, so these are newly probed contexts, not a new corpus or untouched reserved test. Twenty-four fixed independent isotropic random directions are shared across contexts. Their common norm is fixed from the training median budget-8 adaptive write-PCA reconstruction error. Probe responses are local Fisher curvature estimated by central logit differences and full-vocabulary probability variance.

The first 12 probes are observed at an evaluation context; the remaining 12 responses are withheld there. Target directions are measured on training documents, so this is prediction at new contexts for known directions, not extrapolation to never-measured directions.

Four predictors are fitted using training documents only. Static predicts each target direction's training mean. Scalar multiplies that mean by the observed probes' average response relative to their training means. Two richer predictors fit residual directional variation after dividing out this scalar: a rank-two ridge map and a full ridge map. Ridge strength .1 and rank two were fixed before outcomes; no validation selection was performed. These are continuous regression controls, not discrete semantic regimes or groups.

| Predictor | Validation relative RMS error | Median relative error |
|---|---:|---:|
| static | 82.3% | 108.6% |
| scalar | 54.6% | 42.6% |
| scalar_rank2 | 54.2% | 42.2% |
| scalar_full_ridge | 57.1% | 41.3% |

The scalar estimate improves substantially over a context-independent prediction. Rank-two residual structure provides only a small pooled gain, and full residual regression performs worse on validation despite better training fit. Scalar improvement appears at both lengths: relative RMS error falls from 77.9% to 61.0% at length 32 and from 89.2% to 42.0% at length 120. The rank-two correction improves length 32 slightly but worsens length 120.

A descriptive 10,000-draw paired bootstrap resamples the 16 validation documents, averaging the two lengths and 12 target directions within each document. The static-minus-scalar MSE interval is entirely positive. Rank-two-minus-scalar and full-ridge-minus-scalar intervals both include zero. These intervals omit fitted-estimator uncertainty and multiple-comparison correction; they support prioritization, not a broad statistical claim.

The remaining 54.6% scalar RMS prediction error is substantial. A scalar does not adequately describe all directional geometry. Nor does this experiment show that richer geometry cannot be learned with more data, a better estimator, or a different probe bank. It shows that this small directional regression does not yet justify additional complexity over the scalar control.

Crucially, all predictors receive model-derived probe responses at evaluation time. This is not yet an activation-only sensitivity estimator, a new featurizer, or proof that scalar-weighted feature learning improves causal fidelity. Random probes also differ from reconstruction errors and task interventions. Any learned feature objective must be validated on actual KL and causal task edits, not merely probe prediction.

Audits: 11,520 forward evaluations; finite curvatures; two numerical steps agree within .42% relative RMS (median relative difference .32%). Training/validation documents are disjoint and excluded from the specified earlier panels. Hashes unchanged; neither directional predictor required clipping a negative validation factor. Original reserved test untouched; unique natural document pool remains 26,112.

Next: determine whether simple activation-derived quantities predict the scalar gain on held-out documents, using a fixed small predictor and reporting both gain prediction and target-probe errors. If that succeeds, compare sensitivity-weighted and unweighted feature learning at matched capacity. If it fails, obtain training-only probe weights directly rather than claiming a usable activation predictor. Preserve scalar weighting as a control when testing richer conditional geometry. The ultimate gate remains manifold stability, held-out combination transfer and selective causal effects across diverse competent tasks.

## Previous continuation: H768

## H768 — Context sensitivity is highly heterogeneous; special error/context alignment is not established

Previous goal turn was progress: H767 produced a concrete local-versus-global discrepancy and a refreshed hypothesis set. H768 tests that discrepancy without categorical Monte Carlo sampling.

For each of the same 16 validation documents at lengths 32 and 120, take its adaptive write-PCA reconstruction error at budgets 8 and 64. Apply that identical error direction to every one of the 16 contexts of matching length. This yields four 16-by-16 curvature matrices, 1,024 context/direction pairs. Rows identify the context that produced the error; columns identify the context in which its local output sensitivity is measured. Central differences at 1% and 2% estimate directional logit derivatives, and exact full-vocabulary native probabilities give their variance. These are numerical local Fisher evaluations, not full finite-edit transfer tests.

A diagonal entry measures the original context/error pairing. Averaging a row measures that same error direction under the panel-average metric. This directly tests averaging over contexts, without the older metric's categorical sampling noise or training/validation context mismatch.

| Prefix length | Budget | Matched / other-context mean curvature | Ratio after destination sensitivity normalization | Panel-average prediction relative RMS error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | 8 | 8.12 | 1.41 | 90.4% |
| 32 | 64 | 4.81 | 1.31 | 87.0% |
| 120 | 8 | 0.87 | 1.11 | 115.9% |
| 120 | 64 | 0.56 | 0.73 | 274.4% |

Even an average over these same contexts predicts their individual curvatures poorly. Therefore categorical sampling error in H764 cannot fully explain the local-versus-global failure. Increasing sampling precision alone will not eliminate the heterogeneity demonstrated here. This does not establish how much of H764's particular error came from each source.

However, the stronger hypothesis that reconstruction errors systematically align with their own context's special sensitive directions is not established. The raw matched/off-context ratio is large at length 32 but reverses at length 120. Destination sensitivity normalization divides each column by its mean over all 16 error directions; that reduces the apparent length-32 advantage substantially. All four normalized diagonal means lie within their descriptive 95% permutation reference intervals. These permutations are exploratory comparisons on a small reused panel, not confirmatory tests or proof of no coupling.

Across destinations, mean sensitivity to this fixed bank of directions varies by 284–351 fold within a length/budget. This is directional-bank sensitivity, not a claim that the full Fisher matrices differ only by a scalar. A multiplicative source-strength times destination-sensitivity approximation has matrix relative RMS residuals of 19–39%, so non-scalar structure remains. Its diagonal errors are 16–71%; it is fitted to the whole matrix, not a held-out predictor.

The best-supported next distinction is therefore **overall sensitivity versus direction-specific geometry**, rather than immediately introducing a different feature basis for every context. A scalar context weight is a simpler control that must be tested before attributing gains to richer conditional groups or manifolds. None of these diagnostics verifies a semantic manifold or reusable computation.

Numerical checks: 5,120 model forwards; native logit replay <=4.24e-5; diagonal curvatures reproduce H767 within 0.78% relative RMS. Two finite-difference steps agree within 0.08–0.56% curvature RMS across the crossed matrices. Inputs/model hashes unchanged and outputs finite. No original reserved-test evaluation; natural document pool remains 26,112. Only adaptive write-PCA directions are crossed here, so extension to other featurizers and causal swap directions remains untested.

Next experiment: on fresh training contexts, estimate sensitivity using a fixed bank of task-blind probe directions shared across all contexts. Test whether a scalar sensitivity estimate predicts held-out probe curvature and whether adding a small number of directional regimes materially improves it. Keep probes used to infer the scalar/regime separate from probes used to evaluate it, and split by document. Then compare scalar-weighted feature learning against context-dependent geometry with actual KL and diverse causal tasks. This sequence distinguishes a weighting problem from a representation problem before adding architectural complexity.

## Previous continuation: H767

## H767 — Per-context sensitivity predicts finite reconstruction KL much better than the global metric

Previous goal turn: progress. H766 completed and was recorded; its mixed results motivated a test that separates local approximation failure from failure of the averaged metric.

We froze 16 reused validation documents, two prefix lengths (32 and 120), and six reconstruction-error directions per context: adaptive write PCA and both Fisher geometries, at budgets 8 and 64. No models are fit. Scale each error from 1% to 100% and measure actual KL(native||edited). Estimate a local directional logit derivative using symmetric 1% perturbations; its variance under the full native vocabulary distribution gives the local Fisher quadratic prediction. Symmetric 2% differences check numerical stability. This local estimate uses no categorical sampling. Both local and global predictions refer to the same frozen direction. KL uses the same-run zero-edit reference to reduce batch-dependent numerical differences.

| Budget | Edit scale | Mean actual KL, nats | Local prediction RMS error / actual RMS | Global prediction RMS error / actual RMS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 0.1 | 8.12825e-06 | 0.40% | 99.03% |
| 8 | 1.0 | 0.000837553 | 7.09% | 97.84% |
| 64 | 0.1 | 2.63183e-07 | 0.73% | 97.61% |
| 64 | 1.0 | 2.66633e-05 | 3.21% | 97.46% |

The global metric fails to predict individual directional KL even at small steps. The per-context approximation stays much more accurate through full-sized reconstruction edits. This makes large-step nonlinearity an insufficient explanation for the global metric's poor performance. It favors investigating context-dependent sensitivity and its relationship to reconstruction errors before adding more group structure.

The conclusion is narrower than proving that context averaging alone is responsible: the global metric also has Monte Carlo error, training-context sampling error, and a different context distribution. Those remain confounded. The local diagnostic uses access to each evaluation context's model response; it is not itself a deployable featurizer or evidence of held-out learned improvement.

Robustness checks (complete values saved in companion JSON):
- Budget 8: local curvature estimates at the two finite-difference steps differ by 0.08% relative RMS. Median full-step relative prediction error is 2.5% local versus 68.0% global. Removing the three largest-KL cases leaves 38.1% versus 98.2% RMS error.
- Budget 64: local curvature estimates at the two finite-difference steps differ by 0.56% relative RMS. Median full-step relative prediction error is 1.4% local versus 60.5% global. Removing the three largest-KL cases leaves 4.5% versus 160.8% RMS error.

Large-KL cases influence the pooled RMS, especially at budget 8. The median comparison still favors local sensitivity, but some full-step errors are substantial. Directional-derivative vector agreement is less stable in small-signal cases; curvature agreement is the relevant additional check, not a blanket claim of exact derivatives. The 1% point is partly an internal consistency check; the independent 10–100% points provide the finite-step test. No significance claim is made from this small reused panel.

Audits: 1,728 model forwards, finite outputs, immutable inputs/model hashes, native replay below 1e-4. No reserved-test evaluation; unique natural document pool stays 26,112.

### Refreshed hypothesis set: 20 live alternatives

1. Context-specific downstream sensitivity determines which directions matter. Leading explanation; compare local matrices across contexts.
2. Reconstruction error correlates with sensitivity, defeating a single average metric. Leading explanation; compare matched versus shuffled context/error pairings.
3. Rare high-sensitivity contexts dominate a useful objective. Plausible; report document-level tails and equal-weight versus tail-weighted fitting.
4. Finite intervention nonlinearity dominates. Weakened on this panel, remains plausible for larger causal swaps; repeat scale tests there.
5. Global Fisher Monte Carlo noise dominates. Unresolved; compare independent sample halves along these directions or increase sample count on fixed contexts.
6. The 128 training contexts undersample relevant regimes. Plausible; increase contexts at fixed total sampling cost.
7. Prefix-position distribution shift matters. Plausible; compare length-matched metrics and pooled metrics.
8. Output-aware scalar features need direct context-conditioned training rather than metric PCA. Plausible next model only after diagnosing 1–7.
9. Useful units are mostly scalar, with little reusable block structure. Supported relative to tested fixed blocks; not a universal claim.
10. Genuine groups exist but energy-based gates select them incorrectly. Open; compare reconstruction-aware and output-aware gates on a fixed dictionary.
11. Hard selection creates unstable support changes between nearby endpoints. Open; measure endpoint support turnover versus causal error.
12. A good feature basis changes with computational regime. Plausible; infer regimes without task labels, then test transfer and sensitivity.
13. Hierarchical gates capture semantic implication without improving reconstruction. Open; test implication separately from additive contributions.
14. Additive refinements are more appropriate than nested subspaces. Open; synthetic recovery plus matched real-data controls.
15. Shared computations require nonlinear DAG nodes rather than shared directions. Open; held-out compositions and node-removal selectivity are decisive.
16. Dictionary non-identifiability explains seed instability. Plausible; compare subspaces and intervention equivalence, not atom alignment alone.
17. Upstream head interactions make isolated feature effects misleading. Supported by prior nonadditivity; test joint intervention predictions.
18. Task-relevant directions are low variance and omitted by reconstruction objectives. Plausible; test causal error versus omitted variance and local sensitivity.
19. Some apparent manifold structure reflects lexical/template nuisance. Open; cross-template and nuisance-matched tests remain required.
20. There is no compact universal set of units at this site; useful units are conditional and task-relative. Plausible fallback, not established; test cross-regime transfer and complexity curves.

Priority: first discriminate context/error coupling, metric sampling noise, and context coverage (1,2,5,6). A matched-versus-shuffled local metric diagnostic is especially informative, but needs reliable directional evaluations or full local matrices; do not substitute shuffled scalar curvatures for the required cross-context quadratic forms. Then train a context-aware or direct-output objective only if the diagnosis supports it. Preserve the downstream goal of verified manifolds, diverse task transfer and reusable computation; do not equate a better KL surrogate with that goal being solved.

At L5H5, interventions add reconstructed donor minus reconstructed receiver activations to the native head. Query, source and joint positions are tested, with reciprocal answer changes, nuisance changes and identity controls. Comparisons below are query-position answer-change errors against the full head edit, in absolute answer-margin RMS units; lower is better.

| Format | Adaptive write PCA, 8 | Adaptive Fisher .01, 8 | Adaptive Fisher .1, 8 | Adaptive write PCA, 64 | Adaptive Fisher .01, 64 | Adaptive Fisher .1, 64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Semicolon | .2477 | .2091 | .2147 | .0815 | .0991 | .0941 |
| Newline | .3686 | .2520 | .2104 | .0660 | .0693 | .1066 |
| Colon | .3034 | .2463 | .2324 | .0524 | .0668 | .0676 |
| Equals | .2288 | .1648 | .1651 | .0713 | .0809 | .0689 |

Adaptive Fisher improves all four mean errors at budget 8. That advantage does not persist across budgets: at 64, ridge .01 is worse in all four formats, and ridge .1 is worse in three. Together with H765's natural-text replacement KL results, this rules out adopting the current global Fisher geometry as an already-verified improvement. It does not rule out output-aware featurization. The metric averages local sensitivity across contexts and ignores its correlation with individual activation errors; reconstruction also produces finite changes that need not follow the local quadratic approximation.

Audits: 8,064 whole-model forwards; full intervention replay and all rank-128 margin replays exactly match their references. Identity logit discrepancy <=2.17e-5 and full donor-head discrepancy <=1.77e-5. All outputs finite and source/capture/model hashes unchanged. Next information-gaining experiment: compare actual KL along scaled reconstruction-error directions with local per-context and globally averaged quadratic predictions. Small steps test the local approximation; full steps test finite-change failure; the difference between local and global predictions tests context averaging. Lock directions and contexts before inspecting outcomes. Then revisit feature learning according to the diagnosed failure. Manifold verification remains the downstream objective: stable structure across seeds and data, held-out combination transfer, and selective causal effects across diverse competent tasks. | Representation | Mean actual KL at8 | At32 | At64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Fixed write PCA | 0.001416 | 0.000443 | 0.000187 |
| Fixed Fisher, ridge0.01 | 0.001417 | 0.000526 | 0.000161 |
| Fixed Fisher, ridge0.1 | 0.001404 | 0.000521 | 0.000162 |

Units are nats. There is no consistent sensitivity-weighting advantage. Fixed Fisher is approximately tied at8, worse at32, and has a lower mean at64. ## H764 — Refined task-blind output metric is more stable; faithfulness still untested

H763's estimator is refined from8 to64 categorical samples per context, keeping the same128 hashed natural training documents, four balanced prefix lengths and sampling seed. No task outcomes, validation gradients or new documents enter this refinement. The metric is the average outer product of native sampled log-probability gradients with respect to L5H5's final-position output. It approximates local output-distribution sensitivity.

| Sampling diagnostic | Eight samples/context | Sixty-four samples/context |
|---|---:|---:|
| Independent sample-half relative Frobenius discrepancy | 80.4% | 32.1% |
| Sample-half matrix cosine | 0.724 | 0.950 |
| Metric effective rank | 61.8 | 72.8 |

The refined estimate is substantially more stable, but32% matrix discrepancy is still appreciable. These halves share the same contexts and only measure categorical-sampling uncertainty, not uncertainty over natural contexts. Effective rank is a spectral statistic, not a count of features, manifolds or independent computational units. The global metric can be broad even if context-specific computation is sparse.

Both fixed ridge settings remain:0.01 and0.1 times the mean metric eigenvalue. They yield condition numbers26.6 and18.2. All32,768 natural training head vectors are used to fit PCA in each metric, with all4,096 validation vectors used only for reconstruction summaries. No ridge or basis is chosen by copying behavior. Both fitted transforms and the8,192 gradient vectors are saved.

All gradients and fitted quantities are finite, and input/source hashes are unchanged.

This is an averaged local quadratic geometry. It ignores correlations between each activation and its own downstream sensitivity, and does not guarantee accurate KL for large reconstruction edits. The gradient sample uses final positions at four sequence lengths whereas the training covariance pools sixteen positions. The ridge also specifies a coordinate-space regularization choice. These limits matter before calling the result a data-based canonical form.

Next: measure actual native-to-reconstructed output KL on fixed natural validation contexts, report observed-token CE separately, and then test copying causal edits using the same frozen transforms. Keep both ridge settings and PCA/random controls. Improving the estimated metric objective alone will not count as better model faithfulness.

## Previous continuation: H763

## H763 — Output-sensitivity geometry is numerically valid but initially noisy

A task-blind local output-distribution metric is estimated for final-position L5H5 from128 hashed natural training documents, balanced across prefix lengths16,32,64,128. For each context, eight tokens are sampled from the model's own native next-token distribution. Gradients of their log probabilities with respect to additive head-output changes are collected; their average outer product estimates a local Fisher metric. Model weights are frozen. No task labels, validation gradients or reserved-test documents enter the estimate.

Two fixed ridge strengths,0.01 and0.1 times mean metric eigenvalue, regularize the metric. PCA is fitted using all32,768 natural training head vectors in each resulting geometry. Both fits are saved without task-based selection. This is a global averaged local metric: it does not capture every context's sensitivity, correlations between sensitivity and activations, or nonlinear large-intervention KL.

The gradient implementation is verified. Native logits replay exactly; natural head captures agree within3.81e-5. Thirty-two finite-difference checks across all four lengths have maximum absolute derivative error1.91e-4 and maximum relative error2.21%, passing the fixed mixed absolute/relative tolerance. Metric eigenvalues are positive; the factorization and inverse-transform errors are below4.24e-21 and1.56e-15 respectively. All gradients are finite.

However, the first and second four-sample halves differ by80.4% of the full metric's Frobenius norm, with matrix cosine0.724. This reveals substantial Monte Carlo uncertainty despite correct differentiation. The unregularized effective rank is61.8, a numerical spectral summary, not a count of semantic units. The two ridged condition numbers are49.3 and28.8.

Decision: do not treat this pilot geometry as reliable evidence for or against downstream-sensitive featurization. Increase categorical samples per context on the same fixed training contexts before causal benchmarking. This changes estimator precision without fitting to task outcomes.

## Previous continuation: H760

## H760 — Failed-task audit separates conditional discrimination from unconstrained completion

Cached native H732 logits are rescored using symmetric answer-format rules fixed before inspecting predictions in this audit. Three sets are compared: original labels, canonical labels expanded across lower/title/upper case and zero/one leading space, and the existing semantic alternatives with the same case/space expansion. Only exact single-token continuations preserving prompt tokenization are retained; token IDs are deduplicated and classes remain disjoint. No cases are dropped based on predictions. This is posthoc measurement diagnosis, not a new confirmatory task test.

### Sentiment

The original broad answer sets omit capitalized “ Excellent,” although they include lowercase “ excellent.” That token is native top-1 on14/16 format-A endpoints and12/16 format-B endpoints, including negative reviews. Expanding the broad sets therefore raises intended-class top-1 from0% to50%, but both-endpoint choice remains0%: the model still favors the positive semantic bucket at both endpoints. Other top predictions include “ The,” “ Strong” and “ I.”

Canonical positive/negative labels tell a different story. With symmetric case/space variants, both-endpoint binary choice is100% on both formats, while intended full-vocabulary top-1 remains0%. Mean probability mass on the correct canonical class is only0.84%(A)/1.51%(B). Thus the model contains a usable conditional label distinction while its unrestricted next-token distribution does not perform the requested classification reliably. A broad synonym bucket can obscure that distinction because dominant continuation preferences overwhelm the narrow labels.

This does not justify retroactively declaring sentiment competent under the earlier dual criterion. Nor does the earlier failure show that sentiment information is absent. Forced-choice discrimination, answer-format obedience and unconstrained completion are separate measurements. The original causal studies used the original broad margin and remain measurements of that margin; a canonical-label causal test would be a different experiment.

### Capital recall

Format A remains100% correct in paired choice and12.5% intended full-vocabulary top-1 under all scoring rules. Its16 top predictions include eight currency symbols, six country names and two city answers (“ Moscow”). Case/space expansion does not rescue it. Currency predictions suggest that “Capital:” can evoke a financial interpretation, but this audit alone does not prove the cause. Format B, which explicitly asks for the capital city, stays100% on both metrics; its country set also differs, so the comparison does not isolate wording causally.

The appropriate next prompt test should cross explicit city wording with the same countries, and explicit sentiment-label instructions with the same reviews, while keeping scoring rules fixed. The old failures remain visible. A fresh copying/nuisance confirmation should likewise be locked before outputs, with all featurizer seeds frozen and no competence-based individual example filtering.

Audits: original competence metrics replay exactly; class token sets are disjoint; all source/input hashes unchanged. Alternative answer strings failing single-token continuation checks are recorded. Zero model forwards or reserved-test evaluations; natural document pool26,112 unchanged. Multi-token and delayed answers are not assessed here.

Next: design the prospective copying/nuisance panel and a separate prompt/answer-format competence check. Keep canonical forced-choice evidence distinct from full-vocabulary success, and do not silently replace prior causal outcomes with a more favorable score.

Twenty-four frozen representations are evaluated for L5H3/H5 on H732's five task families, two formats and nuisance variants. It is reused research data but was not used to fit these natural-text featurizers.

Edits add F(donor)-F(receiver) at the final position only, in two reciprocal task directions, one nuisance direction and an identity control. This differs from the earlier operation tests' two-position edits and their cross-operation donor pairs; numerical effect magnitudes should not be directly compared across those designs. No downstream query/key clamps are applied here.

Native competence reproduces the earlier panel exactly: agreement, binding and copying pass both formats; capital recall passes format B but fails A's full-vocabulary gate; sentiment fails both formats. Relative errors are reported only when competence passes and full-head margin-change RMS>=0.25logits. Otherwise all absolute errors remain recorded. Three cells meet this combined threshold.

| Eligible cell | Full effect RMS | Scalar error | Block error | Shared-group error | Group-null error | Adaptive PCA error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H3 agreement A, task | 0.293 | 42.3% | 58.6% | 42.7% | 65.3% | 42.9% |
| H5 copying A, task | 0.325 | 71.2% | 103.2% | 61.1% | 88.5% | 85.8% |
| H5 copying A, nuisance | 0.279 | 52.5% | 91.4% | 105.4% | 92.4% | 127.7% |

Errors are mean seed-level relative RMS against the full-head intervention. Fixed write-PCA errors on these rows are59.4%,63.1%,101.7%; random-adaptive means71.2%,93.5%,111.1%. Means over shared examples and rewires are descriptive, not independent statistical replication.

The apparent copying advantage of shared groups is not consistent across dictionary seeds. Scalar copying errors are64.1%,65.2%,84.4%; group errors77.8%,65.2%,40.4%. Thus the mean gain is driven largely by the third dictionary. Its grouping performed poorly on the previous operation panel, so choosing it now would be task-based selection, not proof of a generally superior featurizer. Nuisance errors worsen for all three group models relative to their scalar counterparts.

Nuisance fidelity and semantic invariance are different targets. Group nuisance effects here have smaller RMS(0.107–0.184) than the full-head effect0.279, but their alignment with it varies from-0.306 to0.240. This is not simply a demonstrated useful invariance; one dictionary reverses the aggregate effect direction. Task-specific abstraction could prioritize a different objective, but that would need a separate accuracy/invariance test rather than a faithfulness claim.

Most remaining cells have weak final-position head effects. H3 agreement B has full RMS0.230 with scalar/group absolute errors0.089/0.101logits. H5 copying B has full RMS0.164 with scalar/group absolute errors0.163/0.150. Competent capital-recall B has full RMS only0.005(H3)/0.004(H5). Binding task effects are0.057–0.075 at H3 and0.005–0.010 at H5. These values limit what this intervention can establish about representation quality on those tasks; they are not discarded or converted into misleading percentages.

Interpretation: head function and representation quality depend on context and intervention position. H3's clearest final-position effect in this suite is agreement; H5's is copying. Shared groups can help one task and damage preservation of a nearby nuisance effect, while scalar models remain stronger on the prior operation-dependent target. No universal featurizer winner or verified manifold emerges. Broadening the suite was informative precisely because it exposed these tradeoffs and weak-effect cells.

## Previous continuation: H757

## H757 — Shared groups contain structure, but do not yet improve the featurizer

This test extends each of the six frozen H755 scalar dictionaries with128 overlapping groups of four atoms. Each group retains its own anchor atom; total memberships are fixed at512. Two distinct groups are selected and decoded through their exact union, so shared atoms contribute once. Fixed counts constrain membership capacity instead of fitting an L0 membership penalty. Decoder columns remain normalized through the frozen scalar model.

Memberships are initialized from either stable-half training support correlation or random anchored groups, then updated for ten rounds to maximize captured raw coefficient-squared energy. Assignment uses a greedy start and alternating best responses; membership updates exactly optimize each anchored row for fixed assignments. The best training-scored snapshot, including initialization, is retained. This objective is a proxy for reconstruction because decoder atoms are nonorthogonal. It is not joint dictionary/gate training or a global optimum.

| Head | Scalar8 | Union-size-matched scalar | Initial correlation groups | Learned correlation groups | Degree-preserving randomizations |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| L5H3 | 41.16% | 41.22% | 52.71% | 52.68% | 56.09% |
| L5H5 | 38.91% | 38.98% | 50.21% | 49.66% | 52.65% |

Values are natural validation relative write MSE, averaged over all three dictionaries; randomization values average three rewires per dictionary. Learned random-initialized groups reach55.53%/51.48% at H3/H5, versus their randomized controls56.55%/52.87%. All initializations and nulls remain in the results. Validation is evaluated, not used to select memberships.

The group structure improves over degree-preserving nulls, especially with correlation initialization, but remains substantially worse than the frozen scalar Top8 featurizer. A per-example scalar control selects exactly as many atoms as the group's union; its error remains almost unchanged. Thus the gap is not explained by losing active slots to overlap. Group constraints and/or the energy-proxy optimizer remain plausible bottlenecks.

Learned correlation groups select7.975(H3)/7.982(H5) unique atoms on average. The two selected groups share atoms in only2.47%/1.77% of validation examples. This does not rule out reuse of dictionary atoms across different contexts, but simultaneous sharing is rarely exercised. Overlap as an architectural capability is not evidence of shared computation or a meaningful manifold.

Degree-preserving rewires maintain every group's size and each atom's membership count, but do not preserve the anchor designation. Anchors are a training constraint, not a special decoder role. The comparison controls membership degrees and capacity; it does not eliminate every possible structural confound.

Implementation checks: exact union agrees with binary matrix-product support over every validation example; two gates are selected and at most eight unique atoms decoded; rewiring preserves atom and group degrees; fixed-assignment membership energy never decreases. Seven targeted tests pass, including a known shared-atom example, exhaustive small membership optimization, anchored row sizes, assignment monotonicity and atom-permutation invariance. The actual H757 membership functions were used in the tests and matched the previously audited function sources. All group sizes remain four; inputs/source hashes unchanged and outputs finite.

No model forwards or original reserved-test evaluations occur here; natural document pool remains26,112. These are frozen-dictionary overlapping supports, not evidence against all jointly trained shared-gate, hierarchical or computational-DAG alternatives.

Next: evaluate learned correlation groups and all degree-preserving nulls on the existing total-effect and operation-dependence causal targets, with all scalar seeds retained. Only a reproducible functional advantage would justify treating these groups as better candidate units; otherwise diagnose gate/objective restrictions before adding hierarchy.

Twelve task-blind fits compare signed scalar TopK (eight selected coordinates) with signed block TopK (two four-dimensional blocks), for L5H3/H5 and three seeds. | Head | Scalar8 validation write MSE, three seeds | Block4×2 validation write MSE, three seeds | Adaptive PCA8 reference |
|---|---|---|---:|

| L5H5 | 39.15%,38.82%,38.76% | 50.70%,50.42%,50.73% | 43.20% |

Scalar TopK improves over adaptive PCA; fixed blocks perform worse than both on reconstruction. Equal active dimension and parameter count do not equalize combinatorial support flexibility. This block implementation uses unit decoder rows and block-norm gating; it is not Goodfire's orthonormal-within-block Grassmannian implementation. The result does not reject all block/manifold models, shared-atom groups, or hierarchical alternatives.

Every run selects step3,000 and still improves over step2,750, by0.04–0.28 percentage points of relative MSE. Therefore these are finite-training results, not established optima. There are no dead validation blocks in any run.

Reconstruction gains do not imply uniquely identified computational units.

## H751 — Earlier-output effects mostly persist when the selected L13 nodes are clamped

This systematic causal sweep exchanges each L0–12 attention or MLP output between matched binding/copy contexts at both the final-query and source-key positions. There are26 output sites and240 contexts, producing6,240 paired interventions; native-competent narratives and diagnostic lists remain separate.

The free-minus-clamped answer-margin change measures dependence on these selected nodes under this intervention. It is not a unique mediated path fraction: downstream interactions remain, earlier outputs have many consumers, and clamping the full nodes goes beyond the rank-four coordinates. Both positions are swapped together. Donor output replacements are not constrained to the operation subspace.

| Site, competent narratives | Free margin-change RMS | Clamped RMS | Free-minus-clamped RMS | Alignment of dependence with total change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| L5 attention | 1.775 | 1.675 | 0.126 | 5.7% |
| L4 MLP | 1.127 | 1.020 | 0.125 | 9.7% |
| L6 MLP | 1.486 | 1.400 | 0.119 | 6.0% |
| L5 MLP | 1.209 | 1.125 | 0.114 | 7.1% |

| L11 MLP | 0.637 | 0.569 | 0.088 | 11.1% |
| L11 attention | 0.633 | 0.618 | 0.035 | 2.5% |

RMS values are in intended-answer-margin logits. Dependence alignment is dot(free-minus-clamped,free)/squared_norm(free), aggregated over120 contexts; it is not an accuracy fraction. Across all26 sites, clamped RMS is89.1–99.9% of free RMS, and dependence alignment ranges0.15–11.24%. Thus most measured upstream-swap behavior survives this two-node clamp. This does not mean the head is irrelevant or that all remaining effects follow an independent additive bypass; only the specified query/key states and positions are fixed.

The algebraic and causal rankings differ. L11 attention had the largest direct query-coordinate alignment share in H750, but its clamp-dependent behavioral effect is weaker than several middle-layer outputs. L5 attention causes33.7% alignment with the full donor query-coordinate difference; L6 MLP causes26.6% alignment with the key-coordinate difference. L4/L5/L3 MLP key alignments are21.2%/24.0%/22.1%. These coordinate-movement scores also are not downstream causal fractions.

Interpretation: the verified compact operation component is a reproducible route through computation, not the dominant mediator of these broad upstream output swaps. Earlier output vectors contain effects on other heads, other edges and other features. Distributed construction plus multiple downstream routes remains plausible. We should not select an upstream featurizer site solely by the largest direct attribution or total behavioral effect.

Limitations: full-state clamps do not prove that dependence specifically uses the rank-four component. H747 contexts are reused, and lists remain native-incompetent diagnostics. No claim of unsupervised recovery, manifold identity or general task switching follows from this sweep.

## H750 — The verified operation coordinates have distributed upstream contributions

This experiment exactly expands the residual stream entering L13 attention into embedding/skip injection plus the attention and MLP outputs of layers0–12. Binding-to-copy coordinate differences are decomposed at the final query and source key on all H747 contexts.

An alignment share is the sum over pairs of dot(component difference,total coordinate difference), divided by the summed squared total difference. Shares sum to one but can be negative or exceed one. They are an algebraic attribution of the observed contrast, not causal effect fractions or explained-variance percentages. Each context uses its own observed normalization denominators, so denominator changes are distributed across these terms.

| Direct contribution on competent narratives | Query coordinates | Key coordinates |
|---|---:|---:|
| MLP outputs, L0–12 combined | 57.94% | 83.56% |
| Attention outputs, L0–12 combined | 42.07% | 16.72% |
| Embedding and skip injections | -0.001% | -0.274% |

### Hypothesis refresh: twenty alternatives and discriminating tests

1. A shared operation component is expressed across narratives. Supported by fresh downstream transfer; test selective removal across held-out lexical families.
2. Several template-conditioned components coexist. Supported by pooling tradeoffs; compare conditional subspaces with a matched total-rank global basis on fresh families.
3. Rank four is an arbitrary bottleneck. Compare a predeclared rank curve with matched nuisance controls, without choosing rank on test effects.
4. The strongest singular directions favor high-energy templates rather than causal utility. Compare train-only balanced or effect-weighted fits on held-out effects.
5. A small query component controls task mode while keys carry identity. Mixed support; do upstream separate-query/key mediation, not just output-edge substitution.
6. Query and key jointly encode the operation. Supported by joint versus one-sided swaps; test interaction-preserving versus interaction-destroying controls.
7. Template-specific key directions account for remaining errors. Supported for new list wording; selectively restore omitted key directions on competent fresh tasks.
8. Template-specific query directions account for remaining errors. Supported for new narrative wording; run the analogous query intervention.
9. RoPE or relative positions explain apparent sharing. Exact de-rotation and matched positions weaken this; vary positions independently with semantics fixed.
10. Token identity alone explains the subspace. Nuisance controls weaken this; extend to unseen single-token identities and identity-balanced contrasts.
11. Lexical cues correlated with operation explain it. Still live; construct minimal lexical contrasts and identical final-token controls with different required operations.
12. Global norm changes drive the effect. H745 weakens this; compare fixed-norm and native-norm paths with explicit gain controls.
13. The first attention factor determines operation sign. H741 weakens this within studied cases; test additional heads/tasks where its sign varies.
14. The second factor is a context-sensitive routing gate over a fixed token map. Strong within this edge; test other source positions and values without fitting signs.
15. The absent-name probe measures a special output association. Still live; use held-out absent values from several semantic classes and measure full-vocabulary changes.
16. Downstream nonlinearities create the apparent operation switch. Existing coefficient/effect agreement weakens this locally; map intervention amplitude and compare layerwise effects.
17. Sign misses are mostly near-zero margins. Plausible but untested here; stratify errors by full-target effect size before interpreting counts.
18. Other heads compensate when this head's operation label fails. Test selective head/component ablation and residual pathways on native-competent exceptions.
19. Failed list tasks reflect ambiguous or poor prompts rather than absent computation. Retain failures; use independently specified, competence-tested task families without retroactive template repair.
20. An unsupervised featurizer can recover these causal components without operation labels. Outstanding central question; compare sparse/overlapping/hierarchical representations against the now-verified paired-edit reference on held-out interventions.

Priority: (1),(2),(6),(14) best describe current evidence. (11),(15),(17),(18) are important unresolved alternatives. The next useful steps are effect-size-stratified sign diagnostics and selective upstream intervention, followed by unsupervised recovery comparisons. Improved compression alone would not distinguish these explanations.

## H746 — Operation edits outperform identity and wording nuisance subspaces

This retrospective diagnostic tests a stronger control than random directions: equal-rank subspaces derived from actual changes in identity or wording. All query and key subspaces have rank four and use the same receiver-norm-preserving projection. Training uses only the first four old name pairs. Evaluation uses the other four old pairs and all valid new pairs; an explicit name-set intersection audit confirms no overlap. These evaluation outputs were inspected in previous experiments, so this is not prospective confirmation.

Identity controls use endpoint changes within each operation and format under old wording (16 differences). Wording controls use old-to-new wording changes within each operation, format, and endpoint (32 differences). Operation subspaces use binding-to-copy differences: old wording (the frozen H742 baseline), new wording (16 differences), or both wordings pooled (32 differences). A rank-four union takes two old-wording and two new-wording directions and orthonormalizes them. Separate bases are fitted for query and key. Matched rank does not imply equal numbers of training rows; all row counts are recorded. The nuisance contrasts preserve operation but differ in other contextual details; they do not exhaust every possible surface-cue control.

Findings: the operation subspace is substantially better than ordinary identity or wording variation at approximating this particular operation exchange. Training on new wording recovers much of its missing structure, especially for lists. However, pooling at fixed rank creates tradeoffs: old narrative error rises, while new list error falls. An exact algebraic diagnostic decomposes H744's frozen-subspace coefficient error. With projected query/key q,k and omitted donor residuals dq,dk, the full-minus-projected second-factor dot product is dq·k + q·dk + dq·dk. The model's first-factor gain and signed bus multiplier are retained. Norm restoration is measured separately. This performs no fitting and no additional model forwards; it does not establish downstream effects for the new rescue conditions.

| Competent fresh stratum | Frozen coefficient error | Full query + compact key | Compact query + full key | Captured query/key edit energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| New names, old narrative wording | 12.4% | 11.2% | 6.3% | 92.7% / 96.3% |
| New names, old list wording | 8.8% | 4.0% | 5.7% | 84.0% / 91.9% |

| Old names, new list wording | 29.6% | 15.4% | 16.9% | 55.2% / 51.1% |

Errors are RMS coefficient deviation from the full-factor donor intervention, normalized by its change from native. Energy is mean squared edit length captured by the frozen rank-four subspace, separately for query and key. Rescues replace one compact state with its full donor state while retaining the other norm-preserved compact state. These are explanatory diagnostics on the already evaluated panel, not new held-out successes.

The new-list error is essentially unchanged without norm restoration: 29.66% raw versus29.61% norm-preserved. Norm restoration contributes only0.50% of the full edit's RMS scale, versus17.12% query-residual,15.28% key-residual,3.54% bilinear-interaction component norms. The new-name/new-wording cells remain diagnostic because native binding fails the H744 competence gate. Their coefficient errors are16.2% narrative and33.5% list; the same low list edit-energy capture persists. No selection or refitting is performed using these cells.

The frozen operation edit contains meaningful reusable structure but misses wording-dependent directions at both ends of the attention edge. The next discriminating test should separate a shared causal component from template-specific directions, using independently split wording families and matched nuisance edits. A union of template subspaces may describe the data better than one universal operation manifold; this is a hypothesis, not an established architecture.

Of 128 prompt pairs, eight involving Harold/Doris failed the token-validity or endpoint-length rule, leaving 120 pairs and 240 contexts. All 120 binding/copy endpoint matches had identical source/final tokens and positions. Every valid context was retained; comparisons require both task cells to pass the preregistered native-competence gate.

| Names / wording | Format | Downstream edit error | Random rank-4 error | Eligible sign transfers |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Old / old (replay, includes fit names) | Narrative | 5.9% | 99.4% | 32/32 |
| Old / old (replay, includes fit names) | List | 7.4% | 96.4% | 30/30 |
| New / old | Narrative | 12.4% | 99.4% | 24/24 |
| New / old | List | 8.7% | 96.1% | 26/26 |

| New / new — diagnostic | Narrative | 16.1% | 99.2% | 18/24 |
| New / new — diagnostic | List | 33.8% | 95.8% | 22/26 |

Error is RMS difference from the full-factor intervention, normalized by its RMS change from native, for the Kevin-versus-Brian absent-value contrast. Random results pool three fixed seeds. Observations share templates/names and are not independent statistical replications. Original-value intervention errors follow the same pattern: new names 12.3%/8.8%, new wording 10.4%/33.6%, narrative/list respectively.

Both new-name/new-wording binding cells fail native competence: narrative full-vocabulary top-1 42.9% <50%; list both-endpoint choice 71.4% <75%. They remain diagnostic. Interpretation: compact paired edits reuse substantial causal structure across names and some wording changes, substantially outperforming equal-rank random controls. Wording-dependent residuals and exceptions weaken the claim of a universal operation manifold. This result concerns a single surgically edited attention edge, not whole-model task switching or overall accuracy.

Verification: 5,280 model forwards; all frozen inputs/source hashes unchanged; native head factorization relative error 5.83e-7; old-panel coefficient replay error 5.84e-7; native-value identity error 4.77e-6; zero contrast exactly zero; finite outputs. ## H742 — Compact operation edits generalize across names, but their directions depend on format

We fitted separate uncentered SVD bases for q2 and k2 binding-to-copying changes using name-pair indices 0–3, then evaluated reciprocal edits on indices 4–7. Fits use either both formats pooled, narrative only, or list only. No coefficient labels enter SVD, but the pairing explicitly uses operation labels; this is a supervised paired-edit diagnostic on an already-inspected panel, not unsupervised discovery or fresh confirmation.

To avoid an artificial coordinate-frame explanation, we first invert the actual bf16-cached rotary transform, including its slight departure from exact orthogonality. We project normalized pre-rotary donor-minus-receiver changes, then restore rotary position at each recipient. Query and key bases are fitted separately: rank four means four directions in each state, not one four-dimensional joint feature. Native factor 1 stays fixed; the target is the exact factor-2 swap from H741.

Both raw projected edits and norm-preserving edits were evaluated, with three random orthogonal subspace controls at each rank and a full-rank identity. Below are norm-preserving held-out-name results. Relative RMS error is error in the coefficient divided by the RMS intended coefficient change, and sign transfer is counted only where native and target signs differ.

| Basis fit / evaluation format | Rank per state | Sign transfer | Relative coefficient-edit RMS error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Pooled / narrative | 1 | 13/16 | 18.5% |
| Pooled / narrative | 2 | 13/16 | 16.2% |
| Pooled / narrative | 4 | 16/16 | 4.1% |
| Pooled / list | 1 | 4/14 | 73.6% |
| Pooled / list | 2 | 14/14 | 12.9% |
| Pooled / list | 4 | 14/14 | 8.6% |
| Narrative / narrative | 2 | 16/16 | 6.7% |
| List / list | 1 | 14/14 | 13.9% |
| Narrative / list | 2 | 7/14 | 62.0% |
| List / narrative | 2 | 0/16 | 85.1% |

Random rank-four controls transfer 0/48 narrative signs and 2/42 list signs across three seeds, with approximately 99% and 96% relative edit error. The pooled rank-four bases capture about 93%/97% of query/key edit energy on narrative contexts and 83%/92% on lists. Higher ranks and both normalization variants are retained in the saved results; there is no monotonicity or convergence claim from this small fit.

The promising finding is low-dimensional paired-edit structure that transfers across held-out names. The restriction is equally important: within-format compactness does not imply the same directions implement the operation across formats. Poor cross-format transfer persists after removing the rotary coordinate-frame difference. Relative source/query distance and contextual states still differ across formats; a pooled basis may simply contain multiple format-specific directions.

## H741 — The operation-linked sign is carried by a joint second-query/second-key relation

We crossed the four post-normalization, post-rotary components of L13H0's routing coefficient between matched binding/copying contexts: q1, k1, q2 and k2. All sixteen recipient/donor combinations were evaluated, with no selection of successful hybrids. Source/final tokens and positions remain exactly matched as established in H740.

The coefficient is alpha=lambda*(q1·k1/128)*(q2·k2/128). A hybrid coefficient replaces only the designated source-to-head bus contribution; other edges, local values and downstream computation remain native. This is a surgical single-edge intervention, not replacing all uses of a query or key or the upstream residual stream. Original source values are held fixed for one test; a separate test uses the same three absent-token pairs across every hybrid.

There are 64 directed exchanges from 32 matched context comparisons. One matched comparison already has the same native sign on both operations, leaving 62 directed exchanges with opposite native signs. Sign-transfer counts below use those 62; all 64 remain in the saved data.

| Donor components exchanged | Transfers donor coefficient sign |
|---|---:|
| q1 only | 0/62 |
| k1 only | 0/62 |
| Both components of factor 1 | 0/62 |
| q2 only | 39/62 |
| Both queries | 39/62 |
| k2 only | 23/62 |
| Both keys | 23/62 |
| Both components of factor 2 | 62/62 |
| All four components | 62/62 |

The first dot-product factor is positive in all native primary contexts, ranging approximately 0.35–0.67. The second factor is positive for binding (approximately 0.09–0.32) and usually negative for copying (approximately -0.15 to -0.027 narrative; -0.117 to +0.011 list). Its one list-copy exception reproduces H740's exception. Exchanging factor 2 transfers the sign completely, while the retained recipient factor 1 still changes its magnitude: coefficient RMS error relative to the all-donor coefficient remains approximately 21–30% across the four receiver cells. Thus factor 1 contributes gain even though it does not control this sign contrast.

The component effects are asymmetric:

| Receiver cell, donor is opposite operation | q2-only sign transfer | k2-only sign transfer |
|---|---:|---:|
| Narrative binding | 3/16 | 1/16 |
| List binding | 6/15 | 0/15 |
| Narrative copying | 15/16 | 13/16 |
| List copying | 15/15 | 9/15 |

A binding donor component often makes a copying receiver positive; a copying donor component alone usually does not make a binding receiver negative. Both copying-side components are generally needed. This supports a relational computation involving both contextual states, rather than a clean one-location operation bit. It does not yet identify which directions encode that relation or where those directions were formed upstream.

The surgical coefficient changes have the predicted downstream sign. Across all sixteen hybrids plus the reversed-native control, the fixed-map prediction matches all 3,264 nonzero absent-token contrast signs (64 contexts x 17 conditions x three fixed pairs). Zero-coefficient contrasts are exactly zero. These are correlated tests using reused contexts and three token pairs, not independent population trials. Original-source-value interventions and their intended-answer margin changes are also recorded; sign transfer is not claimed to solve the whole task or establish edge necessity.

Audits: native final-logit replay maximum error was 1.19e-5; native coefficient replay error 9.84e-7; the all-donor coefficient exactly matches the donor coefficient. Native-value identity margin error was at most 5.72e-6; native/zero/reversed absent-token effects replayed H740 within 3.58e-6. All hashes remained unchanged and results were finite. The experiment completed 8,000 full-model example forwards with no new natural documents or original reserved-test evaluations.

Interpretation: a candidate reusable unit is now more concrete than a sparse decoder atom: a signed bilinear relation between a contextual destination query and contextual source key, controlling a fixed token/value map. This is evidence about this head, these matched contrasts and this source edge. It is not a universal operation taxonomy, nor evidence that every relevant state lies on a verified low-dimensional manifold.
