## H715 — Downstream response geometry is context-dependent and only weakly favors coactivation groups

Previous turn classification: progress. H714 completed512causal evaluations and found no reliable group advantage over matched substitute neighborhoods. H715 changes the target: do members of a group influence similar output probabilities locally, rather than making the entire distribution more like a donor?

Freeze16hash-selected H712documents, excluding all64H713swap documents. Evaluate position63in every document with no activation or output selection. Test the union of134directions appearing in the eight real groups and their24frozen H714substitute neighborhoods. Each decoder column has unit residual-space norm. Apply symmetric positive/negative perturbations of1%of residual norm at block1output, preserving the value bus. Compute centered finite-difference logit derivatives; first-context half-dose checks test numerical stability.

For native probability p and logit derivative v, the response signature is sqrt(p)*(v-E_p[v]). Its squared norm is the local Fisher/KL sensitivity, and its direction describes which probabilities change. Compare squared cosine between anchor and neighbor signatures: this removes arbitrary dictionary signs. Also remove the projection onto sqrt(p)*(native_logits-E_p[native_logits]), the local temperature direction. This is a local one-dimensional confidence control, not removal of every confidence-related effect.

The frozen contrast averages the seven real anchor-neighbor squared cosines, subtracts the average over the three substitute neighborhoods, then averages equally over all eight anchors and16contexts. Bootstrap intervals resample16documents, retaining all anchors within each document;10000resamples. They do not cover uncertainty over group discovery or control matching.

| Response metric | Real groups | Substitute groups | Difference | Context bootstrap95%interval |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
|fisher|0.30880|0.28893|0.01987|[0.00149,0.04016]|
|confidence_removed|0.27866|0.26375|0.01491|[-0.00314,0.03540]|

The full response metric gives a modest positive advantage; after temperature projection the interval includes zero. Only9of16contexts have a positive difference for either metric. Group effects vary, so this is not evidence that all eight groups share a common computational role. Temperature accounts for18.6%of anchor response energy on average.

A material matching limitation remains: mean squared decoder cosine is0.06428in the real groups versus0.04186in controls, a static difference0.02242. Thus the control procedure did not fully match geometric alignment. The response advantage cannot be confidently attributed to coactivation-based organization beyond decoder geometry. The two cosine metrics are not interchangeable, and subtracting their differences would not be a valid causal correction.

### What the metric audit adds

After removing the temperature component, all134tested directions' output responses still concentrate in few effective directions within each context. The participation rank (sum eigenvalues squared divided by sum squared eigenvalues) ranges1.80–7.32, median3.51; the leading three response axes carry55.6–94.4%of response energy. This is a local response-space result, not the dimension of a representation manifold. Concentrated native token probabilities can contribute to low Fisher rank; native probability participation varies1.00–124.3across contexts. An anisotropic downstream map may make many unrelated decoder directions appear functionally aligned.

Across different contexts, the same anchor's probability-weighted response vectors have near-zero average signed cosine. Those vectors use different probability weights, so this alone cannot establish unstable computation. A posthoc audit uses one pooled probability vector for all16contexts and recomputes centering and temperature projection. Mean signed cross-context cosine remains low,0.0006–0.0315across anchors; mean squared cosine0.0207–0.0354. A fixed token-output direction is therefore not demonstrated, although reusable context-dependent operations could still exist.

The pooled-weight within-context real-minus-control similarity difference is0.02881on average, positive15of16contexts. This is a sensitivity analysis, not replacement of the frozen primary metric: it changes the weighting objective and retains the decoder-geometry mismatch. Results depend materially on which output differences count as important, reinforcing the distinction between activation reconstruction, local distributional faithfulness and task effects.

### Research implication and next test

These data do not verify the current coactivation neighborhoods as computational units. They do reveal a measurable local functional geometry, potentially closer to the user's data-based canonical-form idea: many activation directions can have redundant or weak effects on the outputs relevant to a context. Its meaning and persistence across contexts still need testing.

The next informative control should preserve decoder geometry exactly. Construct rotations within the measured decoder span that fix the anchor while preserving the full neighborhood Gram matrix, and compare their predicted downstream similarities against real groups. The saved directional derivatives permit this as a local linear-response test; verify a subset with actual finite interventions. This addresses the known geometry mismatch and tests whether coactivation groups align with the downstream map beyond merely pointing in similar residual directions. Such rotations do not preserve natural activation frequencies, so retain the present statistical controls as a complementary comparison. If geometry-corrected advantages survive, proceed to competence-checked diverse tasks and held combinations, not semantic naming from cosine alone.

### Hypothesis refresh: twenty live explanations and discriminating tests

Ranks below are qualitative priorities, not posterior probabilities. Several explanations can coexist.

| # | Hypothesis | Current assessment and discriminating experiment |
|---|---|---|
|1|Shared context drives groups without shared computation.|Plausible: replicated covariance, no causal grouping advantage. Compare downstream response similarity against matched neighborhoods.|
|2|Decoder geometry explains apparent grouping.|Still plausible; present matches are imperfect. Condition on full Gram geometry and compare effective response geometry.|
|3|Token identity plus broader lexical statistics explains activity.|Token/position conditioning is insufficient for context. Test matched windows and lexical/format controls.|
|4|Groups organize confidence rather than content.|Temperature reproduces donorward score but misses shape. Remove the confidence component from response signatures.|
|5|The anchor carries most useful local computation.|Neighbor addition uncertain. Compare anchor and neighbors on predefined outputs across fresh contexts.|
|6|Distributed neurons share downstream targets despite weak donor transfer.|Plausible alternative metric. Cluster Fisher-weighted logit response signatures, then validate on separate contexts.|
|7|A group matters only when several members are jointly active.|Current selection requires only anchor activity. Stratify by frozen multi-member support before measuring effects.|
|8|The relevant unit is a nonlinear manifold rather than a linear span.|Current neighborhoods are not manifold fits. Test local tangent stability and reconstruction of held-out trajectories.|
|9|The unit is a gated subspace with context-dependent coordinates.|Compare response alignment across contexts with similar inferred gates versus unrelated contexts.|
|10|Shared dictionary atoms are meaningful but these group memberships are wrong.|Synthetic success does not identify real groups. Compare coactivation grouping with downstream-effect grouping.|
|11|Group size8is arbitrary and obscures variable-dimensional units.|Evaluate training-selected group sizes with held-out description length and causal selectivity.|
|12|Top32competition manufactures part of the covariance.|Current shuffle null does not preserve that budget. Use fixed-row/column-margin support controls.|
|13|The retained256Dspan omits important computational directions.|Known variance omission. Compare response coverage with directions outside the retained span.|
|14|Whitening/sparsity captures distributional axes, not causal axes.|Plausible. Compare whitened axes, BSF and response-based grouping at matched resources.|
|15|Sparse coding is inadequate because relevant representations are dense.|Current undercomplete candidate remains worse than BSF reconstruction. Test dense low-rank functional models alongside sparse ones.|
|16|Computational reuse is visible only across held-out combinations.|Untested here. Competence-check diverse compositional tasks before component intervention.|
|17|The persistent value bus supplies essential omitted partners.|Residual-only edits preserve bus. Test controlled residual-by-value interactions on demonstrated tasks.|
|18|Single-site edits miss sequence-distributed computation.|All edits target final position. Compare matched multi-position edits while controlling total intervention norm.|
|19|Donor similarity is the wrong objective for a reusable component.|High priority: broad donor contexts differ in many irrelevant ways. Use predefined output contrasts and selective task effects.|
|20|The current sample is simply underpowered.|Possible; intervals are broad. Expand only after choosing a more discriminating response metric and preregistered contrasts.|

Next priority: test whether true group members have more similar downstream response signatures than matched substitutes, across fresh hash-selected contexts. Use small symmetric finite differences, probability-weighted centered logit effects, and a separate projection removing temperature-like changes. Compare both within-context and across-context consistency; freeze context selection and the contrast before evaluation. This directly probes shared downstream computation without assuming that making the entire output more donor-like is the correct target. If it succeeds, validate selective effects on diverse competence-checked tasks and held-out combinations. Keep H702 settings fixed and test three fresh random four-group structures covering eight atoms. Each gets paired clean,5%noise and nonorthogonal versions. ### Where the alternative-featurizer tests now stand

- Shared dictionaries implement union support correctly. Pair coverage and guarded membership search repair conditional synthetic recovery, but joint label-free discovery is not yet demonstrated.
- Gate learning has a large optimization gap. Exact inference, label distillation and expected-cost training expose different tradeoffs between support recovery and reconstruction.
- Hierarchy implementations compose correctly, but ancestor/child mixing can preserve reconstruction while changing component interventions. Residualization selects a convention that works for an orthogonal teacher and changes a nonorthogonal one.
- Computational DAGs can learn sparse shared routes within a supplied candidate graph. Redundant paths and output scaling matter; edge count and accurate prediction alone do not establish the intended internal units.

The highest-priority remaining prerequisite is a joint, label-free shared-dictionary/group/gate experiment from scratch, with oracle-information controls clearly separated and all seeds retained. That closes a more important gap than further tuning this now-repaired DAG. After a bounded attempt, bring practical candidates back to early-layer activations for stability, geometry, intervention specificity and diverse task tests, reporting failures rather than certifying a universally better featurizer. Known synthetic topology, orthogonality or gate labels must not silently carry into claims of LLM discovery.

## H697 — Hierarchical units have a reconstructively invisible coordinate freedom

Construct an explicit decoder mixing D'=D T, where T is invertible with identity diagonal blocks and ancestor-row/descendant-column off-diagonal blocks. Transform coordinates by z'=T^{-1}z. Reconstruction is unchanged because D'z'=Dz. On hierarchy-valid supports, the coordinate transformation introduces activity only into ancestors of active descendants, so it preserves allowed support. A child-only support without ancestors violates that condition.

Test all128seed patterns of H696's seven-node tree,32Gaussian samples per pattern, in double precision. Use both the orthogonal teacher B and a nonorthogonal teacher B S whose children intentionally include0.8times a parent direction. The hierarchy and transforms are supplied; this is a constructive identifiability audit, not training or discovery.

Both teachers retain reconstruction to relative error below8e-32 after mixing, but component-removal effects change substantially (relative squared effect errors0.619–3.230). All valid-support leakage is exactly zero. A deliberately invalid child-only mask gives reconstruction error2.14 after masking the compensating ancestor coordinates. Thus the ambiguity depends on the activation implications, rather than being an unrestricted claim about every independently gated representation.

### An ancestor-residualized convention

Project each node's decoder directions off the span of its ancestors, in topological order. Track the corresponding invertible triangular basis change and apply its inverse to the already-gated coordinates. This preserves total reconstruction, and the hierarchy ensures transformed coordinates remain on valid support. This is a posthoc transformation of gated codes; it is not automatically equivalent to replacing the original raw linear encoder with another raw linear encoder.

| Teacher | Reconstruction error after convention | Largest component-effect error after convention |
|---|---:|---:|
|orthogonal|7.26e-32|1.37e-14|
|nonorthogonal|7.51e-32|1.11|

The convention recovers orthogonal teacher contributions to numerical precision. For the intentionally nonorthogonal teacher, leaf effect errors remain0.390 and root error1.114 despite unchanged reconstruction. The algorithm has reassigned shared ancestor content; it has not discovered the original nonorthogonal generative decomposition. Orthogonality is an assumption/convention, not a consequence of reconstruction.

Applying the same procedure to the three H696 learned fits preserves reconstruction with relative change below5e-32 and reduces non-root effect errors to at most1.22e-10. A small root discrepancy remains if decoder bias is kept separate: relative error0.00135–0.00592. Assigning that fixed bias to the always-active root on H696's nonempty support distribution reduces root effect error below6.7e-12. This is a second explicit attribution convention. Removing the root plus its assigned bias differs from the original intervention that held decoder bias fixed; these must not be conflated. Total reconstruction metrics include decoder bias throughout.

This supports the user's data-based canonical-form direction with a necessary qualification: observationally equivalent decompositions can be represented by a chosen convention, while internal component interventions remain convention-dependent. To claim actual reusable computational units, we need evidence beyond reconstruction, including constraints from model interventions, transfers and robustness to representation choices. Neither the residualized synthetic fit nor this invariance audit establishes a unique unit of LLM computation.

## H696 — Perfect hierarchical reconstruction does not recover causal refinements

Train a seven-node hierarchy: root, two intermediate categories, and four leaves. Each node contributes two independent teacher directions, all14directions orthonormal in20dimensions. Taxonomy union has nested memberships containing all ancestor directions and decodes their union once. Additive refinement has disjoint per-node coordinates and sums ancestor-plus-child terms. The flat control receives already-expanded ancestor gates. These are deliberately functionally equivalent for this supplied support structure; they are not competing discovery algorithms. Their equivalence prevents claiming hierarchical superiority merely from reconstruction. Initial outputs agree within2.38e-7; trained results are also nearly identical.

| Seed | Taxonomy held relative MSE | Mean non-root subspace overlap | Root removal relative effect error | Mean non-root removal effect error |

All nine fits reconstruct held combinations to relative MSE below7e-12. Yet non-root decoder subspaces have teacher overlap only0.486–0.875. Overlap is the average squared cosine of the two principal angles, invariant to rotations within each block.

Interventions remove a node's encoded reconstruction contribution while holding all other codes/gates fixed. The reference effect is that node's true teacher contribution for the same input. Non-root effect errors are substantial: squared error divided by teacher-effect energy ranges0.148–1.584. Between12.9%and52.8%of non-root removed energy lies outside the intended teacher refinement subspace. These are synthetic ground-truth checks, not LLM intervention claims.

The root is especially informative: its decoder subspace matches the true root almost perfectly, with negligible removed energy outside that subspace, yet removal-effect error is1.82–2.55. Correct decoder geometry does not guarantee correct coordinates or contribution attribution. Other blocks can contain ancestor directions that cancel root-coordinate terms in the total reconstruction. Observed reconstruction and intervention errors support this compensation explanation; a constructive invariance audit is the next way to establish the precise freedom.

This is why the user's requested manifold verification must include more than reconstruction or stable subspaces. Hierarchical activation constraints encode implications, but do not by themselves force child coordinates to mean ancestor-independent refinements. Additional constraints or interventions may select such a decomposition, and must be justified rather than assumed. Orthogonalizing child refinements could match this orthogonal teacher while imposing the wrong assumption on a real model.

### Refreshed hypotheses after the alternative-featurizer pilots

1. Missing coactivation constraints explain some composition failures — strongly supported by H688/H689.
2. Excessive learned overlap creates rank deficits — demonstrated for two failed fits in H690.
3. Straight-through discrete membership updates can destabilize good fits — observed in H690; exact source of instability not isolated.
4. Local discrete repair can recover functional structure — supported on this teacher by H691, not yet broad reliability.
5. Supplied group gates conceal a substantial discovery problem — supported by H692–H695.
6. Coordinates can carry sparsity while gates become redundant — all-open controls strongly support this here.
7. Linear gates are poorly matched to sign-symmetric presence — consistent with repeated failures; not a general theorem from these runs.
8. Sign-symmetric detectors contain useful structure — supported by label-distillation recovery, but not complete inference.
9. Straight-through training misses good decisions available to the same family — supported by H694's large accuracy gain, with changed objective.
10. Classification and reconstruction objectives favor different mistakes — supported by H694/H695's tradeoff.
11. A positive group penalty deliberately drops weak true features — supported by exact inference and penalty sweeps.
12. Larger combinations make groups cheaper to omit because other groups cover shared atoms — plausible explanation, marginal-effect audit still needed.
13. Exact inference can provide useful training signals without teacher labels — supported conditionally, not end-to-end discovery.
14. Quadratic detector capacity limits exact gate inference — possible; optimization remains a confound.
15. Noise and coefficient dynamic range determine recoverable group identity — untested in these noiseless pilots.
16. Reconstruction-equivalent dictionary rotations prevent unique atom recovery — imperfect atom alignment with exact reconstruction supports nonuniqueness, not a full characterization.
17. Hierarchical implications improve nested-data recovery beyond flat overlap — trained benchmark still required.
18. Additive refinements and taxonomy gates make different testable predictions — implementation semantics checked; empirical comparison pending.
19. Shared computational nodes generalize and have selective downstream effects — supported only in the fixed-topology synthetic DAG; discovered topology untested.
20. Real LLM blocks may reflect lexical/contextual mixtures rather than clean concept manifolds — earlier atlas and interventions support caution; richer featurizers have not resolved it.

The most actionable supported explanations are1,2,5,6,10and11. Their implication is to keep structural recovery, task output faithfulness, reconstruction and sparsity as separate measurements. The next broadening experiment is a trained nested-structure benchmark comparing taxonomy union gates and additive refinements with flat controls, using known topology to validate semantics before attempting topology discovery. Then test noisy/shared-computation cases and joint discovery. The original early-layer manifold stability, geometry and selective causal investigation remains the destination; no alternative is certified ready as a superior LLM featurizer yet.

Broad goal remains active.

## Previous continuation: H690

## H690 — Learned overlap can lose capacity and drift away from a successful fit

H689's failed learned memberships could reflect poor continuous weights or a support structure unable to represent the data. We distinguish these by calculating per-support rank bounds, then continuing each fit for 6000 additional steps with either frozen membership or live membership. All six continuations use the same H689 training data and batch stream within seed, fresh Adam at learning rate0.001, and supplied true group gates. This is not an exact optimizer resume. No heldout checkpoint selection.

For a support with k independent unit-variance teacher directions and only r selected dictionary atoms, any reconstruction confined to those atoms has expected relative squared error at least max(k−r,0)/k. This holds even with an optimal encoder and decoder. Bias cannot remove independent zero-mean missing variance. Exact population errors are computed analytically, and every initial/final support error respects this lower bound.

Seed11 has no rank deficit. Seed12 has deficits on one training pair and three held supports: for all four groups, it selects7atoms for8independent directions. Seed13 has deficits on four training pairs and all five held supports: all four groups select6atoms for8directions. Thus the failed memberships have provable capacity limitations. Rank counts are necessary, not sufficient, for recovery and do not explain all residual error.

| Seed | Initial held relative MSE | After frozen membership | After live membership |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|11|8.23922e-09|6.36305e-08|0.163317|
|12|0.110975|0.111847|0.250942|
|13|0.217279|0.217592|0.255741|

Frozen memberships preserve the successful fit and do not repair the failed ones. Live continuation changes membership in all three seeds and worsens all three fits, including seed11's previously near-exact solution. Its training relative error rises from2.17e-7 to0.232, so this is not merely heldout overfitting. The straight-through top-k membership optimizer is not a reliable monotonic search over discrete group structure. This experiment does not isolate optimizer restart, step size, surrogate gradients, or discrete switches as the sole cause; all remain candidate contributors.

The useful next comparison is training-only accepted discrete membership changes with continuous refits, against validated best-checkpoint straight-through training and a relaxed/annealed variant. Select by training or independent validation, never these heldout compositions. We should measure recovery reliability across seeds, not report only the successful seed. Thereafter, genuinely unsupervised group gates, trained hierarchy/computation benchmarks, matched budgets, and early-layer manifold/causal validation remain required.

This result does not reject shared dictionaries: known memberships already compose accurately. It identifies a concrete bottleneck in learning reusable groups. No LLM forwards, no new documents, and no access to the reserved LLM test split. All input/code hashes unchanged. Broad goal remains active.

## H688 — Missing coactivation constraints explain synthetic transfer failure

Audit H687 known-membership shared dictionaries analytically. For each group support q, the learned linear map is D diag(q) E plus decoder/encoder biases. With the orthonormal synthetic teacher B and independent unit Gaussian active coordinates, expected relative error is computed exactly from the squared Frobenius norm of (D diag(q) E−I) B diag(q), plus bias error, divided by active atom count. A fresh Monte Carlo check corroborates the formula.

Five unordered teacher-atom pairs never coactivate in training: (1,5),(1,6),(1,7),(2,7),(3,7). Encoder couplings between these coordinates are unconstrained by reconstruction on the observed supports. As a teacher-informed diagnostic, zero only those entries of E B, leaving the rest of the encoder and decoder unchanged.

## H687 — Alternative feature structures implemented; correctness and first synthetic learning tests

User proposal implemented in scripts/feature_structures/models.py:

1. Shared dictionary B, separately encoded atom coordinates and sparse group gates, binary group memberships, exact union decoding so shared atoms contribute once. Column normalization is in the forward parameterization. Membership/group selection supports threshold or fixed TopK budgets with explicitly documented straight-through surrogate gradients. The objective exposes reconstruction and group/coordinate/membership costs. Nonzero coordinate costs count actual nonzero codes in the forward pass. Fixed budgets constrain costs rather than reproducing a learned variable-size penalty solution.
2. Acyclic child-implies-parent closure with multiple parents. Closure changes gates, not extra decoder copies. Shared-union decoding still counts atoms once.
3. Separate additive-refinement module where ancestor and child terms both contribute. This is a distinct hypothesis; architecture alone does not guarantee residual semantic refinement.
4. Ordered computational DAG with learned node/edge gates, explicit products of parent coordinates, one evaluation per node, shared consumers, and node/edge interventions. The topology is supplied; automatic graph discovery is not yet implemented.

Ten semantic/numerical tests pass: shared-atom union and exact counts (including zero coordinates), selective shared-atom removal, multi-parent ancestor closure without duplicate decoding, closure idempotence, invalid/cyclic edge rejection, additive refinement, finite nonzero surrogate gradients and column normalization, fixed-support finite-difference coordinate gradient, exact oracle reconstruction of unseen combinations, and nonlinear shared computation with selective node/edge ablation. Tests are in tests/test_feature_structures.py. Straight-through gradients are tested for connectivity/finiteness, not incorrectly compared with derivatives of hard discrete selection.

Thus H685's coordinate result is not solely a nonorthogonal code-basis artifact. This still does not prove a smooth manifold.

Value0 provides a useful architecture-based control: all selected blocks show effectively zero within-token coordinate variation and no mixed activation support for repeated validation token identities. Token prediction is imperfect mainly because of finite counts/smoothing and rare or unseen identities; it must not be interpreted as contextual information in value0.

Residual support remains strongly lexical. Many stable blocks are dominated by punctuation, common function words, and byte fragments. Mean token-predictor skill is0.626 for selected residual0 blocks and0.705 for residual1. Position alone provides essentially no predictive improvement under this coarse16-position test. Frequency sometimes helps but generally less than token identity.

Yet active residual coordinates vary within token identities: average within-token fraction0.649 for residual0 and0.800 for residual1; after unit normalization,0.706 and0.833. These averages describe the selected blocks and eligible repeated-token occurrences, not the whole representation. They show that contextual variation exists within lexically associated blocks; they do not identify its semantic meaning or demonstrate a low-dimensional smooth manifold.

The promising unit may be a token-conditioned contextual state rather than a task label indicated solely by block activation. For example residual0 block27 often activates at periods, while residual1 block36 often activates at commas/parenthetical boundaries. These are descriptive lexical associations, not semantic names. Differences in internal coordinates could reflect syntax, discourse, nearby content, activation geometry or other nuisance factors. A stable punctuation block is not automatically a sentence-boundary computation.

## H684 — Residual blocks show reproducible structure beyond a scrambled reference

Use the H683 selected featurizers, with no new fitting. For every site/width, compare seed681 to seeds682 and683. Orthonormalize each decoder block and compute overlap as the mean squared principal cosine between subspaces. Hungarian assignment maximizes total overlap under a one-to-one block matching. This permits arbitrary rotations within blocks. Then compare matched binary activation support on4096 validation examples using Jaccard intersection/union.

The reference applies a deterministic signed permutation to the ambient coordinates of the second model's decoder, independently reoptimizes the block assignment, and evaluates support overlap under that assignment. It preserves each model's internal decoder geometry and original support frequencies while disrupting the shared ambient alignment. It is one reference per pair, not a significance test or a comprehensive null distribution.

Table reports pair-averaged means restricted to blocks selected on at least32validation examples in both models. Each method's eligible subset can differ because its matching differs. Full all-block metrics, assignments, scores and counts are retained in JSON; therefore these conditional means must not be treated as global recovery rates.

Occupied width16 residual0/1 blocks reach about0.42 mean subspace overlap and0.36 support Jaccard, versus approximately0.017 and0.025–0.035 under the scrambled reference. The value stream has much weaker learned agreement (about0.128 for both at width16). Across residual sites, width16 has stronger conditional overlap/support stability than widths1/4, despite worse reconstruction. This is useful evidence that reconstruction ranking alone would miss a potentially interesting block organization.

The agreement is partial, not near-identical recovery. Wider subspaces also differ in chance overlap, occupancy, capacity allocation and ease of matching, so the numerical comparison is not a proof that16-dimensional blocks are the correct units. The reference addresses some matching effects, not all. Stable blocks could encode lexical categories, position, activation scale, or mixtures of unrelated factors. Subspace stability says nothing directly about whether the occupied points form a smooth manifold.

Residual0 and residual1 width16 blocks are now justified exploratory candidates for a small atlas, with value0 and width1 serving as useful contrasts. Next inspect robustly matched examples and internal coordinates while testing how much activity can be predicted by token identity/frequency and position. Compare same-token occurrences across contexts and held-out documents. A contextual residual after lexical controls would be stronger evidence for computational regime labels than a coherent list of token types. Use actual-example block swaps and downstream response prediction before assigning computational meaning. PCA and a conventional ReLU SAE comparison remain outstanding.

Relative MSE divides squared reconstruction error by centered/scaled activation energy. Dead means never selected on4096 validation vectors, not provably inactive on the full distribution. Effective rank is the covariance participation ratio (trace squared / sum of squared eigenvalues) of coordinates conditional on block selection, restricted to blocks with at least32 validation selections. It measures dimensional usage, not smoothness, connectedness, semantic unity or causal validity.

The one-dimensional baseline reconstructs better at every site in this fixed-compute comparison. Width4 blocks use roughly2.2–2.8 effective dimensions; width16 blocks roughly5.4–7.0. A block could mix independent factors or unrelated lexical identities.

## H681 — Document-separated activation panel for early block-sparse featurizers

The user's proposed direction is to train block-sparse featurizers on early activations, identify genuinely useful multidimensional structures, and derive candidate computational labels without manually supplied tasks. This experiment prepares the task-blind data and fixes the initial comparison protocol.

The existing corpus includes packed windows, so a naive row split could share documents across train/test. We instead inspect existing document-hashed panels, deduplicate by complete-document token hash, and deterministically order hashes with the H681 salt. The available pool contains26048 unique previously used documents. Select2048 training,256 validation and256 test documents, with no document-hash overlap. This is internal featurizer holdout, not a claim that the model never trained on the text or that related documents are absent.

For each selected existing window, run its first128 tokens through blocks0–2 and sample16 fixed positions (7,15,...,127). Capture the persistent layer0 value vector and residual streams after blocks0,1,2. Each site has32768 training,4096 validation and4096 test activation vectors, width1152, saved in float32. Token IDs, complete windows, positions, source-row mappings and document hashes are retained for subsequent geometry and lexical-control audits. No diagnostic task prompts or labels enter this panel.

The persistent value stream is expected to be strongly token-identity based in this architecture; contextual residuals are separate sites. A visually coherent value block is not automatically a computational regime. Contextual labels should be evaluated beyond lexical identity, token frequency and formatting.

Preregistered first comparison: block dimensions1,4,16, total decoder width2304, active scalar budget32 (32one-dimensional coordinates,8four-dimensional blocks or2sixteen-dimensional blocks), three seeds. Center and globally scale from training statistics only, without per-example normalization. Checkpoints selected on validation; final test reserved for frozen evaluation. Parameter count, active-coordinate budget and reconstruction quality should be reported separately rather than conflated. The one-dimensional signed baseline must be identified as such if used; a conventional ReLU SAE is a distinct comparison, not automatically identical.

Evaluate held-out reconstruction, occupancy/dead blocks, effective within-block rank, and across-seed matched subspace stability before assigning semantic labels. A block can merge unrelated structures or merely group frequent lexical identities. Follow promising blocks with real-example coordinate swaps and downstream write/behavior prediction, comparing against PCA and capacity-matched one-dimensional features. Unsupervised cluster labels remain candidate regimes until they predict intervention responses beyond token and format baselines.

This experiment has collected data, not trained a featurizer or discovered a manifold. Training and causal evaluation remain outstanding. The recent signed content-routing findings provide a benchmark, not supervision for fitting or selecting blocks.

## H680 — Behavioral switch requires matching value identity

On the original eight competent month-copy receivers, exhaustively cross the native copy versus paired task coefficient with all eight copy-context value identities. Replace the full original input write: new coefficient times selected value minus native coefficient times receiver value. Repeat with donor vectors rescaled to receiver norm. Include eight zero-edit baselines;264 forwards total. No outcome-based selection.

At task coefficients, matching values produce8/8 receiver-next outputs. Every mismatched value preserves receiver copying (56/56), under both native and matched norms. Native-copy coefficients preserve copying for all matched and mismatched values. Thus coefficient magnitude alone does not produce the switch; identity alignment matters.

With norm-matched mismatched values, donor-current logits fall in all56 cases (mean−2.9231), while receiver-current logits change only−0.1666 on average. Receiver-next logits fall−0.4081; donor-next logits change−0.0305. Matching values instead lower current logits−2.1063 and raise next logits+0.3402. The effect tracks the value's represented input more clearly than a generic task signal or direct donor-next answer write.

Seven off-diagonal cases count as donor-next top1 only because the donor's next month equals the receiver's unchanged copied month. These labels overlap; they are not evidence of donor-answer transfer.

A posthoc output-level audit substitutes only observed edited logits into native outputs. Replacing the current-input logit alone yields next-month top1 in7/8; replacing next-month logit alone yields0/8; replacing both yields8/8. This supports suppression as the dominant route to the top1 switch, with the next-answer change needed in one example. It is a readout diagnostic using observed effects, not an internal intervention or a causal decomposition. Full distributions remain different.

The supported local account is a signed content-specific write interacting with existing receiver preferences. It is not a free-standing successor operation, universal task switch, or unique canonical basis. Every prompt and value here has been examined previously. The next user-proposed research direction is to investigate block-sparse featurizers on early activations, evaluate the quality of recovered multidimensional structures, and use their activity as candidate unsupervised computational labels. This result supplies a concrete causal benchmark: do discovered early blocks preserve input identity and predict the effects of later content-specific routing?

On month-copy receivers, next-task coefficients yield8/8 next-month predictions. Previous-task coefficients yield7/8 next and1/8 previous, while neither preserves copying. The mean next-minus-previous margin rises with either donor (+0.6046 next donor,+0.5653 previous donor). Therefore importing a coefficient from a previous-task prompt does not reliably import the previous operation. Mean month coefficients are close for next(+0.3394) and previous(+0.3206), versus copying(+0.0605).

Integer effects are weaker: either task coefficient moves copy receivers from1/8 to2/8 next outputs, with no previous outputs and5/8 still copying. Mean coefficients are+0.2216 next,+0.2528 previous and−0.0857 copy. Thus even a similar gate separation across domains does not guarantee the same behavioral switch; receiver values and surrounding computation matter.

The evidence favors a gate that can reduce copying and expose a context-dependent next-item preference, rather than an intrinsic scalar encoding the requested direction. This is a comparison of explanations, not proof that suppression alone generates succession. Native previous tasks fail, so this cannot rule out different gates or coefficients during genuinely successful previous-item computation. It also does not establish which component carries the sequential preference: value/readout geometry, other residual content, or their interaction.

Next cross coefficient and value identity on the original competent H678 month-copy receivers. Keep prompts fixed, choose a deterministic alternate query item as value donor, and compare native/copy versus task gate with receiver versus donor values. Include full native-write replacement accounting rather than simply adding a donor vector. Track both receiver-related and donor-related next/current tokens and full-vocabulary top1. This tests whether the effective control is content-bound, rather than interpreting a scalar alone as the computational unit. Retain the H679 competence failure as evidence of context sensitivity; do not silently replace it with the earlier successful panel.

On month copying prompts, replacing the query coefficient with its paired successor-task value changes all8/8 full-vocabulary top predictions from the copied month to the correct next month. This includes December→January. Mean task-minus-copy logit margin rises2.4465. This is a behavioral switch, not merely damage to copying or a restricted-candidate effect. Same-instruction cyclic donor swaps preserve8/8 copying and have nearzero mean margin change (−0.0033).

In the reverse direction, replacing the successor-task coefficient with the copy coefficient lowers the task-minus-copy margin in all8/8 examples (mean−2.2184), but task top1 remains7/8. Thus this coefficient is sufficient to induce succession in these copying contexts, but its task value is not necessary for top1 succession in the native task contexts. Other context-dependent computation already supports the task. Copy→task swaps do not establish that the coefficient alone implements or uniquely represents the full successor relation.

Plural swaps are qualitatively different: no accuracy switches, small margin changes, and giving copying prompts task coefficients does not consistently favor plurals. Task prompts receiving copying coefficients slightly improve mean correct-target CE even while their plural-minus-singular margin falls. This again separates task loss from the contrast between two selected candidates, and disfavors treating this scalar as a universal transformation gate.

Leading interpretation: a scalar controls access to an input-associated direction which, in these month contexts, can shift behavior from copying to the next-month continuation. A competing explanation remains that suppressing copying unmasks a preexisting sequential prior, rather than the scalar representing the requested operation. Earlier broad-vocabulary probes showed that this value direction was not uniquely next-month selective, so the current result does not erase that alternative.

Next distinguish operation-specific routing from a released prior with a predeclared next/previous/copy demonstration panel using matched month inputs and formats. Freeze the same gate intervention procedure, inspect native competence first, retain all outcomes, and test whether previous-task coefficients can induce previous-month outputs or merely alter copying/next-month bias. Include another ordered domain before claiming generality. No new arbitrary prompt tuning after intervention outcomes.

## H676 — Competent demonstrations enable a sharper mechanism test

The previous no-demonstration held-out transformation subset had0% exact next-token accuracy, limiting claims about successful computation. H676 fixes two demonstration formats before inference and screens six task families with matched copying controls. Four examples precede each query. Queries comprise four prior held-out and four prior fresh-panel inputs, eight per family. Demonstration/query inputs are disjoint. Formats are arrow pairs or Input/Answer lines with a task instruction. Vocabulary/items are reused; prompt sequences are new, not independent fresh-data validation.

Predeclared rule: a family/format qualifies only if both its transformation and copying control achieve at least6/8 full-vocabulary top1 correctness. All192 prompts and all12 cells are retained. No interventions or template revisions were selected after observing results.

| Family | Format | Task correct /8 | Copy correct /8 | Qualified |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
|plural|arrow|7|7|True|
|plural|labeled|6|8|True|

|addition|labeled|2|8|False|

|agreement|labeled|8|8|True|

Five cells qualify: plural in both formats, successor in arrow format, and agreement in both formats. Agreement copying always asks for The, so its perfect copy score is a weak control for item-sensitive copying. Task agreement has balanced is/are answers. Plural and month results supply successful single-token transformations for the previously investigated mechanism. Antonyms, capitals and addition remain below the fixed threshold and are not silently discarded.

This is evidence for competence under these demonstrations, not proof that the earlier mechanism explains it. Format sensitivity is substantial: antonym correctness is5/8 with arrows versus1/8 with labels; capitals4/8 versus2/8. Demonstrations alter context length, attention opportunities and task specification together. The present screen does not attribute the improvement solely to any one of those factors.

### Refreshed hypothesis set and discriminating experiments

These are qualitative priorities, not posterior probabilities. Multiple explanations can coexist.

| # | Hypothesis | Current assessment | Discriminating observation |
|---|---|---|---|
|1|A signed gate controls generic input support.|Strong local evidence on earlier prompts.|Native sign predicts full finite input-write removal on competent prompts.|
|2|The same gate controls whether to copy or transform.|Plausible, incomplete.|Matched task/copy gate changes predict distinct performance effects.|
|3|Carried content is the main value source across formats.|Supported earlier, transfer untested.|Local/bus decomposition stays carried-dominated in demonstration prompts.|
|4|Layer14 projection supplies suppressive alignment.|Supported as a composition, source attribution incomplete.|Matched readout mapping and scrambled-coordinate controls across layers.|
|5|Head4 is a dedicated successor operator.|Disfavored by broad content effects.|Selective successor dependence beyond matched copying and pluralization would revive it.|
|6|Opposing heads cancel broadly during native computation.|Disfavored as a general account.|Measure coefficient-weighted cancellation on new prompts, not bare directions.|
|7|Input support also supports semantically associated answers.|Supported by plural/capital removal effects.|Task-answer damage persists after controlling input-copy competition.|
|8|Transformations rely on additional heads beyond head4.|Likely but not localized.|Whole-input-write removal has distinct task impact beyond head4 removal.|
|9|Demonstration answers provide a competing retrieval route.|New high-priority alternative.|Remove demonstration-answer writes separately from query-input writes.|
|10|Example relation, rather than answer retrieval, specifies the operation.|Plausible.|Change example relations while preserving output-token counts.|
|11|Recent demonstrations dominate task selection.|Untested.|Reverse fixed example order with the same query and compare gates/behavior.|
|12|Output formatting controls much of apparent competence.|Supported as a sensitivity, mechanism unknown.|Transfer across arrow/labeled formats at matched competence and analyze punctuation contributions.|
|13|The tested late gate is a downstream correlate of earlier task selection.|Plausible.|Gate swaps fail while earlier-state interventions transfer behavior.|
|14|Later layers compensate for an altered input write.|Supported in local derivative magnitudes.|Compare small versus full removal and direct versus full responses.|
|15|Distributed redundant heads preserve correctness under removal.|Plausible.|Joint removal produces effects absent from isolated removals.|
|16|A compact task-independent value basis survives context changes.|Plausible but unproven.|Fit only discovery inputs, predict held-out intervention effects across tasks/formats.|
|17|Different task contexts require different effective bases.|Compatible with wording sensitivity.|Shared-basis predictions systematically lose to matched-context bases at equal capacity.|
|18|Behavior-equivalent compression hides distinct causal responses.|Open, central to canonical-form question.|Equal-KL models diverge under the same held-out interventions.|
|19|Observed transfer reflects narrow vocabulary/domain reuse.|Live limitation.|Freeze rules and replicate on independently specified new identities and relations.|
|20|Some apparent task behavior is a shortcut rather than the intended relation.|Live alternative.|Counterbalance answer frequencies, example overlap and relation-consistent distractors.|

Highest immediate information value: test hypotheses1–3 against9 and13 on the competent panel, with failed cells retained as secondary comparisons. Predeclare interventions before outcomes: remove query-input writes from head4 versus all heads, and remove demonstration-answer writes from head4 as a distinct source control. Measure native signed coefficients and full downstream effects; report task/copy CE and exact accuracy separately from KL. Query-input spans and all demonstration-answer spans must be determined from tokenizer offsets, with multi-token agreement/addition inputs handled explicitly. Do not select individual correct examples as the sole analysis set; use every item in each prequalified cell, plus all unqualified cells descriptively.

Removing head4 lowers the input logit under both instructions for nouns, antonyms and capitals, and under copying for months. Month task prompts instead show a small input-logit increase, matching the direct-path sign reversal inferred in H674. Removing all input-position writes lowers input logits in all eight family/context means. Thus the principal direct-path sign pattern survives full downstream computation and finite removal.

The contributions support useful copying: all-head removal reduces copying top1 from93.75% to25% for nouns,75% to25% for adjectives,87.5% to56.25% for countries and100% to43.75% for months. Head4-only removal produces smaller losses, with month copying still100% despite worse CE. This illustrates why accuracy alone can hide weakened predictions.

Task behavior does not improve into successful transformation. All native and edited task top1 rates are0% on this held-out subset. Removing all input writes worsens correct-target CE in every task family; removing head4 modestly improves antonym CE (−0.0389), but worsens the other three. Suppressing the current input is therefore not sufficient for computing the requested answer; these writes can support related answers as well as copying. Native failure also limits how much these prompts can reveal about successful task algorithms.

This supports signed context-dependent control of input-associated content, while arguing against treating removal of copying as a general solution to transformation tasks. A next high-information step is to repeat the gate/value test on independently specified prompts where the native model actually performs the intended transformation, with matched copying controls and a predeclared competence criterion. Keep all attempted prompt families in the report, including failures, to avoid selecting a flattering mechanism after looking at interventions. The diverse-domain mechanism and task-solver claims must remain separate.

## H674 — Native signed gates mostly turn opposing directions into reinforcement

H673 found both boosting and suppressing carried-value directions across heads. H674 includes the actual signed bilinear attention coefficient for the input position, separates weighted local and carried values, and sums the corresponding direct residual/readout derivatives. It uses the same128 contexts across four domains, copy/task instructions, four items and four forms. No fitting or selection.

These coefficients are not attention probabilities. A negative coefficient reverses a suppressive value direction into a boosting write. This distinction materially changes the interpretation of the previous direction probes.

| Family | Context | Net input slope | Positive head sum | Negative head sum | Mean abs(net)/sum(abs(head)) | Head4 input slope | Mean head4 coefficient |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|plural|copy|2.2261|2.2276|-0.0015|0.9987|1.2804|-0.3028|
|plural|task|2.1492|2.1527|-0.0035|0.9964|1.2369|-0.2950|
|antonym|copy|1.7411|1.7597|-0.0185|0.9758|0.4615|-0.2168|
|antonym|task|1.8513|1.8597|-0.0083|0.9901|0.5220|-0.2354|
|capital|copy|0.8689|0.9877|-0.1188|0.7082|0.2557|-0.0664|
|capital|task|0.5718|0.6652|-0.0934|0.7608|0.1797|-0.0475|
|successor|copy|1.5767|1.6630|-0.0863|0.8982|0.3018|-0.1148|
|successor|task|0.6016|0.8597|-0.2581|0.5414|-0.0741|0.0295|

Head effects in this table include both local and carried input-token writes. Positive/negative sums classify each combined head effect before summing across heads. The cancellation ratio is descriptive scalar arithmetic, not a fraction of causal responsibility. It describes only the current-input logit and this token position.

Most contexts exhibit reinforcement, not substantial opposition: plural and antonym family means have ratios near1. Head4's mean coefficient is negative under both copying and task instructions in those domains and in capitals, so its native direct contribution boosts the current input despite the suppressive direction seen when increasing the coefficient. Capitals show some cancellation. Month task instructions have the strongest mean cancellation and a much smaller net boost than month copying. Head4 changes from mean input boost+0.3018 in copy contexts to suppression−0.0741 in successor contexts, with mean coefficient moving from−0.1148 to+0.0295.

This updates the leading hypothesis: the unit under investigation behaves more like a signed, context-controlled content readout than a permanently suppressive head. Earlier intervention findings remain valid: increasing its coefficient suppresses input-associated content, but the native operation can have the opposite sign. Opposing available readout directions do not establish native cancellation. The native weighted evidence is essential.

These are derivatives at the native final residual of scaling each input-token write along the direct skip path. They are not an additive decomposition of finite output logits, do not include later branch responses, and do not establish behavioral necessity. Differences between copy/task means also include different native final readout states; they are not isolated causal effects of changing only the gate. Other token positions remain part of the native attention output but are absent from the reported input-position accounting.

The next test is finite removal of the measured native input-token writes: head4 alone and all nine heads together, followed by full downstream computation. Compare copying versus task instructions, read current/answer logits, output KL and correct-target loss separately. This tests whether the direct sign reversal predicts actual behavior and whether reducing input support helps the requested operation or merely damages useful copying.

Heads0,1,7 boost the current input in every context; heads3,4,6 suppress it in every context. Head4 has the strongest mean input suppression and strongest mean other-input-minus-current margin after residual norm matching, but suppression is not unique to this head. Head3 is less selective against current inputs relative to other domain inputs despite consistently negative current logits.

For head4,32 fixed seed673 signed coordinate permutations scramble its carried-value coordinates before applying its unchanged output projection. Each permutation is shared across contexts. This preserves the head-space value norm; dividing the resulting slopes by projected residual norm also removes output-size differences. These are off-manifold alignment controls, not natural alternative heads or a population null distribution.

| Family | Native unit margin ×10⁴ | Smallest scrambled mean ×10⁴ | Largest scrambled mean ×10⁴ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|plural|4.9227|-0.8195|0.5664|

Native head4 alignment exceeds every scrambled family mean in all four domains. This supports structured alignment of carried content with its learned readout, rather than a consequence of vector size alone. Repeated contexts share inputs and all four families were previously inspected; do not treat128 contexts as independent discoveries or infer statistical significance from the control rank.

The revised leading hypothesis is that multiple heads provide opposing readouts of carried input content, with context-dependent signed gates determining the net effect. This is a candidate mechanism rather than an established circuit: the actual gates can reverse signs, other token positions contribute, local values also contribute, and later branches can change the response. Calling head4 a dedicated successor feature remains unsupported.

Next measure actual coefficient-weighted input-token writes across the nine heads, separate carried and local contributions, and compare their sums under matched copying/task instructions. This will test whether the available opposing directions participate in native cancellation or whether gating makes most irrelevant. Retain full-head/input-token distinctions and follow any direct-readout finding with finite interventions before claiming necessity or behavioral benefit.

## Previous continuation: H672

## H672 — Carried value supplies most of the suppressive response

H671 located suppressive alignment in the projected input value before later branches. H672 separates that value into its actual weighted local and persistent-bus contributions at layer14 head4. The same128 previously inspected contexts cover nouns/plurals, adjectives/antonyms, countries/capitals and months/succession, with copy/task instructions, four items and four forms. No fitting or item selection was performed.

The learned mixing scalar is4.625. Effective value equals−3.625 times the local value plus4.625 times the persistent bus value. This is an unconstrained signed combination, not a convex mixture or a fraction of information. Results below retain these native weights; they do not compare the unweighted sources.

Each weighted projected component was added at the final attention write at strengths±0.025 and±0.05, followed by normal downstream computation. A zero-edit replay was included. Direct residual/readout derivatives were computed separately as in H671.

| Family | Component | Full input slope | Full answer slope | Direct input slope | Direct answer slope |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|plural|local|-0.1194|-0.0961|-0.0408|-0.0328|
|plural|bus|-2.5889|-2.5088|-4.0980|-3.9205|
|antonym|local|-0.1441|-0.0611|-0.0726|0.0036|
|antonym|bus|-1.5908|-0.0261|-2.0555|-0.3224|
|capital|local|-0.0848|-0.1005|0.0745|0.0201|
|capital|bus|-3.1191|-1.6842|-3.9786|-2.3210|
|successor|local|-0.0876|-0.0561|0.0030|0.0203|
|successor|bus|-2.3534|0.6810|-2.5881|0.2060|

The carried component suppresses the input in all128 contexts. The local component has a smaller suppressive full response in127/128 contexts. On family-mean input slopes, the carried contribution accounts for roughly92–97% of the summed signed response; this arithmetic comparison is not a causal share or necessity estimate. Both contributions reinforce suppression on average. Plural/capital answer suppression also comes primarily from the carried contribution. For months, the carried component boosts the next-month answer while the local component modestly suppresses it.

This shifts the leading hypothesis toward a late context-dependent routing gate acting on content carried from an earlier value representation. A locally constructed layer14 semantic operator is less consistent with these observations. However, the layer14 output projection still determines how the carried vector maps into residual space: the experiment does not prove that the earlier representation alone encodes suppression. The next discriminating test should compare how different heads' output projections read the same carried representation, including sign, specificity and intervention magnitude. That separates shared carried content from head-specific suppressive readout geometry.

## H671 — Suppressive alignment is present before later branches

We compared the full finite response to increasing layer14 head4's projected input value with its direct residual path to the final readout. The same128 H670 contexts span nouns/plurals, adjectives/antonyms, countries/capitals and months/succession, with copying and task instructions, four held-out items and four forms each. This is a retrospective analysis of existing contexts, not fresh-data replication.

The direct direction multiplies the projected value by the product of residual coefficients in blocks15–17 (1.443206787109375), then differentiates the final RMS normalization, unembedding and tanh saturation at the native final state. It omits changes in MLP14 and subsequent attention/MLP branches. Full effects use the saved central finite intervention at ±0.05; ±0.025 checks step sensitivity. Raw unembedding alignment is also inspected, without interpreting its scale as an output effect.

All128 contexts have negative current-input logit alignment in the raw projection, negative direct readout slopes, and negative full slopes. Thus later branches are not required to create the observed suppressive sign in these local diagnostics.

| Family | Direct input slope | Full input slope | Direct answer slope | Full answer slope | Vocabulary cosine | Direct/full norm | Relative error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|plural|-4.1388|-2.7083|-3.9532|-2.6048|0.9676|1.4926|0.5830|
|antonym|-2.1281|-1.7349|-0.3188|-0.0871|0.9518|1.1685|0.3979|
|capital|-3.9041|-3.2039|-2.3009|-1.7846|0.9796|1.2083|0.3031|
|successor|-2.5851|-2.4410|0.2263|0.6249|0.9827|1.0145|0.1910|

Vocabulary comparisons center each response by its native-probability-weighted mean and use the native probability distribution as the weighting. Cosine measures directional alignment; relative error is norm(full−direct)/norm(full). These are weighted local metrics, not an unweighted guarantee for rare tokens. Table entries are means over32 contexts per family, pooling copying and task instructions.

Later branches attenuate mean input suppression in all four families, most strongly for nouns. High cosine does not imply numerical equivalence: mean relative error is0.583 for plurals and0.191 for months. Related plural and capital answers are already suppressed by the direct path. For months the full next-month answer slope is0.625 versus0.226 directly, indicating that later processing materially changes the alternative-token response even when the overall direction aligns closely.

The leading explanation is a context-dependent gate applied to an input-associated value direction that already aligns with suppression at the output. This is stronger evidence against interpreting this vector as a dedicated successor operator. It does not establish that suppression is beneficial, that the actual signed coefficient always suppresses, or that this head is necessary. Increasing the coefficient is the tested intervention; a negative coefficient can reverse the effect.

The direct path is an analytic diagnostic, not a finite branch ablation. Full−direct approximates the combined downstream derivative near zero and must not be read as causal shares. The value itself contains local and persistent-bus contributions. The next informative experiment is to separate those two value sources before projection, test whether their sum reconstructs the measured direction, and compare their direct and full responses across the same diverse domains. A fresh-item replication and stronger random-direction controls remain needed before claiming broad generality.

## H670 — Input-linked suppression generalizes, including to associated answers

H669 found current-token suppression in month/number contexts. H670 extends the same finite probe to nouns/plurals, adjectives/antonyms, countries/capitals and months/succession. It uses128 existing held-out single-token-input prompts: four items per family, four forms, copying and task instructions. No items or directions are fitted or selected from the new results. This is a retrospective domain comparison on an existing panel, not an unseen-item replication.

At layer14 head4's final attention write, add alpha times the receiver's projected effective input value, using fixed alphas−0.1,−0.05,−0.025,0,+0.025,+0.05,+0.1. The rest of the model runs normally. Reuse seed669's unit random direction, scaled to each receiver value norm, at±0.05. The actual input-token value is not assumed context invariant.

Readouts distinguish the raw input token from the requested task answer even in copying prompts. Also measure the average logit of the seven other input identities in the same eight-item family, excluding the current item. Those margins guard against interpreting a uniform logit shift as input-selective suppression. The alternative set is limited to this panel, not the whole vocabulary.

**Central finite logit slopes at alpha0.05:** slope=(logit(+alpha)−logit(−alpha))/(2alpha), per unit coefficient.

| Family | Context | Input token | Task answer | Other inputs mean | Answer−input | Other inputs−input |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|plural|copy|-2.7319|-2.6629|0.3612|0.0690|3.0931|
|plural|task|-2.6847|-2.5467|0.3748|0.1381|3.0595|
|antonym|copy|-1.7427|-0.0989|-0.0319|1.6438|1.7108|
|antonym|task|-1.7270|-0.0753|-0.0315|1.6517|1.6955|

|successor|task|-2.4379|0.6282|0.3699|3.0662|2.8078|

Every one of128 tested contexts has a negative input-token slope and positive other-input-minus-current margin slope. Thus input-linked suppression extends beyond ordered sequences and is not simply a common logit offset. The pattern appears under both copying and task instructions. Its magnitude is not normalized across domains because native value norms differ.

The requested answer is not generally boosted in absolute logit terms. Plural answers fall almost as much as singular inputs (about−2.55 to−2.66 versus−2.68 to−2.73); only21/32 noun contexts have a positive answer-minus-input slope. Capitals fall substantially (about−1.74 to−1.83) along with their country inputs (about−3.20). Antonym answer slopes are slightly negative. Month-successor answers instead rise. Therefore the unit is not well described as simply removing the incorrect input while selecting the correct task answer.

A broader interpretation is suppression of content associated with the input value, with uneven effects on related alternatives. Singular/plural and country/capital relations suggest that the affected content can extend beyond the exact token identity. This remains a hypothesis about one tested direction, not proof of a general semantic cluster or feature ontology.

**Norm-matched random control margins, same strength:**

| Family | Context | Answer−input | Other inputs−input |
|---|---|---:|---:|
|plural|copy|-0.1930|-0.0304|

|antonym|task|-0.1515|-0.0714|

|capital|task|0.0819|-0.0715|
|successor|copy|-0.0520|0.1835|
|successor|task|-0.0033|0.2100|

These mean margins are much smaller and have mixed signs. One random direction is only a limited control, not a null distribution or a statistical significance claim. No superiority of all value directions over all random directions is inferred.

The next question is where the suppression originates. Compare the value vector's direct contribution through the residual skip path and final normalized/saturated readout with the measured effect after remaining MLP/attention processing. A strong direct alignment would suggest the projected value already encodes suppressive output structure; a large downstream change would implicate later transformations. Use full-vocabulary and selected-token comparisons, explicitly include residual scaling, and keep that linear path diagnostic distinct from the actual finite intervention. This is more informative than naming a semantic unit from the sign pattern alone.

The original model, native receiver values and context-dependent gate are still required. These probes do not establish head necessity, a unique canonical basis, a full task algorithm or improved task correctness. Previous fidelity improvements are compatible with adjusting the strength of broad content suppression.

The supported description is input-dependent value content multiplied by a coefficient conditioned on the task/form. It is not simply one generic copying→instruction routing change. A shared large coefficient for both next and previous would weaken a succession-specific interpretation even if both differ from copying. Independent item splits and an additional domain are needed to avoid relabeling an input-domain effect as semantics.

## Previous continuation: H665

## H665 — Mean routing change applied to receiver values explains much of head4's item variation

H664 localized layer14 head4 approximation error to input-token contributions. H665 factors the input write into signed routing coefficients c and projected effective value vectors V. For aligned input positions, the true copy→task change is sum(c_task V_task − c_copy V_copy). Copy/task input-token ID sequences are required to match exactly. Every input token is included; coefficient means are fitted per ordinal position, with fixed input-token count checked within each family. Four second-wording discovery items fit each family/form model; no held-out donor factor enters the predictive methods.

The new predictor replaces the unconditional input-write mean with sum(mean_discovery(c_task−c_copy) × V_receiver). It uses the receiver's actual values, preserving input identity, but only a discovery mean for the routing change. All other head-role, attention-layer and boundary predictions remain fixed. An alternative fixed-product control uses the product of discovery mean coefficient change and discovery mean receiver value, removing item-specific receiver values while keeping the factorized form.

Two donor-informed controls isolate factors: exact coefficient change applied to receiver values, and receiver coefficients applied to exact value changes. Exact input-write replacement remains the reference. These partial controls are not an additive decomposition of the full effect: the identity includes the interaction term Δc ΔV, alongside Δc V_receiver and c_receiver ΔV. Effective values are not assumed context invariant.

## Previous continuation: H664

## H664 — Head4 residual error comes predominantly from input-token contributions

H663 localized much of month-succession approximation error to layer14 head4 (zero-based). H664 reconstructs that head's final-position write as a sum over token positions. For each position, multiply the two normalized rotary query–key dot products divided by head dimension128 to obtain the signed bilinear coefficient; multiply by the effective value vector and project through head4's output-projection columns. Effective values include the module's own value contribution and persistent value bus with the checkpoint's native mixing parameter. These coefficients are signed products, not softmax attention probabilities.

Tokenizer offsets partition every position into four roles: instruction text, Input label and intervening formatting, actual input content, and trailing answer suffix. Tokens with non-whitespace characters are required to belong wholly to one role; whitespace-only tokens are assigned by their starting offset. Token IDs are checked against the frozen manifest, input substrings against explicit item fields, and no position is dropped. Role sums are bookkeeping partitions, not assumed semantic units.

Fit separate role-wise copy→task mean shifts on the four second-wording discovery items. For each held-out example, compute each role's true residual beyond that mean. Add selected exact role residuals to the same existing layer14 prediction, leaving all other head/layer predictions fixed. Evaluate all16 subsets of the four roles under both predicted and exact boundary states, retaining all96 cases. Full-role repair must reproduce H663's head4 repair before interpretation. These are donor-informed diagnostics, not deployable predictors.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|addition|0.007949|0.007991|0.007953|0.007310|0.007937|0.007338|
|agreement|0.005285|0.005229|0.005261|0.005242|0.005281|0.005159|

|plural|0.010843|0.010851|0.010783|0.010121|0.010712|0.009940|
|successor|0.086528|0.085965|0.086743|0.032417|0.086553|0.032080|

**Exact boundary:**

| Family | No repair | Input content only | All except input content | All head4 roles |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|addition|0.001671|0.001357|0.001686|0.001366|
|agreement|0.001706|0.001660|0.001646|0.001598|

For month succession, input-content repair alone nearly reproduces the full-head repair:0.08653→0.03242 with predicted boundary, versus0.03208 for all roles. With exact boundary,0.08167→0.02188 versus0.02185 for all roles. Repairing every role except input content leaves0.08621 or0.08164 respectively, essentially retaining the mismatch. The discrepancy is therefore in the input-position contribution to this head's write, rather than principally in instruction or answer-suffix positions.

Capitals and antonyms show the same dominant input-role pattern; plurals also benefit mostly from input repair under exact boundary. Agreement's small head4 error is more distributed among instruction, label and input roles. Addition's head4 contribution is modest because H663 identified head7 as its stronger layer14 residual. Input-only repair can slightly outperform all-role repair due to error compensation, so these numbers are not additive causal shares.

This narrows the mechanism but does not establish successful semantic retrieval or month succession. An input-token write depends both on its effective value vector and on coefficients computed from context-sensitive queries/keys. A large residual could arise because a fixed mean ignores changing token values even when routing changes are simple, because routing itself is item-dependent, or both. The task prompts are often incorrect, and fidelity is to their output distribution rather than to a ground-truth algorithm.

Next factor the aligned input-position contribution into coefficient and projected-value terms. Verify exact token alignment between copy and task prompts, measure how much the effective value changes across contexts, and reconstruct the head/input write from those factors. Then compare simple discovery-only predictions such as a mean coefficient change applied to the receiver's actual input-token value with the current unconditional mean write. For single-token months this is a particularly direct test of whether the useful computational unit is a context-dependent scalar gate on an input-specific vector. Multi-token inputs must be handled explicitly rather than collapsed to a selected token. Exact factor swaps can distinguish missing routing from missing content, but any claim of a predictive unit requires evaluation without held-out donor factors.

## Previous continuation: H663

## H663 — Layer14 head4 concentrates month-succession mean-prediction error

H662 showed that balanced-index and seven-item discovery means only modestly reduce layer14 error. H663 decomposes layer14 into its nine projected head writes (head indices0–8). Capture each head's final-position vector immediately before the attention output projection and multiply by that head's corresponding projection columns. The projection has no bias. These writes sum to the native attention output within floating-point tolerance.

For each family/form, fit each head's original four-discovery-item mean copy→task shift under the second wording. For each held-out item, define the head residual as true task-head write minus native copying-head write minus that head's discovery mean. Add selected exact residuals to the existing layer14 mean prediction. Other attention layers stay predicted. Evaluate all predicted, all nine heads repaired, nine single-head repairs, and nine leave-one-head-predicted conditions, under both predicted and exact boundary states. All96 held-out cases remain, for40 forward conditions.

Repairs use true held-out donor information and localize approximation error; they are not fitted predictors. The head basis is defined by architecture, not a newly discovered unique semantic feature basis. Single-head rankings are descriptive and need independent validation.
