## Previous continuation: H639

## H639 — Later MLP context explains much of wording transfer, while item transfer often requires coordinated attention

H638 was progress: a validated block9/input–downstream–readout factorial localized substantial prompt-dependent variation to the composition of incoming responses and later operators. H639 decomposes those later operators mechanistically.

At every block10–17, independently choose receiver or matched-donor values for three factors: C, bilinear MLP operating context; N, MLP RMS-normalization derivative; A, the normalized-attention Jacobian. A includes attention's own normalization, so N refers only to MLP normalization. Run all eight combinations, crossed with receiver/donor incoming block9 tangents and receiver/donor final readouts, for both donor maps and the three fixed probes. Factor exchanges are applied consistently across the eight later blocks. Residual skip weights are unchanged and shared across contexts. No fitting, prompt changes or output selection occurs.

The metric remains the norm of the remaining donor–receiver full-logit derivative gap under receiver probabilities. Lower is better;1 means no improvement relative to native receiver. These are local derivative counterfactuals, not finite task interventions. An all-donor operator is a validated endpoint, not an independently learned mechanism. Analytical factorizations reproduce both native and donor whole-block chains from H638 within1.35e-6 relative residual error.

**For wording changes with incoming tangent and readout already matched to the donor, later bilinear context is the strongest individual factor.** It reduces the gap from0.510–0.704 to0.192–0.353 across task families. Normalization alone offers little benefit; attention alone offers smaller or inconsistent benefit. Additional normalization or attention improves over context alone, and all three recover the donor to numerical tolerance.

| Cross-wording family; donor input/readout | Native later operators | C | N | A | C+N | C+A | N+A | C+N+A |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|copy|0.704|0.353|0.729|0.605|0.268|0.257|0.625|0.000|
|fact|0.637|0.241|0.614|0.643|0.101|0.178|0.620|0.000|
|plural|0.619|0.270|0.646|0.592|0.209|0.152|0.600|0.000|
|agreement|0.572|0.192|0.574|0.536|0.140|0.118|0.539|0.000|
|addition|0.510|0.293|0.535|0.478|0.218|0.200|0.488|0.000|

This is a conditional mechanistic result: it concerns which later factors reproduce the donor transformation when the donor incoming response and donor readout are available. It does not mean context replacement alone would reproduce the donor response starting from the receiver. With receiver incoming tangent and receiver readout, context-only remaining gaps are0.854–0.992; even complete donor later operators leave0.783–0.917, reproducing H638. The strong improvement in the first table depends on the incoming response and readout.

**Within-wording item changes often require attention and MLP context together.** The same factorial gives a qualitatively different pattern:

| Within-wording family; donor input/readout | Native later operators | C | N | A | C+N | C+A | N+A | C+N+A |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|copy|0.748|0.547|0.765|0.566|0.538|0.135|0.577|0.000|
|fact|1.132|1.208|1.074|0.932|1.346|0.401|0.864|0.000|
|plural|0.954|1.008|0.928|0.590|1.092|0.206|0.578|0.000|
|agreement|0.650|0.292|0.653|0.628|0.134|0.229|0.638|0.000|
|addition|0.755|0.441|0.771|0.527|0.422|0.146|0.544|0.001|

For facts, C alone worsens the gap1.132→1.208; C+N worsens it further to1.346. A alone lowers it to0.932, while C+A lowers it to0.401. Plurals show a similar conditional interaction: C alone worsens0.954→1.008, whereas C+A reaches0.206. Copying and addition also benefit substantially from coordinated C+A. Agreement differs: C alone already helps, and C+N is better than C+A. Thus a universal ranking of attention, MLP context and normalization is not supported.

These findings are consistent with a distinction between construction-related and item-related operator changes, but do not establish a strict division of labor. The within controls change lexical item and, for facts, target identity; cross controls change wording, position, tokenization and sometimes continuation competence simultaneously. Probability-weighted gap norms are relative to each pair's gap, so within/cross numerical ratios are not direct comparisons of absolute effect size. Full context independence is not assumed for any component.

The current most useful model of the evidence is a coordinated sequence of context-dependent transformations. Bilinear MLP operating contexts carry substantial information needed to transfer late computation across wording, conditional on matching the incoming response. Attention and MLP context often need to change together for item transfer. This goes beyond the observation that derivatives differ, but it still uses native donor operators rather than a compact predictive representation or semantic algorithm. The fundamental-unit question remains open.

Refreshed20-hypothesis map, with priorities based on current evidence:

1. Bilinear operating contexts capture construction-related variation in late transformations. Strong current support conditionally; prospectively test matched new wordings.
2. Coordinated attention and MLP context carry item-specific transformation differences. Supported for several within-template contrasts; test novel items and more donor pairings.
3. Incoming-response compatibility is essential to interpreting a later operator. Strong support from H638–639 factorials.
4. Readout effects depend on the incoming/internal response. Strong support; retain readout as an explicit factor.
5. A small fixed output-direction basis explains all responses. Weakened by held-out projection gaps.
6. Residual passthrough explains the apparent need for many units. Explains part of early held-out-direction error, insufficient later.
7. Task labels identify invariant operators. Weakened by wording and item effects.
8. Construction labels identify invariant operators. Plausible approximation, limited by agreement and within-template effects.
9. Normalization is negligible everywhere. Rejected as a general rule: it improves matched combinations and matters for agreement/item transfer.
10. Normalization alone drives the observed changes. Weak on these panels.
11. Attention alone accounts for item-specific transfer. Insufficient for facts/plurals; coordination matters.
12. Later MLP context alone accounts for item-specific transfer. Weakened by worsening on facts/plurals.
13. Independent layer/component effects add into a sufficient explanation. Weakened by factorial interactions and joint versus additive results.
14. Finite-dose curvature is the main source of mismatch. Weak for the small doses already validated; not settled at larger doses.
15. The original selected vector is uniquely special. Weakened by control probes, though it sometimes transfers better.
16. A shared internal low-dimensional basis rescues universality. Still possible with richer structured discovery, but tested spans remain insufficient.
17. A low-dimensional basis of *operator changes* transfers better than response bases. Open and promising after prospective replication; do not infer it from response spectra.
18. Apparent semantic structure comes from generic context mismatch. Still viable; same-wording controls and new minimally different prompts are needed.
19. Poor competence creates the whole phenomenon. Insufficient for competent copying/facts, but material for plural/addition interpretations.
20. Positional or tokenization changes masquerade as construction effects. Open: current template swaps are not controlled minimal pairs.

Next prioritize1,2,3,18,20 with a frozen prospective replication on copying and capital facts. Cross new items with matched paraphrases sharing an answer-introducing ending, include same-wording donor exchanges, and retain exact competence/format checks. Freeze the C/N/A contrasts and input/readout choices before evaluating results. This will test whether the wording-versus-item distinction survives improved controls rather than continuing to explain the same80 prompts. Only after replication should an operator-change basis be fitted and evaluated on held-out contexts/directions.

All five families, two donor conditions and three probes retained. Existing competence limitations and retrospective probe history carry over. No new natural-text documents; FineWeb remains26,112. Broad goal active and incomplete.

## Previous continuation: H638

## H638 — The block9 response and later operators must be matched; readout effects depend on the incoming computation

H637 was progress: cumulative MLP5–9 context replacement partly closed actual prompt-response gaps, leaving substantial unexplained differences. H638 localizes those differences with an exact local factorization rather than expanding layer replacements blindly.

Use the same frozen80-prompt panel, original/span2/orthogonal2 probes and two involutive donor maps: opposite wording with identical item, or same wording with item shifted by four. Factor the local full-logit derivative into three components: I, the residual tangent leaving block9; D, the product of downstream block10–17 native Jacobians; R, the native final RMS-normalization, unembedding and softcap derivative. Evaluate all eight receiver/donor choices, giving R_c D_b I_a. The injection itself remains the same direction. All tangent exchanges occur at the final position, consistent with causal propagation.

The donor map being an involution allows reciprocal mixed computations to be reused exactly. Incoming tangents are the centrally measured H635 values at±0.02; downstream maps are automatic derivatives at frozen native states. Mixed combinations need not be jointly realizable as prompts. These are local operator counterfactuals, not replacements of a complete finite forward computation.

**The all-donor endpoint validates the decomposition, rather than establishing a new semantic unit.** All-native and all-donor responses reproduce their original finite-difference responses within0.000983 and0.000928 relative error respectively. The largest endpoint error divided by the donor–receiver gap is0.001615. Recovery is expected when all components come from the same native donor; it is an implementation and numerical positive control, not evidence of compression.

**Across wording, the incoming block9 response and later operators both matter.** The table reports mean remaining gap relative to the native donor–receiver gap under receiver probabilities. Values below1 indicate movement toward the donor response; above1 indicate worsening. “I+D” uses donor incoming tangent and donor downstream transformations but retains the receiver readout.

| Family | I only | D only | R only | I+D | I+R | D+R | I+D+R |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|copy|0.738|0.869|1.092|0.369|0.704|0.841|0.000|
|fact|0.648|0.783|0.984|0.317|0.637|0.781|0.000|
|plural|0.659|0.917|0.967|0.283|0.619|0.854|0.000|
|agreement|0.601|0.893|0.997|0.335|0.572|0.826|0.000|
|addition|0.564|0.897|0.983|0.275|0.510|0.854|0.000|

Changing I alone leaves mean ratios0.564–0.738. Changing D alone leaves0.783–0.917. Changing both leaves only0.275–0.369. Thus neither a universal downstream transformation acting on different incoming responses nor a fixed incoming response followed by context-dependent processing captures the full contrast. Both sources of variation contribute, and their compatibility matters. These are average results over three probes, eight items and both exchange directions per task; they are not independent statistical trials.

**Readout cannot be assigned a fixed importance independent of the internal response.** Swapping R alone leaves ratios0.967–1.092 across wording, offering little improvement and worsening copying. Yet with donor I and D, the receiver readout leaves a0.275–0.369 gap, and donor R removes it to numerical tolerance. Therefore “readout alone does little” must not be converted into “readout does not matter.” Its effect depends on the tangent produced by preceding computation. Nor does the final drop give a unique causal share: changing factors in another order gives different incremental reductions.

Within-wording item controls show another pattern:

| Family | I only | D only | R only | I+D | I+R | D+R |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|copy|0.738|0.697|1.060|0.390|0.748|0.631|
|fact|0.972|1.061|1.179|0.678|1.132|0.569|

For facts, donor incoming tangent alone barely helps (0.972), while donor downstream operators plus donor readout leave0.569. This differs from the cross-wording pattern and argues against interpreting the components solely by task or syntax labels. Item changes can alter how the later computation and readout use a perturbation. The within controls change lexical identity and are not perfect minimal pairs.

**Interaction is substantial and explicitly measurable.** The complete2×2×2 factorial permits exact vector inclusion–exclusion terms: single effects, I×D, I×R, D×R and I×D×R. Averaged across cross-wording cases, their interaction norms divided by original gap norm are0.616,0.299,0.226 and0.222 respectively. Summing just the three single effects leaves mean gap0.656 even though all components jointly recover the donor. Within-wording corresponding interaction norms are0.443,0.226,0.173 and0.103, and the additive remaining gap is0.496. Norms do not add and are not causal percentages. The interaction decomposition reconstructs the full vector within1.2e-16 absolute error. This is composition of context-dependent linear maps, not finite-dose nonlinearity.

The working account is increasingly a context-conditioned sequence of transformations over residual directions. What is available by block9 and how it is processed later cannot be treated as interchangeable independent semantic labels. But this factorial by itself is descriptive localization: donor Jacobians are large objects taken from the model, not an interpretable or compact recovered algorithm. Finding a reusable computational unit still requires reducing those operator differences to structured, predictive factors.

Next break D into interpretable alternatives: matched donor bilinear contexts in later MLPs versus normalized attention or full-MLP operator changes, keeping incoming tangent and readout choices explicit. The central comparison is whether bilinear-context replacement alone captures the benefit of full donor downstream operators, for both native and donor incoming tangents. Use full donor D as a validated ceiling and same-wording item donors as controls. This tests a mechanistic account of the large I×D interaction instead of merely restating that the model is context-dependent.

Competence limitations carry over: explicit copying succeeds; capital/agreement candidate scores perform well; plurals and addition fail their declared candidate tasks. None of the factorial response comparisons tests improved task accuracy. All cases remain included.

## Previous continuation: H637

## H637 — Cumulative early-MLP context replacement partially closes the actual prompt-response gap

H636 was progress: matched MLP5 context replacements changed responses strongly but left roughly90–101% of the full cross-prompt response gap. H637 tests whether extending the replacement across later early MLPs provides a more explanatory transformation.

Keep the same80 prompts, donor maps and three propagated probes: original, span2, orthogonal2. Cross-template donors preserve exact item identity; within-template donors shift item by four modulo eight, preserving agreement number. Replace only bilinear operating contexts at MLP6–9, or at MLP5–9 together. Normalization, attention, residual paths and final readout remain receiver-native; their tangent inputs change as the intervention propagates. Native operating states are fixed. These are local derivative counterfactuals, not finite patched forward runs or task-accuracy interventions.

The primary outcome is the remaining norm of the donor-versus-receiver full logit-response gap, weighted and centered under receiver-native probabilities. Ratio1 means no improvement; below1 means movement toward the donor response. This is a geometric comparison, not a causal mediation fraction. The donor endpoint includes all its own context-dependent stages and readout, whereas the intervention changes only selected factors.

**Cumulative replacement partially closes the gap.** MLP6–9 context replacement improves213/240 cross-template comparisons; adding MLP5 improves217/240. Mean remaining-gap ratios fall to0.644–0.797 across families for MLP5–9, compared with0.897–1.008 for MLP5 alone. All three probe groups improve on average: original0.664, learned-span probe0.690, orthogonal probe0.854. Improvement is weaker on the orthogonal probe, limiting generality claims.

| Family | Cross: MLP5 only | Cross: MLP6–9 | Cross: MLP5–9 | Within: MLP6–9 | Within: MLP5–9 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|copy|0.957|0.805|0.770|0.827|0.805|
|fact|1.008|0.776|0.732|0.976|0.971|
|plural|0.945|0.830|0.737|0.911|0.889|
|agreement|0.907|0.770|0.644|0.778|0.734|
|addition|0.897|0.843|0.797|0.794|0.754|

Within-template controls also improve198/240 comparisons for each cumulative intervention. Agreement and addition show substantial within-template improvement; facts improve little. Therefore donor-context transfer reflects both item and construction variation. A construction label alone is not a sufficient description of the operator. Repeated prompt/probe measurements are not independent trials, and the two donor conditions differ in what they hold fixed.

The intervention remains incomplete: large residual gaps persist in every family. In some cases it worsens the gap. A large mean output-change magnitude does not itself establish explanation; the gap metric is the substantive advance over H636. No claim is made that the task has become more accurate, and competence failures in plurals/addition remain visible.

**Composition matters beyond summing separate changes.** A supplemental audit adds the MLP5-only response change to the MLP6–9-only change, both measured against their native baseline, and compares that additive prediction with the actual combined replacement. This is an interaction of local linear operators, not finite-amplitude neural nonlinearity: replacing an upstream operator changes the tangent entering the replaced downstream operators.

| Family | Additive prediction: remaining cross gap | Actual joint replacement: remaining gap | Interaction norm / original gap norm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|copy|0.854|0.770|0.483|
|fact|0.908|0.732|0.581|
|plural|0.829|0.737|0.422|
|agreement|0.689|0.644|0.227|
|addition|0.882|0.797|0.547|

Joint replacement beats the additive prediction on average in every family. Interaction norms are substantial relative to the original gap, but cannot be interpreted as percentages of computation explained: vectors can reinforce or cancel. Additive predictions already improve over the native response on average, so interaction is not required for any improvement at all. This parallels the earlier lesson that accumulation and composition must be separated rather than calling every combined effect irreducible synergy.

The supported working hypothesis is a distributed, context-conditioned sequence of transformations. Operating-context replacement across several MLPs transfers more of the actual response than one MLP alone, including a learned-span and random orthogonal probe. At the same time, incomplete transfer and nonadditive composition argue against reading individual directions or layer effects as independent fixed semantic units. These observations remain local to the sampled model, prompts and injected directions.

Next locate the remaining gap with a controlled boundary at block9. Cross receiver/donor block9 incoming tangents with receiver/donor downstream block10–17 operators and receiver/donor final readouts. Full donor components should reproduce the donor response as a positive control. Mixed combinations can separate information already missing by block9 from later operator and readout differences, with their interactions reported explicitly. Keep the same donor maps and competence audit; use this localization before expanding replacement to more layers indiscriminately.

## Previous continuation: H636

## H636 — Matched MLP5 context effects are strong but explain little of the full prompt-response gap

H635 was progress: residual passthrough and readout-aware projection controls left substantial internal context dependence. H636 returns to a local mechanistic test rather than another rank search.

Use the frozen80-prompt five-task panel. For every receiver, define two donors before evaluation: the opposite template with exactly the same item, and the same template with item shifted by four modulo eight. The latter preserves singular/plural number in the agreement task. It is an item-variation control, not a perfect causal minimal pair. Both directions of template exchange are retained. No task, prompt, donor or direction is selected on output.

At the first affected MLP (block5), the response to an injected direction q is B(y,t), where y is the normalized native residual, t is the derivative of RMS normalization applied to q, and B is the symmetric bilinear derivative of the MLP. Exchange donor y while keeping receiver t (“context”), exchange donor t while keeping receiver y (“normalization”), or exchange both. The interaction remainder is exactly B(y_donor−y_receiver,t_donor−t_receiver). The residual q is retained in all modes. Hybrids are well-defined local operator counterfactuals but need not correspond to a naturally occurring prompt.

Evaluate all nine probes locally. Predeclare original, span2 and orthogonal2 for downstream propagation through the receiver's native block6–17 Jacobians and final readout. These sample the selected direction, an existing learned-span direction and an orthogonal control. The two latter directions were withheld from the H634–635 basis fitting; this experiment fits no basis or response predictor.

**Bilinear operating context dominates normalization on these replacements.** Context replacement changes the local MLP response more than normalization replacement in all720 receiver–probe comparisons for each donor type. After downstream propagation, the same ordering holds in all240 comparisons for each donor type. These are repeated measurements on a structured panel, not independent statistical trials.

| Family | Local within-context change | Local cross-wording context change | Local cross-wording normalization change | Output within-context change | Output cross-wording context change | Output cross-wording normalization change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|copy|0.252|1.151|0.067|0.153|0.633|0.026|
|fact|0.126|1.088|0.078|0.075|0.702|0.053|
|plural|0.322|1.084|0.063|0.205|0.541|0.020|
|agreement|0.657|0.634|0.105|0.379|0.344|0.058|
|addition|0.183|1.148|0.091|0.107|0.701|0.029|

Local numbers divide Euclidean response-change norm by native MLP-response norm, averaging all nine probes, items and both templates. Output numbers divide probability-weighted centered-logit response-change norm by the receiver's full native logit-response norm, averaging the three propagated probes. The two columns use different spaces and denominators; they cannot be read as a fraction transmitted through the network.

Cross-wording context replacement is substantially larger than the matched item replacement for copying, facts, plurals and addition. **Agreement is an exception:** same-wording item changes are as large or larger than changed-wording effects. Thus a universal “template determines the operator” account is too strong. Item-dependent operating context remains material even when grammatical number is held fixed.

**A large local effect does not mean it explains the full difference between prompts.** A supplemental descriptive audit compares the propagated replacement with the actual donor-versus-receiver difference in full logit derivatives, measured in the receiver's probability metric. The donor endpoint includes all native downstream and readout differences. This is a response-gap comparison, not a mediation percentage or task-accuracy measure. Oracle fitting is not involved.

| Family | Remaining cross-wording gap after context-only replacement | Remaining gap after replacing both factors | Context-change alignment cosine |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|copy|0.957|0.957|0.316|
|fact|1.008|1.018|0.376|
|plural|0.945|0.950|0.350|
|agreement|0.907|0.912|0.457|
|addition|0.897|0.891|0.450|

A remaining-gap ratio of1 means no improvement over the native receiver; above1 means a larger mismatch. Despite positive average alignment with the donor gap, context-only replacement leaves roughly90–101% of its original norm on average across these cells. Replacing both MLP5 factors does not substantially improve this. Facts even move slightly farther away by this metric. The replacement can therefore change the response strongly while failing to reproduce the other prompt's full response. This directly weakens an account in which MLP5 alone explains the construction-dependent transformation.

The current supported picture is distributed context dependence: MLP5 bilinear operating context matters, normalization is a smaller contributor for this intervention, and later computation/readout differences remain essential to explaining the complete prompt contrast. Earlier H630 results support cumulative later-MLP effects on the narrower language panel, but that finding has not yet been established for these matched cross-task contrasts.

Competence limitations remain unchanged. Explicit-copy wording is fully successful on this panel; first-copy wording often predicts “ a” first. Capital and agreement candidate tests perform well, while plural and addition candidates fail. Neither a positive derivative nor a smaller response gap demonstrates a corrected answer. All failures remain included.

Next apply matched donor bilinear contexts to MLP6–9, separately and together with MLP5, retaining native normalization, attention, residual path and readout. Include the same within-template item controls. Compare both the intervention magnitude and the remaining donor-response gap. This tests whether cumulative context replacement explains the observed response contrast or merely produces another large but poorly aligned transformation. Only expand to additional layers if the fixed early-window contrast leaves informative residual structure.

## Previous continuation: H635

## H635 — Residual passthrough explains early direction-holdout error, but internal computation remains context-dependent

H634 was progress: discovery-only output subspaces left substantial error on held-out directions and wording, even with oracle coefficients. H635 asks whether this is an artifact of ignoring the residual identity path or of the receiver-specific final readout.

Reuse the frozen five-task80-prompt panel, nine probes and retrospective five-fit/four-held-out direction split. Run native and±0.02 interventions for every probe, capturing final-position residuals after blocks5,9,13,17. This requires1520 model forwards. Replayed native logits and derivative logits match H633 exactly. The exact native readout derivative applied to measured block17 residual tangents matches measured logit derivatives within0.000904 relative weighted error.

For each stage, fit global Euclidean SVD bases using only20 discovery contexts times five discovery probes. Fixed ranks4,16,32,100. Compare two representations: the full residual tangent, and the additional response after subtracting the exact direct residual path. For injection after Attention5, that direct contribution is q at block5, then q times the product of subsequent block residual lambdas. Scale factors at blocks5/9/13/17 are1.000,0.5054,0.5453,0.8300. We call the remainder “innovation” only as an algebraic definition: it includes all attention/MLP response contributions and their interactions along the derivative chain, not an identified semantic feature.

Reconstruct the innovation with oracle Euclidean coefficients and restore the known direct path. Report error relative to the full true tangent so both methods are comparable. The direct path is known from the injected direction and weights; it is not fitted using held-out responses. Basis coefficients do use true test responses, so these remain representational tests rather than predictive models.

**The identity path is a major early confound for input-direction holdout.** At block5, full-span100 mean residual error for held-out directions is0.920 with original wording and0.923 with changed wording. Restoring the direct path lowers these to0.545 and0.561. Thus much of the early error comes from trying to express new orthogonal input directions in a basis learned from other directions. It should not be interpreted entirely as context-specific feature computation.

**Substantial missing structure remains after that correction.** For held-out directions, full-span100 innovation reconstruction errors rise through blocks9 and13 before falling at block17. The fall is descriptive: each stage has a separately fitted basis and its own denominator, so this is not a causal accounting of information creation or destruction.

| Context wording | Block5 full / skip-restored | Block9 full / skip-restored | Block13 full / skip-restored | Block17 full / skip-restored |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|Original wording, new items|0.920 / 0.545|0.843 / 0.784|0.798 / 0.769|0.550 / 0.539|
|Changed wording|0.923 / 0.561|0.897 / 0.847|0.877 / 0.854|0.540 / 0.533|

Reused input directions also show construction sensitivity after correcting the direct path: block5 mean error grows from0.137 on same-wording new items to0.464 with changed wording; at block9 the corresponding errors are0.326 and0.796. This is not explained by holding out an orthogonal injected direction. Four coarse stages were captured; no claim is made about the exact earliest token or sublayer that creates these differences.

**Euclidean residual fidelity and output fidelity differ.** Mapping Euclidean block17 reconstructions through each receiver's exact native readout yields held-out-direction errors0.694/0.797 at rank100 with skip restoration. These exceed fixed-output-basis errors from H634. That alone would be misleading: Euclidean coefficients are not optimized for the output metric.

A supplemental audit therefore maps each fixed internal basis through the receiver-native readout and solves the best receiver-probability-weighted output projection. For innovation bases, subtract the known direct-path output before fitting, then restore it. This uses oracle test responses and exact receiver readout; it gives the favorable representational ceiling available within the tested affine space. The audit was added after inspecting the Euclidean results, not selected from alternative bases.

| Contexts / directions | H634 fixed output basis100 | Internal full basis100, output-optimal | Internal innovation100 plus direct path, output-optimal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|Original wording / fit|0.251|0.249|0.249|
|Original wording / heldout|0.440|0.435|0.426|
|Changed wording / fit|0.481|0.474|0.470|
|Changed wording / heldout|0.502|0.489|0.482|

Receiver-specific readout and the direct-path correction give only modest improvements over H634's output basis at the full discovery span. They do not rescue high-fidelity transfer: held-out-direction errors remain0.426 with original wording and0.482 with changed wording. Fully competent changed-wording copying still has0.599 error. Consequently, final-readout geometry alone is not a sufficient explanation for these discovery-coverage failures. This conclusion is limited to the tested spans and oracle projection methods, not all possible structured representations.

The main update is twofold: preserve the known identity path when evaluating novel-direction generalization, and avoid interpreting Euclidean residual reconstruction as optimal output preservation. After both controls, internal response variation remains substantial, including variation across constructions for the same injected directions. A universally shared fixed response basis is not currently supported at high fidelity. A context-conditioned operator remains a more plausible object to investigate than repeatedly increasing a fixed output basis's rank.

Next return to mechanistic contrasts rather than more rank searches. Use matched item pairs across the two copying/factual/agreement constructions, retain the inflection/arithmetic failure controls, and decompose changes in normalized-MLP responses into bilinear operating-context and normalization contributions. Compare matched within-construction references against cross-construction references, preserving direction and item identity where possible. Propagate decisive local contrasts to output with native downstream operators. This can test whether construction-dependent operators explain the newly localized differences, rather than only documenting lack of compression. Unseen-direction and held-out-item checks remain required before a transferable unit can be claimed.

## Previous continuation: H634

## H634 — Discovery response subspaces leave substantial held-out structure

H633 was progress: task-average responses transferred across items better than across wording, even when changed-wording copying was successful. H634 tests whether allowing multiple response directions can rescue a compact representation.

Use the frozen80-prompt, nine-direction H633 captures. Fit on20 discovery contexts (first four items of the first template in each of five tasks) and only five input probes: original, span0, span1, orthogonal0, orthogonal1. Hold out span2, span3, orthogonal2, orthogonal3 from basis fitting. This partition was declared after H633 outputs had been observed, so it is a retrospective holdout, not a blinded prospective replication. No new prompts or model evaluations occur.

Center output-logit derivatives under the pooled discovery token probabilities, then fit weighted SVD bases. The global fit has100 response rows; each task fit has20. Initial global ranks are1,4,16,32; task ranks1,4,16,20. After inspecting those results, add the global full100-row span as an exploratory ceiling check. Do not select a winning rank on test data. All bases use the same discovery-only probability metric.

For every test response, solve its best weighted least-squares projection under that receiver's native probabilities. **These coefficients use the true test response.** This is a representational upper bound for a frozen basis, not a predictive model, compressed language model, or canonical form. A future coefficient predictor can only do worse in this metric for the same basis. Native probabilities are also receiver-specific. Learned task labels select a task basis without using the test derivative; only projection coefficients are oracle.

**Allowing a subspace helps, but transfer remains incomplete.** A rank32 global basis has mean relative error0.352 for fitted input directions on new same-template items, versus0.572 for held-out input directions. Changed wording raises those to0.610 and0.635. A rank20 task basis leaves0.351/0.616 on same-template fitted/held-out directions and0.652/0.689 on changed wording. Thus favorable performance on reused directions substantially overstates generality to new directions.

| Test contexts | Input directions | Global rank4 error | Global rank16 | Global rank32 | Full discovery span100 | Mean energy captured at100 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|New items, original wording|fit|0.753|0.480|0.352|0.251|92.7%|
|New items, original wording|heldout|0.792|0.649|0.572|0.440|79.5%|
|Changed wording, all eight items|fit|0.825|0.696|0.610|0.481|74.9%|
|Changed wording, all eight items|heldout|0.840|0.710|0.635|0.502|73.2%|

Error is the receiver-probability-weighted norm of the centered residual divided by the true response norm. Energy captured is one minus squared relative error, averaged per example; it is not one minus squared mean error. Results average equally across five task families and input probes within each direction split. The changed-wording set contains both previously seen and held-out identities.

**The missing structure is not just the rank32 cutoff.** The full discovery span still leaves mean relative error0.440 on held-out directions in the original template and0.502 with changed wording. For explicit copying, where the changed template has100% top1 accuracy, even the full span leaves0.624 error on held-out directions and0.635 on reused directions. The full span recovers its actual fitting responses to below1e-14 relative error, so this gap is not failure to solve the projection.

This is evidence of incomplete coverage by the discovery response span, not proof that the model has no compact structure. Only five input directions and four examples per task/template informed the bases. More diverse discovery data, an internal representation, or a structured context-dependent operator could generalize better. A fixed output basis may be the wrong object because the final readout itself depends on the receiver's residual state. Generic random probes may also explore operations outside a small semantic task circuit.

Finite-dose KL diagnostics for the original direction at±0.1 are retained in the result JSON. They reconstruct logits with oracle projection coefficients and receiver-native logits. They are not an independent test of coefficient prediction; derivative error is the primary measure here. H633 already verified that the original receiver's own tangent predicts those finite doses accurately. This experiment leaves causal operator replacements and internal/readout separation untested.

Current hypothesis update: a single output vector or tiny fixed output basis is inadequate for these captures. Construction-dependent transformations remain plausible. A shared larger subspace is only partially supported: the global100-row span captures about79.5% of held-out-direction response energy on same-wording contexts and73.2% on changed wording. The remaining gaps are too large to call high-fidelity canonicalization. The particularly strong changed-wording copy failure cannot be dismissed as lack of native task competence. Failed plural/addition cells retain the limitations established in H633.

Next localize the gap. Capture internal residual tangents before the final readout, fit discovery-only internal bases under the same context/direction splits, then pass reconstructed tangents through each receiver's exact native readout. Compare this with the fixed logit-space bases. If internal reconstruction transfers while fixed output bases fail, readout geometry explains part of the apparent diversity. If internal reconstruction also fails, locate the earliest stage where held-out directions or constructions leave the discovery span. These tests should precede an expensive search for a universal low-rank representation; matched within-task versus cross-task factor replacements remain needed for causal interpretation.

## H633 — Task means transfer across items better than across constructions

H632 was progress: nine frozen input probes showed that bilinear-context sensitivity extends beyond the original selected direction. H633 measures whether grouping by task is sufficient to predict native output responses, before fitting a more elaborate context-conditioned representation.

Freeze80 prompts: copying, capital facts, plural inflection, subject–verb agreement and single-digit addition; two templates and eight items per family. Reuse all nine equal-norm H632 directions at the final Attention5 output. For each direction, estimate full-logit derivatives by central differences at ±0.02. Fix the first four items of template0 in each family as discovery data (20 prompts). Predict the other60 contexts with either the global discovery mean or that task's discovery mean. Means are fitted separately for each direction. This tests unseen contexts, not unseen input directions, low-rank operators, or causal reference replacements.

The held-out template0 cell has four new items per family. Template1 has all eight items, including four identities shared with discovery. No output-based selection or prompt edits were made. Grammar labels alternate singular/plural; generic subject continuation permits grammatical alternatives beyond is/are. Numerical labels are fixed sums. Plural candidates explicitly include singular competitors. These first-token scores are not free-generation semantic accuracy.

**Task grouping helps across items in the same construction, but is generally insufficient across wording.** Averaged equally over family, probe and held-out item, mean relative derivative error is0.620 for task means versus0.904 for global means within template0. For template1, errors are1.244 versus1.078. Task means beat global means on all five same-template cells, but only agreement and addition on the changed-template cells. An error of1 is the error of predicting no derivative; values above1 are worse than that zero baseline. These are means of per-example probability-weighted centered-logit errors, not causal fractions or statistical confidence estimates.

KL columns use only the original vector at finite doses±0.1, averaging both signs. For each receiver, the predictor adds its own derivative or the frozen task mean to its native logits; the zero predictor uses unperturbed logits. KL is from the actually perturbed token distribution to the prediction. The native logits are known receiver-specific information in every method; this is a local surrogate, not a substitute language model. The full derivative-error columns include all nine probes. Absolute KL is small because doses are small; failure relative to zero still matters for explaining the response.

**Wording failure is not merely a consequence of failed tasks.** Explicit “Copy exactly: … / Copy:” has100% held-out top1 accuracy, yet its task-mean derivative error is1.314, and finite-dose task-mean KL exceeds the zero-response baseline. Capital question prompts have100% candidate accuracy and50% immediate top1 accuracy, but task-mean error1.538. The model's own context-specific tangent predicts finite-dose distributions much better, with mean KL around1e-7–7e-6 across cells. Thus a linear approximation can work locally while a shared task-average tangent fails to transfer.

**Competence must remain separate from the geometry.** The first copy template often predicts “ a”, despite ranking the intended word best among the eight copy candidates. Its candidate score cannot establish successful immediate copying. Both plural templates fail against singular competitors. Addition often repeats the first operand; all held-out addition candidates are wrong. Agreement candidate choice succeeds throughout, while native top1 sometimes selects another continuation. These failures are retained and prevent broad claims about mechanisms of successful inflection or arithmetic.

The experiment makes construction-conditioned transformations more plausible than task-label-only response units. It does not establish that all within-construction variation is low rank, that a context-conditioned predictor will generalize, or that the MLP6–9 bilinear mechanism causes every cross-task difference. Output means also conflate internal transformation with receiver-specific final readout.

Refreshed hypothesis set (20 alternatives; qualitative priority, not posterior probabilities):

1. Construction-dependent bilinear operating contexts alter several input directions. Strongest current mechanistic support from H626–632; test across these task contexts with internal factor interventions.
2. A small family of transformations indexed by construction generalizes across identities. Plausible from same-template transfer; require held-out context prediction, not clustering after seeing responses.
3. Task identity alone indexes reusable responses. Weakened by changed-template errors, including competent copying.
4. A task-independent fixed output direction suffices. Weakened by varied probe responses and global-mean errors.
5. The final readout accounts for much of apparent construction specificity. Earlier work rules out a complete explanation for the original vector; compare internal tangents and fixed/readout-swapped predictions on new tasks.
6. A scalar gain on a shared response is sufficient for some task cells. Still possible locally; compare direction-only cosine errors with amplitude errors, with any gain learned on discovery contexts.
7. Broad lexical emission or continuation preference explains much of the original vector. Plausible; compare target, competitor and non-answer probability changes.
8. Target identity changes the transformation even within a template. Supported as a residual possibility by nonzero within-template errors; hold out identities with matched context geometry.
9. Syntax rather than task semantics indexes transformations. Plausible; cross grammatical forms and task content independently.
10. Prefix or punctuation positions are the dominant context cues. Open; matched minimal-pair prompts can isolate them.
11. Current context replacement effects are generic mismatch rather than meaningful computation. Open; compare matched within-task references with cross-task references and native controls.
12. Several additive downstream changes explain sign reversals. Supported in H630; test attribution on new constructions without assuming irreducible synergy.
13. Strong nonlinear interactions between downstream operators are essential. Limited by additive sign predictions in H630, though interactions affect magnitude.
14. Normalization alone explains the context dependence. Weakened on H632 probes; remains a possible contributor in other tasks and doses.
15. Curvature explains poor transfer. Unlikely to explain these small-dose errors because own tangents predict±0.1 well; larger doses remain untested here.
16. The selected original direction is unusually sensitive, but controls are generic. Supported in magnitude on earlier language cells; sample more independently specified directions before ranking semantic specificity.
17. A shared low-dimensional output subspace exists even when mean vectors fail. Open and not tested by mean baselines; fit on discovery responses and evaluate held-out projection errors.

## H632 — Bilinear-context sensitivity extends across sampled directions

H631 was progress: fresh countries reproduced the original sign contrast while wording and competence limited its interpretation. H632 asks whether that contrast is peculiar to the discovered vector or reflects a broader local transformation.

Nine equal-norm orthogonal directions were frozen before evaluation: the original vector, four orthogonalized directions from the existing learned 64-dimensional span, and four seeded Gaussian directions projected outside that span and the other probes. The original vector was historically selected; this is not an unbiased comparison of nine random features. Control signs are arbitrary.

The 36 H631 prompts and exact original four capital reference contexts remain fixed. They include 24 prospective prompts: eight fresh countries crossed with three language constructions. For each direction, analytically recompute the initial block5 tangent, then propagate it through native operators, through bilinear-context replacements at MLP6–9, or through normalization-Jacobian replacements there. Later operators and final readout remain native. These are local derivative counterfactuals, not finite activation replacements or task-accuracy interventions.

**Context sensitivity is not confined to the discovered vector.** In all216 prospective prompt–direction pairs, bilinear-context replacement changes the full-vocabulary response more than normalization replacement does. This counts repeated measurements, not216 statistically independent trials. The metric is the norm of the change in centered logit derivatives, weighted by the model's native token probabilities; it describes local output-distribution sensitivity.

On fresh “People in … speak”, the original vector has mean context-change norm0.553 versus normalization-change norm0.021. The eight controls have context-change norms0.149–0.250 versus normalization-change norms0.011–0.044. Their mean per-example relative context changes range0.782–1.683, compared with2.357 for the original. Thus the original is especially sensitive on this construction, but substantial sensitivity also appears inside and outside the learned span.

| Construction | Original: context / normalization change norm | Eight controls: context change range | Eight controls: normalization change range |
|---|---|---|---|
| People in … speak | 0.553 / 0.021 | 0.149–0.250 | 0.011–0.044 |
| Residents of … speak | 0.554 / 0.032 | 0.182–0.502 | 0.018–0.113 |
| The main language spoken in … is | 0.189 / 0.089 | 0.062–0.103 | 0.011–0.062 |

The native model was correct on25%,25%,100% of these respective cells in H631. All prompts remain included. Large full-vocabulary response changes also occur in the fully competent main-language cell; intended-token sign reversal is not the only evidence. On the original speak construction, the original vector again changes from negative intended-token derivative in all eight cases to positive in all eight under context replacement. Controls show heterogeneous signs, and reversing a control direction reverses its derivative. Their signs should not be read as inherent semantic labels.

**A compact description is plausible but not yet demonstrated to transfer.** Among the nine sampled directions on fresh “People in … speak”, the leading eigenvalue accounts for67.6% of the context-change Gram-matrix trace; the top two account for75.1%. The corresponding native-response fractions are29.8% and51.7%. Across other fresh constructions, context-change top-two fractions are79.4% and60.5%. These are eigenspectra of prompt-averaged, probability-weighted response Gram matrices. They measure energy concentration within nine input probes only. They do not establish the full operator's rank, a shared output basis across contexts, or a unique canonical form. The particularly large original-vector response can contribute to concentration. No low-rank model was fitted or prospectively tested here.

The most supported interpretation is a context-conditioned transformation affecting multiple directions, with the discovered vector unusually sensitive on the original construction. A single isolated semantic direction is insufficient to describe these measurements. Still viable are a small transferable family of transformations, a larger task-specific transformation, or generic sensitivity to replacing operating contexts. This experiment does not distinguish those explanations decisively.

Next test frozen response models across genuinely different tasks: copying, factual completion, inflection with singular competitors, agreement, and simple numeric or symbolic continuations, retaining a competence audit for each. First capture the native transformations and compare context-conditioned predictions with a context-independent baseline on held-out directions, templates and identities. Use matched within-task reference replacements alongside cross-task replacements to distinguish generic replacement damage from structured context effects. Choose rank or context groups on a discovery split only; evaluate full-vocabulary local fidelity and finite-dose KL separately from intended-token effects and accuracy. Failure should identify whether the missing information is direction, context, or nonlinear dose. This remains a proposed next experiment, not a completed result.

**The precise “People in … speak” contrast transfers to all eight fresh countries.** The native addition-signed intended-token log-probability derivative is negative in all eight (mean−0.274). On the main-language statements, all eight native derivatives are positive; context-sharing leaves seven positive and changes the mean only slightly. Thus fresh identities confirm the narrow mechanism on its original construction, while new wording limits any universal sign claim.

A derivative concerns how probability changes locally; a positive derivative need not make the target most probable. No finite-amplitude replacement or generated answer correction was tested here. The shared operators are counterfactual local transformations and need not be realizable as a native prompt. Four-reference averages remain part of the intervention definition.

The token audit is descriptive and did not alter prompts, rules or reported competence.

The result strengthens a construction-conditioned operator account: a fixed direction encounters different bilinear operating contexts, and replacing those contexts can reverse its effect on specified language tokens in a reproducible construction. It weakens the concern that the original sign contrast only memorized the eight old countries. It does not establish an abstract language-answer unit, task-independent operator semantics, or a universal behavior-improvement intervention. Wording sensitivity and incomplete task execution remain central limitations.

The native tangent chain starts from the centrally measured block5 tangent on the new prompts, rather than a newly fitted model. End-to-end chain error against those finite differences is at most0.000541. These controls support the local operator comparison, not broad semantic claims.

Operator composition changes the perturbation that reaches subsequent operators. Consequently, neither differences nor response-error norms can be interpreted as percentages of the native effect attributable to a region.

**MLP5 is not the whole explanation.** For language “speak”, native intended-token derivative is−0.235; shared context changes it to−0.111, still negative. Shared normalization gives−0.225. **Removing MLP5's response does not remove the overall intervention.** The injected residual vector still travels through the skip path and later computation. Zeroing the MLP5 perturbation response changes final response norm and shape, but all tested cell-mean response norms remain nonzero; the “speak” answer derivative stays negative at−0.104. This is compatible with distributed downstream transformation. It does not establish that MLP5 is unnecessary for native behavior, because its native output is preserved.

The experiment substitutes first-order writes, not native finite-dose MLP functions. Small symmetric alpha and the analytic control justify the local interpretation. At large dose, higher-order responses and their interactions would need separate testing. Shared bilinear factors are analytic operators and need not correspond to attainable native states. The panel and capital discovery examples are familiar; this is a mechanism test within an adaptive research sequence.

Twenty hypotheses after this causal check:

1. The injected direction has one context-independent semantic output effect — weakened by H623–H627.
2. It supports answer-emission modulation on the tested capital prompts — supported locally.
3. Its effect is solely a vocabulary bias — weakened by small-dose response-shape changes.
4. A common bias with a signed scalar gain is sufficient — weakened by oracle-gain errors.
5. A fixed vector can still be a useful local intervention — supported despite context dependence.
6. It primarily encodes a specific donor country — weakened by cross-country transfer and selectivity checks.
7. Capital identity probabilities never change — false; rank can persist while probability shifts.
8. The final position suffices for approximate output-distribution effects — supported on the earlier matched panel.
9. Final-only and full intervention are exactly decision-equivalent — false on some recipients.
10. Rank2 gives a useful compact output approximation — supported locally, not universal.
11. Raw context cosine measures functional equivalence well — weakened by H626.
12. Input RMS variation dominates the first response divergence — weakened for this vector at MLP5.
13. Bilinear operating context drives much of that local divergence — supported analytically and causally.
14. MLP5 alone creates the language sign reversal — weakened; replacement does not remove it.
15. Later computation can transform a shared block5 response differently — supported by both-shared/zero-response controls.
16. Final readout alone explains all response variation — weakened by H625.
17. Both intermediate transformations and readout matter — supported.
18. Small-dose response predicts all finite-dose behavior — weakened by H624's curvature tests.
19. High choice accuracy among an incomplete answer set proves task competence — contradicted by plural controls.
20. A compact context-conditioned operator is a better unit than a standalone feature vector — plausible research direction, not yet a validated general model.

The current evidence favors a conditional-computation description: a reusable direction is transformed by a sequence of context-dependent local operators. This is more informative than assigning the direction a universal semantic name, but it is not yet a predictive explanation of the full mechanism or a canonical form. The next experiment should test a concrete operator model rather than merely adding labels.

Next build and validate final-position tangent propagation through later blocks. Hold native states fixed while applying each block's local derivative to an incoming perturbation, then compare with end-to-end finite differences. Once validated, substitute reference-context Jacobians at selected stages while retaining the propagated incoming response. That preserves the distinction between changing a local operator and replacing its output with a fixed vector. It can test which contextual transformations are necessary for the remaining response variation without assigning nonadditive layer shares.

**Local numerical estimates are stable, while large-dose linearization fails.** Held-out0.02-versus0.05 derivative discrepancies are about0.0003–0.0005 in relative weighted norm. Two issues therefore coexist: context changes the local response, and finite-strength curvature changes its extrapolation. Mechanistic implication: the fixed hidden direction is transformed into a context-dependent logit effect. This does not yet locate where dependence arises. Final RMS normalization and logit saturation are themselves context-dependent, so failure of a shared logit vector cannot be attributed specifically to intermediate attention or MLP computation. A common pre-readout residual response could still produce different logit responses through the same context-dependent final readout.

Next capture response vectors through downstream layers and analytically separate final RMS-normalization and tanh derivatives. Compare a shared pre-readout residual response passed through each recipient's native readout with the observed logit tangent. If that explains transfer, the main dependence is in readout; if not, locate where intermediate response trajectories diverge. This tests a concrete mechanistic alternative rather than merely fitting another output basis.

The previous turn was progress: H622 localized most of the frozen effect to Attention5's final output position. Test native, addition1, subtraction0.25/1, and equal-norm random-complement addition/subtraction1. No coefficient fitting, direction refitting or recipient scaling occurs.

Answer-format scoring is expanded to two explicitly enumerated continuations per candidate: a leading-space direct answer and a leading-space/opening-double-quote answer prefix. The quoted event stops immediately after the answer, without requiring a closing quote. Tokenized prefixes are checked to be mutually disjoint, and their probabilities are summed per identity. This is probability of specified answer beginnings, not general semantic correctness or probability of all possible answer forms. There are432 prompt-condition records supported by1,728 sequence evaluations across288 unique teacher-forced prefix queries per mode. During every continuation forward, the intervention remains at the original prompt's final position; it is not moved to each newly appended token.

**Capital transfer extends beyond the original six-token scaffold.** On short prompts such as "France's capital is", adding the vector raises correct-token top1 from12.5% to87.5% and answer-prefix mass0.0485→0.2483. Subtraction lowers mass to0.0027 and top1 to0%. On capital question-answer prompts, addition raises mass0.1773→0.2045 and top1 from50% to62.5%; subtraction lowers mass to0.0763 and top1 to0%. Every capital identity remains best among the eight scored candidates across all modes. This supports a reusable intervention on these relations, beyond the original length and final token, but does not imply that all factual rankings or probabilities are invariant.

**A language construction reverses the effect.** On "People in France speak" and corresponding country prompts, addition lowers intended-answer-prefix mass0.1705→0.1258 and candidate accuracy75%→62.5%; subtraction raises mass to0.2035. In contrast, language question-answer prompts show addition0.7413→0.7630 and subtraction0.5852, with perfect candidate/top1 accuracy throughout. The same vector is therefore not a universally signed answer-emission control. Relation, wording, final token and downstream state vary together, so this experiment cannot identify which causes the reversal.

A descriptive native greedy audit generates eight tokens on all24 plural prompts. None contains the intended plural word. It does not establish global inability: only these prompts and eight greedy tokens were examined. The audit was not used to modify scoring or filter results. Future competence tests should include singular forms and other plausible errors as competitors, not only unrelated correct-type answers.

Quoted prefixes contribute little to capital/language mass and modestly to the already tiny plural mass. We therefore cannot explain the transfer reversal as an artifact of omitted opening-double-quote answers. Other formats remain outside the measured event set. Teacher-forced prefix probability and greedy generation are different measurements; neither alone provides an exhaustive semantic evaluation.

Current hypothesis update: a fixed final-layer5 output direction can modulate factual answer emission over multiple capital formats, but its sign and identity effects depend on recipient context. A context-sensitive readout of a reusable direction is better supported than a universal scalar answer variable. A simpler vocabulary bias, interacting with which answers are currently likely, remains a live alternative. The plural audit warns that apparent task transfer must be distinguished from noun matching under an incomplete candidate set.

Compare a common vocabulary-wide response with context-dependent responses, preserving all candidate and generic-token effects. In particular, ask whether language reversal reflects a stable preference for particular language tokens or a change in the downstream transformation of the vector. Freeze any predictive response fit on a declared discovery subset and test other surfaces; report exact answer-versus-plausible-error contrasts. For each recipient, subtract every same-template, same-token-length donor's complement to frozen H615 joint64, scaled to the recipient complement's total norm. Doses0.25 and1 include self removal, native replay, and one seeded norm-matched random-complement control per recipient. No new basis is fitted.

This yields1,364 evaluations including48 native replays. Each capital template has56 cross-country ordered donor/recipient pairs per dose. Copying has240 cross-donor pairs; agreement has210 because token-length matching splits that panel. Counts are repeated interventions on a small set of prompts, not independent samples. No output-based filtering occurs.

**The harmful component transfers across countries.** At dose1, cross-country removal has nearly the same mean output KL, answer mass and generic-token competition as self removal. Correct capital remains first among all8 candidate capitals in every capital intervention, including self, cross-country and random controls at both doses. However, unrestricted correct top1 falls sharply under self and cross-country removal.

At full dose, cross-country correct top1 is14.3%/8.9%, versus12.5%/12.5% under self removal and100%/100% for random controls. Mean KL is0.906/0.591 versus0.897/0.587 for self and0.0098/0.0064 for random controls. The correct capital's mean probability drops from0.360/0.265 to0.060/0.043, whereas its conditional probability among the eight capitals remains0.943/0.933. That conditional probability does fall somewhat from0.973/0.972; “identity preserved” means rank preservation here, not exactly unchanged factual probabilities.

Capital-vs-generic margin compares the correct token with the combined probability of "the", "a", "not", fixed from H618. It flips from+1.40/+0.58 natively to−1.46/−1.85 under cross-country removal. At quarter dose, probability mass and margins already shift, but every full-vocabulary capital answer remains correct. These results describe graded distribution changes before accuracy crosses a threshold.

**The donor directions are already almost identical.** Within each template, flattened body-write complement cosine ranges0.9922–0.9986 and0.9892–0.9982. Successful transfer therefore supports a common scaffold/context component on this panel; it is not evidence of transporting distinct country-specific facts between unrelated coordinates. Norm matching is global over all body positions; per-position magnitudes are not separately matched.

**There is little donor-specific capital preference beyond the common effect.** A donor/recipient log-odds shift alone would be misleading: at dose1 the donor capital gains about1.19 nats relative to the recipient capital on average, but other wrong capitals can gain similarly. We therefore inspect all eight capital log probabilities. The donor's change relative to the mean log probability change of the other six wrong capitals averages−0.0036/−0.0031 nats. Relative to the corresponding self-removal contrast, per-pair changes range−0.060 to+0.050 and−0.041 to+0.041 nats. This weakens a donor-identity-content explanation. It does not prove exact identity independence; small effects remain, and the panel is finite. Token log probabilities were added to the result schema in a second identical run to permit this audit; conditions and donor selection were unchanged.

Copying remains correct throughout, with negligible complement effects. Agreement remains correct throughout this selected template; donor KL is about0.0063 at dose1, versus0.0012 for random controls. These are within-family transfers, not cross-task transplantation of capital directions. They do not establish a shared semantic unit across tasks.

Twenty competing hypotheses, refreshed after the last five experiments:

1. A shared component spans countries within these capital templates — strongly supported locally.
2. The harmful complement primarily stores donor-specific capital identity — weakened by cross-country transfer and selectivity audit.
3. It controls direct-answer emission versus generic continuation — supported as an operational description on these prompts.
4. Capital identity probabilities are completely unchanged — false; conditional probabilities shift despite preserved rank.
5. High correct-answer accuracy implies internal fidelity — contradicted by earlier copying results.
6. Correct paired choice implies full factual preservation — insufficient; eight-way checks strengthen but do not universalize it.
7. Any equal-magnitude perturbation causes answer suppression — weakened by random controls and H619.
8. The effect is only a large-dose artifact — weakened by quarter-dose probability changes; accuracy failures remain dose-dependent.
9. Nonlinearity alone explains poor frozen-space transfer — weakened by small-dose complement effects.
10. Finite-dose nonlinearity contributes — supported by H617.
11. The copying-trained span is task-general — weakened by H618.
12. A universal low-dimensional semantic basis has been found — unsupported.
13. Data coverage determines useful compact coordinates — supported across H614–H618.
14. Internal Euclidean error predicts output KL monotonically — weakened by rank/objective reversals.
15. A response-distribution quotient may be smaller than an internal-vector representation — plausible, conditional on distribution and tolerance.
16. Prefix-absence/lowercase context is especially relevant — supported by H619, though direction and context remain coupled.
17. Initial-token position effects explain the common direction without semantic content — open.
18. Repeated lexical scaffold explains the common direction — open and important given cosine near1.
19. A general answer-emission direction transfers across unrelated factual relations — untested.
20. A fixed one-dimensional intervention can predict emission changes in unseen scaffold/task combinations — untested; a stronger candidate-unit test than further donor swaps within this scaffold.

Most likely current account: a nearly country-independent, scaffold-dependent interaction component influences whether a direct answer is emitted. This is a useful functional distinction from fact identity, but calling it a fundamental or semantic unit would outrun the evidence. The high cosine may reflect common syntax/position and normalization pathways rather than a learned abstract “answer” variable.

Next distinguish shared wording from shared function. Freeze a direction using only a country subset and one template, then test it on held-out countries, the other capital template where positions align, and different factual relations with matched scaffolds. Keep copy/agreement controls and separate exact-answer rank among a complete declared answer set from generic competition. Include both subtraction and addition, with magnitude matching and native competence reported. Do not tune direction or examples after observing transfer. A mean direction is a proposed intervention, not a unique canonical basis or a model of where the interaction originates.

Audits:48 unique recipient strings,8 unique countries per template, complete56 cross-country pairs per dose, all eight capital candidates included; all source/manifest/basis/runner hashes unchanged; exact native replay; maximum norm mismatch6.38e-7; finite metrics;1,364 evaluations. No new natural-text documents; FineWeb remains26,112. Broad research goal active and incomplete.

## Previous continuation: H619

## H619 — Equal-magnitude prefix interactions have very different effects on answer emission

The previous turn was progress: H618 found large capital-answer suppression outside the copying span, but preserved paired factual discrimination. Unprefixed lowercase factorial corners already favored generic continuations. H619 tests that context confound using two explicit four-token prefixes: "As a reminder," and "For the record," crossed with initial capitalization. Both have identical body positions and token IDs. Three tasks (copying, agreement, capital recall), two templates, and free continuation versus appended "Next word:" give768 native prompts. Native plus full/span/complement removals at doses0.25 and1 give1,344 evaluations, including192 zero-removal baselines. The joint64 copying basis stays frozen.

**Replacing the unprefixed baseline sharply weakens the damaging capital effect.** On free-continuation capital prompts all combined recipients start with correct top1, and full/span/complement removals preserve correct top1 at both doses. Full dose1 native-reference KL is0.00172/0.00190 across templates, versus0.666/0.489 for H618's absent-prefix interaction. Every native free-continuation competence cell passes the predeclared gate, although the second capital template's reminder/lowercase cell has only50% accepted-token top1. Passing a threshold is not perfect response-mode matching.

The new interaction is smaller: mean new/old write norm ratios are0.352/0.386 on the two capital templates, with mean flattened-vector cosines0.385/0.349. The new contrast changes both size and direction. Therefore raw effect reduction cannot by itself establish a response-mode mechanism.

**A matched-magnitude audit rules out size alone.** After observing the smaller norms, rescale each new full interaction to the old interaction's total Frobenius norm across body positions. Test old and new directions, plus each direction's fixed-basis span and complement, on identical free-continuation recipient token sequences. This adds576 forwards across the three tasks. Scaling is per example; it does not match every position's norm or match span/complement norms separately. It is a follow-up diagnostic on familiar data, not independent confirmation.

The old complement reduces top1 to12.5% in both templates; the new complement preserves100%. Correct-capital versus paired-wrong-capital choice remains perfect throughout the matched audit. Thus the old direction is particularly effective at suppressing direct answer emission on these recipients; a generic large perturbation explanation is insufficient.

“Capital vs generic margin” is log probability mass for the correct capital minus log probability mass for three fixed tokens: "the", "a", "not". These were chosen from the previous completion audit and fixed for H619. Positive means the capital outranks their combined mass. This is a narrow diagnostic, not all nonanswer continuations. The old full direction flips the mean margin to−1.05/−1.65; the matched new direction leaves it+1.52/+0.33. Probability mass and KL concern the whole model distribution or explicit token sets; preserved paired discrimination does not prove all factual knowledge is intact.

Copying anchors retain all answers under matched old/new directions. Agreement remains mostly/all correct and the new direction produces less KL than the old one. These controls show the contrast is not simply catastrophic disruption everywhere, but task wording, length and recipient sensitivity are not independently isolated.

**The requested fixed-answer-format control failed.** Appending "Next word:" produces0% accepted-token top1 in every native task/template/prefix/case cell. Copying and capital paired-choice tests remain perfect; agreement paired-choice rates are only0.125–0.25. Top tokens include "A", "The", quotes, "capital" and country names. This suffix did not reliably induce the intended task in this model. All failed cells remain in the experiment, and their small intervention effects cannot be used to conclude that stabilizing response format removes the effect. No prompt was discarded or rewritten using these outputs.

Current inference: the harmful interaction depends specifically on the prefix-absence/lowercase context and its resulting output direction, not just total perturbation magnitude. A context-sensitive answer-emission mechanism is more plausible than a general factual-memory direction, but is not established as a reusable unit. Prefix identity, position changes in the old contrast, and broad continuation statistics remain alternative explanations. The failed answer-label control leaves response-mode isolation incomplete.

Next test whether the harmful complement generalizes across country identity: cross-donor interventions on identical scaffold/positions, with self and norm-matched donor controls, evaluate correct capital against all capitals as well as generic continuations. ## Previous continuation: H618

## H618 — Diverse-task transfer fails; capital effects implicate continuation mode more than paired fact discrimination

The previous turn was progress: H617 established that omitted directions can affect outputs and that nonlinear effects grow with dose. H618 extends the frozen H615 copying space to five families: copying, agreement, entity binding, capital recall and sentiment, each with two templates and eight pairs. Prefix presence × initial capitalization gives640 native prompts. On160 combined-condition recipients, compare native, full Attention5 contextual interaction removal, joint32, joint64, joint64 complement and random64:960 interventions. No basis refit or competence-based filtering. Entity-binding prompts receive a fixed "Today," lead-in so case changes affect a scaffold token rather than a name. No answer tokens or pairs were excluded.

**The copying space is not a general representation of this interaction across tasks.** Rank64 internal-effect errors are about0.66–0.72 on agreement,0.82–0.83 on binding,1.05–1.07 on capital recall, and0.70–0.82 on sentiment. The same copying anchor has error0.061; another copying template has0.417. This supports dependence on the prompt distribution, but task and wording change together, so these numbers do not isolate task identity as the cause.

Write error compares vectors at Attention5. Internal-effect error compares the downstream normalized MLP11 input against full interaction removal, normalized by the full removal's effect. Reference KL compares output distributions against full removal and normalizes by no removal. Native KL instead compares the original model with an intervention. Its component ratios are comparisons, not additive causal shares. Values above1 are possible because components can counteract one another and downstream transformations are nonlinear. Group NLL and single-token CE are both stored, separately; for agreement/sentiment the latter uses the first predeclared accepted token and is not a complete task metric.
