All paired candidate tests pass except sentiment template1, where they all fail. Several unrestricted-answer gates fail despite correct paired choice. For unprefixed lowercase agreement, the model often prefers punctuation or another continuation. For unprefixed lowercase capital prompts, it prefers generic continuation tokens such as "the". Sentiment answer sets are incomplete: "Excellent" and multiword starts such as "Very" can express the intended sentiment but are outside the frozen accepted set. No post hoc expansion rescues reported scores. These failures prevent claiming that all factorial corners execute the same task in the same response mode.

**Capital recall has a large answer-selection effect that the copying span misses.** Combined recipients initially give correct capital top1 throughout. Full interaction removal reduces top1 to0.375/0.125 across templates; complement removal gives0.125/0.125. Span-only removal preserves1.0/1.0. Full native-reference KL is0.666/0.489 nats, substantially larger than the copying examples.

A targeted128-forward completion audit then shows that the correct capital remains preferred over the paired wrong capital in every native/full/span/complement case. The winning tokens after damaging interventions are usually "the", "a" or "not", not the paired wrong capital. Intended-capital CE rises from1.031/1.381 nats natively to2.583/3.096 after full removal and2.883/3.266 after complement removal. Span-only CE is0.998/1.267. This supports a change in propensity to emit the direct factual answer, while the narrow paired fact distinction remains intact. It does not prove that all factual ranking, knowledge or retrieval is preserved: the audit only compares the specified alternative. Country prompts repeat across neighboring pairs, so the16 endpoints per template are not16 independent countries.

The native completion audit also exposes a confound: the unprefixed lowercase corner often uses a generic continuation mode already. Subtracting its factorial interaction may transfer that behavior into an otherwise competent prefixed prompt. Therefore the intervention is causal for answer emission on these recipients, but cannot yet be named a country–capital feature or a universal retrieval unit. It may reflect a broader context-dependent continuation mechanism.

Most likely current hypotheses: (1) compact output coordinates depend on distribution coverage; (2) directions outside copying coordinates can control answer-emission behavior in other prompts; (3) response mode and answer identity are partly separable here; (4) a factual-memory interpretation is weaker than an answer-emission interpretation given preserved paired discrimination; (5) task identity alone is not isolated from scaffold and case effects. We should now prioritize disambiguating these mechanisms rather than fitting more spans to explain away failures.

Next control: compare two explicit prefixes crossed with initial case, preserving body alignment, and include a fixed direct-answer format alongside free continuation. Predeclare strings using tokenization alone and retain all competence failures. Measure correct-capital versus paired alternative separately from correct-capital versus generic continuation probability, and repeat span/complement/full removals at small and full dose. If the effect disappears when response mode is held stable, the earlier failure was primarily a continuation-mode interaction. If it persists with stable competence and alters factual discrimination, a stronger retrieval-specific hypothesis survives. Keep copying/agreement anchors so this is not inferred from capital prompts alone.

## Previous continuation: H617

## H617 — Missing directions matter on unseen constructions; nonlinear effects grow with dose

H616 showed frozen copying coordinates transfer poorly across constructions despite perfect copying accuracy. To distinguish behaviorally irrelevant residual directions from nonlinear interactions, decompose every Attention5 contextual interaction I into P (its projection onto frozen H615 joint64) and Q=I−P. Subtract P, Q or I across body positions at doses 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2. Use the same 128 combined-condition recipients, giving 1,536 interventions plus128 native baseline evaluations. No fit, selection or additional natural text.

The previous goal turn was progress: H616 completed new experiments and changed the hypothesis ranking. This turn directly tests the alternatives raised by that evidence. The broad goal remains incomplete.

**The complement is not generally behaviorally negligible.** At dose1, complement-only native-reference KL is 0.5–1.3% of full-removal KL in familiar constructions, but 29–36% in the unseen sentence and 22–23% in the list. Ratios compare mean KL within each cell; they are not fractions of an additive causal effect. All copied answers remain top1. Thus output distributions reveal an effect that copied-answer accuracy misses.

The factorial cross-term at a downstream vector z is z(full removal)−z(P removal)−z(Q removal)+z(native). A zero cross-term means the two separate perturbation effects add. Internal cross-terms use the normalized MLP11 input; logit cross-terms remove the probability-weighted common offset and use native-probability-weighted RMS over the vocabulary. This weighting is a local distribution-sensitive diagnostic, not exact KL. A second check compares actual full-removal logits with logits predicted by adding the two separate shifts, using exact softmax KL.

**Finite-strength nonlinearity is present but is not the whole failure.** In unseen constructions, relative logit cross-terms are about 1.7–4.4% at quarter dose, 7.6–17.2% at dose1, and 14.5–30.6% at dose2. Internal cross-terms likewise grow from about 1.6–2.3% to 6.1–8.9% to 11.5–16.8%. The missing directions already produce appreciable KL at quarter dose, where vector/logit additivity is closer. That weakens an explanation in which only large-intervention nonlinearity creates the transfer gap.

|Different|Name list|2.0|0.1449|0.00097304|0.05342816|

For the unseen sentence, P-only KL exceeds full-removal KL (1.28–1.34 times at dose1), consistent with partial cancellation between component effects. For the list, both separate KLs are smaller than full-removal KL. Neither comparison alone measures nonlinearity: KL is nonlinear even if logits add exactly. The direct factorial logit test above is what diagnoses nonadditivity. A weighted cosine between separate logit shifts would be a more direct cancellation measurement; it was not computed here.

At dose1, additive-logit prediction KL is around 0.000027–0.000062 nats on unseen forms, compared with full native-reference KL about0.0012–0.0097. At dose2 the prediction discrepancy grows to about0.00033–0.00135 nats. These are small absolute distribution changes; describing relative errors without that scale would exaggerate their practical size. No task accuracy change is established.

Updated hypothesis ranking: (1) construction-dependent output directions omitted by a familiar-format fit remains best supported; (2) downstream sensitivity weights those directions differently, so an internal Euclidean basis does not automatically preserve output KL; (3) finite-dose component interactions contribute, especially under format shift; (4) the complement is universally irrelevant is weakened; (5) preservation of this interaction is necessary for correct copying remains unsupported. This is a conditional representation of one interaction, not a discovered universal feature ontology or executable compression of the model.

Next move the same frozen-space/complement test to genuinely different tasks: grammatical agreement, entity binding, capital recall, sentiment, with copying anchors. Use fixed templates and initial-case/prefix conditions, audit token alignment before inference, report candidate-choice and full-vocabulary competence separately, retain failed competence cells, and do not fit new bases to rescue failures. This distinguishes copying-format dependence from broader task dependence. Any excluded token-incompatible prompt must be reported before model-output selection; use semantic-group NLL where multiple accepted tokens are needed and keep that distinct from single-token CE.

“Rank64” means 64 directions in the 1,152-dimensional output space. Write error compares the projected interaction with its full vector. **Internal reconstruction and behavioral fidelity separate.** Rank64 improves internal errors over rank32 on both unseen forms, but worsens relative KL for the unseen sentence: 0.341→0.510 for familiar names and 0.291→0.391 for different names. All 32 native competence cells have perfect paired candidate choice and full-vocabulary top1; all 640 interventions preserve correct copied-name top1. This demonstrates a representational transfer gap in a task the model can perform. It does not establish that this interaction is necessary for copying. The task is still copying throughout; construction diversity is not task diversity. Earlier diverse-task studies remain relevant, but this run alone cannot support cross-task claims.

Most likely explanations now are (1) shared but construction-dependent output directions, with coverage determining compactness; (2) context-dependent downstream sensitivity causing the KL/internal-fidelity mismatch; and (3) a substantial interaction component that is behaviorally dispensable for this easy task. A universal rank64 space covering unseen constructions is weakened. Name identity as the dominant source of failure is weakened on this panel.

The next discriminating experiment should separate omitted directions from nonlinear downstream sensitivity: remove the frozen in-span and out-of-span components separately and jointly at multiple doses, retaining all forms and names. If complement removal causes little output change despite large internal shifts, an output-based quotient could be much smaller. If combinations are strongly nonadditive, separate component importance is misleading. Follow this with the same predeclared comparison across agreement, copying, factual retrieval and controlled relational reasoning, using competence checks per task without deleting failed cells. Do not infer a universal computational unit from further copying-only fits.

The shared basis generally matches or improves on conditional bases at equal total stored directions, especially at small budgets. For new wording, joint rank8 relative KL is 0.143 versus 1.320 for the conditional rank4 used within its total8 budget. This does not prove an inherent advantage of shared coordinates: the shared representation has twice as many active directions per token, and PCA optimizes reconstruction under its weighting rather than downstream KL. At total64, the two approaches have similar fidelity, with conditional KL/CE slightly better in some cells.

The separate spaces are not identical. Their mean squared principal-angle cosine is about 0.302 at rank4, 0.321 at rank8, 0.273 at rank16 and 0.288 at rank32. This is a geometric overlap measure, not a percentage of shared semantic features. Old-only rank32 has new-wording write/target errors 0.693/0.621; new-only rank32 has old-wording errors 0.644/0.636. Yet a single span fitted to both covers held-out names well. Different local directions do not force disjoint computational units.

All fidelity metrics refer to the full contextual-interaction removal. They are not task error rates or causal shares. All interventions retain correct copied-name top1. Rank64 shared output KL errors are about 0.015/0.023, but intended-token CE errors remain 0.137/0.218, so no universal faithfulness threshold is met across all objectives. A random rank64 span remains near omission in target-effect fidelity (0.947/0.923).

A refreshed hypothesis set connects these local results to the broader goal:

1. The Attention5 interaction is distributed across heads — supported on this panel.
2. A single dominant head is sufficient — weakened by H613.
3. High write variance guarantees output fidelity — contradicted by H614's weighting comparison.
4. Token weighting materially changes useful coordinates — supported locally.
5. Shared output coordinates can cover both known wordings — supported at finite error.
6. Separate wording-specific units are necessary here — weakened by the joint-basis result.
7. The two separately learned spans are nearly identical — not supported by overlap geometry.
8. Different wording spans encode the same abstract operation in different coordinates — open; geometric approximation alone cannot establish semantics.
9. A universal additive prefix direction predicts all contexts — weakened by H604–H605.
10. A common shift plus normalization explains the dependence — weakened by H605.
11. Boundary-token changes explain most Attention0 interaction — supported by H609's control.
12. Tokenization explains the entire later interaction — weakened by substantial remaining interaction.
13. A large MLP0 cross term drives the later target — weakened by H610's body removals.
14. Later non-final writers materially influence the target — supported by H611.
15. Attention5's direct persistent-value interaction dominates — weakened by H612.
16. Persistent values contribute upstream to local routing/value formation — still open.
17. Routing alone is the relevant computational unit — weakened by factor removals.
18. Coordinated contextual values and routing form the relevant local object — supported, with baseline-dependent decomposition.
19. Preserving this interaction is necessary for copied-name accuracy — not demonstrated; top1 survives interventions.
20. The shared span transfers to unseen constructions without growing rank — open and the highest-value next test.

Most likely current account: context-dependent computations can share a compact, data-dependent output representation when discovery covers the relevant regimes. Architectural units and fitted coordinates are different descriptions. The evidence supports neither a unique canonical basis nor universally stable semantic directions. The important next question is how required dimension grows as genuinely new constructions enter the distribution, not whether we can fit the two familiar wordings more closely.

Next freeze the shared rank32/rank64 bases for new lexical items crossed with familiar and previously unseen constructions, with token-boundary alignment and competence checks retained. Do not refit after viewing failures. This separates lexical generalization from construction generalization and tests the strongest remaining hypothesis directly.

H613 found distributed head contributions. This does not imply a high-dimensional combined write. Fit uncentered output-space PCA to Attention5's full contextual interaction using only old-wording items0–3 (eight endpoints). Compare raw token-row PCA with PCA after normalizing each training token row to unit norm, so large-magnitude positions do not dominate. Include one seeded orthonormal random basis and the H613 four-head baseline. Freeze bases and ranks1/4/8/16/32 before downstream evaluation.

Project each observed body-position interaction write onto the chosen output directions, then subtract that approximation on the combined prompt. Coefficients still require the actual four-condition interaction; this is conditional reconstruction, not prediction from raw text or elimination of the original model's computation. Per-token balancing changes the fitting measure, not a learned causal objective. The reference is full contextual-interaction removal. Head pruning and direction projection have different parameter/computation costs; this is a fidelity comparison, not a matched compute-budget benchmark.

There are 152 discovery token rows, eight same-wording holdout endpoints and sixteen new-wording endpoints. The familiar panel makes this adaptive transfer evaluation rather than independent confirmation. 576 interventions plus32 native baseline forwards complete.


**Within familiar wording, a few shared output directions can be useful even though no single head suffices.** On held-out items, token-balanced rank4 gives relative output KL 0.0385 versus 0.9704 for raw rank4. Yet its write reconstruction is worse (0.419 versus 0.369 error). MLP11 effect fidelity also improves (0.295 versus 0.495 error), but is far from exact. Thus retaining more write variance is not the same as preserving the downstream behavior of this intervention.

All errors concern fidelity to full contextual-interaction removal. MLP11 effect error compares target shifts, and relative KL divides approximation-to-full KL by unchanged-to-full KL. These are not task error rates. Full copied-name top1 remains correct in every intervention. Margin and token CE are separately reported because low KL does not guarantee a selected answer statistic is equally faithful.

Rank32 gives strong familiar-wording approximation: write error about 0.080, MLP11 effect error about 0.099–0.100, and relative KL 0.014–0.015. But frozen rank32 fails to transfer nearly as well to new wording: write error about 0.692, target-effect error about 0.621–0.622, and relative KL 0.265–0.288. Random32 remains near omission in target fidelity, supporting learned structure rather than arbitrary low-dimensional compression. This is evidence for within-distribution compactness, not a global canonical form.

The two training objectives also behave differently as rank increases. Raw rank4 retains 86.3% of discovery squared write norm yet has poor held-out KL; rank8 reaches 95.1% and substantially improves output fidelity. Balanced PCA's corresponding normalized-row fractions are 84.2% and 93.6%, which are fractions under a different measure and cannot be compared directly as retained raw energy. Output KL need not decrease monotonically with reconstruction rank because downstream computation is nonlinear and errors can cancel.

Interpretation: several architectural heads can jointly implement an approximately low-dimensional operation on a specified data distribution. Which directions count as important depends on token weighting and on whether fidelity means write reconstruction, downstream target, output KL or answer loss. This directly supports studying data-based equivalence with an explicit distribution and objective, while the wording failure warns against calling the fitted directions universal features. No semantic meaning or uniqueness of these basis vectors is established.

Next compare shared versus wording-conditioned output spans at fixed total direction count, fitting both only on discovery items and evaluating held-out names. A joint basis versus two smaller conditional bases can distinguish insufficient coverage from intrinsically different local coordinates without simply increasing capacity. Report principal-angle/overlap geometry alongside interventions, and preserve the distinction between representation fidelity and a predictor that avoids observing the full response.

## H613 — Influential contextual interaction is distributed across heads

Decompose Attention5's contextual-value four-condition body-write interaction into its nine projected head contributions. Their sum reproduces the full contextual interaction. Test each head alone, full-minus-one-head, per-position norm-matched random controls, and small fixed head sets. The reference is removal of the full contextual interaction, rather than whichever intervention produces the smallest target norm.

Choose head sets of size1/2/3/4 by exhaustive minimization of mean relative squared write error on old-wording items0–3 only (eight endpoints). Freeze selections before downstream evaluation. Evaluate those discovery cases, eight held-out old-wording endpoints, and all16 new-wording endpoints. The panel was previously explored; this is adaptive item/wording transfer, not an independent benchmark or fresh vocabulary. The new-wording set includes both discovery lexical items and other items.

Locked selections (zero-based heads) are H7; H5+H7; H5+H7+H8; and H0+H5+H7+H8. These minimize the specified internal write objective on discovery; no claim is made that they optimize output KL, CE or target fidelity. No evaluation outcome is used to reselect them. Each head contribution still requires its observed four-condition routing/value data.

MLP11 effect error is the distance between the approximate-removal and full-removal target vectors, divided by the full-removal shift from native. It is not the remaining native factorial-interaction norm. Relative output KL similarly compares the approximation with the full-removal distribution, normalized by full-removal versus unchanged. These are fidelity errors, not task error rates or explained shares. All interventions retain the correct copied name as full-vocabulary top1.

The four-head set has MLP11 effect error 0.524 on held-out old wording and 0.613 on new wording. Its relative output KL is 0.177 and 0.364, while intended-token CE fidelity is less uniform (0.308 and 0.710). Thus it is a useful partial approximation, not a faithful compact replacement under all objectives. Individual-head results likewise fail to identify one generally dominant carrier.

Leave-one-head-out results expose objective and context dependence. Omitting H4 is comparatively mild: old-wording holdout write error 0.106, target-effect error 0.108 and relative KL 0.007; new wording gives 0.105, 0.100 and 0.016. This retains eight of nine heads, so it is not substantial compression. Omitting H5 has relative KL 0.055 on old-wording holdout but 0.401 on new wording, with new-wording intended-token CE error 1.539. H7 was the best discovery single-head write approximation, but its new-wording single-head relative KL is 0.938. Head importance depends on context and the fidelity criterion.

The output interactions are exactly additive over heads, but their downstream effects are not additive causal shares. Norm-matched random head controls use one seeded direction per head/body position; they are directional checks. Selection rankings are not significance estimates across independent datasets.

Interpretation: this particular contextual interaction is spread across multiple heads rather than localized to one head. That does not imply high intrinsic computational dimension or rule out shared features across heads. Several heads may write into a common low-dimensional output subspace, and discrete head pruning is only one representation choice. Nor does preserving copying top1 establish that the approximated internal interaction is behaviorally necessary.

Next compare head pruning with a low-rank output-space representation of the combined contextual interaction. Fit directions only on discovery writes, freeze ranks and basis before held-out evaluation, and keep internal-write, MLP11-effect, output-KL and intended-token-CE fidelity separate. Such a result would test data-based compactness across heads rather than equating architectural head count with number of computational units. It would remain a conditional representation unless coefficients can later be predicted without observing all four context responses.

## Previous continuation: H612

## H612 — Attention5 interaction is carried by contextual values with coordinated routing/value effects

H611 localized an influential Attention5 body write. Decompose it exactly before attributing the effect. Reconstruct native signed attention patterns from RMS-normalized rotary Q/K and Q2/K2. Separate the contextual local values from persistent values using the native coefficients: local weight 1.056396484375 and persistent weight -0.056396484375. These are signed learned mixing coefficients, not probabilities.

Align body query positions and pad absent prefix-key slots with zero routing and zero values in unprefixed runs. This preserves the exact output; it also makes the expansion convention explicit. For each value stream write the output as F(R,V), including the output projection, and anchor the four-condition expansion at unprefixed uppercase:

- Routing-only term: F(R_interaction,V00).
- Value-only term: F(R00,V_interaction).
- Mixed term: the full interaction minus those two terms.

The mixed term collects all remaining co-variation, including appearance of prefix slots. This is an exact baseline-anchored decomposition, not a unique attribution or a claim that all three terms are independently meaningful features.

Native reconstruction passes before interventions. On combined prefix/lowercase prompts subtract full, local, persistent, routing, value, mixed, and stream-specific components across the body, with per-position norm-matched random controls and identity. 800 interventions; same panel and no new fitting. Persistent values remain live during these output-write subtractions.

**The direct Attention5 interaction is overwhelmingly carried by the contextual-value stream.** Its norm is about 1.001–1.002 times the full interaction, while the persistent-stream contribution is about 0.041–0.044. Removing the contextual stream leaves target MLP11 interaction norm 0.577/0.509, almost matching full removal at 0.574/0.507. Removing the persistent-stream contribution leaves 0.997/1.000. This concerns the direct Attention5 output contribution; persistent values may still affect earlier computations that produce its routing and local values.

Interpretation: the localized object is a coordinated routing-and-contextual-value computation. It is not well described here as a single preexisting value feature, and it is not primarily a direct persistent-value read. The factorization does not yet identify a minimal or unique unit; its baseline convention and the restricted prompt family matter. The result nevertheless narrows the search from an entire layer/bus system to Attention5's contextual-value interaction across body positions.

Next resolve this interaction by attention head, retaining exact output additivity and testing individual removals and leave-one-head-out reconstructions. This can distinguish a compact head-level carrier from distributed cancellation. Compare fidelity to the full intervention, not merely which individual removal gives the smallest target norm. Any subsequent head selection must be labeled adaptive and checked on held-out examples/wording.

The learned architecture supplies a concrete candidate explanation for this attenuation: the next block scales the incoming residual by 0.0126953125 while adding 8 times the original embedding residual. Updated interpretation: an algebraically identifiable bilinear interaction is not automatically a behaviorally important computational unit. Here the local term is real and large, yet removing it across the body barely changes the downstream interaction or copying behavior. The next useful target is where interaction is reintroduced or amplified after the strong residual rescaling, rather than further decomposing this early term solely because it is mathematically clean.

Next sweep aligned-body interaction removals at later attention/MLP writes, especially after the first residual rescaling and around layers 2–5, while retaining later Attention9 as a readout. Compare those results with the final-position sweep to locate positional carriers. Then distinguish residual-stream transmission from fresh mixing through the persistent value pathway. This preserves the broader goal of finding causally useful units rather than equating large local products with important features.

## H609 — Boundary matching removes most earliest interaction, but bilinear mixing creates a remaining interaction

Add one leading space to every unprefixed H607 prompt. This makes the aligned body token IDs identical across prefix presence, for each capitalization choice. The prefixed prompts are unchanged. Audit all 64 body comparisons: each prefixed token sequence after its four-token prefix exactly equals its corresponding unprefixed sequence. The first-word alternatives are now ĠHe/Ġhe in both prefix conditions and ĠA/Ġa in both. The final token remains unchanged.

Repeat the H608 native trace and all 23 predeclared final-position write removals with norm-matched controls: 128 native prompts and 1,504 interventions. All eight competence cells remain perfect. This is an input control, not a new fit. It changes the boundary conditions of the comparison; differences from H608 are not additive causal shares of the original interaction.

**Attention0's interaction shrinks by more than 99.6%, strongly implicating the token-boundary asymmetry in the earliest signal.** It does not become exactly zero. Later interaction remains substantial, and the normalized MLP11 interaction norm is about 57–60% of its former value. The boundary confound therefore matters greatly but does not account for all context dependence.

| Wording | Measurement | Original boundary norm | Matched boundary norm |
|---|---|---:|---:|
|0|Attention0 write|8.525559|0.023916|
|0|MLP0 write|428.251539|9.719131|
|0|MLP0 normalized input|0.509222|0.002150|
|0|MLP11 normalized input|2.727935|1.646987|
|1|Attention0 write|8.553003|0.032541|
|1|MLP0 write|479.901087|19.690745|
|1|MLP0 normalized input|0.501035|0.003602|
|1|MLP11 normalized input|2.408702|1.368058|

The small Attention0 residual is reported rather than interpreted as a new semantic interaction or assumed to be exactly roundoff. Rotary/cache precision and other implementation details would require additional controls to explain that residual. Large raw write norms at different layers are not directly comparable measures of causal importance because residual scales and skip coefficients differ.

We can explain the local MLP0 interaction algebraically. Let B be its ungated bilinear map, z=z00 its native normalized input, P=z10-z00, C=z01-z00, and I=z11-z10-z01+z00. The four-condition MLP interaction is exactly:

B(z11)-B(z10)-B(z01)+B(z00)
= T(P,C) + [B(z+P+C+I)-B(z+P+C)].

The first term is the direct bilinear cross response between the prefix-associated and capitalization-associated input changes. The second term propagates input non-additivity, which can include RMS normalization and inherited attention interaction; it must not be called a pure normalization effect.

| Wording | Full MLP0 interaction norm | Direct bilinear cross norm | Input-nonadditivity remainder norm | Cross/remainder cosine |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|0|9.7191|9.9034|2.7481|-0.2052|
|1|19.6906|19.8060|5.8146|-0.1666|

The direct cross term is comparable to the full local interaction; the smaller remainder partly cancels it. This is concrete evidence for local multiplicative formation after the boundary asymmetry is removed. It is a decomposition of this operation's output, not a claim that the same term explains a corresponding percentage of the later MLP11 interaction or task behavior.

As before, removing an early interaction only at the final position has little effect on MLP11. The strongest tested removal is Attention9 for old wording (remaining target norm 0.806), and Attention5 for new wording (0.839; Attention9 leaves 0.850). Rankings are exploratory on the same panel. These effects are conditional interventions, not additive attributions; earlier body positions remain untouched and can carry or regenerate interaction.

Updated interpretation: the original effect contained a large boundary-token component, but interaction also arises through the model's bilinear computation under aligned token IDs. Thus it is too strong to dismiss the entire result as tokenization, and too strong to interpret it as an abstract prefix feature. We now have an explicit local interaction term whose causal downstream role can be tested.

Next capture aligned body positions and subtract the MLP0 bilinear cross term or full interaction across those positions, with first-token/final-token/all-body contrasts and norm-matched controls. Leave prefix-only positions explicit rather than inventing unmatched counterparts. This tests whether early multiplicative formation is carried from earlier body positions to the later attention writers, addressing the main limitation of final-position-only removals.

Audits: all 64 aligned bodies exactly match IDs; all eight competence cells perfect; old/new manifests and runner unchanged; exact identity replay; final embedding interaction zero; 1,504 interventions finite. The native float32 residual accounting has maximum relative discrepancy 2.55e-4, larger than H608 because the controlled interaction is smaller. A float64 local MLP decomposition verifies the identity within 1.56e-12. Its replay of the native float32 four-way MLP0 difference differs by at most 0.349% (old wording) / 0.172% (new wording), consistent with cancellation sensitivity; local norms agree closely. ## H608 — Token-boundary differences seed an early interaction; later attention writes carry stronger final-position influence

Trace all four H607 prefix/capitalization conditions through final-position attention writes, MLP writes, residuals and normalized MLP inputs at all 18 layers. Use the same 128 prompts, previously fully competent in all eight cells. The target is the native four-condition interaction at normalized MLP11 input. This experiment does not inject the number/task/random signals from H607; it studies the upstream interaction that those experiments used as context.

Then, on each combined prefix+lowercase prompt, subtract the native four-condition interaction vector at one final-position write, allowing downstream computation to run normally. Test every attention/MLP write in layers 0–10 plus Attention11: all 23 sites are predeclared. Compare a seeded norm-matched random subtraction per site and unchanged replay. There are 1,504 interventions: 32 identity runs plus 32 recipients ×23 sites ×2 subtraction modes. No site is selected before evaluation; reported rankings are exploratory on this panel.

**The input manipulation contains a concrete token-boundary confound.** The first body token in the four conditions is:

| Wording | Native | Case only | Prefix only | Both |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| He sent… | He (1544) | he (258) | ĠHe (679) | Ġhe (339) |
| A letter… | A (32) | a (64) | ĠA (317) | Ġa (257) |

Ġ denotes a leading-space token, not an extra displayed character. The prefix adds four tokens; among aligned original body tokens, only the first changes. Thus capitalization is implemented with different token pairs at the sequence boundary and after the prefix. These are distinct embedding inputs, so the H607 factors are not two identical token-level operations in different contexts. This is a plausible source of their earliest interaction, not yet an isolated causal explanation of all later effects.

The final-position embedding interaction is exactly zero because the final token is unchanged. Nevertheless, the first attention output already has a nonzero interaction (mean norm 8.526/8.553 in old/new wording). MLP0's write interaction is much larger (428.3/479.9 raw norm). Raw norms vary with residual scaling and cannot be read as causal importance. Normalized-input interaction grows and shrinks through later blocks, reaching mean norm 2.728/2.409 at MLP11. Exact residual accounting, including learned skip coefficients, verifies that the trace is internally consistent.

**Early appearance is not the same as strong influence under a final-position removal.** Subtracting Attention0 or MLP0 interaction at the final position leaves MLP11's interaction norm almost unchanged. Other token positions remain live and may regenerate or transmit the interaction; this does not establish that the early layers are unimportant. Attention9 is the strongest tested single final-position removal in both wordings, leaving approximately 0.820 and 0.786 of the original target norm.

## H607 — Prefix and capitalization interact strongly before MLP11

The earlier prefix edit prepended "For the record," and lowercased the first character of the original sentence. This factorial separates those changes in the two copying formats. Hold names and answers fixed; cross prefix present/absent with initial uppercase/lowercase. Use eight name pairs and both endpoints in each format: 128 native prompts. All eight wording/prefix/case competence cells have both-endpoint candidate correctness and full-vocabulary intended-answer top1 of 1.000. This removes task incompetence as an explanation for the measured local changes.

Let z00 be the native normalized MLP11 input, z01 lowercase-only, z10 prefix-only retaining the initial uppercase character, and z11 both changes. Define:

- Case component C=z01-z00.
- Prefix component P=z10-z00.
- Interaction I=z11-z10-z01+z00.
- Total change D=z11-z00=C+P+I.

The interaction measures non-additivity of upstream context formation. It is not the quadratic-in-e term of MLP11's bilinear response expansion. The local response map T(dc,e) is linear in dc for fixed incoming e, so its three component responses sum exactly to the full response. Downstream behavioral effects need not add, and component norms are not causal percentage shares.

For each original uppercase/unprefixed recipient, inject equal-norm number/task/random Attention5 signals with both signs. Capture 192 incoming responses. Run full/unchanged, individual components, additive C+P, and matched cross-format component replacements using the same name/endpoint: 1,920 interventions. No fitting or selection occurs. The prefix-only strings retain an uppercase word after a comma; case changes tokenization/orthography and is not a clean semantic factor. Nevertheless, all cases preserve copying competence.

**The capitalization confound is material, but does not by itself explain the earlier prefix results.** Mean context-component norms relative to the total are:

| Wording | Case / total norm | Prefix / total norm | Interaction / total norm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|Old: He sent|0.6996|0.8123|1.0544|
|New: A letter was delivered|1.0560|0.9962|1.2319|

The interaction is as large as or larger than the total because the vectors partly cancel. Ignoring it gives substantial error. At the new wording, additive C+P has relative output KL 1.326–1.421: worse than leaving the entire context-switch contribution out. Prefix-only is closer (0.401–0.943) but still incomplete. Case-only is substantially worse (2.282–2.427). Thus the full effect cannot be explained by summing two independent edit effects.

| Wording | Signal | Case-only relative KL | Prefix-only relative KL | Additive C+P relative KL | Interaction-only relative KL | Full cross-format replacement relative KL |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|0|number|1.2026|0.5666|1.2291|1.6342|0.4995|
|0|task|0.8955|0.4550|0.8202|1.3638|0.3609|
|0|random|0.9950|0.4805|0.9893|1.5021|0.6181|
|1|number|2.2823|0.4014|1.4200|2.1867|0.9178|
|1|task|2.4272|0.5074|1.4213|1.3541|1.0430|
|1|random|2.2936|0.9434|1.3264|1.6268|1.1605|

Cross-format geometry also depends on component identity. Mean old/new cosine similarity is about 0.697 for the total change, but only 0.487 for case, 0.408 for prefix, and 0.559 for interaction. The total can appear more stable than its constituent changes because of cancellation. Replacing one component with its counterpart from the other format produces substantial errors; the replacement is conditional on retaining the recipient's other two components. These are not additive attributions of the total transfer failure.

All relative KL/margin/CE errors are normalized against full-context-switch versus unchanged-context discrepancy. They measure fidelity to this conditional local intervention, not total task error. Full reconstruction is a reference, not a claim that the prefix should alter the copied answer. The actual incoming e remains observed. Raw internal, answer-margin and intended-token CE metrics are stored separately.

Interpretation: two simple textual factors interact non-additively in the representation reaching MLP11 even though the task answer remains unchanged and the model is fully competent. This gives a more concrete mechanism behind part of the earlier format dependence: context effects are jointly formed, not necessarily sums of reusable edit directions. It neither establishes universal feature interactions nor rules out a different coordinate system that exposes simpler structure. Prefix content, added length/positions, orthography and tokenization remain entangled within these controlled factors.

Next locate where this interaction emerges and which computations carry it. Trace the four-condition difference through attention and MLP writes across layers; distinguish a large upstream interaction from downstream amplification or cancellation. Then intervene on candidate writes to test whether reducing that interaction changes the later context-switch response. Length and verb-construction controls remain useful, but locating this now-verified interaction has higher immediate information value than treating the combined edit as a single feature.

Audits: all eight competence cells perfect; 128 native prompts, 192 perturbed captures, 1,920 interventions; exact unchanged-response logit replay; component response sum error <=7.67e-7 relative; runner and manifest unchanged; all metrics finite. No new natural-text documents; FineWeb remains 26,112. Broad goal remains active and incomplete.

## Previous continuation: H606

## H606 — Within-format prediction works much better; earlier state does not broadly fix transfer

H605 held out task and wording simultaneously. This control separates them and tests predictor location. Capture 320 native prompt records covering all eight items and both wordings for the five tasks, with/without the prefix. Fit only item IDs 0–3 and evaluate only IDs 4–7 under new wording. For each target task, compare four training regimes: same task/new wording, same task/old wording, other tasks/new wording, other tasks/old wording. These labels refer to task-specific template versions; they do not impose one common sentence shell across different tasks.

For each regime fit a fixed mean and three otherwise identical ridge predictors from final-position MLP11 normalized input, MLP5 normalized input, or Attention5 output. The attention write is used as observed; ridge regularization scales with each input's Gram trace. The predictors never receive the evaluation edited-context difference. All use observed incoming e to execute the predicted bilinear response. Training uses eight contexts in same-task regimes and 32 in other-task regimes, so training-set size is not matched; the other-task regime has more data. No model or hyperparameter selection occurs on evaluation.

There are 240 identical evaluation signal cases across 18 modes, giving 4,320 interventions. This is an adaptive test on familiar evaluation prompts with newly captured training items/states, not independent confirmation. Item IDs are disjoint, but lexical overlap is possible. In same-task/new-wording capital recall, two evaluation endpoint prompt strings exactly duplicate training strings through neighboring country pairs. That condition is not a clean lexical holdout and must not support a generalization claim. No exact prompt overlap occurs in the other regime/family combinations.

**Prediction is much better when both task and wording are represented in training.** For competent copying, native-MLP11 prediction gives relative KL 0.073–0.094 on held-out items with matching wording, versus 0.762–0.921 from old wording. For competent agreement the corresponding ranges are 0.103–0.130 versus 0.343–0.658. The within-format constant mean already gives copying relative KL 0.083–0.103, so a large part of that predictable effect is shared within the format; ridge adds a modest improvement. Agreement benefits more from conditioning on native input.

| Task | Signal | Same task/new wording MLP11 KL | Same task/old wording MLP11 KL | Other tasks/new wording MLP11 KL | Other tasks/old wording MLP11 KL |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|agreement|number|0.1029|0.3426|0.7066|0.5610|
|agreement|task|0.1078|0.3433|0.7220|0.5915|
|agreement|random|0.1295|0.6576|0.8057|0.6908|
|capital_recall|number|0.0247|0.5345|0.8458|1.0174|
|capital_recall|task|0.0296|0.3667|0.7646|0.8822|
|capital_recall|random|0.0299|0.3693|0.8411|0.8060|
|entity_binding|number|0.4073|0.7980|1.1861|1.0817|
|entity_binding|task|0.1672|0.5309|0.9769|1.1178|
|entity_binding|random|0.3217|0.5884|1.7192|1.7400|
|sentiment|number|0.0354|0.1355|1.2608|1.1053|
|sentiment|task|0.0530|0.1603|2.1152|1.6236|
|sentiment|random|0.0424|0.1518|1.4122|1.3306|
|sequence_copy|number|0.0725|0.9208|1.6426|1.5379|
|sequence_copy|task|0.0938|0.9079|0.9900|1.2454|
|sequence_copy|random|0.0867|0.7616|3.2087|2.8642|

Earlier-state predictors do not consistently rescue the wording shift. In copying, same-task/old-wording MLP5 KL is 0.881–1.485 and Attention5 KL 0.838–1.357, versus MLP11 0.762–0.921. In agreement the earlier inputs likewise worsen transfer. Within matching wording, MLP5 is slightly better than MLP11 for agreement and similar for several other cases, so this is not a claim that later state is universally superior. It specifically weakens the hypothesis that simply replacing final-position MLP11 input with one of these earlier local vectors solves the transfer problem. Full-sequence state and richer predictors remain untested.

All numbers are fidelity errors relative to the full local context switch versus leaving its contribution unchanged, not task accuracy or shares of total computation. Internal response, answer-margin and intended-token CE errors are reported separately in the JSON. Good relative KL does not imply faithful reconstruction of all internal components or all answer statistics.

Competence remains as in H603: copying and agreement pass fully for recipients and prefixed donors; binding recipients pass but prefixed donors are weak; sentiment reaches the recipient threshold but prefixed donors are weak; new-wording recall recipients fail. The clearest task-level inference therefore comes from copying and agreement. All cases remain in the result.

Interpretation: the difficult part is transfer between context/format regimes, not basic inability to predict the edit within a regime. A nearly constant format-conditioned component plus item-dependent variation is a plausible account for copying. The current evidence does not establish whether format dependence is caused by sentence length, lexical construction, token positions, routing, or semantics. Task and surface form still covary across families. Nor does a family of format-specific predictors constitute a canonical form or identify unique units.

Next isolate those structural variables with matched edits that preserve task competence: hold the copied content fixed while changing sentence length, verb construction and repetition/position separately. Measure which changes alter prefix response geometry and which changes alter downstream use of otherwise similar responses. This can turn the current descriptive conditioning into a mechanistic account instead of fitting another more flexible predictor.

Audits: actual saved training/test metadata checked for every regime; zero item-ID overlap; exact prompt overlap reported above; frozen source/runner/manifest/fitted objects unchanged; 320 native capture records, 240 cases, 4,320 interventions; native replay max logit error 3.87e-5, matched prior native capture difference <=2.82e-5; ridge normal-equation residual <=1.91e-15; all metrics finite. Source response algebra was independently audited in H603. No new natural-text documents; FineWeb remains 26,112. Broad goal remains active and incomplete.

## Previous continuation: H605

## H605 — Simple native-context predictors do not restore cross-task transfer

H604's projection modes observed the actual edited-minus-native context difference dc. This experiment removes that information from all predictive modes. Fit dc as a function of native normalized MLP11 input z using the same five leave-task/wording-out folds: 32 other-task old-wording endpoint records for fitting; eight held-out-task new-wording endpoints for evaluation. All predictions still use the actual incoming perturbation e to execute the bilinear response T(predicted_dc,e). The exact/full reference necessarily uses the true dc, but it does not enter predictor fitting or evaluation coefficients.

Compare five shared models: constant mean; isotropic affine change mean_dc + beta*(z-mean_z); centered ridge regression; isotropic change plus ridge residual; and a common shift followed by RMS normalization, predicted_dc=normalize(z+u)-z. Ridge regularization is fixed at 0.1 times the mean training Gram diagonal, without an evaluation sweep. Shift fitting uses 500 Adam steps on training normalized-input MSE only. Same-task old-wording ridge and shift fits are separately labeled diagnostics, not task holdouts. No evaluation-task label is supplied to a shared model, but native context can encode task and format.

The constant shift and normalized-shift models each use one 1,152-dimensional vector. The isotropic affine form adds a scalar and a native-context mean. Ridge uses up to 31 centered training directions plus a vector intercept and many more parameters. These are not equal-capacity comparisons, and a separate dictionary for every task has greater total storage than a single model. The experiment probes prediction forms rather than selecting a smallest representation.

**Predicting from native context does not rescue broad transfer for these models.** Ridge fits training differences much better than a constant shift: relative training error is 0.114–0.199 versus 0.783–0.819. But this advantage largely disappears on the held-out task/new wording. A common shift plus normalization also gives only small, inconsistent benefits. Its training error remains 0.766–0.808. The fitted isotropic contraction beta ranges from -0.0644 to -0.0426; such a small contraction does not explain most of the contextual variation.

|agreement|task|0.6139|0.4942|0.6003|0.5005|0.5044|0.2992|
|agreement|random|0.7107|0.7519|0.6907|0.7432|0.7420|0.6000|

|capital_recall|task|0.9061|0.8913|0.8711|0.8749|0.8894|0.3647|
|capital_recall|random|0.7914|0.7307|0.8356|0.7775|0.7322|0.3708|
|entity_binding|number|1.1386|1.1670|1.1114|1.0356|1.1581|0.5717|
|entity_binding|task|1.1353|1.2270|1.0206|1.0687|1.2260|0.2840|
|entity_binding|random|1.8924|2.0404|1.7164|1.7669|2.0265|0.9484|

|sentiment|task|1.6096|1.8418|1.7271|1.9992|1.8181|0.1379|
|sentiment|random|1.4564|1.2290|1.4780|1.2707|1.2282|0.1599|
|sequence_copy|number|1.7076|1.6965|1.6377|1.7475|1.7052|0.7728|
|sequence_copy|task|1.1446|1.1473|1.4017|1.3617|1.1475|1.0601|
|sequence_copy|random|2.8723|2.5560|3.1759|2.8363|2.5763|0.7625|

For competent copying, shared ridge relative KL is 1.402–3.176, worse than omitting the context-switch correction; same-task ridge gives 0.763–1.060 and still does not reliably recover the effect. Agreement benefits more from isotropic correction but remains approximate. Same-task sentiment prediction performs better, but its prefixed donors have weak competence, so that is evidence about local response prediction rather than a clean successful-task mechanism.

Relative errors compare each approximation with the exact local context switch, normalized by full-versus-unchanged discrepancy. They are not task error rates. Raw KL, internal response error, answer-margin error and intended-token CE fidelity are stored separately; lower intervention-fidelity error is not necessarily lower task loss. Recipient competence is inherited from H603: copying/agreement fully pass, binding passes with weak prefixed donors, sentiment barely passes with weak donors, recall fails under new wording. No examples are filtered.

An independent training-only L-BFGS refinement checks whether normalized-shift failure is just incomplete Adam fitting. Across shared and same-task fits, it reduces training MSE by at most 0.00178% and changes training predictions by at most 0.276% of the edit norm. The frozen evaluation models are unchanged. This supports near convergence for these fitted solutions; it does not prove a global optimum or a bound on all normalization-based mechanisms.

Updated interpretation: a universal shift or simple contraction/normalization rule at this normalized MLP input does not explain the prefix effect. Linear context prediction can fit the small training sample but generalizes poorly across task and wording together. This favors richer context dependence, or dependence on information not captured by this particular native-input predictor. It does not prove that native context is insufficient in principle, that a larger nonlinear predictor cannot work, or that model features are necessarily task-specific.

Next separate data coverage, structural cues and missing state before increasing predictor flexibility. Use a common sentence shell/terminal format while varying task content, and compare native MLP11 context with earlier residual or attention-derived context as predictors. Include a within-task held-out-item baseline and a within-format held-out-task baseline. These controls can distinguish a task/format distribution shift from missing causal information; merely lowering training error again has little information value.

Audits: actual saved fold IDs verified to exclude evaluation task and wording in main fits; same-task exceptions explicit; source, runner and fitted folds unchanged; 240 cases and 2,160 interventions; native replay max logit difference 3.87e-5 across batching; ridge normal-equation error <=1.42e-15; finite metrics; training-only optimizer audit above. Exact source context-switch algebra was independently checked in H603. No new natural-text documents; FineWeb remains 26,112. Broad goal remains active and incomplete.

## Previous continuation: H604

## H604 — Prefix responses transfer better within task than across held-out tasks

Can a shared prefix component predict the previously observed failures? For each of five tasks, fit only old-wording prefix context differences from the other four tasks: 32 endpoint records. Evaluate the held-out task under new wording: eight endpoints and six signed signals, 48 cases per fold. Use the H603 data and no new task examples. This is adaptive cross-validation, not independent confirmation. Task and wording are excluded from the main fits; lexical items and other surface properties are not guaranteed disjoint.

Compare a fixed mean context difference, projection onto its direction, uncentered shared rank8 and full-training-span projections, matched random spans, and per-case response oracles. Also fit a small span from the same task's old wording as a separately labeled diagnostic. That last condition is not a task holdout; it tests wording transfer with familiar task/items. It uses up to eight directions and eight training contexts, whereas the pooled other-task fit uses 32 contexts. Per-case active rank8 can be compared, but maintaining separate task dictionaries is not equal total storage to one shared dictionary.

The fixed mean is the only mode that predicts the context difference without observing each evaluation dc. All projection modes still observe actual dc; all modes use actual incoming perturbation e to evaluate T(dc,e). No response metric is fitted here: this isolates the availability of shared context components. Per-case oracles see the full target response and diagnose the available span.

An initial rank assertion caught exact dependencies from repeated capital prompts before intervention results existed. We excluded singular values <=1e-6 times the largest before continuing. Full shared spans have rank29 in four folds and rank32 in the capital-recall fold; same-task spans have rank8 except recall rank5. Random controls match each effective shared rank. No arbitrary null directions are used. All fitted folds were saved and hashed before 2,640 interventions.

**Neither a universal mean nor the other-task spans predicts this prefix well.** The fixed mean is frequently worse than leaving the context contribution unchanged. The full shared span's internal errors remain about 0.845–0.985; its relative KL ranges 0.663–1.134. The same-task old-wording span has much smaller internal errors, about 0.347–0.775, and relative KL 0.107–0.657, despite fewer active directions. It improves both internal error and relative KL over the full other-task span in all 15 task/signal cells.

Relative KL is fidelity to the full local context switch divided by the full-versus-unchanged discrepancy. Values above one are worse than omitting that context-switch contribution. They are not task error rates. Margin and intended-token CE remain separately available in the JSON and can behave differently from KL. No overall accuracy improvement is claimed.

Copying and agreement have fully competent recipients and prefixed donors. Binding's recipients pass, but prefixed donors are weak; sentiment's recipients only reach the threshold and prefixed donors are weak. Recall's new-wording recipients fail full-vocabulary competence. The cleanest functional claims therefore come from copying and agreement; other cells characterize local response geometry and remain included rather than filtered away.

For competent copying, same-task old-wording KL is 0.322–0.556, versus 0.681–0.871 from other tasks. For agreement it is 0.290–0.506, versus 0.663–0.718. Thus the benefit does not depend solely on the weak or failed cells. Large errors remain even in the better condition; this is partial transfer, not faithful reconstruction.

The other-task response oracle still leaves internal errors about 0.793–0.954. A better coefficient rule within those spans cannot erase that missing local component. That statement does not lower-bound output KL or CE. Shared components do exist—many learned projections beat random controls—but they are insufficient for the full prefix response.

Interpretation: "the same textual edit" is not a universal additive feature at this MLP input. Its effect depends strongly on the recipient context. A context-conditioned family of components is currently more plausible than one reusable prefix direction. This does not establish task-specific semantic units: task identity is entangled with sentence structure, length, final-token patterns and other surface factors. Same-task transfer across wording might exploit these shared properties. Nor does this exclude a compact nonlinear or bilinear parameterization of the dependence.

Next discriminate task/semantic dependence from structural dependence. Cross a common terminal format and matched prefix placement with varied task content, or predict prefix responses from a small set of native-context coordinates and test unseen wording/tasks. Compare a shared interaction model with task-specific dictionaries under explicit total-capacity accounting. The useful target is a rule that predicts interventions from context, not just another span that reconstructs observed dc.

Audits: actual saved training/evaluation IDs checked against source metadata for every fold; main training excludes evaluation task and wording; same-task diagnostic exception explicit; orthonormal learned spans checked; source, runner and fitted folds unchanged; 240 cases/2,640 interventions; native replay max logit error 3.87e-5 across batching; oracle normal-equation error <=1.20e-15; finite metrics. Exact context-switch algebra was independently verified for these source cases in H603. FineWeb remains 26,112 documents; broad goal active and incomplete.

## Previous continuation: H603

## H603 — Wording and context-edit changes each break frozen-span transfer

H602 changed wording and context edits together. This matched factorial separates them on H601's held-out item IDs 4–7 across all five tasks. Cross original/new wording with original nuisance edit/For-the-record prefix. Preserve the lexical content of the original edit across wordings: letter→message for copying, folder→notebook for binding, window→door for agreement, Fact-prefix for recall, performance→show for sentiment. New wordings change sentence construction while retaining those edit pairs. The prefix condition prepends For the record and lowercases the original initial character; it is not a pure token-position intervention.

Freeze H601's broad64 basis and number/multi-signal metrics. Use number/task/random signals at equal Attention5 norm with both signs. Template codes: 0=old wording/old edit, 1=old wording/prefix, 2=new wording/old edit, 3=new wording/prefix. No fitting or outcome filtering. The item split excludes fitting items but the old cells were already observed; this is an adaptive diagnostic, not an independent confirmation.

The manifest contains 320 prompt records and 222 unique exact strings. Recipient prompts repeat across edit conditions. There are 960 capture forwards (480 recipient/signal/sign records before repetition across edit conditions), followed by 5,760 interventions.


Copying and agreement remain fully competent in all four conditions. Binding also passes recipient competence in both wordings; its prefixed donors do not. Sentiment passes at 0.625 for old wording and 0.500 for new wording; some prefixed donors are weak. Recall's new wording fails full-vocabulary competence despite candidate correctness. Gate labels therefore apply to recipients, not proof that both ends of every context switch perform the intended task.

**Both changes independently reduce fidelity.** With familiar wording held fixed, replacing the original edit by the prefix increases relative KL in every task/signal cell. With the original edit held fixed, changing wording also increases relative KL in every cell. These are paired panel findings, not independent statistical replications.

These are number-metric KL errors relative to full-switch versus unchanged-context discrepancies. They are not task error rates. Each cell has its own normalization denominator; the raw absolute KL remains in the JSON. The changed wording affects both native context and propagated incoming e, so its effects cannot all be assigned to dc alone.

Nevertheless, context geometry independently shows the shift. Mean Euclidean context reconstruction errors are:

| Condition | Mean relative context reconstruction error |
|---|---:|
|Old wording / old edit|0.2178|
|Old wording / prefix|0.8662|
|New wording / old edit|0.5954|
|New wording / prefix|0.8748|

These means repeat each identical context over six signed-signal cases, with balanced weighting. The jump from about 0.218 in familiar conditions to 0.595 under new wording and 0.866–0.875 under prefix edits supports span coverage as a material limitation. A single nuisance operation such as letter→message is not represented by a fully wording-invariant direction in this frozen span. The fact that the old edit transfers imperfectly does not establish that no alternative invariant representation exists.

The losses are visible in competent copying and agreement, so they cannot be explained entirely by model task failure. However, the size of the wording effect differs strongly by task: sentiment's familiar edit degrades much less than copying's or agreement's. Task labels alone do not predict representational stability.

Updated hypothesis ordering:

1. Context coverage depends on both edit type and sentence construction. Strongly supported here.
2. Some edits have shared components plus wording-specific residuals. Plausible; the partial transfer and task variation motivate measuring the shared versus conditional response components directly.
3. The previous basis largely learned a small inventory of surface/context changes. Still plausible; H601's item transfer cannot rule this out.
4. Merely changing the coefficient metric can restore general transfer in this span. Weakened by H602's high oracle residuals and the present context geometry.
5. Every task needs unrelated computational units. Still unsupported: failure of one frozen span is not evidence against a better shared or conditional representation.

Next test whether new context coverage yields reusable edit-specific components. Train on several context constructions, hold out both task and wording where possible, and compare a fixed-rank shared span against condition-specific spans with matched total capacity. Keep output KL, answer margin, intended-token CE and internal response residuals separate. A stronger mechanistic result would identify a component that predicts interventions across constructions, not merely a basis that reconstructs more training differences.

## H602 — Fresh context edits break much of the shared basis's transfer

Freeze H601's broad 64-dimensional basis and both fitted response metrics before new inference. Construct five tasks with eight pairs each, using familiar lexical inventories but new wording: package-arrival copying, museum/ticket binding, close-to-the-gate agreement, city-that-serves-as-capital recall, and concert-felt sentiment. For each endpoint create a same-answer context by prefixing "For the record,". Also use the opposite-answer endpoint as a separate context donor. This gives 160 native prompts with zero exact string overlap against the checked H581/H582 manifests. It does not establish novel vocabulary or training-data novelty.

Cross context type with number/task/random Attention5 signals at the same norm and both signs. Keep the random direction from H600 so wording/context transfer is not confounded with a new random vector. Capture 960 runs (480 distinct recipient/signal/sign conditions repeated for the two context types), then execute 5,760 downstream interventions: full, unchanged, Euclidean projection, number-trained metric, multi-signal metric and oracle. No basis or map fitting occurs.

Agreement and copying pass competence with full-vocabulary intended-group top1 1.000. Sentiment passes at 0.5625; its prefixed nuisance variants fall to 0.3125. Recall and binding both fail with full-vocabulary top1 0.000 despite correct candidate contrasts. All examples remain. Findings on recall and binding cannot be treated as successful-task mechanisms. The copying and agreement failures below do not depend on those competence failures.

The broad basis loses much of its fidelity. In competent copying, number-metric relative KL is 0.722–1.061 for prefixed contexts and 0.819–0.888 for answer-changing contexts. Relative internal errors are about 0.905–0.921. These are far worse than the familiar-context H601 results, where broad number-metric KL was 0.018–0.076 across the panel. These comparisons characterize a distribution shift; wording, edit type and item composition changed, so they do not isolate which change caused it.

Agreement is a useful exception with limits: answer-changing contexts under number/task signals retain relative KL around 0.074–0.076, but margin errors remain about 0.264–0.266 and internal errors 0.647–0.665. Under random signals the same context class has relative KL 0.261. Good output fidelity can coexist with large local response error.

The ultimate unit-of-computation question remains open: a useful coordinate span is not itself evidence for uniquely identifiable semantic units.

## H601 — Context coverage dominates signal-metric choice at fixed rank

H600's cross-task failure left two explanations: the context span was too narrow, or its metric was adapted to number signals. This factorial separates them. Keep rank at 64. Compare the old agreement-trained basis with a broad basis built from 80 same-answer nuisance context differences across five tasks and two templates. Fit only item IDs 0–3; evaluate only IDs 4–7. Within each basis compare Euclidean coefficients, a response metric trained on number signals, and a response metric trained equally by case on number/task/random signals. Include each basis's target-informed oracle and the historical H598 map as diagnostics.

Number metrics use 160 signed discovery responses; multi-signal metrics use 480. No evaluation-item vectors enter basis or metric fitting. Freeze the fitted maps before 5,280 live downstream interventions on 480 held-out signed responses. Templates and some vocabulary are shared across the item split. This is an adaptive experiment on previously observed H600 data, not independent confirmation or complete lexical isolation. The broad basis retains 99.957% of discovery context energy; that training statistic alone does not establish transfer.

Recompute competence on the four held-out pairs in each task/template. Seven cells pass; agreement1, binding1 and sentiment1 fail and are retained. Capital recall1 now passes on this subset, although it failed on the full H600 cell. This subset distinction is reported rather than used to select cases.

Even ordinary Euclidean projection in the broad basis gives relative KL 0.020–0.100 across all 30 task/template/signal cells.

Better KL does not establish fidelity for every answer statistic. Broad number-metric margin error ranges 0.056–0.372, and relative target-token CE error ranges 0.065–0.588. Broad multi-signal CE error reaches 0.653. The distribution can be close while a selected token's loss or a small contrast is less faithfully preserved. CE here is fidelity to the full intervention's intended-token loss, not a demonstrated improvement in task accuracy.

The new basis's response oracle errors remain 0.144–0.281 internally, much smaller than the old oracle's errors but nonzero. The new basis therefore captures genuinely more of the tested response map, rather than merely choosing better coefficients in the old span. Internal oracle residuals still do not give a lower bound on output KL or CE.

Updated interpretation: H600's weak transfer was chiefly inadequate context coverage on this panel, not evidence that each task requires unrelated computational units. A shared fixed-size span can support these five families' local context-switch responses. Metric choice remains relevant to particular output contrasts, but adding signal diversity has much smaller effects than replacing the narrow span. Because the metric uses natural e magnitudes, equal training case counts are not equal response-energy weighting; this study does not exhaust all possible metric designs.

Remaining explanations include (a) reusable local computational coordinates, (b) a shared subspace for these few nuisance edits and prompt templates, and (c) wider rank requirements once contexts vary more. The current result cannot distinguish them. Next freeze the broad basis and both maps, then test unseen wording and different same-answer context edits across all five tasks. Use matched task-changing context differences as an additional scope challenge, clearly separated from nuisance changes. Keep competence failures, new-case target-informed oracles and separate KL/margin/CE reporting. Fresh wording/context transfer has higher information value than refitting this panel again.

Among the six competence-passing task/template cells, both margin and KL improve in 4/6 for number, 3/6 for task, 3/6 for random. These counts describe this panel, not independent statistical replications.

The clearest preserved benefit is agreement's answer contrast: with its task-derived signal, relative margin error falls 1.452 to 0.269. Yet relative KL remains 0.788 and target-token CE fidelity barely changes (0.966 to 0.967). With a random signal, agreement's relative margin error worsens 1.023 to 1.252. For competent copying template0, task-signal margin improves only 1.068 to 0.958, and KL 0.936 to 0.895. These are weak approximations despite improvements. Sentiment task-signal margin improves 0.524 to 0.460 while KL worsens 0.917 to 0.948 and relative target-token CE error worsens 1.323 to 1.785.

Single-token CE is measured against the explicit intended answer token, separately from semantic-group NLL. CE fidelity here means preserving the full intervention's CE; it does not mean lowering the model's task loss. In failed-competence cells, intended answers remain labels, not proof of a behavior the model performs.

Most important, even the per-case oracle retains large local response errors: approximately 0.806–0.910 across all cells. The frozen context span lacks much of the new responses. Since the oracle uses the target response, changing only the fixed coefficient rule cannot remove that internal error within this span. This is not a lower bound on output KL or CE, nor a proof that the full computation lacks a compact representation in a different span.

Updated hypotheses and discriminating next experiment:

1. The agreement-trained context span has narrow coverage. Strongly supported by large oracle residuals. Broaden context discovery while holding rank fixed, then test held-out items.
2. The coefficient metric depends on the incoming signal distribution. Supported by agreement's number/task versus random contrast; one random direction is insufficient to characterize all generic directions. Compare number-only and multi-signal metrics in the same span.
3. A reusable representation exists but needs both broader context coverage and a broader response metric. Still open. Use a factorial of old/broad basis and old/broad metric to separate them.
4. Output-selective insensitivity hides large internal errors. Consistent with agreement margin improvement alongside weak KL/CE fidelity. Keep all three objectives separate rather than treating margin as complete faithfulness.
5. Prompt format or the kind of nuisance change drives some differences. Unresolved because context changes differ by task. Hold out wording and report each context-change type rather than pooling them as equivalent.
6. Each task needs unrelated units. Not established: a narrow span failing transfer cannot establish that no shared span exists. Compare a shared fixed-rank basis against task-specific bases with matched capacity and held-out evaluation.

Next use discovery items only to fit broader context coverage and multi-signal metrics, freeze before evaluating held-out items, and compare the factorial against the current map and oracle. Preserve failed competence cells and explicitly distinguish exploratory familiar-wording evaluation from fresh confirmation. This has higher information value than more agreement wording variants.

Independent float64 evaluation on all 960 cases matches the saved float32 cross terms within 4.14e-7 and verifies the algebraic identity within 6.42e-13. No evidence of an intervention implementation error. Finite KL/CE/margin/internal metrics. FineWeb document count remains 26,112; broad goal remains active and incomplete.

Most likely interpretation: the useful notion of context similarity depends on the operation and incoming signal distribution. Ordinary Euclidean context similarity discards distinctions that matter downstream; a fixed response-informed rule transfers within this family. Alternatives still open include a broadly reusable response metric versus a grammar/number-specific metric, and downstream insensitivity hiding substantial internal differences. Larger-dose success weakens a strictly infinitesimal-only account but does not resolve those alternatives.

Next prioritize cross-signal and cross-task transfer over further wording variants. Freeze K and compare its behavior on copying, factual recall, entity binding and sentiment as well as agreement, with competence gates and retained failures. Compare fixed metric versus ordinary projection and per-case oracle for each operation; report internal error, output KL and target-token CE separately. A task-specific benefit would support conditional computational units; broad transfer would support more reusable units. Do not infer diverse-task success from this agreement-only panel.

The previous goal turn made progress by identifying MLP11's contextual and incoming-response dependence.
