## Previous continuation: H591

## H591 — MLP11's response depends jointly on contextual state and incoming perturbation

Following H590's discovery-selected suppressor, capture MLP11's normalized native input z and the input change e induced by the same signed Attention5 perturbation. The model's ungated bilinear MLP obeys exactly:

B(z+e)-B(z) = Down[Left(z) Right(e) + Left(e) Right(z)] + Down[Left(e) Right(e)].

The first term is linear in e but depends on native context z; the second is quadratic in e. The output bias cancels. The identity is applied after input normalization, so it does not separately explain the effect of normalization upstream.

For each recipient, independently choose its own or matched unfronted z and its own or matched unfronted e. Replace only MLP11's response around the recipient's native output, keeping the Attention5 perturbation and other computation live. These are counterfactual post-normalization combinations, not asserted natural states. Four crossings at two doses and both signs over 192 prompts give 3,072 intervention forwards; native/perturbed capture uses 960 forwards. Unfronted recipient cells give exact duplicate controls.

| Type/frame, small dose | Own context/input | Unfronted context only | Unfronted input response only | Both unfronted |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|regular/relative_clause|1.2251|1.1588|1.3181|1.2527|
|regular/fronted_preposition|0.6522|0.7065|0.6652|0.7765|
|irregular/relative_clause|1.0620|1.0616|1.1955|1.1803|
|irregular/fronted_preposition|0.6711|0.7290|0.6791|0.8074|

In fronted prompts, unfronted context alone increases central response modestly; unfronted incoming response alone changes it less. Replacing both has a larger effect than either alone: irregular 0.671 native, 0.729 context-only, 0.679 incoming-only, 0.807 both. The factorial interaction is not assignable solely to the local bilinear term, because later computation is nonlinear too. The same qualitative pattern persists at half dose.

Relative clauses differ. On irregular nouns, native 1.062 becomes 1.062 with context-only replacement, 1.196 with incoming-only replacement, and 1.180 with both. Thus the explanation cannot be a universal fixed MLP11 suppression gate: different frames change the contextual operator and incoming response in different proportions. This also does not explain all downstream suppression—H590's selected operations accounted for only part of the frame gap.

The quadratic term's relative norm averages 0.0129 at small dose (maximum 0.0501), and 0.1029 at half dose (maximum 0.4349). This makes a context-conditioned linear approximation plausible locally, but does not prove the quadratic term is causally negligible. Earlier experiments already showed that norm size and behavioral influence can rank components differently. Small perturbation nonlinearity also does not eliminate the bilinear dependence between native context and response direction.

This is a more concrete candidate computational description than “a number neuron”: a shared number-associated direction is transformed by a context-conditioned local operator, with incoming state and later readout jointly determining its effect. It remains a local mechanistic account on a narrow agreement panel, not a complete circuit or general feature ontology.

Next causally separate the linear-in-response and quadratic terms: replace MLP11's response with each term alone, their sum, or zero at both doses; retain all frames and lexical types. Compare actual output shifts, KL and answer-group loss instead of inferring importance from norm. Then use the surviving causal term to identify which context directions or upstream writes alter its action. Do not treat successful compression or an algebraic identity alone as the explanation.

Audits: exact-form response matches direct MLP output differences within 2.33e-4 relative error under float32 subtraction; native response replacement replays H588 within 1.53e-5 margin; unfronted duplicate crossings match exactly; finite metrics and unchanged source/basis. No new prompts or natural-text documents; FineWeb total 26,112. Broad goal active and incomplete.

The previous goal turn made progress by separating propagated response from terminal sensitivity. Capture all downstream attention/MLP final-position writes after the fixed Attention5 perturbation, including MLP5. Residual gains are products of subsequent block skip coefficients.

For a common scalar comparison, map each term through the matched unfronted prompt's native terminal-readout gradient. This is a local descriptive chart, not a causal percentage. The exact vector reconstruction and chart's finite-difference error are audited separately. Rank components by the most negative fronted-minus-unfronted mean chart contribution at small dose on regular nouns only. This selects MLP11, MLP17 and MLP9. Lock that selection before causal tests.

Then overwrite each selected operation's final-position output with its same-prompt unperturbed value while preserving the original Attention5 perturbation. Test each alone, jointly, every downstream write clamped, and an unchanged control on all three frames, both noun types and both doses. There are 4,608 intervention forwards, plus 960 capture forwards. Irregular nouns validate the selection on an already-explored panel; no untouched population claim.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|regular/unchanged|1.2763|1.2251|0.6522|-0.6241|
|regular/mlp_11|1.3427|1.3010|0.8421|-0.5006|
|regular/mlp_17|1.0546|1.1492|0.5058|-0.5488|

|regular/all|0.1524|0.1930|0.1391|-0.0132|
|irregular/unchanged|1.2786|1.0620|0.6711|-0.6075|
|irregular/mlp_11|1.3531|1.2364|0.8901|-0.4630|

|irregular/all|0.1650|0.1959|0.1598|-0.0051|

MLP11 behaves as an active suppressor under this intervention: clamping it increases the response, especially in fronted prompts. In irregular nouns, fronted response rises 0.671 to 0.890, while unfronted rises 1.279 to 1.353. MLP9 differs: clamping it reduces both responses, particularly unfronted (1.279 to 0.952 versus 0.671 to 0.553). MLP17 also supplies more amplification in unfronted contexts. Thus the frame gap combines active suppression and differential amplification; calling every negative frame contrast a suppressor would be incorrect.

The selected joint clamp reduces the small-dose gap from -0.624 to -0.285 on regular nouns and -0.607 to -0.250 on irregular nouns. The effect persists at half dose. A substantial gap remains, and the changes are not additive independent shares. Intervening on an earlier write changes later responses.

Clamping all downstream responses leaves only a small direct-path response (~0.14–0.20) and nearly removes the fronted gap. This is a strong algebra/control condition, not a natural computation or a claim that these operations can safely be deleted. Relative to the direct path, the network's net response is amplifying in all frames. “Fronted attenuation” describes a contrast with the unfronted frame, not overall attenuation below the direct path.

Next H591 examines MLP11 specifically using its exact bilinear response. Cross the recipient versus matched unfronted native MLP input with the recipient versus unfronted incoming perturbation. Replace only the resulting response around the recipient native output. This distinguishes context-conditioned local transformation from the form of the incoming perturbation. All other downstream computation remains live.

## Previous continuation: H589

## H589 — Frame-dependent attenuation mostly arises before the terminal readout; compensation can conceal it

Capture the native final residual and the response to identical number-axis perturbations at +/-0.0625 and +/-0.5 discovery units for all 192 prompts. This uses 960 model forwards including native captures. For each matched lexical/type/subject-number/attractor-number combination, cross three donor-frame final response vectors with three recipient-frame native final residuals. Apply the model's unchanged final RMS normalization, unembedding, tanh cap and answer-group measurement. There are 2,304 terminal residual crossings; the 768 same-frame diagonals must replay H588.

An off-diagonal state is recipient_native_final_residual + (donor_perturbed_final_residual - donor_native_final_residual). This isolates a propagated response from its terminal readout baseline; it is a counterfactual state, not a naturally generated prompt. Responses from different frames are not asserted semantically interchangeable outside this test.

At small dose, rows below specify recipient terminal context and columns specify the frame that produced the response. Values are mean central plural response per discovery unit.

| Type / terminal context | Response from preposition | Response from relative clause | Response from fronted phrase |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|regular/preposition|1.2763|0.9881|0.6835|
|regular/relative_clause|1.5235|1.2250|0.8520|
|regular/fronted_preposition|1.2294|0.9341|0.6522|
|irregular/preposition|1.2786|0.8754|0.6714|
|irregular/relative_clause|1.4852|1.0620|0.7893|
|irregular/fronted_preposition|1.2628|0.8726|0.6711|

For regular nouns, the native fronted response is 0.652 versus unfronted 1.276. Putting the unfronted response into the fronted terminal context gives 1.229; putting the fronted response into the unfronted terminal context gives only 0.683. Irregular nouns show the same pattern (1.263 and 0.671 respectively). Thus most of this frame contrast follows the propagated response vector, rather than terminal-readout sensitivity alone. The half-dose crossings agree qualitatively.

Relative clauses reveal compensation. For regular nouns, native responses look similar: 1.276 unfronted versus 1.225 relative clause. But a relative-clause response read in the unfronted terminal context gives only 0.988, while the unfronted response read in the relative-clause terminal context gives 1.523. Intermediate attenuation and stronger terminal sensitivity offset. Similar observable effects therefore need not imply the same internal computation.

An exact symmetric allocation of each 2x2 cross is saved: propagation contribution = half of the donor-response change under each terminal context; terminal-context contribution = half of the context change under each donor response. These sum to the diagonal contrast by construction; interaction is reported separately. At small dose, regular fronting has total change -0.624, allocated -0.585 propagation and -0.039 terminal context; irregular fronting -0.607 = -0.599 + -0.008. For relative clauses the opposing terms are -0.293 +0.242 (regular) and -0.413 +0.197 (irregular). These are algebraic summaries of this crossing, not independent causal percentages or unique mediation shares.

Research implication: a common residual direction has context-dependent downstream transformations. A data-based equivalence class defined only by final margin can merge states with different internal responses and compensation. That may be acceptable for a behavioral objective, but cannot establish mechanistic equivalence. We still have not identified the later operations that attenuate, rotate or compensate for the number response.

Next trace the perturbation's residual response through later blocks, accounting exactly for residual scaling and attention/MLP write changes. Use that accounting to select targeted response clamps on discovery items and test on irregular/held-out items. Prioritize explaining the fronted attenuation and relative-clause compensation rather than adding more descriptive compression. Keep fixed-input and context-crossing predictions distinct.

Audits: 768 diagonal crossings replay H588 within 1.63e-5 margin; symmetric decomposition closes exactly; finite metrics, unchanged source/basis. No new prompts or natural-text documents; FineWeb total 26,112. Broad goal active and incomplete.

| Type | Subject coefficient main effect | Attractor coefficient main effect | Full subject donor movement | Rank1 subject donor movement | Rank1 relative margin error | Rank1 relative reference KL |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|regular|224.3145|114.2498|0.3921|0.3045|0.3640|0.5819|

But the attractor also shifts the coefficient: 63 of 64 attractor contrasts are positive. 312 token-valid prompts, 78 lexical pairs and 6,552 paired evaluations (13,104 intervention-stage forward passes). Binding and sentiment transfer cells remain failed and reported; they do not establish competent transfer.

The clearest result is Attention5 in agreement. Averaged over the two sites, donor-directed margin change is 1.264 discovery and 1.150 transfer, versus transfer nuisance absolute change 0.041. At the final “usually” token alone, mean donor-directed change is 2.369 discovery and 2.158 transfer; all 16 endpoint interventions in each split move in the predicted donor direction. At the penultimate token, means are 0.159 and 0.141. These are paired endpoints from only eight lexical items per split, not 32 independent population observations.

The final token is identical across singular/plural variants, so the effect cannot be attributed to exchanging that token's lexical identity. The earlier subject still differs in number and surface form, and nuisance swaps differ in content and magnitude; their smaller effects do not by themselves establish a pure number feature. Attention5 is the entire attention output, not one identified head or one feature.

The isolated L7H8 value path remains small: averaging both sites gives transfer donor movement 0.056 versus whole-write 1.150. This is not an additive mediation percentage. The principal agreement effect must be explained through additional routes or interactions under these interventions.

Recall and copying show much smaller donor-directed effects, often no larger than nuisance effects, at these fixed sites. Nearby operations also vary. Thus this supports a particularly useful agreement response at a specific operation/site, not a task-universal feature. Failed binding and sentiment transfer cells show donor movement but remain below their competence gates; do not promote them to confirmed transfer evidence.

Next use the replicated agreement effect to test a representation directly. Learn low-rank directions from discovery singular/plural Attention5 write differences at “usually”, freeze ranks/basis, then replace only the projected difference on every transfer item. Compare internal residual error against preservation of the full donor-swap output distribution (KL), grammatical-number margin and answer-group loss. Include norm-matched random subspaces and nuisance directions; retain all ranks and cases. If a compact shared direction preserves causal effects across nouns, test new wording and the other competent tasks before labeling it a reusable number feature. If internal and behavioral rank requirements differ, that directly informs the proposed data-based equivalence classes. This does not yet validate response-based grouping or a canonical basis.

## H582 — Small format changes improve competence, but threshold-passing formats need not transfer

The previous goal turn made progress: H581 established a diverse causal panel and exposed second-template failures. Before further causal interpretation, preregister task-specific two-by-two format factors over discovery and lexical-transfer sets. Each condition has eight attempted pairs with both answer endpoints and both same-answer nuisance versions. Factors: agreement beside/near x empty/usually ending; recall national capital/capital city x is/is the city of ending; binding school/library x gave/handed; sentiment Text/Review x Overall sentiment/Sentiment; copying He/She x spoke with/talked to.

Score 1,248 prompts. Eight condition-pairs (32 prompts) fail single-token answer eligibility: the Dennis/Jacqueline transfer pair in binding and copying across four conditions. These exclusions happen before model scoring, not from performance. Some discovery prompts repeat H581. Transfer lexical combinations are new to this panel, not claimed unseen by the model or all earlier studies.

Gate stays >=4 valid pairs, >=75% both-endpoint candidate correctness and >=50% intended-group full-vocabulary top1. Before transfer inference, choose the lexicographically first discovery-passing condition, not the best transfer condition. Keep every result and the earlier failed panel.

| Task | Locked condition | Discovery top1 | Transfer top1 | Discovery nuisance top1 | Transfer nuisance top1 | Transfer gate |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
|agreement|01|1.000|0.938|1.000|0.938|pass|
|capital_recall|10|1.000|1.000|1.000|1.000|pass|
|entity_binding|00|0.500|0.357|0.438|0.357|fail|
|sentiment|01|0.500|0.438|0.250|0.188|fail|
|sequence_copy|00|1.000|1.000|1.000|1.000|pass|

Agreement: adding “usually” after the beside phrase raises discovery top1 from 0.438 to 1.000 and transfer from 0.563 to 0.938. Both-endpoint candidate accuracy was already 1.000. This is consistent with making a finite-verb continuation more likely, not adding number knowledge.

Recall: changing “national capital” to “capital city” yields 1.000 top1 in both splits. Appending “is the city of” is not a universal fix: with “national capital” it reaches only 0.375 discovery top1 but 0.875 transfer. A direct boundary explanation alone is insufficient; wording and lexical context interact.

Binding: selected condition 00 barely passes discovery (0.500) and fails transfer (0.357). Other cells perform better, but choosing them after inspecting transfer would invalidate this particular locked selection test. Sentiment: selected condition 01 similarly falls from 0.500 to 0.438, and its nuisance variants perform worse. Review+Sentiment performs better in both splits, but remains an alternative observed condition rather than a replacement for the locked primary. Copying passes all cells on both splits.

This demonstrates why mere threshold passing on one small discovery set is weak evidence for generalization. It also explains why candidate-only scores can conceal continuation-format differences. Factor changes can alter the underlying computation; this is not a pure answer-boundary causal intervention.

Next H583 retests fixed writer operations on these locked conditions, reporting three competent transfer tasks and retaining the two failed cells. This preserves the selection rule. Future stronger format selection should use discovery-only robustness criteria and a genuinely new confirmation set, not retrofit this transfer set.

## H581 — Diverse-task transfer favors shared writers with context-dependent downstream routes

H580 made progress by distinguishing internal restoration from downstream effect. This experiment expands beyond copying: 80 lexical pairs across five tasks and two templates, with base, opposite-answer, and answer-preserving nuisance prompts at both endpoints, totaling 320 prompts. No token-validity exclusions. Prompt combinations were composed for this experiment; lexical items overlap previous studies and training novelty is not claimed.

Before inference, lock candidate operations MLP3, MLP6 and Attention5, with neighboring controls MLP2, MLP5, Attention4 and Attention6. Fix sites at final and penultimate tokens across all tasks. These positions are not assumed to have the same syntactic or semantic role. For each recipient, swap the selected writer output from the counterfactual donor, same-answer nuisance donor, or itself. In a separate pass replay only the induced local value change through native routing of L4H0 (MLP2/3) or L7H8 (other operations), with the identity bus fixed. The target head can be only a small route among many.

6,720 paired evaluations give 13,440 intervention-stage forward passes. All items, failed templates and controls are retained. Effects are conditional interventions; whole and isolated paths are not an additive mediation decomposition. Donor values can come from different surface tokens at the fixed site, and nuisance edits vary by task. This is not a matched semantic-feature experiment.

Attention5 has larger average donor-directed effects in agreement (0.430) and sentiment (0.569) than in copying (0.047). Yet the isolated L7H8 value path carries only 0.0016 and 0.0383 donor-directed margin respectively. This rejects treating that single copying-derived route as the explanation for the whole operation's cross-task effect at these sites. It is consistent with shared upstream operations whose effects reach output through context-dependent routes. It does not identify a shared feature or rule out other carrier positions.

Neighboring controls matter: Attention4 gives agreement donor movement 0.081, while Attention6 gives 0.017. In sentiment, Attention6 gives 0.193 and MLP5 gives 0.106. In copying, Attention6 (0.074) exceeds selected Attention5 (0.047). Candidate operations are neither uniquely effective nor uniformly ordered. Nuisance effects often exceed counterfactual effects in recall, binding and copying. We therefore do not assign task-semantic labels from these swaps.

Full-output KL and intended-answer-group NLL are saved independently from internal writer/value norms and candidate margins. Group NLL uses the fixed answer set; it is not single-token CE. This batch measures the necessary responses but does not yet fit or validate a response-based canonical representation or whole-task-held-out predictor.

### Refreshed hypothesis set after the basic tests

1. Shared contextual writers support several tasks through different downstream routes.
2. Reader gates select task-relevant directions from broad contextual state.
3. One feature can have several token carriers rather than a unique location.
4. A low-dimensional causal-response representation transfers better than raw-state similarity.
5. Large state variance mainly describes answer-preserving context.
6. Small state directions can dominate a selected readout.
7. Punctuation changes contextual state, not just positional phase.
8. Relative position can still change which contextual directions are read.
9. Some apparent semantic effects are lexical-identity effects.
10. Syntactic roles, rather than token identities, organize transferable carriers.
11. Sentence boundaries alter routing or contextual-state construction.
12. Bilinear MLPs implement context-conditioned local operators rather than fixed feature detectors.
13. Attention and MLP writes cooperate; single-write clamps miss interactions.
14. Residual normalization changes the effective importance of a writer.
15. Persistent identity values and contextual local values support distinct routes.
16. Downstream compensation can hide large upstream state differences.
17. One-token competence gates confuse formatting preferences with underlying knowledge.
18. Apparent low-dimensionality depends strongly on data/task coverage.
19. Off-manifold donor swaps can distort otherwise meaningful representations.
20. Data-equivalent computations admit multiple useful bases, with different equivalence classes under internal, KL and loss criteria.

The leading working explanation is 1–2, with 3, 6, 7 and 12 supported locally by earlier tests. Hypothesis 17 directly explains several observed gate failures. Hypotheses 4 and 20 remain proposals, not established results; 9–11, 13–16 and 19 remain important alternatives or confounds.

### Next discriminating experiments

First repair evaluation coverage: preregister second-template continuations with an unambiguous answer boundary, keep original failed cases, and assess newly composed lexical combinations before interventions. Then freeze candidate operations and compare response signatures across held-out tasks/templates. A response grouping must predict donor-directed changes and KL better than raw-state proximity and neighboring-operation controls. Keep answer loss separate. Test role-aligned versus fixed-position sites to distinguish shared computation from a position artifact. For the strongest transfer, cross writer contribution with downstream reader routing to test hypothesis 1 against a fixed-feature/fixed-route account. Do not call geometric compression an explanation unless these causal predictions transfer.

Audits: self full margin error <=3.82e-6 and isolated <=4.30e-6; finite metrics; source and locked manifest unchanged. An independent 40-case live value/projection-hook audit spanning all task/templates and both target heads/sites agrees with routing reconstruction within 3.79e-5 absolute preprojection error (max relative 2.44e-4). The first attempt stopped at a rotary tensor-slicing error before interventions; corrected axis slicing, unchanged panel/hypotheses, then successful rerun. No new FineWeb documents; tracked total 26,112. Broad goal remains active and incomplete.

## H580 — Upstream value restoration and downstream influence rank writers differently

The previous goal turn made progress: H579 localized the carrier positions and supplied the fixed targets for this experiment. Test L4H0's period and pronoun values and L7H8's verb value. At the carrier token, replace every single earlier attention or MLP output with its aligned base-prompt output. This changes the model normally thereafter. Separately, take only the resulting local value difference and inject its contribution through native producer routing at the final destination; keep the persistent bus and all other producer reads native. These are different interventions, not an additive mediation decomposition.

All 128 edited copying prompts are retained: two templates, four phrases, two delimiters, four name pairs and both variants. Include self controls and direct base-value controls. There are 4,608 paired evaluations (9,216 forward passes in the intervention stage, including controls). Direct base-value controls have only a meaningful isolated-path intervention; their upstream pass is a native capture. No new prompts or natural-text documents.

Measure three distinct quantities: local value distance from base divided by native distance; downstream L14H4 gate distance from phase-only divided by native distance; and full-vocabulary native-to-intervened KL plus intended-answer CE change. KL measures prediction-distribution change; CE measures answer loss. Candidate-margin magnitude is retained separately. None is automatically a semantic explanation or a percentage of independent computation.

Select the upstream writer giving the lowest mean value-distance ratio over old-template delimiters, without using the new template for selection. The selected operations are MLP3 for both L4H0 carriers and MLP6 for L7H8's verb. New-template evaluation is within an already explored panel, not an untouched confirmatory sample.

| Carrier | Selected writer | Old parentheses value ratio | Old commas | New parentheses | New commas |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|L4H0_pos1|mlp_3|0.575|0.539|0.535|0.516|
|L4H0_pos2|mlp_3|0.521|0.495|0.566|0.527|
|L7H8_pos3|mlp_6|0.611|0.657|0.673|0.647|

The selected writer leaves roughly half to two-thirds of the internal difference. These ratios do not imply that the remainder is an independent component. Single-writer clamps change later operations and can introduce counterfactual states.

Crucially, the geometric winner need not have the largest downstream gate effect. For L7H8's verb on old-template commas, MLP6 yields value ratio 0.657 and gate ratio 0.971. Attention5 restores less of the value (0.748), yet has a larger gate movement toward phase-only (0.899). On new-template commas, Attention5 yields gate ratio 1.006, while MLP6 gives 0.981. Thus even the directional influence remains context dependent. For L4H0's period, MLP3 roughly halves the internal difference but leaves the old-template gate nearly unchanged (0.997/1.015). Large internal changes can lie in directions with weak effect on the measured downstream read.

Whole-write and isolated-path behavioral effects also differ. For new-template commas, the verb's MLP6 clamp gives mean absolute candidate-margin change 0.0774 in the full run versus 0.0402 through the isolated value path; native-to-intervened KL is 0.00059 versus 0.00018 (rounded), and mean answer CE change is +0.0290 versus +0.0150. These are not additive shares. Other altered paths and downstream nonlinearities can contribute or cancel.

Audits: self full and isolated-path margins match exactly; direct base-value replay agrees with H579 within 1.53e-5 margin and 7.43e-7 gate coefficient; all measured fields finite; source hash unchanged. Computation is float32 after loading bf16-rounded weights. Tracked FineWeb documents remains 26,112.

Research implication: causal response directions are a more promising unit to test than raw value-vector similarity alone. This is a hypothesis, not proof of a canonical basis. The nearest MLP contributes strongly to contextual state, while a different upstream operation can dominate a selected readout. We should not compress away directions merely because their variance is small, or identify a feature solely from a large norm restoration.

Next priority is a fresh diverse panel, before further narrowing this copying circuit: copying, person binding, agreement, factual recall, and sentiment, each with at least two templates, answer-changing counterfactuals and matched answer-preserving context edits. Lock MLP3/MLP6 and Attention5 as candidate writer operations and include neighboring controls. Check whole-family competence without dropping individual failures. Compare held-out internal value restoration against full-output KL, answer CE, and donor-directed effects. Test whether response-based grouping transfers better than raw-state grouping; use whole-task holdouts as well as template holdouts. Carrier positions must be declared from syntax before interventions; failure to find an analogous position is itself a limitation, not permission to select the best token after seeing effects.

The objective remains active and incomplete: these tests establish conditional routes on a small panel, not the model's general feature ontology.

| Condition/head | Both restored | Routing restored only | Values restored only |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|copying_old_paren_L4H0|0.903|0.985|0.919|

Restoring values generally reproduces substantially more of the suffix effect than restoring routing. For L4H0 in new-template parentheses, both restores give residual ratio 0.681, values-only 0.764 and routing-only 0.924. In new-template commas, values-only produces 1.212, close to both-restored 1.262, whereas routing-only is 1.014. Thus the sign-changing influence largely remains when routing is held native and only contextual values are changed.

The bus vectors match exactly at aligned suffix tokens. Consequently the value difference comes entirely from the local context-dependent value path, after its fixed mixture coefficient. An exact vector expansion into routing-only, value-only and interaction terms is retained in geometry. The value term's average projection onto the total suffix-write change ranges about 0.78–1.00 across cells, but these signed projections can cancel and are not independent causal percentages. The live crossings provide the stronger evidence.

This refines the mechanism: inserted text changes representations at later suffix tokens; producer heads read those contextualized values into the destination; this alters the subsequent L14 query and its name read. It is a partial causal chain, not an end-to-end circuit proof. We have not identified which earlier computation writes that information into suffix values, its semantic content, or whether the same carrier works on unrelated tasks.

Next H579 should localize the suffix contribution to individual aligned positions (yesterday, punctuation, pronoun and spoke/wrote in these templates), replacing only local values while holding routing/bus fixed. Preserve all punctuation/template conditions and full-suffix controls. Then trace the strongest carrier's input through earlier layers and test lexical/template transfer before assigning a feature label.

|copying_new_comma_L7H8|0.990|0.936|1.008|1.000|

L4H0's new-template punctuation reversal is largely reproduced by replacing only the suffix contribution: residual ratio 0.681 for parentheses versus 1.262 for commas, almost the same as whole-head replacement (0.675/1.260). Replacing the inserted span or selected name does little in comparison. This localizes the relevant edit-induced change to reading later words, rather than a direct read from the insertion itself. It does not show that inserted tokens are globally unimportant: earlier layers may have propagated their information into those later words.

L7H8 also depends on suffix and final-token contributions, with more distributed effects across conditions. Group effects need not sum in the live model. Norm and projection summaries in JSON describe the writes, not unique additive causal mediation. Output-margin changes remain separate from the target L14H4 gate statistic.

## H576 — A single producer head retains the punctuation-dependent transfer failure

Freeze H575's selected heads: binding L9H7/L9H6, copying L7H8/L4H0. Test on H572's 128 new-template edited cases. Conditions are each of the four individual heads, own-task pair, other-task pair, all-four union, whole parent attention layer(s), MLP10 and self: ten modes, 1,280 interventions. The prompt panel was already characterized; these are new interventions, not independent new lexical examples. No head choices are updated after seeing transfer results.

| Condition | Own head pair | Other head pair | Four-head union | Whole parent layer(s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|binding_new_paren|0.824|0.941|0.752|0.794|

Binding's selected pair removes about 14–18% of the gate correction; this is partial transfer. Copying's pair removes about 52% with parentheses but increases comma discrepancy about 29%. L7H8 helps parentheses about 20% and has little comma effect.

The four-head union can therefore be less effective than the copying pair alone in that condition. More components do not automatically give a better explanatory circuit.

These effects do not establish whether the head's native contribution is helpful or harmful for task accuracy, nor whether its gate effect mediates its whole output effect. They show that the operation attributed to an isolated producer head depends on context and downstream consumers. A head name or a task label is not yet a stable semantic/computational unit.

This tests whether the change in effect comes from what the head reads or from how later computation interprets its write. Retain L7H8 as a control and distinguish source-group evidence from a full circuit explanation.

## H573 — Query construction is distributed; descriptive shares differ from causal effects

Trace all old-template binding and competent copying delimiter cases from H572. Capture final-position attention and MLP writes at layers 0–13, and the residual entering L14 attention normalization. Compare each edited prompt with its base prompt at its own final position. Final token and initial embedding are identical. Each prior write difference is multiplied by the product of subsequent residual lambdas through L14. Their sum reconstructs the edited-minus-base pre-attention residual.

For r0,r1 and RMS denominators s0,s1, normalized input difference is (r1−r0)/s0 + r1*(1/s1−1/s0). Map this exact finite decomposition through L14's first query projection. The normalization allocation depends on choosing the base denominator; it is descriptive, not a unique causal attribution. Query-head normalization and rotary effects remain active in the subsequent gate tests.

Then clamp each of 28 prior final-position writes separately to its base-prompt value, with all other computation live, plus self control. Only the destination position is changed; the earlier selected source key remains unaffected by causality. There are 128 edited prompts and 3,712 interventions. Measure how much contextual gate correction remains: mean absolute distance from the phase-only coefficient, divided by its native value. Smaller ratios mean movement toward the phase-only prediction, not necessarily better task behavior.

| Condition | Lowest residual-ratio single clamp | Residual ratio | Descriptive raw-query projection share |
|---|---|---:|---:|
|binding_old_paren|mlp_10|0.777|0.114|
|binding_old_comma|attn_9|0.790|0.128|
|copying_old_paren|attn_6|0.711|0.015|
|copying_old_comma|attn_7|0.690|0.042|

No single write removes most of the gate correction. The best conditions leave about 69–82%. Descriptive shares and causal effects need not agree: copying-parentheses attention6 accounts for about 1.5% of the raw-query difference projected onto its total change, yet its clamp reduces gate discrepancy by about 29%. Later responses, normalization and gate sensitivity intervene between those measurements. Projection shares can cancel and are not fractions of independent causal mediation.

Binding's attention9 and MLP10 consistently rank near the top. For a locked follow-up, select the two writes with lowest mean residual ratio across punctuation forms separately per task. This gives attention9/MLP10 for binding and attention7/attention4 for copying. Selection is discovery on the old templates, not a validated minimal circuit.

At L14H4 binding, the pooled same-task correction reduces error by about 69% in the old template and 68% in the new one. Length-specific and all-length pooling are almost identical there. The result is not universal. L8H3 binding gets worse under the pooled corrections. Copying L8H3 improves modestly in the old template and substantially in the new one; L14H4 copying does not consistently improve. These counterexamples limit the claim to particular reader/context regimes. Knowing that the first query factor carries a correction does not establish that its correction is constant or transferable everywhere.

All models still receive the recipient's base query, source key and edited rotary position. The learned object is only a pooled raw-query offset, and interventions change one source-edge coefficient while the rest of the edited model stays native. This is not a replacement model or a prediction of the entire sentence-edit effect.

The transferable adjustment may represent punctuation, clause structure or interruption, rather than the phrases' meanings or an abstract task. ## H567 — First query factor carries most contextual gate correction

Reuse all 192 edited H566 prompts. At each edited destination position, hold the recipient source key fixed and independently choose base or edited context for each of the two query projections. For base factors a,b and edited factors u,v, the coefficient change is lambda*((u−a)*b + a*(v−b) + (u−a)*(v−b)). These are exact algebraic terms, not independently identified semantic features. Cancellation can make individual absolute terms larger than the total change. This diagnostic holds the edited position fixed, so it isolates query-content changes relative to the phase-only prediction.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

At L14H4, first-factor-only updates remove about 93% of binding coefficient error and 91% of copying error. Updating only the second factor removes little. L8H3 is less clean: first-only updates remove about 57% of binding and 68% of copying error, leaving a material second-factor contribution. The interaction term is small on average in these cases but is retained exactly in the accounting.

This supports asymmetric factor roles for the selected reader/edits, not a universal first-factor semantic label. It is not a complete query swap: source-specific coefficient interventions need not reproduce all effects of changing a query throughout attention. Original competence and all edit cases are retained.

## H566 — Equal-position query content changes gate strength substantially

Extend H565 with four insertion texts selected by tokenizer length before inference. Four-token group: “(as usual)”, “(in fact)”, “(for once)”. Five-token group: “(as everyone expected)”, “(as people said)”, “(as others expected)”. Within each source/task case and group, source token/position, final token/position and prefix through the source are identical. All candidates remain single tokens. These controls change query content, not the selected source's causal key or the assigned positional rotation.

There are 224 native prompts (96 reused H565 anchors plus 128 new insertion prompts), 448 predictions saved before edited-prompt evaluation, and 1,792 interventions. All 14 task/gap cells have 16/16 candidate and full-vocabulary correctness. This panel contains no native accuracy failure to explain.

| Task | Head | Gap length | Mean within-length coefficient range | Mean phase-only predicted change magnitude | Range / predicted change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|binding|L8H3|4|0.02164|0.04040|53.6%|
|binding|L8H3|5|0.01737|0.05041|34.5%|
|binding|L14H4|4|0.13313|0.46530|28.6%|
|binding|L14H4|5|0.07584|0.57162|13.3%|
|copying|L8H3|4|0.02478|0.08800|28.2%|

|copying|L14H4|4|0.06332|0.07083|89.4%|
|copying|L14H4|5|0.03225|0.08111|39.8%|

Identical phase predictions do not imply identical actual gates. The mean range across the three content variants is 13–89% of the phase-only change magnitude, depending on task/head/length. These range ratios are descriptive comparisons, not additive causal fractions or independent sample estimates. Source keys agree within 3.06e−5, much smaller than the observed gate differences.

The importance of query content is also visible in prediction error: for binding L8H3, the four-token “in fact” insertion makes phase prediction worse than the unchanged-gate baseline (error ratio 1.79), whereas “for once” is well predicted (0.129). At L14H4 binding, “as usual” is poorly predicted (1.81), while the equal-length “in fact” is better predicted (0.557). This is not captured by insertion length alone. All outcomes and per-source interventions remain in JSON; no favorable phrase is selected away.

The emerging object is a conditional identity reader: position modifies a gate whose strength also depends on destination content, with downstream consumers determining its final effect. This is more informative than a distance-only rule, but it does not yet identify a semantic query feature or a complete computation unit. The inserted parentheticals have different meanings; the result is a controlled position comparison, not a pure semantic-variable experiment.

Next H567: separate the two query–key factors of bilinear attention. With source key and position controlled, cross base/edited query factors independently and replay their local source-edge effects. Use the same 40 H561 evaluation prompts at +1/16 amplitude. For each discovery coverage level, allow all centered context directions: 39, 79 and 159. The copying oracle floor drops from 32–54% to 17–28% mean relative vector error; binding drops from 16% to 10%. Ordinary full-span projection also improves. The compactness branch now has a bounded conclusion: within this intervention class, a simple context mean/PCA account preserves some behavioral statistics while missing substantial internal computation; metric reweighting within the old span did little, and broader coverage helps. No unique feature basis or canonical computational unit has been identified. ## Previous continuation: H562

## H562 — Even a response oracle cannot reconstruct copying within the discovery span

Evaluate the 40 excluded H558 prompts and 40 fresh H561 prompts at +1/16 amplitude. Use every one of the 39 centered training-context directions. First project the recipient context normally. Then, separately for each recipient displacement, solve a float64 least-squares system using the exact target linear response to choose oracle coordinates in the same span. Keep the mean-context response and quadratic term exact. This measures the minimum attainable local response error under these constraints. The oracle is not a usable predictor: it is given the target response. No downstream intervention or KL is evaluated here.

| Fresh family | Full-span projection response error | Oracle response error |
|---|---:|---:|
|binding|17.9%|16.0%|
|color_prose|56.8%|46.7%|
|color_record|65.3%|54.2%|
|name_prose|39.7%|31.6%|
|name_record|56.5%|44.9%|

Even the oracle leaves 32–54% mean response error on fresh copying and 16% on binding. It improves the ordinary full-span projection but does not approach exact reconstruction. The old held-out panel gives a similar result, with copying oracle errors 31–45%. These values are relative vector-norm errors, not squared explained-variance fractions.

Therefore reweighting or learning better coefficients confined to this fixed discovery span cannot eliminate the remaining local vector error for these directions. Important response components lie outside the span of its induced outputs. This is a limitation of the sampled representation, not proof that the underlying mechanism is intrinsically high-dimensional or that all compact models must fail. A different span, more diverse contexts, token-conditioned structure, or a behavioral rather than internal objective may behave differently.

Audits: all 80 oracle solutions no worse than ordinary projection; maximum relative normal-equation residual 6.14e−16; finite results; source unchanged. This is 80 algebraic response diagnostics, not 80 causal interventions.

Next H563 should expand discovery-context coverage while keeping evaluation lexical pairs and rank budgets fixed. Compare coverage curves and oracle residuals to separate insufficient sampling from dimension requirements. Choose token-valid donor examples before inference, exclude evaluation vocabulary from discovery, and use an additional prospective test panel if making new generalization claims. Retain a task/behavior distinction and physical-position/downstream-layer questions; context compression remains only one branch of the feature/computation investigation.

These are correlated probes, not independent population estimates.

Binding offers a clear example of why fidelity metrics must be separated. A name-copying context yields 134% mean relative local-response error and cosine 0.087, yet retains all 32 live-effect directions. Its margin MAE is 0.000829 nats against mean absolute native effect 0.003561, so even this behavioral agreement is limited: it preserves signs, not exact margins, logits, KL or loss. A mean binding context is closer internally (21% relative error, cosine 0.978) and has smaller margin MAE, 0.000192.

This connects to data-based canonical forms: many internal responses could share a coarse output statistic while differing internally. A useful representation should state its equivalence criterion and evaluation distribution. Current results support neither a unique fundamental basis nor a KL/CE-equivalent simplification. They identify a concrete, testable candidate object: a context-conditioned local response operator whose value depends on whether we require internal reconstruction or downstream behavioral fidelity.

Next H558 should test whether a small number of context modulation directions predicts these operators on held-out lexical pairs. Fit only on discovery pairs; evaluate internal vector error, output margins and full-distribution KL separately. Include the family mean and exact operator as baselines, freeze ranks/criteria before evaluation, and retain binding/copying and vocabulary crossings. This tests compactness only after the causal object has been specified. Continue to track downstream layers and physical-position controls as unresolved; no small L8 model alone explains the complete circuit.

## Previous continuation: H556

## H556 — Small L8 responses are dominated by bilinear linear cross terms

Reuse all 80 H554 prompts and destination-phase edge deltas, at ±1 and ±1/16 amplitudes. Capture the actual residual x entering L8 MLP normalization; define z=RMSNorm(x), e=RMSNorm(x+delta)−z, and B(z)=Down(Left(z)*Right(z))+bias. The exact finite algebra is:

B(z+e)−B(z) = Down(Left(z)*Right(e)+Left(e)*Right(z)) + Down(Left(e)*Right(e)).

The first term is linear in normalized displacement e but depends on native context z. The second is quadratic in e. This does not make the full model globally linear: normalization, context and later responses remain variable.

Test five local responses: full, linear normalized term only, quadratic only, fixed native RMS denominator, and the full first-order tangent including the RMS derivative. Replace only the final-position L8 MLP output response; preserve the attention perturbation and live later computation. This yields 1,600 causal interventions. The fixed-denominator counterfactual uses (x+delta)/s0 rather than renormalizing, so its difference from full is not a unique additive normalization attribution.

| Family, +1/16 amplitude | Quadratic / full response norm | Fixed-denominator relative error | Tangent relative error | Linear-only output-margin MAE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|binding|0.21%|1.71%|0.22%|0.0000030|
|color_prose|0.51%|7.19%|0.47%|0.0000326|
|color_record|0.43%|10.38%|0.37%|0.0000236|
|name_prose|0.51%|5.42%|0.49%|0.0000255|
|name_record|0.65%|7.02%|0.61%|0.0000511|

At +1/16, quadratic response norm averages 0.21–0.65% of the full response across families. Linear-only replacements preserve the live margin closely (mean absolute deviations 3e−6 to 5.1e−5 nats). Omitting the linear term causes much larger deviations. The context-dependent linear cross term is therefore a useful local approximation for this selected MLP response.

At full positive amplitude, quadratic fractions grow to 3.4–11.1%, and linear-only margin errors reach 0.00076–0.01260 nats. Finite-amplitude corrections matter. Freezing the RMS denominator changes the local response by 1.7–10.4% at +1/16; normalization contributes but does not account for most of the response under this comparison. The smallest positive perturbations average 0.069–0.232% of the pre-MLP residual norm, giving a concrete scale for the local approximation.

Audits: reconstructed pre-normalized input matches captured normalization exactly; full-response causal replay agrees with H555 within 8.59e−6 nats. Float32 bilinear decomposition has max coordinate error 3.37e−4 and maximum relative vector error 7.26e−4, consistent with subtracting large native outputs. A separate audit promotes the same normalized endpoints and bf16-rounded weights to float64: the algebra agrees to max coordinate error 5.30e−12 and relative error 2.53e−12. This verifies the formula numerically; it does not establish that L8 alone explains the downstream reversal. Source unchanged, all results finite.

Next H557 tests whether the local bilinear response operator transfers between native contexts: substitute the base context z in the linear term while retaining the recipient's actual displacement e, quadratic term and native output. Compare opposite tokens, formats, vocabularies and a leave-pair-out family mean. This separates context dependence of the bilinear operator from the recipient normalization change; it is not a whole-state activation transplant.

This is stronger evidence that an apparently identity-aligned attention write can have an opposing live effect after downstream computation. It is not evidence that the model becomes inaccurate under every intervention; effect-direction agreement and task accuracy are different quantities. ### Updated hypothesis set and discriminating tests

These are alternatives and compatible mechanisms, not calibrated probabilities. “Higher” means the evidence currently favors pursuing the idea, not that it has been established.

| # | Hypothesis | Priority / evidence | Discriminating test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Computation depends on a reader and its downstream consumers | Higher: live copying reverses frozen effects | Predict consumer responses on held-out contexts |
| 2 | Several MLP layers jointly transform the write | Higher: no single clamp restores discovery; all-MLP transfers | Cumulative and leave-one-live interventions |
| 3 | Same-layer L8 response provides a substantial first transformation | Higher: best single-layer discovery, transfer MAE reduction | Exact L8 input/output response decomposition |
| 4 | Context gates bilinear MLP response to the same write | Plausible | Match write direction across contexts, compare finite response |
| 5 | Token vocabulary, rather than task, explains copying/binding contrast | Unresolved major confound | Copy names and colors in identical templates |
| 6 | Physical source–destination distance explains contrast | Unresolved | Matched-distance templates and actual text-position controls |
| 7 | Rotary phase interacts with contextual key/query content | Supported locally by H549–H550 | Cross content and phase on fresh matched cases |
| 8 | A universal monotone distance preference explains all readers | Weakened by H550 | Prospective distance sweeps without fitting |
| 9 | A single MLP layer explains the reversal | Weakened by H552–H553 | Locked single-layer transfer and joint-layer tests |
| 10 | Residual normalization creates most of the response reversal | Open | Separate normalization-induced input change from bilinear response |
| 11 | Bilinear first-order cross terms dominate the finite response | Open | Exact linear-versus-quadratic response decomposition |
| 12 | Large interventions create off-distribution nonlinear reversals | Open | Positive/negative amplitude sweep approaching zero |
| 13 | Late layers counteract earlier transformations | Supported in discovery, not yet transferred | Boundary clamps and layerwise signed response accounting |
| 14 | Attention–MLP feedback rather than MLP alone is essential | Plausible: attention clamps also help | Factorial clamps at selected boundaries |
| 15 | Readout saturation creates apparent reversals | Weakened: exact frozen readout still disagrees | Compare residual/logit effects before and after bounded readout |
| 16 | Color copying has a special lexical subspace | Open | Hold templates fixed across colors, names and common nouns |
| 17 | The selected source is atypical among copying sources | Open | Repeat source-role intervention at first and second occurrences |
| 18 | A few neurons or a low-dimensional MLP response span the transformation | Open; not implied by whole-write clamps | Fit on discovery, test intervention reconstruction on held-out prompts |
| 19 | Effects are mainly additive cancellations rather than new feature construction | Open | Dose-response and exact path/response decomposition |
| 20 | Prompt-family surface conventions explain the transfer | Still possible despite two formats | New templates with matched tokens, positions and competence |

Next H554 prioritizes hypothesis 5: use the same name pairs for copying and binding, and cross name versus color vocabulary within identical copying templates. Freeze heads, layer and intervention conditions. Only after that distinction should the result be labeled task-specific. In parallel conceptual planning, retain amplitude/normalization decomposition as the route to specifying what the downstream consumers compute. Physical-position validation is still outstanding.

## H551 — MLP and attention responses alter the copying edge's downstream meaning

Posthoc follow-up to the H550 L8H3 copying failure. Retain all 16 copying prompts and all four nonnative position conditions. Run 256 interventions with four downstream modes: live, native MLP writes clamped at L8–L17, native attention writes clamped at L9–L17, and both. Clamps replace whole writes at every position, preserving the L8 attention edge intervention. These are broad dependency tests, not identification of individual neurons or a unique mediator.

| Downstream condition | Frozen-prediction direction agreement | Mean absolute effect | Prediction MAE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|live|42.2%|0.045203|0.098785|
|freeze_mlp|100.0%|0.055037|0.017299|
|freeze_attention|87.5%|0.057147|0.041317|
|freeze_both|100.0%|0.069637|0.000002|

Live computation agrees with the frozen prediction in 27/64 cases. Freezing MLP responses restores agreement in 64/64; freezing later attention restores 56/64. Freezing both exactly recovers the analytical final-residual prediction within 5.73e−6 nats. This numerical replay supports the intervention accounting rather than merely matching a direction label.

MLP responses are therefore important to the observed direction mismatch under these clamps; attention responses also matter. This is not an additive decomposition into independent MLP and attention shares: the components interact, and freezing either alters the inputs seen by the other. It does not establish that one particular MLP is necessary or that the same mechanism holds for all copying prompts.

The working unit of computation needs a source, a conditional reader, and its downstream consumers. A token-identity write may have a different live task effect than its frozen final-readout effect. H550 binding at these heads is more directly predictable; L8H3 copying requires a richer causal account. The original question remains unresolved at the level of a general ontology, but this supplies an experimentally testable distinction between direct readout and downstream transformation.
